The Third Adhyāya of the First Aṣṭaka

original p. 1

Printed on the page: the Om emblem; the invocations śrīḥ and śrī mahāgaṇādhipataye namaḥ; six verses of homage (the same as in the earlier volumes); the series title Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, Bhāga 4; and the heading prathamāṣṭake tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ "In the First Aṣṭaka, the Third Adhyāya".

॥ श्रीः ॥ श्री महागणाधिपतये नमः ॥ वागीशाद्याः सुमनसः सर्वार्थानामुपक्रमे । यं नत्वा कृतकृत्याः स्युस्तं नमामि गजाननम् ॥ यस्य निःश्वसितं वेदा यो वेदेभ्योऽखिलं जगत् । निर्ममे तमहं वन्दे विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरम् ॥ वेदः शिवः शिवो वेदो वेदाध्यायी सदाशिवः । तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन वेदमेव सदा जपेत् ॥

śrīḥ | śrī mahāgaṇādhipataye namaḥ || vāgīśādyāḥ sumanasaḥ sarvārthānām upakrame | yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāḥ syus taṃ namāmi gajānanam || yasya niḥśvasitaṃ vedā yo vedebhyo 'khilaṃ jagat | nirmame tam ahaṃ vande vidyātīrthamaheśvaram || vedaḥ śivaḥ śivo vedo vedādhyāyī sadāśivaḥ | tasmāt sarvaprayatnena vedam eva sadā japet ||

"Śrī. Homage to the Lord of the Gaṇas. — I bow to Gajānana (Gaṇeśa), by bowing to whom the Lord of Speech and the other gods are fulfilled at the beginning of every undertaking. I praise Vidyātīrtha-Maheśvara, whose breath the Vedas are, and who made the whole world out of the Vedas. The Veda is Śiva, and Śiva is the Veda; the student of the Veda is Sadāśiva; therefore, with every effort, one should always recite the Veda alone." Read letter by letter from the Kannada-script print; the verses are the standard ones that open each part, and the reading here is consistent with the same opening in the earlier volumes.

Sāyaṇa's introduction to the Third Adhyāya printed in Kannada script; read from the 150-dpi image:

अथ तृतीयाध्याय आरभ्यते । त्वमग्ने प्रथम इति सप्तमानुवाके पञ्च सूक्तानि । तत्रैतायामोपेति तृतीयं सूक्तं पञ्चदशर्चम् । ऋषिश्चान्यस्मादिति परिभाषयाऽऽङ्गिरसो हिरण्यस्तूप ऋषिः । अनुक्तत्वादिन्द्रो देवता । त्रिष्टुप् छन्दः । एतेत्यनुक्रमणिका । गोसववीवधयोर्निष्केवल्ये एतायामेति सूक्तं विनियुक्तम् । तथा च सूत्रितमतिमूर्तिना यक्ष्यमाण इति खण्डे । गोसववीवधौ पशुकाम इन्द्र सोममेतायामेति मध्यंदिने । आ. ६-८ । इति ॥

atha tṛtīyādhyāya ārabhyate | tvam agne prathama iti saptamānuvāke pañca sūktāni | tatraitāyāmopeti tṛtīyaṃ sūktaṃ pañcadaśarcam | ṛṣiś cānyasmād iti paribhāṣayāṅgiraso hiraṇyastūpa ṛṣiḥ | anuktatvād indro devatā | triṣṭup chandaḥ | etety anukramaṇikā | gosavavīvadhayor niṣkevalye etāyāmeti sūktaṃ viniyuktam | tathā ca sūtritam atimūrtinā yakṣyamāṇa iti khaṇḍe | gosavavīvadhau paśukāma indra somam etāyāmeti madhyaṃdine | ā. 6-8 | iti ||

Translation: "Now the Third Adhyāya is begun. In the seventh anuvāka, [the one beginning] tvam agne prathamaḥ, there are five sūktas. Of these, the third is the sūkta etāyāmopa, of fifteen ṛks. By the rule 'and the ṛṣi [is the same] as the other' (ṛṣiś cānyasmāt), the ṛṣi is Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa. Since no deity is stated, Indra is the deity. The metre is Triṣṭup — [so says] the Anukramaṇikā ("etā..."). This sūkta has its application (viniyoga) at the Niṣkevalya [śastra] of the Gosava and Vīvadha [rites]. So it has been stated by Atimūrti in the section beginning 'for him who is about to sacrifice': 'In the Gosava and Vīvadha, for one desiring cattle, [the sūkta addressed] to Indra and Soma, etāyām, at the midday [pressing]' — Āśv. [śrauta-sūtra] 6-8." Reading notes: the printed words "ऋषिश्चान्यस्मादि[ति]" and "सोममेतायामेति" are what the Kannada letters give; the word "पञ्चदशर्चम्" and the reference "ā. ६-८" were re-read at 300 dpi with zoom and are as printed. The form "atimūrtinā" is as in the Kannada anuvāda below, which also names the sūtra "Gosavavīvadhau paśukāma indrasomam etāyām iti madhyandinaḥ".

Anuvāda (Kannada explanation, as it begins on this page): "Having finished the Second Adhyāya in the previous part, we now begin the translation of the meaning of the Third Adhyāya. In the Seventh Anuvāka, which begins 'tvam agne prathamo aṅgirā ṛṣiḥ', the sūkta etāyāma is the third sūkta. In it there are fifteen ṛks [the sentence is continued on the next page]…"

original p. 2

heading of Sūkta 33

Anuvāda (continued): "…In the five sūktas of this anuvāka, 31 to 35, since 'Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa' is stated as the ṛṣi, the ṛṣi of this sūkta is Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa. Indra is the deity. The Anukramaṇikā states that the metre is Triṣṭup. This sūkta has its application, in the Gosava and Vīvadha sacrifices, when the Niṣkevalya śastra [hymn] is recited. This matter is stated in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section beginning 'atimūrtinā yakṣyamāṇa', by the sūtra 'gosavavīvadhau paśukāma indrasomam etāyām iti madhyandinaḥ' (Āś. 6-8)."

॥ ॐ ॥ — oṃ

Sūkta 33 — "etāyāmopa"

॥ मण्डल — १ ॥ अनुवाक — ७ ॥ सूक्त — ३३ ॥ ॥ अष्टक — १ ॥ अध्याय — ३ ॥ वर्ग, १—३ ॥ ॥ सूक्तदल्लिरुव ऋक्संख्यै १—१५ ॥ ॥ ऋषिः — हिरण्यस्तूप आङ्गिरसः ॥ ॥ देवता — इन्द्रः ॥ ॥ छन्दः — त्रिष्टुप् ॥

maṇḍala 1 | anuvāka 7 | sūkta 33 | aṣṭaka 1 | adhyāya 3 | varga 1–3 | number of ṛks in the sūkta: 1–15 | ṛṣi: Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa | devatā: Indra | chandas: Triṣṭup.

Translation of the heading: "Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 7, Sūkta 33; Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 3, Varga 1–3; number of ṛks in the sūkta: 1–15; Ṛṣi: Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa; Deity: Indra; Metre: Triṣṭup." In the line "sūktadalliruva ṛksaṅkhye" the Kannada word "sūktadalliruva" is normalised from the print's "sūktadalliruva ṛksaṃkhye"; the line is Kannada, not Sanskrit.

Saṃhitā-pāṭha printed with accent marks, in Kannada script; reproduced here: Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. Marks: underline below a syllable = anudātta ॒, short vertical stroke above = svarita ॑; the acute in the IAST line is set only on an unmarked syllable that stands directly before a svarita or directly after an anudātta. [accent ?]: in "kuvidā dasya" the underline lies between da and sya; it is taken as da. Reading note: the underlines in the print are the anudātta accent marks, not word-dividers (corrected on the better scan); The first word is read as printed "etāyāma upa" run together, "etāyāmopa". The last word is printed split over two lines as "paramāva-rjate"; read "param āvarjate". Sandhi in "gavyanta indram" is as printed.

Rik 1

एताया॒मोप॑ ग॒व्यन्त॒ इन्द्र॑म॒स्माकं॒ सुप्रम॑तिं वावृधाति । अ॒ना॒मृ॒णः कु॒विदा द॒स्य रा॒यो गवां॒ केतं॒ पर॑मा॒वर्ज॑ते नः ॥ १ ॥ [accent ?]

etāyāmópa gavyánta índram asmā́kaṃ súprámatiṃ vāvṛdhāti | anāmṛṇáḥ kuvídā dasyá rāyó gavāṃ kétaṃ páramāvárjate naḥ || 1 || [accent ?]

Translation: provisional rendering, to be replaced by the Pada, the bhāṣya and the source's own English, which follow on the next pages "Come, [we] desiring cattle, to Indra, who greatly strengthens our good intelligence; he, the unharmed, indeed [bestows] this wealth; [he] turns toward us the highest signal-mark of cattle."

Rik 1 — Pada-pāṭha, bhāṣya, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, English, Special Topics (pp. 3–5, PDF 17–19)

Correction to the note under the Saṃhitā text on p. 2 above (made after reading the Pada on p. 3): the Pada-pāṭha divides the first words as ā | ita | ayāma | upa | gavyantaḥ …, so the Saṃhitā's etāyāmopa is simply ā-ita-ayāma-upa run together by sandhi (ā + ita → eta; eta + ayāma → etāyāma; + upa → etāyāmopa). My remark there about the word being "divided with underline marks" was wrong, and the "provisional rendering" under Rik 1 is superseded by the bhāṣya and by the source's own English given below; read those instead.

Pada-pāṭha printed with accent-marks, not reproduced

आ । इत । अयाम । उप । गव्यन्तः । इन्द्रम् । अस्माकम् । सु । प्रऽमतिम् । ववृधाति । अनामृणः । कुवित् । आत् । अस्य । रायः । गवाम् । केतम् । परम् । आऽवर्जते । नः ॥ १ ॥

ā | ita | ayāma | upa | gavyantaḥ | indram | asmākam | su | pra-matim | vavṛdhāti | anāmṛṇaḥ | kuvit | āt | asya | rāyaḥ | gavām | ketam | param | ā-varjate | naḥ || 1 || The print has "ವವೃಧಾತಿ" with the vowel-sign of the Pada; the compounds are marked with the avagraha-like sign "ऽ" in the transcription for pra-matim and ā-varjate, where the print shows a small separating mark.

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya Kannada script converted letter by letter

देवाः परस्परमेवं कथयन्ति । हे देवा गव्यन्तः पणिनामकेनासुरेणापहृता अस्मदीया गाः प्राप्तुमिच्छन्तो यूयमेत । आगच्छत । युष्माभिः सहिता वयमिन्द्रं गवानयनक्षममुपायाम । प्राप्नवाम । स चेन्द्रोऽनामृणो हिंसकरहितः सन्नस्माकं देवानां प्रमतिं गोलाभेन हर्षयित्वा प्रकृष्टां बुद्धिं सु ववृधाति । सुष्ठु वर्धयति । आदनन्तरं स इन्द्रोऽस्य रायो धनस्य गवां गोरूपस्य सम्बन्धि परं केतमुत्कृष्टं ज्ञानं नोऽस्माकं कुविदावर्जते । अधिकं प्रापयति ॥

devāḥ parasparam evaṃ kathayanti | he devā gavyantaḥ paṇināmakenāsureṇāpahṛtā asmadīyā gāḥ prāptum icchanto yūyam eta | āgacchata | yuṣmābhiḥ sahitā vayam indraṃ gavānayanakṣamam upāyāma | prāpnavāma | sa cendro 'nāmṛṇo hiṃsakarahitaḥ sann asmākaṃ devānāṃ pramatiṃ golābhena harṣayitvā prakṛṣṭāṃ buddhiṃ su vavṛdhāti | suṣṭhu vardhayati | ādanantaraṃ sa indro 'sya rāyo dhanasya gavāṃ gorūpasya sambandhi paraṃ ketam utkṛṣṭaṃ jñānaṃ no 'smākaṃ kuvid āvarjate | adhikaṃ prāpayati ||

Translation: "The gods speak thus to one another: 'O gods, you who desire cows — wishing to obtain our cows carried off by the asura named Paṇi — come (eta = āgacchata). Together with you, let us approach (upāyāma = let us reach) Indra, who is able to bring the cows (gavānayanakṣamam). And he, Indra, being anāmṛṇa — free of any injurer's nature — will, by the gaining of cows, gladden the good understanding (pramati) of us, the gods, and greatly increase (su vavṛdhāti = suṣṭhu vardhayati) our excellent intelligence. Thereafter this Indra will bring to us in abundance (kuvit) the supreme, excellent knowledge (ketam) relating to this wealth, in the form of cows' (gavām).' ('āvarjate' = he brings to us in greater measure; [adhikaṃ prāpayati — 'brings in greater measure'] )."

Grammar within the bhāṣya pp. 3–4, characterized rather than transcribed, as the convention directs for dense accent-and-sandhi argument; named words and the sūtras that could be read are given: The bhāṣya goes through the forms word by word. eta/ita — root iṇ (to go), loṭ 2nd plural, ending tha, replaced by ta; the śap is elided as the root is of the ad class. ayāma — the āṭ augment on the first-person ending (āḍuttamasya pic ca — आडुत्तमस्य पिच्च — āḍuttamasya pic ca, "the first person takes the augment āṭ, and it is pit" — Pā. 3-4-92), then guṇa and ayādeśa; the rule that yaṇ would replace the i of iṇ (iṇo yaṇ — इणो यण् — iṇo yaṇ, Pā. 6-4-81, which agrees with the standard numbering) is discussed against the maxim "exceptions set aside the rules preceding them, those in between" (madhye 'pavādāḥ pūrvān vidhīn bādhante, Paribhāṣā 60). gavyantaḥ — from go with the suffix kyac (supa ātmanaḥ kyac — सुप आत्मनः क्यच् — "[the suffix kyac] after a noun, in the sense of desiring for oneself"), av in place of o before a y-suffix (vānto yi pratyaye — वान्तो यि प्रत्यये — Pā. 6-1-79), then śatṛ; the accent stays on the root. pramatim — root man (to know), suffix ktin (the print has ಕ್ತಿನ್, ktin), loss of the nasal (anudāttopadeśa-vanati-tanoty-ādīnām anunāsikalopo jhali kṅiti, number not read). vavṛdhāti — root vṛdhu vṛddhau, leṭ with the āṭ augment, the śap replaced by ślu by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (number not read), and the lengthening of the reduplication in the Veda (saṃhitāyām abhyāsasya dīrghaś chāndasaḥ). anāmṛṇaḥ — root mṛṇa (to injure), the suffix ka (igupadha-lakṣaṇaḥ kaḥ — the print reads "igupadhalakṣaṇaḥ kaḥ"; number not read), a bahuvrīhi "he who has no injurers", with the final-syllable accent after nañ and su (the rule nañsubhyām, number not read). rāyaḥ — the accent on the ending (ūḍidam…, number not read). gavām — the ending would take the accent by "sāvekāca…" (number not read), but this is prevented by "na go-śvan-sāvavarṇa…" (number not read). ketam — root kit (to know), suffix ghañ, accent on the first syllable. āvarjate — root vṛjī varjane; the śap should be elided as for the ad class, but the Veda allows the contrary ("bahulaṃ chandasi"); śap is pit, hence unaccented; with tiṅ a verbal prefix loses its accent before an accented tiṅ; and the accent of āvarjate is not lowered (nighāta) because of its connection with kuvit (a rule of the group "kuvidyogān nipātair yad-yadi-hanta…", no sūtra number printed). The "iti nighāta-pratiṣedhaḥ" citation could not be read beyond these opening words.

Pratipadārtha Kannada; translated — "gavyantaḥ — O gods, who wish to obtain the cows [carried off by the demon Paṇi]; ā ita — (all of you) come (join together); indram — to Indra (who is able to recover the cows); upāyāma — let us go; (that Indra is) anāmṛṇaḥ — non-violent; asmākam — our; pramatim — the mind delighted (by the gain of cows); vavṛdhāti — he increases; āt — thereafter; sa indraḥ — that Indra; asya rāyaḥ — of this wealth [of ours]; gavām — concerning the cows; param ketam — the excellent knowledge; naḥ — to us; kuvit — in abundance; āvarjate — makes us attain."

Bhāvārtha — "O gods, the asura named Paṇi has stolen your cows. You have the wish to get them back. Therefore come, let all of us go together to Indra. He is non-violent. By getting each of us our cows back he will increase our gladness and will give us excellent understanding in regard to our whole wealth, the cows."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 4) — "Come, let us approach Indra to recover our stolen cattle ; He being without malice exhilarates our minds ; he will bestow upon us perfect knowledge of this wealth consisting of cows."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 5 — "The asura named Paṇi stole the gods' cows and kept them hidden in a cave. This ṛk describes the gods speaking among themselves that they should go to Indra in order to recover them." — gavyantaḥ = gā ātmana icchantaḥ, "those who wish to obtain cows". — su pramatiṃ vāvṛdhāti: "he gives excellent knowledge; he increases our understanding." — anāmṛṇaḥ — hiṃsakarahitaḥ; mṛṇa hiṃsāyām; mṛṇanti hiṃsantīti mṛṇāḥ; igupadhalakṣaṇaḥ kaḥ; na santy āmṛṇā asyeti bahuvrīhiḥ (devanāgarī of the print's Sanskrit: "अनामृणः — हिंसकरहितः । मृण हिंसायाम् । मृणन्ति हिंसन्तीति मृणाः । इगुपधलक्षणः कः । न सन्त्यामृणा अस्येति बहुव्रीहिः"). "The root mṛṇ means to injure. Because he is not one who injures he is called anāmṛṇaḥ: Indra does not injure those who praise him; or, since no one is able to injure Indra, Indra is 'harmless' — such is the meaning." — kuvit — adhikam, "more, in abundance". "Among the twelve words of the many-meaning group beginning uru, tuvi, the word kuvit is read (Ni. 3-13)." — rāyaḥ = dhanasya ("of wealth"; dhanada). — ketam — utkṛṣṭaṃ jñānam: "excellent knowledge; since in the eleven words for 'understanding' beginning ketaḥ, ketuḥ the word ketaḥ is read (Ni. 3-13), ketam means good knowledge, understanding."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā p. 5, grammar page — noted briefly: ite (root iṇ "to go", loṭ 2nd plural tha, replaced by ta by tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ — तस्थस्थमिपां तांतंताम: — tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ, Pā. 13-4-10 as printed [sic; usual number 3-4-101; the print has ∩ and the 3-shape, then 4, then ∩ and ○, zoom-checked]; the śap elided, no guṇa) and āyāma (iṇ, loṭ 1st plural mas; loṭo laṅvat — लोटो लङ्वत् — Pā. 3-4-85; nityaṃ ṅitaḥ — नित्यं ङितः — Pā. 3-4-99, the s of mas is always elided; āḍuttamasya pic ca — आडुत्तमस्य पिच्च — Pā. 3-4-92, the augment āṭ; the page breaks off in the discussion of its being pit).

Rik 1 — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā, continued (pp. 6–7, PDF 20–21; grammar pages, noted briefly)

The grammar of Rik 1 runs on from p. 5 through p. 7 in Kannada prose, with the sūtras quoted in Kannada script. Noted briefly, not transcribed line by line; sūtras whose numbers could be read are given in three layers.

  • āyāma (continued from p. 5): the ending is pit (by the augment āṭ), so it is not ṅit (sārvadhātukam apit — सार्वधातुकमपित् — sārvadhātukam apit, "a sārvadhātuka ending that is not pit is treated as ṅit"; number not read), hence there is no room for the ban on guṇa; guṇa gives e + āma and then ay-substitution, whence āyāma. The page then argues whether iṇo yaṇ — इणो यण् — iṇo yaṇ (Pā. 6-4-81, as printed) or the iyaṅ substitution (aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau — अचि श्नुधातुभ्रुवां य्वोरियङुवङौ — Pā. 16-4-77 as printed [sic; the first digit ∩ = 1 is clear on the better scan, so the print reads 16-4-77, evidently for 6-4-77]) should apply before a vowel-initial ending, using the maxim madhye 'pavādāḥ pūrvān vidhīn bādhante — मध्येऽपवादाः पूर्वान्विधीन्बाधन्ते — "exceptions in the middle debar the earlier rules" (Paribhāṣā 60, as printed) and vipratiṣedhe paraṃ kāryam — विप्रतिषेधे परं कार्यम् — "in a conflict the later rule prevails" (Pā. 1-4-2, as printed): the later guṇa rule wins. It adds that the "Vedha-bhāṣya" settles the matter by accepting that yaṇ is an exception, and that kṅiti ca — क्ङिति च — kṅiti ca (Pā. 1-1-5) bars guṇa only in the ṅit case (i + anti); the maxim is therefore not needed here. The ending, being pit, is anudātta (anudāttau suppitau), so the root's own accent remains.
  • gavyantaḥ: gāḥ ātmana icchantaḥ; kyac after the object-word go by supa ātmanaḥ kyac — सुप आत्मनः क्यच् — supa ātmanaḥ kyac (Pā. 3-1-8, as read from the print), the verbal status of the stem (sanādyantā dhātavaḥ), the elision of the case-ending (supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ — सुपो धातुप्रातिपदिकयोः — Pā. 2-4-71), av for o before a suffix beginning with y (vānto yi pratyaye — वान्तो यि प्रत्यये — Pā. 6-1-79), then laṭ, śatṛ, śap, the doubling in gavya + at, the addition of num, and the visarga; the accent of śatṛ is anudātta by tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāt… — ताश्यनुदात्तेन्ङिदुपदेशात्… — (the sūtra number is not printed on pp. 6–7), so the root accent remains.
  • pramatim (p. 6 end – p. 7): root man jñāne, striyāṃ ktin — स्त्रियां क्तिन् — striyāṃ ktin (Pā. 3-3-94), loss of the nasal by anudāttopadeśa-vanati-tanoty-ādīnām anunāsikalopo jhali kṅiti (Pā. 6-4-32 as printed [sic]; usual number 6-4-37; the last digit is the curled 2, zoom-checked), and the preverb pra keeps its own accent by tādau ca niti kṛtyatau — तादौ च नितिकृत्यतौ — Pā. 6-2-50.
  • vāvṛdhāti (p. 7): root vṛdhu vardhane; leṭ, with the augment āṭ by leṭo 'ḍāṭau — लेटोऽडाटौ — Pā. 3-4-94; śap's elision by ślu through "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 2-4-73); doubling of the root by ślau — श्लौ — Pā. 6-1-10; the reduplicate is cut down by halādiḥ śeṣaḥ — हलादिः शेषः — "of the consonants the first remains" (Pā. 7-4-60, not numbered in the print); the lengthening of the reduplicate in the Saṃhitā is Vedic.
  • anāmṛṇaḥ: root mṛṇa hiṃsāyām; ṛ belongs to the ik group, so mṛṇ ends in a vowel-penultimate root, whence the suffix ka (igupadhajñāprīkiraḥ kaḥ — इगुपधज्ञाप्रीकिरः कः — Pā. 3-1-135); na santi āmṛṇā asya (bahuvrīhi); nalopo nañaḥ — नलोपो नञः — Pā. 6-3-73 (the n of nañ is dropped before a following member) and tasmān nuḍ aci — तस्मान्नुडचि — Pā. 6-3-74 (the augment nuṭ if a vowel follows); the final member is accented on its last syllable by the rule nañsubhyām (number not read).
  • ketam: root kit jñāne, ending in the suffix ghañ. (Rik 1's grammar ends here, p. 7.)

Rik 2

Saṃhitā-pāṭha Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. In "vasatiṃ" the anudātta underline lies between sa and ti; it is taken as sa [accent ?].

उपेद॒हं ध॑न॒दामप्र॑तीतं॒ जुष्टां॒ न श्ये॒नो व॑स॒तिं प॑तामि । इन्द्रं॑ नम॒स्यन्नु॑प॒मेभि॑र॒र्क्यैर्यः स्तो॒तृभ्यो॒ हव्यो॒ अस्ति॒ याम॑न् ॥ २ ॥

upedaháṃ dhanadā́mápratītaṃ júṣṭāṃ ná śyenó vasatíṃ patāmi | [accent ?] índraṃ namasyánn upamébhir arkyáir yaḥ stotṛ́bhyo hávyo ásti yā́man || 2 ||

Pada-pāṭha the line "arkyaiḥ" was checked on an enlarged slice at 300 dpi: the print reads arkyaiḥ, with a y; the bhāṣya below writes the word as arkaiḥ — recorded as printed

उप । इत् । अहम् । धनऽदाम् । अप्रतिऽइतम् । जुष्टाम् । न । श्येनः । वसतिम् । पतामि । इन्द्रम् । नमस्यन् । उपऽमेभिः । अर्क्यैः । यः । स्तोतृऽभ्यः । हव्यः । अस्ति । यामन् ॥ २ ॥

upa | it | aham | dhana-dām | apratī-itam | juṣṭām | na | śyenaḥ | vasatim | patāmi | indram | namasyan | upa-mebhiḥ | arkyaiḥ | yaḥ | stotṛ-bhyaḥ | havyaḥ | asti | yāman || 2 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

य इन्द्रः स्तोतृभ्यः स्तोतॄणां मनुष्याद्यानामनुग्रहार्थं यामन् तदीयशत्रुभिः सह प्रवृत्ते युद्धे हव्योऽस्ति तैराह्वातव्यो भवति तमिन्द्रमहमनुष्ठातोपेत्य पतामि । उपाप्नोम्येव । किं कुर्वन् । उपमेभिरुपमानस्थानीयैरुत्तमैरर्कैः स्तोत्रैः सह नमस्यन् पूजयन् । कीदृशमिन्द्रम् । धनदां धनप्रदम् अप्रतीतमप्रतिगतम् । बलिभिरतिरस्कृतमित्यर्थः । इन्द्रप्राप्तौ दृष्टान्तः । जुष्टां पूर्वैः सेवितां वसतिं स्वकीयनीडरूपां निवासभूमिं श्येनो न । यथा श्येनोऽनुकोवेगवान्पक्षी स्वकीयं स्थानं प्रत्यादरेण धावति तद्वदहमिन्द्रं त्वरया प्राप्नोमि ॥

ya indraḥ stotṛbhyaḥ stotṝṇāṃ manuṣyādyānām anugrahārthaṃ yāman tadīyaśatrubhiḥ saha pravṛtte yuddhe havyo 'sti tair āhvātavyo bhavati tam indram aham anuṣṭhātopetya patāmi | upāpnomy eva | kiṃ kurvan | upamebhir upamānasthānīyair uttamair arkaiḥ stotraiḥ saha namasyan pūjayan | kīdṛśam indram | dhanadāṃ dhanapradam apratītam apratigatam | balibhir atiraskṛtam ity arthaḥ | indraprāptau dṛṣṭāntaḥ | juṣṭāṃ pūrvaiḥ sevitāṃ vasatiṃ svakīyanīḍarūpāṃ nivāsabhūmiṃ śyeno na | yathā śyeno 'nukovegavān pakṣī svakīyaṃ sthānaṃ pratyādareṇa dhāvati tadvad aham indraṃ tvarayā prāpnomi ||

Translation: "The Indra who, for the benefit of the praisers [= human beings and the like], at the yāman — in a battle that has begun with their enemies — is havya, i.e. is to be invoked by them: to that Indra I, the performer, going up to him (upetya, clear in the print), patāmi — I simply approach. Doing what? Namasyan — worshipping with upamebhiḥ, 'those standing in the place of the comparison [i.e. the best, worthy to be compared]', with the excellent arkaiḥ — hymns of praise. What sort of Indra? Dhanadām — the giver of wealth; apratītam — 'not gone against', that is, not defeated by the mighty. An illustration for reaching Indra: juṣṭām — frequented by earlier [birds], vasatim — a dwelling, the resting-place in the form of its own nest — śyeno na — as a hawk. Just as the hawk, the swift bird, runs with eagerness to its own place, so do I reach Indra with haste."

Pratipadārtha — "yaḥ — which Indra; stotṛbhyaḥ — from the devotees; yāman — at the time of battle (for help); havyaḥ asti — is called (with prayer); dhanadām — [that] giver of wealth; apratītam — [one] not struck back (by enemies); indram — Indra; aham — I; upamebhiḥ — worthy of comparison (endowed with the best qualities); arkyaiḥ [the print here: arkyaiḥ] — with hymns; namasyan — worshipping; juṣṭām — the beloved, (inhabited — vāsamāḍuttiruva, "in which [it] dwells"); vasatim — the nest; śyenaḥ na — as a hawk arrives; upet patāmi — I will go swiftly and arrive."

Bhāvārtha — "Indra has a mighty valour that cannot be struck back by enemies. All his devotees call upon him at the time of battle, praying for help. He is the giver of wealth. As a hawk flies off and reaches its own beloved nest, so I also, worshipping that Indra with the most excellent hymns, will go swiftly to him."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 9) — "Indra is to be inovked [sic] by his worshippers in battle; Indra who is invincible and true giver of wealth is to be glorified with excellent hymns; I approach Indra like a hawk to its cherished nest."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), pp. 9–10 — dhanadām — dhanaṃ dadātīti dhanadāḥ (Kannada gloss: "one who gives wealth, riches"). apratītam — śatrubhir na pratigataṃ ("one who cannot be conquered by enemies"). juṣṭām — juṣī prītisevanayoḥ, sevitām: "an object of love, desired". śyenaḥ — "a hawk, a particular bird; this bird is renowned for flying swiftly. As such a bird flies swiftly to its beloved nest, so I too go swiftly to Indra, who is very dear to me, because he gives me what I wish — such is the sense of the illustration." upamebhiḥ — upamānasthānīyaiḥ, uttamaiḥ, "worthy of comparison, excellent, the very best". ārkyaiḥ [the print's form here: ārkyaiḥ with a long ā] — "with mantras. There is a Nirukta statement, arko mantro bhavati ('arka is a mantra')" (Ni. 5-4; the middle digit is the lobed 5, zoom-checked). havyaḥ — āhvātavyaḥ: "one who is called for help at the time of battle. People who fall into difficulties such as war take refuge in Indra; they call upon Indra for help."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā p. 10, grammar page — noted briefly: dhanadām (dhanaṃ dadāti → dhanadāḥ; the suffix vic by āto maninkvanibvanipaś ca — आतो मनिन्क्वनिब्वनिपश्च — Pā. 3-2-74 (zoom-checked), with all the letters of vic dropped; the su of the compound's member elided by luk; accusative singular). juṣṭām (juṣī prītisevanayoḥ; the root is īdit, so the iṭ augment is barred before the participial suffix by śvīdito niṣṭhāyām — श्वीदितो निष्ठायाम् — Pā. 7-2-14; the first syllable is accented by nityaṃ mantre — नित्यं मन्त्रे — Pā. 6-1-210 with the preceding juṣṭārpite ca chandasi — जुष्टार्पिते च छन्दसि — Pā. 6-1-209, which the Kaumudī's author says need not be made a separate sūtra). patāmi (liṅarthe leṭ — लिङर्थे लेट् — Pā. 3-4-7; first-person singular mip; the augment āṭ by leṭo 'ḍāṭau — Pā. 3-4-94; śap; lengthening). namasyan (namovarivaścitraṅaḥ kyac — नमोवरिवश्चित्रङः क्यच् — Pā. 3-2-19 as printed [sic: the middle digit is a clear curled 2; the usual number is 3-1-19], with the word karaṇe carried on from the preceding sūtra on śabdavaira-…, and the vārtikas karaṇaṃ kriyā, namasaḥ pūjāyām, varivasaḥ paricaryāyām, citraṅa āścarye — "namas in the sense of worship, varivas in service, citra in the sense of wonder"; kyac is udātta by its suffix-accent; then laṭ, śatṛ, anudātta by tāsyanudāttenṅid… Pā. 6-1-186 (zoom-checked), śap pit; the page breaks off in the discussion of the single substitute of a and the kyac's ac).

Rik 2 — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā, continued (p. 11, PDF 25; grammar page, noted briefly)

upamebhiḥ (upamīyante ebhir ity upamāḥ; root māṅ māne; the suffix ka in the sense of ghañ — ghañarthe kavidhānam — "the suffix ka is prescribed in the sense of ghañ", cited with a vārtika under Pā. 3-3-58; Sāyaṇa's view is that it applies beyond the cases listed in the vārtika; loss of ā by ātolopa iṭi ca — आतो लोप इटि च — Pā. 6-4-64; instrumental plural bhis and the Vedic bahulaṃ chandasi which prevents the usual ais; accent of the first member by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt — गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत् — Pā. 6-2-139, the final syllable being acute by the suffix). havyaḥ (root hve̐ śabde; the semivowel v gives u as the "former form" by bahulaṃ chandasi — Pā. 6-1-34 (zoom-checked); the suffix yat after a root ending in a vowel, ac̄o yat — अचो यत् — Pā. 3-1-91 as printed [sic: the last two digits are a clear 9 and ∩ = 1; the usual number is 3-1-97]; guṇa by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ — सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः — Pā. 7-3-84; av in place of o by dhātos tannimittasyaiva — धातोस्तन्निमित्तस्यैव — Pā. 6-1-80, with the companion rule vānto yi pratyaye — Pā. 6-1-79; the initial accent, because yato nāvaḥ — यतो नावः — Pā. 6-1-213 would apply only to nau + yat, not here). Rik 2 ends at the close of this page (|| 2 ||).

Rik 3

Saṃhitā-pāṭha Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. Svarita marks stand over va of "sarva" and over ra of "-rasakta" as read from the strokes; where a conjunct carries a repha the stroke was placed on the vowel-bearing consonant.

नि सर्व॑सेन इषु॒धीँर॑सक्त॒ सम॒र्यो गा अ॑जति॒ यस्य॒ व॑ष्टि । चो॒ष्कू॒यमा॑ण इन्द्र॒ भूरि॑ वा॒मं मा प॒णिर्भू॑र॒स्मदधि॑ प्रवृद्ध ॥ ३ ॥

ni sárvasena iṣudhī́m̐r asakta sámaryó gā́ ajati yásya vaṣṭi | coṣkūyámāṇa indra bhū́ri vāmáṃ mā paṇírbhūr asmádádhi pravṛddha || 3 ||

Pada-pāṭha

नि । सर्वऽसेनः । इषुऽधीन् । असक्त । सम् । अर्यः । गाः । अजति । यस्य । वष्टि । चोष्कूयमाणः । इन्द्र । भूरि । वामम् । मा । पणिः । भूः । अस्मत् । अधि । प्रऽवृद्ध ॥ ३ ॥

ni | sarva-senaḥ | iṣu-dhīn | asakta | sam | aryaḥ | gāḥ | ajati | yasya | vaṣṭi | coṣkūyamāṇaḥ | indra | bhūri | vāmam | mā | paṇiḥ | bhūḥ | asmat | adhi | pra-vṛddha || 3 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

सर्वसेनः कृत्स्नसेनायुक्त इषुधीन्बाणानामाधारभूतान्निषङ्गान्न्यसक्त । नितरां पृष्ठभागे संयोजितवान् । अर्यः स्वामिरूप इन्द्रो यस्य देवस्य वष्टि असुरेणापहृता गाः प्रदातुं कामयते तस्य देवस्य गृहे ता गाः समजति । सम्यक् प्रापयति । हे प्रवृद्ध प्रकृष्टवृद्धियुक्तेन्द्र भूरि वामं प्रभूतं गोरूपं धनं चोष्कूयमाणोऽस्मभ्यं प्रयच्छन् अस्मदध्यस्मासु पणिर्मा भूः । व्यवहारी मा भूयोः । गवां मूल्यं मा याचस्वेत्यर्थः ॥

sarvasenaḥ kṛtsnasenāyukta iṣudhīn bāṇānām ādhārabhūtān niṣaṅgān nyasakta | nitarāṃ pṛṣṭhabhāge saṃyojitavān | aryaḥ svāmirūpa indro yasya devasya vaṣṭi asureṇāpahṛtā gāḥ pradātuṃ kāmayate tasya devasya gṛhe tā gāḥ samajati | samyak prāpayati | he pravṛddha prakṛṣṭavṛddhiyuktendra bhūri vāmaṃ prabhūtaṃ gorūpaṃ dhanaṃ coṣkūyamāṇo 'smabhyaṃ prayacchan asmadadhyasmāsu paṇir mā bhūḥ | vyavahārī mā bhūyoḥ | gavāṃ mūlyaṃ mā yācasvety arthaḥ ||

Translation: "Sarvasenaḥ — he who has the whole army — ni asakta — has fixed iṣudhīn, the quivers that are the receptacles of arrows, firmly on his back. Aryaḥ — Indra, in the form of the lord — to the house of whichever god he vaṣṭi ('wishes') to give back the cows carried off by the demon, he sam ajati — leads those cows rightly, brings them. O pravṛddha, Indra of surpassing growth, [you who are] coṣkūyamāṇaḥ — giving us abundantly bhūri vāmam, plentiful wealth in the form of cows — do not become a paṇi towards us (asmad adhi): do not be a trader; the meaning is 'do not ask the price of the cows'."

Grammar within the bhāṣya pp. 12–13, characterized, not transcribed: the bhāṣya parses sarvasenaḥ (bahuvrīhi; its accent via pratyayalakṣaṇa and a Kāśikā citation), iṣudhīn (iṣu + dhā, suffix ki by karmaṇy adhikaraṇe ca — Pā. 3-3-93 (zoom-checked); n → ru by the rule on a long vowel before aṭ and the optional nasalization of the previous vowel by anunāsikaḥ pūrvasya tu vā — Pā. 8-3-2, as printed), asakta (root ṣaca samavāye, śap elided by bahulaṃ chandasi), aryaḥ (aryaḥ svāmivaiśyayoḥ — अर्यः स्वामिवैश्ययोः — Pā. 3-1-103, yat-ending irregularly formed; final-acute by a Phiṭ-sūtra, printed as "Phi. Sū. 17" [aryasya svāmyākhyā cet] and "Phi. Sū. 14" [aṅguśmodakabakavaśānāṃ chandasy antaḥ], zoom-checked), ajati (root aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ), vaṣṭi (root vaśa kāntau, śap elided as it belongs to the ad class; ṣ-substitution then ṣṭutva), coṣkūyamāṇaḥ (root skui āpravaṇe, yaṅ by dhātor ekāca…, lengthening, doubling, ś-initial reduplicate cut down; the last ś [sakāraḥ] is dropped; śānac for laṭ (printed yajantāl laṭaḥ śānac; the first word is read at 450 dpi as yajantāt [?] — yaṅantāt may be meant); stem accent from the lasārvadhātuka ending), bhūḥ (aorist; luk of sic by gātisthā…). Several of these sūtra numbers on pp. 12–13 are small and they were not pursued.

Pratipadārtha — "sarvasenaḥ — Indra, who has all armies; iṣudhīn — the quivers that hold arrows; ni asakta — has fastened firmly (on his back); aryaḥ — Indra, the lord; yasya — [with regard to] which deity; vaṣṭi — he wishes; (to the house of such a deity) gāḥ — the cows; sam ajati — he drives rightly; (he) pravṛddha — (O) one endowed with excellent growth; indra — Indra; bhūri — in abundance; vāmam — abundant (cow-form) wealth; coṣkūyamāṇaḥ — giving bountifully; asmadadhi — with regard to us; paṇiḥ — a trader (a haggler); mā bhūḥ — do not become."

Bhāvārtha — "Indra, the lord of all the gods, with all his armies, has bound the quivers firmly on his shoulder. He leads the cows that were carried off, to the houses of his own gods. O Indra of excellent prosperity, give us more and more of the wealth of cows that we wish. But do not ask us for only their price, and do not behave towards us like a trader."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 13) — "Indra, the leader of the whole army ties the quivers on his back ; the lord drives the cattle to the dwelling of whom he pleases ; O, mighty Indra, the giver of abundant wealth, do not take advantage of us like a dealer."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), pp. 13–14 — sarvasenaḥ = kṛtsnasenāyuktaḥ: "The leader of all armies [the print adds this English], the overlord of all the armies, one who has all armies." iṣudhīn = iṣava iṣu dhīyante itīṣudhayaḥ, "quivers in which arrows are placed." aryaḥ = svāmivaiśyayoḥ (Pā. 3-1-103 [as printed]): "master, sacrificer, Lord [English in the print]." coṣkūyamāṇaḥ = asmabhyaṃ prayacchan, "one who gives [cows] to us." mā paṇir bhūḥ [the print's heading reads mā phaṇir bhūḥ, sic] = vyavahārī mā bhūyoḥ: "Do not become a trader and haggle; that is, in giving us wealth do not stint, nor haggle over how much to give, but give wealth as is wished." The print adds in English: "Do not make a hard bargain, dont [sic] haggle, do not demand too much from worshippers etc."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā p. 14, grammar page — noted briefly: sarvasenaḥ — sarva belongs to the uñchādi group, so it is final-acute by uñchādīnāṃ ca — उञ्छादीनां च — Pā. 6-1-160; ina = master; inena saha vartate iti senā, a bahuvrīhi, with sa for saha by vopasarjanasya — वोपसर्जनस्य — Pā. 6-3-82; then sarvā senā yasya saḥ, the case-ending of the first member elided by supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ — सुपो धातुप्रातिपदिकयोः — Pā. 2-4-71. Because sarvasya supi — सर्वस्य सुपि — Pā. 6-1-191 gives sarva the first-syllable accent before a sup ending, the page asks how this applies once the ending is elided; it cites the Kāśikā-author that the accent comes by pratyayalakṣaṇa — pratyayalope pratyayalakṣaṇam — प्रत्ययलोपे प्रत्ययलक्षणम् — Pā. 1-1-62 — and explains that the prohibition na lumatāṅgasya — न लुमताङ्गस्य — Pā. 1-1-63 does not obstruct, and that the "seventh case" in accent-rules means "ending in …", i.e. applies to words in a subanta. After the bahuvrīhi the first-member accent supervenes and the same accent remains.

Rik 3 — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā, continued (pp. 15–16, PDF 29–30; grammar pages, noted briefly)

Kannada prose with sūtras quoted; the numerals are small; those given were re-read on the better scan, and a bracketed question mark marks any that stay unsettled.

  • iṣudhīn (p. 15): iṣavaḥ iṣu dhīyante — "arrows are placed in them" (the quiver; Kannada battalike); the suffix ki after dhā when a word for the object stands in front, karmaṇy adhikaraṇe ca — कर्मण्यधिकरणे च — karmaṇy adhikaraṇe ca (Pā. 3-3-93); loss of the ā by ātolopa iṭi ca — आतो लोप इटि च — Pā. 6-4-64; accusative plural śas; in the Saṃhitā the n becomes ru after a long vowel in one foot (dīrghād aṭi samānapāde — दीर्घादटि समानपादे — Pā. 8-3-9, zoom-checked) and the preceding vowel is optionally nasalized (anunāsikaḥ pūrvasya tu vā — अनुनासिकः पूर्वस्य तु वा — Pā. 8-3-2).
  • asakta: root ṣaca samavāye (1st class, ubhayapadin), laṅ [print: "if the ātmanepada is intended, laṅ pra. pu. e. va., sac + ta" — the print says laṅ]; śap elided by bahulaṃ chandasi (Pā. 2-4-73, zoom-checked); c → k by coḥ kuḥ — चोः कुः — Pā. 8-2-30; the augment aṭ.
  • aryaḥ: aryaḥ svāmivaiśyayoḥ — अर्यः स्वामिवैश्ययोः — Pā. 3-1-103; root ṛ gatau, yat as an exception to ṇyat, guṇa and raparatva giving ārya-type form; the final syllable acute by the Phiṭ-sūtras aryasya svāmyākhyā cet and aṅguśmodakabakavaśānāṃ chandasy antaḥ (printed Phi. Sū. 17 and 14, zoom-checked), which override the first-syllable accent that yato nāvaḥ — यतो नावः — Pā. 6-1-213 or yo 'ntasyāntyāt pūrvam — यो ऽन्तस्यान्त्यात्पूर्वम् (letters read at 658 dpi; the sūtra is not identified here) [?] — would give.
  • ajati: root aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ, laṭ, tip, śap. vaṣṭi: root vaśa kāntau, ad-class, śap elided; ś → ṣ by vraścabhrasjasṛjamṛjayajarājabhrājacchaśāṃ ṣaḥ — व्रश्चभ्रस्जसृजमृजयजराजभ्राजच्छशां षः — Pā. 8-2-36; then ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ — ष्टुना ष्टुः — Pā. 8-4-41, giving vaṣṭi.
  • coṣkūyamāṇaḥ (p. 16): root skui āpravaṇe; yaṅ in the sense of repetition or intensity after a root with one vowel and an initial consonant (dhātor ekāco halādeḥ kriyāsamabhihāre yaṅ — Pā. 3-1-22), lengthening (akṛtsārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ — Pā. 7-4-25), doubling (sanyaṅoḥ — Pā. 6-1-9), shortening of the reduplicate (hrasvaḥ — Pā. 7-4-59), the first s of the doubled skū lost (śarpūrvāḥ khayaḥ — Pā. 7-4-61), k of the reduplicate → c (kuhoś cuḥ — Pā. 7-4-62), guṇa of the reduplicate (guṇo yaṅluktoḥ — Pā. 7-4-82), s → ṣ by the list suṣāmādiṣu ca (Pā. 8-3-98), śānac for laṭ (laṭaḥ śatṛśānacau — Pā. 3-2-124), a + o → single o (ato guṇe — Pā. 6-1-97), the augment muk (āne muk — Pā. 7-2-82), n-substitution (aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi — Pā. 8-4-2) giving coṣkūyamāṇa; the śānac ending is unaccented (tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāt…, Pā. 6-1-186), so the root accent stays.
  • bhūḥ: root bhū sattāyām, luṅ, sic; the augment aṭ is barred when mā is connected (na māṅyoge); the luk of sic by gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu — गातिस्थाघुपाभूभ्यः सिचः परस्मैपदेषु — Pā. 2-4-77; itaś ca — इतश्च — Pā. 3-4-100 drops the i of the ending; ru and visarga. Rik 3 ends at this point (|| 3 ||).
