Rik 4

Saṃhitā-pāṭha Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented; the last word is divided across two lines in the print: prēti-mīyuḥ Reading note: the Saṃhitā text of the second line is read as printed — viṣuṇak te — the second word being a single printed unit "ವಿಷುಣಕ್ತೇ"; the Pada on the next page will show how the print divides it. The Saṃhitā is not completed with the Pada here; Rik 4's Pada, bhāṣya and the rest follow from p. 17 and are not yet written.

वधी॒र्हि दस्युं॑ ध॒नि॑नं घ॒नेनँ॒ एक॒श्चर॑न्नुपशा॒केभि॑रिन्द्र । धनो॒रधि॑ विषु॒णक्ते व्या॑य॒न्नय॑ज्वा॒नः सन॒काः प्रेति॑मीयुः ॥ ४ ॥

vadhīr hí dásyuṃ dhaninaṃ ghanéna̐ ékaś cáran nupaśākébhir indra | dhanor ádhi viṣuṇák té vyāyann áyajvānáḥ sanakā́ḥ prétimīyuḥ || 4 ||

Rik 4 — Pada-pāṭha, bhāṣya, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, English, Special Topics (pp. 17–20, PDF 31–34)

Pada-pāṭha — this settles the reading noted under the Saṃhitā: viṣuṇak te is viṣuṇak | te.

वधीः । हि । दस्युम् । धनिनम् । घनेन । एकः । चरन् । उपऽशाकेभिः । इन्द्र ॥ धनोः । अधि । विषुणक् । ते । वि । आयन् । अयज्वानः । सनकाः । प्रऽइतिम् । ईयुः ॥ ४ ॥

vadhīḥ | hi | dasyum | dhaninam | ghanena | ekaḥ | caran | upa-śākebhiḥ | indra || dhanoḥ | adhi | viṣuṇak | te | vi | āyan | ayajvānaḥ | sanakāḥ | pra-itim | īyuḥ || 4 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya the print's first half is given in full; the grammatical tail is characterized below

हे इन्द्र धनिनं बहुधनोपेतं दस्युं चोरं वृत्रं घनेन कठिनेन वज्रेण वधीर्हि । त्वं हतवान्खलु । धनित्वं वाजसनेयिनोऽपि स्पष्टमामनन्ति । वृत्रस्यान्तः सर्वे देवाः सर्वाश्च विद्याः सर्वाणि हवींषि चासन्निति । उपशाकेभिः समीपवर्तिभिः शक्तियुक्तैर्मरुद्भिः सहितोऽपि भूत्वैकश्चरन् । प्रहर्तुं स्वयमेक एव गच्छन् । यद्यपि मरुतः समीपे वर्तन्ते तथापि ते प्रोत्साहयन्त्येव न तु वृत्रं प्रहरन्ति । प्रहर्ता तु स्वयमेक एव । तथा च ब्राह्मणे समाम्नातम् । मरुतो हैनं नाजहुः प्रहर भगवो वीरयस्वेत्येवैनमेतां वाचं वदन्त उपातिष्ठन्त । ऐ. ब्रा. ३-२० । इति । धनोरधि इन्द्रसम्बन्धिनो धनुष उपरि विषुणक् विविधं नाशमुद्दिश्य यद्वा विष्वक् सर्वतस्ते वृत्रानुचरा व्यायन् । विविधमागच्छन् । आगत्य चायज्वानो यज्ञविरोधिनः सन्तः सनका एतन्नामका वृत्रानुचराः प्रेतिमीयुः । मरणं प्राप्ताः ॥

he indra dhaninaṃ bahudhanopetaṃ dasyuṃ coraṃ vṛtraṃ ghanena kaṭhinena vajreṇa vadhīr hi | tvaṃ hatavān khalu | dhanitvaṃ vājasaneyino 'pi spaṣṭam āmananti | vṛtrasyāntaḥ sarve devāḥ sarvāś ca vidyāḥ sarvāṇi havīṃṣi cāsann iti | upaśākebhiḥ samīpavartibhiḥ śaktiyuktair marudbhiḥ sahito 'pi bhūtvaikaś caran | prahartuṃ svayam eka eva gacchan | yadyapi marutaḥ samīpe vartante tathāpi te protsāhayanty eva na tu vṛtraṃ praharanti | prahartā tu svayam eka eva | tathā ca brāhmaṇe samāmnātam | maruto hainaṃ nājahuḥ prahara bhagavo vīrayasvety evainam etāṃ vācaṃ vadanta upātiṣṭhanta | ai. brā. 3-20 | iti | dhanor adhi indrasambandhino dhanuṣa upari viṣuṇak vividhaṃ nāśam uddiśya yadvā viṣvak sarvatas te vṛtrānucarā vy āyan | vividham āgacchan | āgatya cāyajvāno yajñavirodhinaḥ santaḥ sanakā etannāmakā vṛtrānucarāḥ pretim īyuḥ | maraṇaṃ prāptāḥ ||

Translation: "O Indra, you slew with the ghana, the hard vajra, the dhanin — the possessor of much wealth — the dasyu — the thief — Vṛtra: you have indeed killed [him]. The Vājasaneyins also state clearly that he has wealth: 'Inside Vṛtra were all the gods, all the sciences, and all the oblations.' Upaśākebhiḥ — though accompanied by the Maruts who stand near, endowed with power — ekaḥ caran — going alone, going by yourself to strike. Though the Maruts are near, they only encourage; it is not they who strike Vṛtra: the striker is you alone. So it is handed down in a Brāhmaṇa: 'The Maruts did not abandon him; saying "Strike, O Lord, show your valour!" they stood by him' (Ai. Brā. 3-20, zoom-checked). Dhanor adhi — upon Indra's bow; viṣuṇak — with various destruction in view, or on all sides — those followers of Vṛtra vy āyan, came in various ways; and having come, being ayajvānaḥ — enemies of sacrifice — the followers of Vṛtra by the name sanakāḥ pretim īyuḥ — met their death."

Grammar within the bhāṣya pp. 17–18, characterized: the bhāṣya's tail treats vadhīḥ (root han replaced by vadha in the luṅ by luṅi ca (printed Pā. 2-4-43, zoom-checked); loss of the a and absence of vṛddhi; sic lost before īṭ, the īṭ augment Pā. 8-2-28, zoom-checked), ghanena and ekaḥ (the Vedic prakṛtibhāva in the Saṃhitā text before īṣā-akṣādi-type compounds, printed Pā. 6-1-127, vārtika 2, zoom-checked — the first-digits ∩ ∩ then 2 and 7 are clear, so the earlier "6-1-115" is not what the print gives; the nasalisation is Vedic), upaśākebhiḥ (upaśaktaṃ kurvantīty upaśākāḥ, from śakḷ śaktau, in the causative sense, with ac; the last syllable of the second member acute), viṣuṇak (kvip after naś [or añc] preceded by viṣu; kutva by naśer vā — Pā. 8-2-63, zoom-checked), sanakāḥ (ṣaṇu dāne, "they who give", sanā dātāraḥ; pacādyac; sanān nāyanti śabdayantīti sanakāḥ; suffix ka by ato 'nupasarge kaḥ; loss of ā by ātolopa iṭi ca), pretim (the preverb keeps its accent by tādau ca niti (no number printed on p. 18)), and īyuḥ (root i, liṭ third plural us, yaṇ-substitution, doubling, lengthening of the reduplicate by dīrgha iṇaḥ kiti — Pā. 7-4-69, zoom-checked).

Pratipadārtha — "(he) indra — O Indra (you); upaśākebhiḥ — though your powerful Maruts, staying near you, are close at hand; ekaḥ — you alone; caran — moving about (by your own strength alone); dhaninam — the rich; dasyum — the thief Vṛtra; ghanena — with the hard vajra weapon; vadhīr hi — [you] killed; (and) ayajvānaḥ — the enemies of sacrifice; te — those followers of Vṛtra; sanakāḥ — Sanaka and the other rākṣasas; dhanor adhi — in front of (your) bow; viṣuṇak — from many directions; vy āyan — came; (and) pretim — death; īyuḥ — obtained."

Bhāvārtha — "O Indra, you are exceedingly heroic. Though the powerful Maruts were with you, near you, for your help, you alone, without expecting their help, killed Vṛtra with your vajra. Moreover, the enemies of sacrifice and the followers of Vṛtra — Sanaka and the other rākṣasas — who came from many directions in the sky against your weapon, also met death."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 18) — "O Indra, though you are accompanied by your powerful allies Maruths, you alone did slay the rich demon Vritra with your thunderbolt ; those unsacrificing Sanakas coming against your bow from all sides met with their death."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), pp. 19–20 — dasyuṃ dhaninam — "Vṛtra the thief is famed as very rich. 'Within Vṛtra were all the gods, all the sciences, all the oblations' — [this] is known from the Śukla-Yajurveda. Although the word dasyum here means only 'thief', its meaning must be given as Vṛtra: because it is stated here that Indra struck him with his vajra, and because it is said in many places that Vṛtra was struck down and killed with the vajra, dasyum must be understood to refer to Vṛtra the dasyu. The sense is that by thieving he gained wealth and became famous as rich."

ekaś carann upaśākebhiḥ — "Though the Maruts, who are Indra's friends, were near, encouraging [him], Indra did not look for their help but leapt alone upon the enemy and struck him with the vajra. Hence Indra needs no help from anyone else; he alone has immeasurable strength and power. On this the bhāṣyakāra has cited the Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa sentence":

मरुतो हैनं नाजहुः प्रहर भगवो वीरयस्वेत्येवैनमेतां वाचं वदन्त उपातिष्ठन्ते [print here: -nte; in the bhāṣya: -nta] । (ऐ. ब्रा. ३-२०)

maruto hainaṃ nājahuḥ prahara bhagavo vīrayasvety evainam etāṃ vācaṃ vadanta upātiṣṭhante | (ai. brā. 3-20)

"The Maruts did not abandon him; saying to him these words, 'Strike, O lord, show your valour', they stood by him."

upaśākebhiḥ — upaśaktaṃ kurvantīty upaśākāḥ | upaśākebhiḥ samīpavartibhiḥ śaktiyuktair marudbhiḥ: "by the powerful Maruts who stand near." āyajvānaḥ — yajvavirodhinaḥ: "opponents of those who sacrifice, or those who do not sacrifice." sanakāḥ — etannāmakā vṛtrānucarāḥ: "the sanakas are Vṛtra's followers. The word sanaka (sanakāt) occurs in the Ṛgveda in only two ṛks:"

१. प्र सप्तहोता सनकादरोचत मातुरुपस्थे यदशोचदूधनि । न नि मिषति सुरणो दिवेदिवे यदसुरस्य जठरादजायत ॥ (ऋ. सं. ३-२९-१४ [?]) २. अयमग्निर्वध्र्यश्वस्य वृत्रहा सनकात्प्रेद्धो नमसोपवाक्यः । स नो अजामीरुत वा विजामीनभि तिष्ठ शर्धतो वाध्र्यश्व ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-६९-१२ [?])

1. pra saptahotā sanakād arocata mātur upasthe yad aśocad ūdhani | na ni miṣati suraṇo dive-dive yad asurasya jaṭharād ajāyata || (ṛ. saṃ. 3-29-14 [?]) 2. ayam agnir vadhryaśvasya vṛtrahā sanakāt preddho namasopavākyaḥ | sa no ajāmīr uta vā vijāmīn abhi tiṣṭha śardhato vādhryaśva || (ṛ. saṃ. 10-69-12 [?])

"1. 'The seven-priested one shone forth from of old, when he blazed in the lap of the mother, in the udder [?]; the glad one does not wink day by day, since he was born from the belly of the asura.' 2. 'This Agni, Vṛtra-slayer of Vadhryaśva, kindled from of old, is to be addressed with homage: overcome for us, O Vādhryaśva, the hostile [?] — both the kinsfolk and the non-kinsfolk — who press upon us.'" The translations are editorial and tentative: the source leaves these two ṛks untranslated, and the second verse's second line is dense. The source then notes: "In these two ṛks the word sanakāt has Agni as its sense; it does not suggest the meaning 'Vṛtra's follower'."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā p. 20, grammar page — noted briefly: vadhīḥ — root han hiṃsāgatyoḥ, luṅ, tip; the i of the parasmaipada ending is lost by itaś ca — इतश्च — Pā. 3-4-100; cli in place of śap by cli luṅi — च्लि लुङि — Pā. 3-1-43; sic for cli by cleḥ sic — च्लेः सिच् — Pā. 3-1-44; vadha for han in luṅ by luṅi ca — लुङि च — Pā. 2-4-43; the a of vadha dropped by ato lopaḥ — अतो लोपः — Pā. 6-4-48 (the print, in the Veda-bhāṣya, cites this as "ātolopaḥ", which the author says is a slip — pramādikavāgi); the optional vṛddhi by ato halādeḥ laghoḥ — अतो हलादेर्लघोः — Pā. 7-2-7, and its non-occurrence because of the sthānivadbhāva rule acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau — अचः परस्मिन्पूर्वविधौ — Pā. 1-1-57; the augment iṭ by asti-sico 'pṛkte — अस्तिसिचोऽपृक्ते — Pā. 7-3-96, the īṭ; the s lost by iṭa īṭi — इट ईटि — Pā. 8-2-28; the pūrvatrāsiddham — पूर्वत्रासिद्धम् — Pā. 8-2-1 does not make the loss of s "unseen"; the augment aṭ is Vedic and does not appear; the augments iṭ and īṭ are unaccented (āgamā anudāttāḥ), so the root's accent remains.

Rik 4 — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā, continued (pp. 21–22, PDF 35–36; grammar pages, noted briefly)

  • ghanena ekaḥ (p. 21): the Saṃhitā keeps the vowels unchanged — īṣākṣādiṣu chandasi prakṛtibhāvamātram — ईषाक्षादिषु छन्दसि प्रकृतिभावमात्रम् — "in the Veda the compounds īṣā-akṣa and the like keep their natural form only" (Pā. 6-1-127, vārtika 2, as printed here and on p. 17); mātram excludes shortening as well as guṇa. The nasalisation in ghanena [the print marks the e with the nasal sign] is Vedic and is not produced by a sūtra of Pāṇini but belongs to the Prātiśākhya process.
  • upaśākebhiḥ: upaśaktaṃ kurvanti, root śakḷ śaktau, causative ṇic by hetumati ca — हेतुमति च — Pā. 3-1-26; vṛddhi of the penultimate by ata upadhāyāḥ — अत उपधायाः — Pā. 7-2-116; suffix ac of the pacādi class (nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ — Pā. 3-1-134); loss of ṇi by ṇer aniṭi — णेरनिटि — Pā. 6-4-51; final acute by thāthaghañktājabitrakāṇām — थाथघञ्क्ताजबित्रकाणाम् — Pā. 6-2-144.
  • viṣuṇak: suffix kvip after naś adarśane with viṣu in front (sampadādibhyaḥ kvip, a vārtika); kutva of ś by naśer vā — नशेर्वा — Pā. 8-2-63 (the page shows the whole chain: ṣa by vraścabhrasja… — Pā. 8-2-36, ḍa by jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte — Pā. 8-2-39, ka by khari ca — Pā. 8-4-55, then ṇa for n); alternatively root añcu gatipūjanayoḥ with viṣu, kvip, the augment nuṭ, and kutva by coḥ kuḥ — चोः कुः — Pā. 8-2-30.
  • sanakāḥ: the name of a class of asuras; root ṣaṇu dāne, sanvanti iti sanāḥ "givers"; or root kai śabde with ā for ai (ādeca upadeśe 'śiti — आदेच उपदेशेऽशिति — Pā. 6-1-45), sanān kāyati "he who calls out the sana [praises?]"; suffix ka by ato 'nupasarge kaḥ — अतोऽनुपसर्गे कः — Pā. 3-2-3; loss of ā by ātolopa iṭi ca — Pā. 6-4-64; accent of the first member of a kṛt compound.
  • pretim: pra + root iṇ + ktin, guṇa; the preverb keeps its accent by tādau ca niti kṛtyatau — Pā. 6-2-50.
  • īyuḥ (p. 22): root iṇ gatau, liṭ, jhi replaced by us (parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatusustha-lathusaṇalvamāḥ — Pā. 3-4-82); doubling by liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya — Pā. 6-1-8; iṇo yaṇ — Pā. 6-4-81 gives y for the second i, but a doubling-condition sūtra dvirvacane 'ci — Pā. 1-1-59 makes the replaced i count as present for doubling; lengthening of the reduplicate by dīrgha iṇaḥ kiti — दीर्घ इणः किति — Pā. 7-4-69; ī + y + us, ru, visarga: īyuḥ. Rik 4 ends here (|| 4 ||).
original pp. 22–24

Rik 5

Saṃhitā-pāṭha Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. The word yajvabhiḥ: at 658 dpi its subscript is the same -va form as in ayajvānaḥ in the same line, so jva is settled; the old Devanagari had an extra va in vavṛjus, corrected to the print's vavṛjus ta.

परा॑ चिच्छी॒र्षा व॑वृजु॒स्त इ॒न्द्राय॑ज्वानो॒ यज्व॑भिः॒ स्पर्ध॑मानाः । प्र यद्दि॒वो ह॑रिवः स्थातरुग्र॒ निर॑व्र॒ताँ अ॑धमो॒ रोद॑स्योः ॥ ५ ॥

párā cic chīrṣā́ vavṛjus tá indrā́yajvāno yájvabhiḥ spárdhamānāḥ | pra yaddivó harivaḥ sthātarugra níravratā́m̐ adhamo ródasyoḥ || 5 ||

Pada-pāṭha

परा । चित् । शीर्षा । ववृजुः । ते । इन्द्र । अयज्वानः । यज्वऽभिः । स्पर्धमानाः ॥ प्र । यत् । दिवः । हरिऽवः । स्थातः । उग्र । निः । अव्रतान् । अधमः । रोदस्योः ॥ ५ ॥

parā | cit | śīrṣā | vavṛjuḥ | te | indra | ayajvānaḥ | yajva-bhiḥ | spardhamānāḥ || pra | yat | divaḥ | hari-vaḥ | sthātaḥ | ugra | niḥ | avratān | adhamaḥ | rodasyoḥ || 5 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya the first half in full, the grammatical tail characterized

हे इन्द्र ते वृत्रानुचराः शीर्षा स्वकीयानि शिरांसि परा चित् पराङ्मुखान्येव कृत्वा वववृजुः । गतवन्तः । कीदृशास्ते । अयज्वानः स्वयं यागरहिताः प्रत्युत यज्वभिर्यागानुष्ठातृभिः सह स्पर्धमानाः । हे हरिवो हरिनामकाश्वयुक्त स्थातः स्थितियुक्त युद्धे पलायनरहित उग्र शौर्ययुक्तेन्द्र यद्यदा दिवोऽन्तरिक्षाद्रोदस्योर्द्यावापृथिव्योः सकाशाच्च वृत्रानुचरान्निःप्राधमो [sic: as printed] निःशेषेण धमनं कृतवानसि । तदानीं त्वदीयमुखवायुना नुन्नाः सन्तो वववृजुरिति पूर्वत्रान्वयः ॥

he indra te vṛtrānucarāḥ śīrṣā svakīyāni śirāṃsi parā cit parāṅmukhāny eva kṛtvā vavṛjuḥ | gatavantaḥ | kīdṛśās te | ayajvānaḥ svayaṃ yāgarahitāḥ pratyuta yajvabhir yāgānuṣṭhātṛbhiḥ saha spardhamānāḥ | he harivo harināmakāśvayukta sthātaḥ sthitiyukta yuddhe palāyanarahita ugra śauryayuktendra yad yadā divo 'ntarikṣād rodasyor dyāvāpṛthivyoḥ sakāśāc ca vṛtrānucarān niḥprādhamo niḥśeṣeṇa dhamanaṃ kṛtavān asi | tadānīṃ tvadīyamukhavāyunā nunnāḥ santo vavṛjur iti pūrvatrānvayaḥ ||

Translation: "O Indra, those followers of Vṛtra, having made their own heads (śīrṣā) turned away (parā cit = facing backwards), fled (vavṛjuḥ = went). What were they like? Ayajvānaḥ — themselves without sacrifice, and, moreover, contending with the yajvans, the performers of sacrifices. O harivaḥ — you who have the horses named Hari; sthātaḥ — steadfast, not fleeing from battle; ugra — Indra endowed with valour: when (yat = yadā) you blew away completely (niḥśeṣeṇa dhamanam) those followers of Vṛtra from the sky, from [the realm] of the rodasī — heaven and earth — then, driven by the breath of your mouth, they fled: thus the connection with the preceding."

Grammar within the bhāṣya p. 23, characterized: śīrṣā (loss of śe by śeś chandasi bahulam — शेश्छन्दसि बहुलम् — no number printed); vavṛjuḥ (root vṛjī varjane; liṭ after a root not ending in a conjunct is kit — asaṃyogāl liṭ kit — असंयोगाल्लिट् कित् — Pā. 1-2-5, so no guṇa); ayajvānaḥ (root yaj with the suffix ṅvanip — suyajor ṅvanip — सुयजोर्ङ्वनिप् — Pā. 3-2-103 — in the past sense; nañ-compound with first-member accent); divaḥ (the ending accented by the rule on ūḍ-forms); harivaḥ (harī asya staḥ iti harivān; matup's m → v in the Veda by chandasīra (no number printed on p. 23); ru in the vocative by sambuddhau matuvasor ru); avratān (nañ-bahuvrīhi, final acute; n → ru after a long vowel before aṭ, with a nasalised ā); adhamaḥ (root dhmā śabdāgnisaṃyogayoḥ, laṅ, sip, śap; dhama in place of dhmā by pāghrādhmāsthā… (no number printed on p. 23)).

Pratipadārtha — "harivaḥ — O one who has the horses named Hari; sthātaḥ — (in battle) steadfast; ugra — fearsome; indra — Indra; yat — when; divaḥ — from the heaven; rodasyoḥ — from the earth and the mid-region (they came); avratān — those who have no Vedic observances (the followers of Vṛtra); niḥ pra adhamaḥ — you blew away utterly (with the breath of your mouth) [as read from the print]; ayajvānaḥ — those who are not performers of sacrifices; yajvabhiḥ spardhamānāḥ — contending with the sacrificers; te — they; śīrṣā — their heads; parā cit — turning back; vavṛjuḥ — fled."

Bhāvārtha — "O Indra, the two horses called Hari are your excellent vehicles. In battle you fight steadily, never turning your back on the enemy. You are fearsome to your enemies. When those followers of Vṛtra, who observe no Vedic vows and have fallen from sacrifice, come, contending with the performers of sacrifices, to do harm from the heavenly world, from the earth and from the mid-region, then you blow them away utterly with the breath of your mouth. They fled without showing their faces, turned back."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 24) — "O Indra, the neglecters of sacrifices striving hard with the sacrificers fled with their faces turned back ; O mighty Indra, lord of horses, when you blew the unreligious they disappeared from the heaven, earth and sky."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 24 — parācit śīrṣā = parāṅmukhā: "turning (bending) their heads, and looking backwards, they fled — such is the sense." — āyajvānaḥ yajvabhiḥ spardhamānāḥ — "those who do not sacrifice (that is, the dasyus, rākṣasas, and the like), contending with those who sacrifice (those who please the gods, Indra and the others, by invoking them at the sacrifice)." — adhamaḥ = dhmā śabdāgnisaṃyogayoḥ: "the root dhmā means blowing for kindling a fire, or blowing forcibly so that a sound results (as with a conch and the like). Therefore adhamaḥ means: you drove them off, making them flee, by roaring and other sounds, with the breath of your mouth." — harivaḥ = harī asya staḥ iti harivān: "Indra, who has two horses named Hari." — avratān = "those who have not performed vows such as the performance of sacrifice — the dasyus and the like." — rodasyoḥ = dyāvāpṛthivyoḥ "from the earth and the mid-region" the entry continues on p. 25.

Rik 5 — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (pp. 25–26, PDF 39–40; grammar pages, noted briefly)

Kannada prose with sūtras quoted; the numerals are small; those given were re-read on the better scan (zoomed) and "no number printed" means the page gives the sūtra name without a number.

  • śīrṣā: śirasa + śas; śas → śī by jaśśasoḥ śiḥ — जश्शसोः शिः — Pā. 7-1-20, which is sarvanāmasthāna by śi sarvanāmasthānam — शि सर्वनामस्थानम् — Pā. 6-1-42 as printed [sic; the usual number is 1-1-42; the first digit is the hooked 6, as in 6-1-60 below]; śiras → śīrṣan in the Veda by śīrṣañ chandasi — शीर्षञ्छन्दसि — Pā. 6-1-60; loss of śi by śeś chandasi bahulam — Pā. 6-1-70; lengthening by sarvanāmasthāne cāsambuddhau — Pā. 6-4-8; loss of the final n by nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya — नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य — Pā. 8-2-7.
  • vavṛjuḥ: root vṛjī varjane, liṭ, jhi → us, doubling; the reduplicate's ṛ becomes ar by ur at — उरत् — Pā. 7-4-55 as printed [sic? the last two digits are two lobed ಣ-shapes, not hooked 6s; the usual number is 7-4-66; the first digit, flat-footed with a small round head, is read 7], with halādiḥ śeṣaḥ trimming the reduplicate; guṇa of the root would be expected by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ — Pā. 7-3-84, but it is barred by kṅiti ca — Pā. 1-1-5, the ending us being treated as kit because of asaṃyogāl liṭ kit — असंयोगाल्लिट् कित् — Pā. 1-2-5 (the root does not end in a conjunct).
  • ayajvānaḥ: root yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu; suffix ṅvanip in the past sense by suyajor ṅvanip — सुयजोर्ङ्वनिप् — Pā. 3-2-103; yaj + van = yajvan, the suffix pit and so unaccented; na yajvā as a nañ-compound; the first member, an indeclinable, keeps its accent (tatpuruṣe … avyayadvitīyākṛtyāḥ — Pā. 6-2-2), so the same accent remains after the compound is formed (particles being first-syllable-acute by the Phiṭ-sūtra nipātā ādyudāttāḥ, printed Phi. Sū. 80).
  • divaḥ: ablative singular, which by its sup-ending should be unaccented, but ūḍidaṃ padādyappumraidyubhyaḥ — ऊडिदं पदाद्यप्पुम्रैद्युभ्यः — Pā. 6-1-171 makes the ending acute.
  • harivaḥ: harī asya staḥ; the suffix matup by tadasyāsminn iti matup — तदस्यास्मिन्निति मतुप् — Pā. 5-2-94; m → v in the Veda by chandasīraḥ — छन्दसीरः — Pā. 8-2-18 as printed [sic; the usual number is 8-2-15; the last digit is the ಲ-shape = 8]; the augment num by ugidacāṃ… — उगिदचां… — (no number printed on p. 26); su dropped, the final conjunct-letter dropped; ru of the vocative by matuvasor ru sambuddhau chandasi — मतुवसोरु सम्बुद्धौ छन्दसि — Pā. 8-3-1; visarga.
  • avratān: na vidyate vrataṃ yeṣāṃ te; final-acute of the second member after nañ by nañsubhyām — नञ्सुभ्याम् — Pā. 6-2-172; n → ru after the long ā before a vowel in the Saṃhitā (dīrghād aṭi samānapāde — no number printed on p. 26) with a nasalised ā by ato 'ṭi nityam — अतोऽटि नित्यम् — Pā. 8-3-3 (zoom-checked).
  • adhamaḥ: root dhmā śabdāgnisaṃyogayoḥ, laṅ, sip, śap; dhama for dhmā by pāghrādhmāsthāmnādāṇdṛśyartisartiśadasadāṃ pibajighradhamatiṣṭhamanayacchapaśyarcchadhauśīyasīdāḥ — Pā. 7-3-78 (zoom-checked); ru, visarga. Rik 5 ends here (|| 5 ||).
original pp. 26–30

Rik 6

Saṃhitā-pāṭha Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented

अयु॑युत्सन्ननव॒द्यस्य॒ सेना॒मया॑तयन्त क्षि॒तयो॒ नव॑ग्वाः । वृ॒षा॒युधो॒ न वध्र॑यो॒ निर॑ष्टाः प्र॒वद्भि॒रिन्द्रा॑च्चितय॑न्त आयन् ॥ ६ ॥

áyuyutsann anavadyásya sénām áyātayanta kṣitáyo návagvāḥ | vṛṣāyúdho ná vádhrayo níraṣṭāḥ pravádbhir índrāc citáyanta āyan || 6 ||

Pada-pāṭha

अयुयुत्सन् । अनवद्यस्य । सेनाम् । अयातयन्त । क्षितयः । नवऽग्वाः । वृषऽयुधः । न । वध्रयः । निःऽअष्टाः । प्रवत्ऽभिः । इन्द्रात् । चितयन्तः । आयन् ॥ ६ ॥

ayuyutsan | anavadyasya | senām | ayātayanta | kṣitayaḥ | nava-gvāḥ | vṛṣa-yudhaḥ | na | vadhrayaḥ | niḥ-aṣṭāḥ | pravat-bhiḥ | indrāt | citayantaḥ | āyan || 6 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

अनवद्यस्य गर्हणीयदोषरहितस्येन्द्रस्य सेनां प्रत्ययुयुत्सन् [sic: as printed; the Pada has ayuyutsan] । वृत्रस्यानुचरा योद्धुमिच्छन् । तदानीं नवग्वा नवनीयगतयः स्तोतव्यचरित्राः । यद्वा । अङ्गिरसां सत्रमासीनानां मध्ये ये नवभिर्मासैरवाप्तफला उत्थितास्तेषां नवग्वा इति संज्ञा । नवग्वासः सुतसोमास इन्द्रम् [print: इद्रं, sic] ऋग्वेदे ५-२९-१२ इत्यादिषु तथाभिहितत्वात् । क्षितयो मनुष्या अङ्गिरःप्रभृतयः । क्षितयः कृष्टय इति तन्नामसु पाठात् । अयातयन्त । युद्धार्थमिन्द्रं नानाविधैर्मन्त्रैः प्रोत्साहितवन्तः । इन्द्रे योद्धुं गते सति निरष्टास्तेनेन्द्रेण निराकृता वृत्रानुचराश्चितयन्तः स्वकीयामशक्तिं ज्ञापयन्त इन्द्रादिन्द्रस्य सकाशात्प्रवद्भिः पालयितुं सुशक्यैर्मार्गैरायन् । दूरे गतवन्तः । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । वृषायुधो वृषेण सेचनसमर्थेन पुंस्त्वयुक्तेन शूरेण सह युद्धं कुर्वन्तो वध्रयो न नपुंसका इव । निसर्गपण्डो वध्रिः इत्यादिस्मृतिषु प्रयोगात् । ते यथा प्रबलेन दूरे निराकृता भवन्ति तद्वत् ॥

anavadyasya garhaṇīyadoṣarahitasyendrasya senāṃ pratyayuyutsan [sic] | vṛtrasyānucarā yoddhum icchan | tadānīṃ navagvā navanīyagatayaḥ stotavyacaritrāḥ | yadvā | aṅgirasāṃ satram āsīnānāṃ madhye ye navabhir māsair avāptaphalā utthitās teṣāṃ navagvā iti saṃjñā | navagvāsaḥ sutasomāsa indram [print: idraṃ, sic] ṛgvede 5-29-12 ity ādiṣu tathābhihitatvāt | kṣitayo manuṣyā aṅgiraḥprabhṛtayaḥ | kṣitayaḥ kṛṣṭaya iti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | ayātayanta | yuddhārtham indraṃ nānāvidhair mantraiḥ protsāhitavantaḥ | indre yoddhuṃ gate sati niraṣṭās tenendreṇa nirākṛtā vṛtrānucarāś citayantaḥ svakīyām aśaktiṃ jñāpayanta indrād indrasya sakāśāt pravadbhiḥ pālayituṃ sukaśyair [read: sukaraiḥ?] mārgair āyan | dūre gatavantaḥ | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | vṛṣāyudho vṛṣeṇa secanasamarthena puṃstvayuktena śūreṇa saha yuddhaṃ kurvanto vadhrayo na napuṃsakā iva | nisargapaṇḍo vadhriḥ ity ādismṛtiṣu prayogāt | te yathā prabalena dūre nirākṛtā bhavanti tadvat ||

Translation: "Anavadyasya — of Indra, who is free of any blameworthy fault — the followers of Vṛtra wished to fight against his army. Then the navagvāḥ — those of praiseworthy conduct, of 'new' ways [?] — [encouraged him]. Or: of the Aṅgirases sitting at a long sacrifice (satra), those who rose up having gained the fruit in nine months have the name navagvāḥ; for it is so stated in passages such as 'navagvāsaḥ sutasomāsa indram' (Ṛgveda 5-29-12 as printed, zoom-checked). Kṣitayaḥ — human beings, the Aṅgirases and others, since kṣitayaḥ is read among the names of man (kṛṣṭayaḥ). Ayātayanta — they encouraged Indra with various mantras for the sake of the fight. When Indra went to fight, they were niraṣṭāḥ — driven off by that Indra — the followers of Vṛtra, who, citayantaḥ — making known their own weakness — went away from Indra by pravadbhiḥ, easily-managed paths [?] for saving themselves; they went far off. The illustration: like vadhrayaḥ — eunuchs — fighting with a vṛṣāyudha, a hero of virility, able to shower (vṛṣā + āyudha); eunuchs are, as in the smṛti passages ('the vadhri is a eunuch by nature'), thrown far off by a strong man; so were they."

Grammar within the bhāṣya pp. 27–28, characterized; the print is crowded and the small numerals were not pursued: the bhāṣya's tail parses, word by word, ayuyutsan (root yudha saṃprahāre, the desiderative san, with a sūtra on kit-ness so that there is no guṇa, and a ban on the iṭ augment for a one-vowel root), senām (inena saha vartate, sa for saha, accent of the first member), ayātayanta (root yatī prayatne, causative), kṣitayaḥ (root kṣi nivāsagatyoḥ, "those who go", i.e. men), navagvāḥ (navabhir māsair gacchantīti navagvāḥ, with a suffix after the root gam — a ḍa/kvip alternative is argued — and loss of the nasal, lengthening to ū; the exact sūtra numbers on p. 27 and p. 28 were not read), vṛṣāyudhaḥ (a denominative in kyaṣ/kvip, with a dispute whether the prefix word may be compounded), niraṣṭāḥ (root aśū vyāptau in the sense of the state, the niṣṭhā ending, no iṭ by yasya vibhāṣā; the ṣ of vraścādi-type; first-member accent of the bahuvrīhi; the form with ṣ for s is Vedic), pravadbhiḥ (root vana paṇa sambhaktau, the suffix kvip, the augment tuk [?] — the small numbers printed on pp. 27–28 here (about 1-2-10, 2-2-10 or 7-2-10, 6-4-40 with a vārtika number, Kā. 3-2-… and one of the form 6-4-…) were zoomed once but not all settled; they are repeated with fuller print on pp. 31–33 below) and citayantaḥ (root citī saṃjñāne, śatṛ, śap; the absence of guṇa of the penultimate is explained by "the rule on augments is not universal", anityam āgamaśāsanam).

Pratipadārtha — "anavadyasya — (when Vṛtra's followers) of the irreproachable Indra; senām — the army; ayuyutsan — wished to fight [the print's words "ಪ್ರತಿಭಟಿಸಲಿಚ್ಛಿಸಿ…" are partly obscured: "wished to confront"]; navagvāḥ — those of praiseworthy conduct (or: those who obtained the fruit of the whole sacrifice in nine months); kṣitayaḥ — (the Aṅgirases and others) human beings; ayātayanta — encouraged Indra with various mantras; (te — those rākṣasas who came to fight Indra); niraṣṭāḥ — made powerless (by Indra); citayantaḥ — showing their own powerlessness; vṛṣāyudhaḥ — fighting with a strong, mighty one; vadhrayaḥ na — like eunuchs; pravadbhiḥ — by precipitous paths (suited to flight); indrāt — from Indra; āyan — went away (fled)."

Bhāvārtha — "Indra is faultless. The wicked followers of Vṛtra wished to fight his army. The Aṅgirases and other praiseworthy leaders of men encouraged Indra with many kinds of mantras. Then, when Indra went out to battle, those rākṣasas became powerless. Showing their weakness, like eunuchs against a strong man, they were unable to fight Indra, and fled in various directions along whatever paths they found."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 29) — "They ( followers of Vritra ) desired to fight with the army of irreproachable Indra. Men (Angirasas) engaged in offering libations to Indra for nine months encouraged Indra to give them fight; like eunuchs fighting with a hero they fled by precipitous paths exposing their backs away from Indra."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), pp. 29–30 - anavadyasya = garhaṇīyadoṣarahitasya: "one without any bad faults." - kṣitayaḥ = kṣi nivāsagatyoḥ; kṣiyanti gacchantīti kṣitayo manuṣyāḥ: "since the root kṣi has the senses of 'dwelling' and 'going', kṣitayaḥ means men who are going about, able to move. Since the word kṣitayaḥ is read among the twenty-five names of man beginning with narāḥ (Ni. 3-2 as printed, zoom-checked), kṣitayaḥ means men." - navagvāḥ = navabhir māsair gacchantīti navagvāḥ | aṅgirasāṃ satram āsīnānāṃ madhye ye navabhir māsair avāptaphalā utthitās teṣāṃ navagvā iti saṃjñā: "Some in the family of the ṛṣi Aṅgiras gained their wish in nine months, through performing a sacrifice (satra) that lasts a year. These are called navagvāḥ; there is a convention that this name is given to the best of the Aṅgirasa ṛṣi-family, who obtained their wish in nine months. In some passages those who obtained the fruit in ten months are called daśagvāḥ. On this, Western scholars, explaining the word, [say], in the print's own English: 'the term Navagva is applied to a man, generally an Angiras in the highest degree (Angirastama—ಅಂಗಿರಸ್ತಮ) who appear as a mystic race of olden times coupled with, and conceived probably as related to the Angirases. they are often associated with the Dasagvas (ದಶಗ್ವ)' [as printed; the English is not attributed]. The usage of this word occurs in many ṛks of the Ṛgveda. We give some examples:"

१. येना नवग्वो दध्यङ्ङपोर्णुते येन विप्रास आपिरे ॥ (ऋ. सं. ९-१०-८४) २. नवग्वो नु दशग्वो अङ्गिरस्तमः सचा देवेषु मंहते ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-६२-६) ३. सरण्युभिः फलिगमिन्द्र शक्र बलं रवेण दरयो दशग्वैः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-६२-४) ४. सखा ह यत्र सखिभिर्नवग्वैरभिज्ञ्वा सत्वभिर्गा अनुग्मन् ॥ (ऋ. सं. ३-३९-५) ५. अङ्गिरसो नः पितरो नवग्वा अथर्वाणो भृगवः सोम्यासः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-१४-६) ६. येना नवग्वे अङ्गिरे दशग्वे सप्तास्ये रेवती रेवदूष ॥ (ऋ. सं. ४-५१-४)

1. yenā navagvo dadhyaṅṅ apornute yena viprāsa āpire || (ṛ. saṃ. 9-10-84) 2. navagvo nu daśagvo aṅgirastamaḥ sacā deveṣu maṃhate || (ṛ. saṃ. 10-62-6) 3. saraṇyubhiḥ phaligam indra śakra balaṃ raveṇa darayo daśagvaiḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. 1-62-4) 4. sakhā ha yatra sakhibhir navagvair abhijñvā satvabhir gā anugman || (ṛ. saṃ. 3-39-5) 5. aṅgiraso naḥ pitaro navagvā atharvāṇo bhṛgavaḥ somyāsaḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. 10-14-6) 6. yenā navagve aṅgire daśagve saptāsye revatī revad ūṣa || (ṛ. saṃ. 4-51-4)

The source leaves these six half-verses untranslated. My glosses, editorial and tentative: 1. "[the aid] by which Navagva Dadhyañc opens [?], by which the inspired ones obtained [?]." 2. "The Navagva and the Daśagva, most Aṅgirasa-like, rejoice together among the gods." 3. "O mighty Indra, with the swift ones [?] you split the phaliga [?], with a roar, [your] strength, with the Daśagvas." 4. "Where the friend [Indra], with his friends the Navagvas, [following] the cows with the brave [?] went after them." 5. "Our fathers the Aṅgirases, the Navagvas, the Atharvans, the Bhṛgus, worthy of soma." 6. "[That aid] by which, O wealthy [dawn], you shone richly on Navagva, Aṅgiras, Daśagva, Saptāsya." The reference numbers were read from small Kannada numerals and are all uncertain. The source adds that the same word navagva is used in many Ṛgveda ṛks and in Atharva-veda passages, "Ath. Saṃ. 19-1-56; 18-3-20" (as printed, zoom-checked; the earlier reading "18-1-36; 19-2-30" is replaced), and that "in the second of these examples [no. 2 above], the one called navagva and daśagva, the most distinguished among the Aṅgirasa ṛṣi-family, is honoured even by the gods — which is worth noting."

  • vṛṣāyudhaḥ = vṛṣeṇa secanasamarthena puṃstvayuktena śūreṇa: "with a hero who is capable of showering [virility], i.e. a man of manly strength."
  • vadhrayaḥ = napuṃsakāḥ: "eunuchs, the weak, men without strength; cowards."
  • pravadbhiḥ = pravaṇaiḥ sukarair mārgaiḥ: "by favourable [easy] paths."
  • citayantaḥ = citī saṃjñāne; svakīyām aśaktiṃ jñāpayantaḥ: "showing their own powerlessness."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā p. 30, grammar page — noted briefly: ayuyutsan — root yudha saṃprahāre; the form is explained as yoddhum icchan, "wishing to fight"; the wishers are the followers of Vṛtra, who are the agents of both iṣ and yudh; the san suffix in the sense of "wishing" comes after a root whose agent is the same as that of the wishing (dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samānakartṛkād icchāyāṃ vā — धातोः कर्मणः समानकर्तृकादिच्छायां वा — Pā. 3-1-7, as printed); then yudh + sa, with sanyaṅoḥ — सन्यङोः — Pā. 6-1-9 [?] for the doubling; the page breaks off in the discussion of the doubling.

Rik 6 — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā, continued (pp. 31–33, PDF 45–47; grammar pages, noted briefly)

Kannada prose with sūtras quoted; numerals re-read on the better scan (zoomed on pp. 31–33).

  • ayuyutsan (p. 31, continued): doubling of the root (sanyaṅoḥ — Pā. 6-1-9, zoom-checked), halādiḥ śeṣaḥ trimming the reduplicate; the san ending after a consonant-final root is kit (halantāc ca — हलन्ताच्च — Pā. 1-2-10), so no guṇa of the penultimate (also kṅiti ca — Pā. 1-1-5); no iṭ augment, as the root is one-vowelled and anudātta (ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt — एकाच उपदेशेऽनुदात्तात् — Pā. 7-2-1 as printed [sic: the print ends in a single ∩ = 1; the usual number is 7-2-10]); the Saṃgraha-kārikā verse "bandhir yudhi rudhī …" lists yudh as anudātta. The root is of the 4th class, ātmanepada, and by pūrvavat sanaḥ — पूर्ववत्सनः — Pā. 1-3-62 (zoom-checked) san would also take ātmanepada so that śānac is expected; but by Vedic vyatyaya parasmaipada comes, then laṭaḥ śatṛśānacau — लटः शतृशानचौ — Pā. 3-2-124, whence ayuyutsan.
  • senām: inena saha vartate iti senā; tena saheti tulyayoge — तेन सहेति तुल्ययोगे — Pā. 2-2-28 (saha compounded with an instrumental in the sense of simultaneity, a bahuvrīhi); sa for saha by vopasarjanasya — वोपसर्जनस्य — Pā. 6-3-82; first-member accent by bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam — Pā. 6-2-1.
  • ayātayanta: root yatī prayatne; the causative ṇic by hetumati ca — हेतुमति च — Pā. 3-1-26; hetu defined by tatprayojako hetuś ca — Pā. 1-4-55; laṅ, aṭ, upadhā-vṛddhi, ātmanepada, śap, guṇa, jhaḥ → ant, ayādeśa: ayātayanta.
  • kṣitayaḥ (p. 31 end – p. 32): root kṣi nivāsagatyoḥ; the suffix ktic (ktic ktau ca saṃjñāyām — क्तिच्क्तौ च संज्ञायाम् — Pā. 3-3-174), kṣiyanti gacchanti = "those who go, or know", men.
  • navagvāḥ (p. 32): navabhir māsaiḥ gacchantīti navagvāḥ — "ṛṣis who obtained their fruit in nine months"; root gam with the Uṇādi suffix ḍva (the ḍ-marker explains the loss of am): gv; or an alternative: kvip after gam, loss of the nasal (gamaḥ kvau — गमः क्वौ — Pā. 6-4-40, zoom-checked), ūṭ for the verb-root (a vārtika: ūj ca gamādīnām, printed Pā. 6-4-40-2; the sūtra after it, on the replacement of the final letter, is cited by a short name I could not read, with the number printed 1-1-53), lengthening to ū before jas; oḥ supi — ओः सुपि — Pā. 16-4-83 as printed [sic: the first two digits are ∩ and the hooked 6; the usual number is 6-4-83] gives yaṇ (ū → v): navagvaḥ; the Vedic lengthening gives navagvāḥ.
  • vṛṣāyudhaḥ: vṛṣeṇa saha yuddhyati; kvip ca — क्विप् च — Pā. 3-2-29 as printed [sic? the usual number is 3-2-76; the last glyph pair is a curled 2 and a 9-shape] (kvip after all roots, even without an upapada, in the Veda and in the world, as the Kāśikā shows on sopapadebhyo nirupapadebhyaḥ); Vedic lengthening of the first member by anyeṣām api dṛśyate — अन्येषामपि दृश्यते — Pā. 6-3-137.
  • niraṣṭāḥ: root aśū vyāptau, ūdit, so iṭ is optional (svaratisūtisūyatidhūñūdito vā — Pā. 7-2-44); the niṣṭhā suffix in the state-sense (niṣṭhā, Pā. 3-2-102); no iṭ by yasya vibhāṣā — यस्य विभाषा — Pā. 7-2-15; ś → ṣ by vraścabhrasja… — Pā. 8-2-36, ṣṭutva giving aṣṭa; the bahuvrīhi with first-member accent; an alternative derivation with asta from the root as, niḥ + asta; the preverb keeps its accent by gatir anantaraḥ — गतिरनन्तरः — Pā. 6-2-49 (zoom-checked).
  • pravadbhiḥ (p. 33): root vana paṇa sambhaktau after pra; kvip; the nasal lost by gamaḥ kvau — Pā. 6-4-40 (with the vārtika "gamādīnām iti vaktavyam"); n lost; the augment tuk by hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk — ह्रस्वस्य पिति कृति तुक् — Pā. 6-1-71: pravat; bhis; first-member accent by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt.
  • citayantaḥ: root citī saṃjñāne; causative ṇic by hetumati ca — Pā. 3-1-26; guṇa of the penultimate would be expected by pugantalaghūpadhasya ca — पुगन्तलघूपधस्य च — Pā. 7-3-86, but "all rules are optional in the Veda" (sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante); the augment's non-universality (anityam āgamaśāsanam) is also cited; then laṭ, śatṛ, śap, guṇa → ay; the augment num by ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ — उगिदचां सर्वनामस्थानेऽधातोः — Pā. 7-1-80 as printed [sic? zoom-checked: the tens digit is the 8-shape, as in 7-3-86 two lines above; the usual number is 7-1-70]; ru and visarga. Rik 6 ends here (|| 6 ||).
original pp. 33–36

Rik 7

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

त्वमे॒तान्रु॑द॒तो जक्ष॑त॒श्चायो॑धयो॒ रज॑स इन्द्र पा॒रे । अवा॑दहो दि॒व आ दस्यु॑मु॒च्चा प्र सु॑न्व॒तः स्तु॑व॒तः शंस॑मावः ॥ ७ ॥

tvam etā́n rudató jákṣataś cā́yodhayo rájasa indra pāré | ávādaho divá ā dásyum uccā́ prá sunvatáḥ stuvatáḥ śáṃsam āvaḥ || 7 ||

original p. 34

Pada-pāṭha

त्वम् । एतान् । रुदतः । जक्षतः । च । अयोधयः । रजसः । इन्द्र । पारे । अव । अदहः । दिवः । आ । दस्युम् । उच्चा । प्र । सुन्वतः । स्तुवतः । शंसम् । आवः ॥ ७ ॥

tvam | etān | rudataḥ | jakṣataḥ | ca | ayodhayaḥ | rajasaḥ | indra | pāre | ava | adahaḥ | divaḥ | ā | dasyum | uccā | pra | sunvataḥ | stuvataḥ | śaṃsam | āvaḥ || 7 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya p. 34, in full; numerals zoom-checked

हे इन्द्र त्वं रुदतो रोदनं कुर्वतो जक्षतो भक्षणं हसनं वा कुर्वतश्चैतान्द्विविधानपि वृत्रानुचरान्रजसः पारेऽन्तरिक्षस्य परभागे । रजःशब्दोऽन्तरिक्षवाची लोका रजांस्युच्यन्ते । नि. ४-१९ । इत्युक्तत्वात् । अयोधयः युद्धमकरोः । युद्धेन मारितवानित्यर्थः । दस्युमुपक्षयितारं वृत्रं दिव आ द्युलोकादानीयोच्चोत्कर्षेणावादहः । दग्धवानसि । वृत्रं सपरिवारं विनाश्य तत ऊर्ध्वं सुन्वतः सोमाभिषवं कुर्वतः स्तुवतः स्तोत्रं कुर्वतो यजमानस्य शंसं स्तुतिं प्रावः । प्रकर्षेण रक्षितवानसि ॥ रुदतः । रुदिर् अश्रुविमोचने । लटः शतृ । अदादित्वाच्छपो लुक् । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तत्वम् । शतुरनुम इति शस उदात्तत्वम् । जक्षतः । जक्ष भक्षहसनयोः । पूर्ववच्छपो लुक् । जक्षित्यादयः षट् पा. ६-१-६ । इत्यभ्यस्तसंज्ञा । अतोऽभ्यस्तानामादिरित्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । सुन्वतः । षुनोतेः शतरि स्वादिभ्यः श्नुः । हुश्नुवोरित्यादिना यणादेशः । शतुरनुम इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । स्तुवतः । ष्टुञ् स्तुतौ । अदादित्वाच्छपो लुक् । उवङादेशः । पूर्ववत्स्वरः ॥ ॥ ७ ॥

he indra tvaṃ rudato rodanaṃ kurvato jakṣato bhakṣaṇaṃ hasanaṃ vā kurvataścaitāndvividhānapi vṛtrānucarānrajasaḥ pāre 'ntarikṣasya parabhāge | rajaḥśabdo 'ntarikṣavācī lokā rajāṃsyucyante | ni. 4-19 | ityuktatvāt | ayodhayaḥ yuddhamakaroḥ | yuddhena māritavānityarthaḥ | dasyumupakṣayitāraṃ vṛtraṃ diva ā dyulokādānīyoccotkarṣeṇāvādahaḥ | dagdhavānasi | vṛtraṃ saparivāraṃ vināśya tata ūrdhvaṃ sunvataḥ somābhiṣavaṃ kurvataḥ stuvataḥ stotraṃ kurvato yajamānasya śaṃsaṃ stutiṃ prāvaḥ | prakarṣeṇa rakṣitavānasi ‖ rudataḥ | rudir aśruvimocane | laṭaḥ śatṛ | adāditvācchapo luk | pratyayasvareṇāntodāttatvam | śaturanuma iti śasa udāttatvam | jakṣataḥ | jakṣa bhakṣahasanayoḥ | pūrvavacchapo luk | jakṣityādayaḥ ṣaṭ pā. 6-1-6 | ityabhyastasaṃjñā | ato 'bhyastānāmādirityādyudāttatvam | sunvataḥ | ṣunoteḥ śatari svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ | huśnuvorityādinā yaṇādeśaḥ | śaturanuma iti vibhakterudāttatvam | stuvataḥ | ṣṭuñ stutau | adāditvācchapo luk | uvaṅādeśaḥ | pūrvavatsvaraḥ ‖ ‖ 7 ‖

Translation: "O Indra, you [fought] these followers of Vṛtra, of both kinds — those who weep and those who eat or laugh (jakṣataḥ = eating, or laughing) — at the far side (pāre) of the rajas, the mid-region. The word rajas means the mid-region, since it is said 'the worlds are called rajāṃsi' (Ni. 4-19, zoom-checked). Ayodhayaḥ — you fought; the sense is that you killed them in battle. The dasyu, the destroyer Vṛtra, having brought down from the heavenly world, uccā — loftily, with distinction — avādahaḥ — you burnt up. Having destroyed Vṛtra with his retinue, after that (tata, as printed) you prāvaḥ — protected excellently — the praise (śaṃsa, stuti) of the sacrificer who presses the soma (sunvataḥ) and recites hymns (stuvataḥ)." (The grammatical tail: rudataḥ — root rudir, śatṛ, śap elided as an adādi root, final acute by the suffix accent, śas acute by śatur anumaḥ; jakṣataḥ — root jakṣ, abhyasta by "jakṣityādayaḥ ṣaṭ", Pā. 6-1-6, hence initial acute; sunvataḥ — śnu, yaṇ by huśnuvoḥ, ending acute; stuvataḥ — uvaṅ, accent as before.)

Pratipadārtha — "he indra — O Indra; tvam — you; rudataḥ — weeping (those who are weeping); jakṣataś ca — or laughing (those who are laughing); etān — these rākṣasas, followers of Vṛtra; rajasaḥ pāre — at the edge of the mid-region; ayodhayaḥ — you have fought; dasyum — (and) the thief Vṛtra; divaḥ ā — dragging him from the mid-region; uccā — completely; avādahaḥ — you have burned to ashes. (Thereafter)

original p. 35

sunvataḥ — of the one pressing the soma-juice; stuvataḥ — of the one reciting praises (the sacrificer); śaṃsam — the praise; pra āvaḥ — you have protected well (made it true to its meaning)."

Bhāvārtha — "O Indra, you are the punisher of the wicked and the protector of the good. Whether the rākṣasas, followers of Vṛtra, were weeping or laughing, you struck them down at the very edge of the mid-region. You destroyed Vṛtra, the thief, and made the praise offered to you by the sacrificer in the sacrifice true to its meaning."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 35) — "O Indra, you have destroyed them whether weeping or laughing off the other end of the sky ; you have burned the demon (or robber) having dragged him from heaven and have received the praises of him who pressed the Soma juice for you and sang your glories."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 35 — jakṣataḥ = jakṣa bhakṣahasanayoḥ | bhakṣaṇaṃ hasanaṃ vā kurvantaḥ: "the root jakṣ means to eat or to laugh; therefore jakṣataḥ means those who are eating or those who are laughing." — rajasaḥ pāre: "rajas here is the mid-region (Ni. 4-19, zoom-checked); therefore rajasaḥ pāre means at the end of the mid-region, in the mid-region, at a great height." — uccā: "greatly, especially."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 35–36, grammar pages — noted briefly; numerals zoom-checked: rudataḥ — root rudir aśruvimocane; laṭ replaced by śatṛ; śap elided by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ — अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शपः (adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ) — Pā. 2-4-72; tāsyanudāttenṅid… does not make the lasārvadhātuka śatṛ unaccented, so the suffix accent stays and rudat is final-acute; then the accusative plural śas, acute by śatur anumo nadyajādī — शतुरनुमो नद्यजादी (śatur anumo nadyajādī) — Pā. 6-1-173 (a final-acute stem in śatṛ without the augment num makes a following nadī ending or vowel-initial case-ending acute)

original p. 36

(the explanation continues: "… the śas is acute"). — jakṣataḥ — root jakṣa bhakṣahasanayoḥ, laṭ, śatṛ, śap elided as before; jakṣityādayaḥ ṣaṭ — जक्षित्यादयः षट् (jakṣityādayaḥ ṣaṭ) — Pā. 6-1-6: jakṣ and the six roots beginning with jāgṛ (the bahuvrīhi "ādir yeṣāṃ te" read as tadguṇasaṃvijñāna, so that jakṣ itself is included) are called abhyasta; then abhyastānām ādiḥ — अभ्यस्तानामादिः (abhyastānām ādiḥ) — Pā. 6-1-189 makes the first syllable acute before a vowel-initial lasārvadhātuka without iṭ. — sunvataḥ — root ṣuñ abhiṣave; dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ — धात्वादेः षः सः (dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ) — Pā. 6-1-64; laṭ–śatṛ; svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ — स्वादिभ्यः श्नुः (svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ) — Pā. 3-1-73; huśnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke — हुश्नुवोः सार्वधातुके (huśnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke) — Pā. 6-4-87 gives yaṇ (u → v); genitive singular ṅas; ending acute by śatur anumaḥ. — stuvataḥ — root ṣṭuñ stutau; ṣ → s, and the ṭ goes by nimittāpāye naimittikasyāpy apāyaḥ; śap elided (adādi); aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau — अचि श्नुधातुभ्रुवां य्वोरियङुवङौ (aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau) — Pā. 6-4-77 gives uvaṅ: stuvat; ṅas acute as before. Rik 7 ends here (|| 7 ||).

च॒क्रा॒णास॑ः परी॒णहं॑ पृथि॒व्या हिर॑ण्येन म॒णिना॒ शुम्भ॑मानाः । न हि॑न्वा॒नास॑स्तितिरु॒स्त इन्द्रं॒ परि॒ स्पशो॑ अदधा॒त्सूर्ये॑ण ॥ ८ ॥

cakrāṇā́saḥ parīṇáhaṃ pṛthivyā́ híraṇyena maṇínā śúmbhamānāḥ | ná hinvānā́sas titirus tá indram pári spáśo adadhāt sū́ryeṇa || 8 ||

चक्राणासः । परिऽनहम् । पृथिव्याः । हिरण्येन । मणिना । शुम्भमानाः ॥ न । हिन्वानासः । तितिरुः । ते । इन्द्रम् । परि । स्पशः । अदधात् । सूर्येण ॥ ८ ॥

cakrāṇāsaḥ | pari-naham | pṛthivyāḥ | hiraṇyena | maṇinā | śumbhamānāḥ || na | hinvānāsaḥ | titiruḥ | te | indram | pari | spaśaḥ | adadhāt | sūryeṇa || 8 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya p. 37, in full; numerals zoom-checked

ये वृत्रानुचराः पृथिव्या भूमेः परीणहमाच्छादनं सर्वतो व्याप्तिं चक्राणासः कुर्वाणा हिरण्येन हिरण्ययुक्तेन मणिना कण्ठबाह्वादिगतेन मण्याद्याभरणेन शुम्भमानाः शोभमाना हिन्वानासो वर्धमानाः सन्तो वर्तन्ते ते तथाविधा वृत्रानुचरा इन्द्रं युद्धायोद्यन्तं न तितिरुः । जेतुं न समर्था आसन् । तदानीं स इन्द्रः स्पशो बाधकान्वृत्रानुचरान् सूर्येणादित्येन पर्यदधात् । परिहितान् व्यवहितानकरोत् । तथा च ब्राह्मणम् । आदित्यो ह्येवोद्यन् पुरस्ताद्रक्षांस्यपहन्तीति ॥ चक्राणासः । करोतेश्छन्दसि लिडिति वर्तमाने लिटः कानच् । ततोऽसुक् । चित इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । परीणहम् । परिणहनं परीणत् । परिपूर्वान्नह्यतेर्भावे क्विपि नहिवृतीत्यादिना । पा. ६-३-११६ । पूर्वपदस्य दीर्घः । पृथिव्याः । उदात्तयण इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । हिन्वानासः । हि गतौ वृद्धौ च । ताच्छीलिकश्चानश् । तितिरुः । तिरतिर्गत्यर्थः ॥ ॥ ८ ॥

ye vṛtrānucarāḥ pṛthivyā bhūmeḥ parīṇahamācchādanaṃ sarvato vyāptiṃ cakrāṇāsaḥ kurvāṇā hiraṇyena hiraṇyayuktena maṇinā kaṇṭhabāhvādigatena maṇyādyābharaṇena śumbhamānāḥ śobhamānā hinvānāso vardhamānāḥ santo vartante te tathāvidhā vṛtrānucarā indraṃ yuddhāyodyantaṃ na titiruḥ | jetuṃ na samarthā āsan | tadānīṃ sa indraḥ spaśo bādhakānvṛtrānucarān sūryeṇādityena paryadadhāt | parihitān vyavahitānakarot | tathā ca brāhmaṇam | ādityo hyevodyan purastādrakṣāṃsyapahantīti ‖ cakrāṇāsaḥ | karoteśchandasi liḍiti vartamāne liṭaḥ kānac | tato 'suk | cita ityantodāttatvam | parīṇaham | pariṇahanaṃ parīṇat | paripūrvānnahyaterbhāve kvipi nahivṛtītyādinā | pā. 6-3-116 | pūrvapadasya dīrghaḥ | pṛthivyāḥ | udāttayaṇa iti vibhakterudāttatvam | hinvānāsaḥ | hi gatau vṛddhau ca | tācchīlikaścānaś | titiruḥ | tiratirgatyarthaḥ ‖ ‖ 8 ‖ Print: "ಆದಿತ್ಯೋ ಹ್ಯೇವೋದ್ಯನ್" = आदित्यो ह्येवोद्यन्, where the earlier text had हैवोद्यन्; "परीणत्" as printed, for the kvip form parīṇah.

Translation: "Those followers of Vṛtra who cakrāṇāsaḥ — making — a parīṇaha of the earth, a covering, an all-round pervasion; hiraṇyena maṇinā — shining with golden jewel-ornaments worn on the neck, arms and so on; hinvānāsaḥ — growing — na titiruḥ — were unable to overcome Indra as he rose for battle: they were not strong enough to conquer. Then that Indra pari adadhāt — put round, i.e. cut off, hid away — the spaśaḥ, the harassers, the followers of Vṛtra, by means of Sūrya, the Sun. So says a Brāhmaṇa: 'The sun indeed, rising in the east, drives away the rākṣasas.'" (The grammatical tail: cakrāṇāsaḥ — root kṛ, Vedic liṭ in the present, kānac, then asuk, final acute because kānac is cit; parīṇaham — pari + nah + kvip in the state-sense, lengthening of the first member by nahivṛti…, Pā. 6-3-116; pṛthivyāḥ — the ending acute by udāttayaṇaḥ…; hinvānāsaḥ — root hi, the habitual cānaś; titiruḥ — the root tṛ in the sense of going.)

Pratipadārtha — "(ye — those followers of Vṛtra who) pṛthivyāḥ — for the earth; parīṇaham — a covering all round; cakrāṇāsaḥ — making; hiraṇyena — with ornaments of gold; maṇinā — with gem-set

original p. 38

ornaments; śumbhamānāḥ — shining; hinvānāsaḥ — though they were growing; te — those rākṣasas; indram — Indra; na titiruḥ — could not conquer; spaśaḥ — those harassing rākṣasas; sūryeṇa — by means of the sun; pari adadhāt — (Indra) scattered and destroyed."

Bhāvārtha — "The rākṣasas, the followers of the asura Vṛtra, covered all the earth. They shone with ornaments set with gold and gems, and they were increasing. Yet they could not conquer Indra. With the help of the Sun Indra scattered such oppressing rākṣasas."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 38) — "Decorated with gold and jewels they (demons) were spreading over (round) the earth ; but though they were mighty they could not vanquish Indra ; he (Indra) dispersed them (with the light of the Sun) at Sunrise" no full stop in the print.

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 38 — parīṇaham = ācchādanaṃ sarvato vyāptim: "pervasion, covering. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda (Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-1-1, zoom-checked), in the sentence पारीण्यह्यस्यैशे पत्नि[य्यै?]वानुमतं निर्वपति (pārīṇyahyasyaiśe patni[yyai?]vānumataṃ nirvapati) [as printed, letter by letter; the print's conjuncts are crowded], the word pārīṇahya is used in the sense 'vessels used for household work'."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 38–39, grammar pages — noted briefly; numerals zoom-checked: cakrāṇāsaḥ — root (ḍu)kṛñ karaṇe; liṭ in the present sense by chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ — छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिटः (chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ) — Pā. 3-4-6; kānac for liṭ by liṭaḥ kānaj vā — लिटः कानज्वा (liṭaḥ kānaj vā) — Pā. 3-2-106; doubling by liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya — लिटि धातोरनभ्यासस्य (liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya) — Pā. 6-1-8; a (with r) for the reduplicate's vowel by ur at — उरत् (ur at) — Pā. 7-4-55 as printed [sic: both digits are the 5-glyph, as in 7-1-50 below; the usual number is 7-4-66]; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, ścutva, yaṇ: cakrāna, n → ṇ; jas takes asuk by ājjaser asuk — आज्जसेरसुक् (ājjaser asuk) — Pā. 7-1-50; ru and visarga; kānac is cit, so by citaḥ — चितः (citaḥ) — Pā. 6-1-163 the word is final-acute.

परि । यत् । इन्द्र । रोदसी इति । उभे इति । अबुभोजीः । महिना । विश्वतः । सीम् ॥ अमन्यमानान् । अभि । मन्यमानैः । निः । ब्रह्मऽभिः । अधमः । दस्युम् । इन्द्र ॥ ९ ॥

pari | yat | indra | rodasī iti | ubhe iti | abubhojīḥ | mahinā | viśvataḥ | sīm || amanyamānān | abhi | manyamānaiḥ | niḥ | brahma-bhiḥ | adhamaḥ | dasyum | indra || 9 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya p. 40, in full; numerals zoom-checked

हे इन्द्र यद्यदा रोदसी उभे द्युलोकभूलोकावुभौ महिना त्वदीयेन महिम्ना विश्वतः सीं सर्वतः परिगृह्य पर्यबुभोजीः परितो भुक्तवानसि । तदानीं त्वममन्यमानान्मन्त्रार्थमनुध्यातुमशक्तानपि केवलपाठकान्यजमानानभि मन्यमानैरस्मदीया एते यजमाना रक्षणीया इत्यभिमानं कुर्वद्भिर्ब्रह्मभिर्मन्त्रैर्दस्युं चोरं वृत्रादिरूपमसुरं निरधमः । निःसारितवानसि । धमतिर्गतिकर्मा । नि. ६-२ । इति यास्कः । अबुभोजीः । भुज पालनाभ्यवहारयोः । लङि सिपि बहुलं छन्दसि । पा. २-४-७६ । इति विकरणस्य श्लुः । बहुलं छन्दसि । पा. ७-३-९७ । इतीडागमः । अडुदात्तः । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । महिना । महिम्ना । महच्छब्दात्पृथ्वादिलक्षणो भावे इमनिच् । टेरिति टिलोपः । तृतीयैकवचनेऽल्लोपे सत्युदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेणोदात्तत्वम् । मलोपश्छान्दसः । अमन्यमानान् । मन्यन्ते जानन्तीति मन्यमानाः । मन ज्ञाने । दिवादिभ्यः श्यन् । श्यनो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । समासेऽव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । संहितायां रुत्वानुनासिकावुक्तौ ॥ ॥ ९ ॥

he indra yadyadā rodasī ubhe dyulokabhūlokāvubhau mahinā tvadīyena mahimnā viśvataḥ sīṃ sarvataḥ parigṛhya paryabubhojīḥ parito bhuktavānasi | tadānīṃ tvamamanyamānānmantrārthamanudhyātumaśaktānapi kevalapāṭhakānyajamānānabhi manyamānairasmadīyā ete yajamānā rakṣaṇīyā ityabhimānaṃ kurvadbhirbrahmabhirmantrairdasyuṃ coraṃ vṛtrādirūpamasuraṃ niradhamaḥ | niḥsāritavānasi | dhamatirgatikarmā | ni. 6-2 | iti yāskaḥ | abubhojīḥ | bhuja pālanābhyavahārayoḥ | laṅi sipi bahulaṃ chandasi | pā. 2-4-76 | iti vikaraṇasya śluḥ | bahulaṃ chandasi | pā. 7-3-97 | itīḍāgamaḥ | aḍudāttaḥ | yadvṛttayogādanighātaḥ | mahinā | mahimnā | mahacchabdātpṛthvādilakṣaṇo bhāve imanic | ṭeriti ṭilopaḥ | tṛtīyaikavacane 'llope satyudāttanivṛttisvareṇodāttatvam | malopaśchāndasaḥ | amanyamānān | manyante jānantīti manyamānāḥ | mana jñāne | divādibhyaḥ śyan | śyano nittvādādyudāttatvam | samāse 'vyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | saṃhitāyāṃ rutvānunāsikāvuktau ‖ ‖ 9 ‖

Translation: "O Indra, when you paryabubhojīḥ — enclosed on every side, viśvataḥ sīm, the two rodasī, heaven and earth, with your greatness, and enjoyed them all round — then, with brahmabhiḥ, mantras uttered by those who hold that 'these sacrificers are ours, to be protected' (manyamānaiḥ, 'those who have this conviction'), on behalf of sacrificers who are amanyamānān — mere reciters, unable to reflect on the meaning of the mantras — you nir adhamaḥ — drove out — the dasyu, the robber, the asura in the form of Vṛtra and others. Dhamati is a verb of motion — so says Yāska (Ni. 6-2, zoom-checked)." (The grammatical tail: abubhojīḥ — root bhuj, laṅ, sip; ślu of the vikaraṇa by bahulaṃ chandasi, Pā. 2-4-76; the augment īṭ by bahulaṃ chandasi, Pā. 7-3-97; aṭ is acute, and the verb keeps its accent because of the connection with yat; mahinā = mahimnā — imanic in the state-sense of the pṛthvādi class, ṭi-loss, the instrumental acute by the rule on the loss of an acute, the loss of m Vedic; amanyamānān — "those who know", root man (4th class) with śyan, initial acute because śyan is nit; the nañ-compound keeps the accent of the indeclinable first member; in the Saṃhitā ru and nasalisation.)

Pratipadārtha — "indra — O Indra; yat — when (tvam — you); ubhe rodasī — both earth and the mid-region; mahinā — by your power; viśvataḥ sīm — pervading all round; pari abubhojīḥ — you enjoyed everything (then); amanyamānān — the sacrificers who merely recite the mantras without knowing (their meaning); abhimanyamānaiḥ — with mantras that hold the conviction 'the performer of the sacrifice who belongs to me must be protected'; dasyum — the thief in the form of Vṛtra; niḥ adhamaḥ — you drove away."

original p. 41

Bhāvārtha — "O Indra, you are all-powerful and the protector of those who depend on you. By your greatness you pervade both the earth and the mid-region, and you enjoy the lordship of both worlds. Pleased with the mantras that praise you, saying of those performers of sacrifice who merely recite the mantras without knowing their meaning 'these are ours; they must be protected', you drove away the robber Vṛtra."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 41) — "Indra, when you surrounded heaven and earth with your greatness simultaneously on all sides, you have blown away the robber ( Vritra ) being pleased with the prayers of those who know how to worship on behalf of those who do not worship."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 41 — sīm: "sīm iti parigrahārthīyo vā padapūraṇo vā (Ni. 1-7, zoom-checked), says Yāska — 'sīm is a word of the sense of "taking all round", or a mere filler of the verse'. That is, one uses the word sīm when one wishes to convey the sense of encompassing, or merely to fill out the foot. Here the bhāṣyakāra has given the sense of encompassing."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 41–42, grammar pages — noted briefly; numerals zoom-checked: abubhojīḥ — root bhuja pālanābhyavahārayoḥ (protecting, eating); laṅ, sip; bahulaṃ chandasi — बहुलं छन्दसि (bahulaṃ chandasi) — Pā. 2-4-76 gives ślu (elision) of the vikaraṇa in the Veda, and by the word bahulam even after roots outside the juhotyādi class, so the śnam is elided here; doubling and the reduplicate operations by ślau; guṇa of the light penultimate: bubhoj + s; bahulaṃ chandasi — Pā. 7-3-97 gives the augment īṭ; aṭ, ru, visarga; the word is connected with yat, so the verb does not lose its accent. — mahinā — = mahimnā; pṛthvādibhya imanij vā — पृथ्वादिभ्य इमनिज्वा (pṛthvādibhya imanij vā) — Pā. 5-1-122 gives imanic optionally in the state- and action-senses after words of the pṛthvādi class: after mahat, imanic; ṭeḥ — टेः (ṭeḥ) — Pā. 6-4-155: before iṣṭhan, imanic, īyasun the ṭi of a bha-stem is dropped, so at goes:

original p. 42

mah + iman = mahiman; the ending ṭā; allopo 'naḥ — अल्लोपोऽनः (allopo 'naḥ) — Pā. 6-4-134 drops the a of an before y-initial or vowel-initial suffixes up to the one that prescribes ka (prāg ivāt kaḥ — प्रागिवात्कः (prāg ivāt kaḥ) — Pā. 5-3-70): mahimnā; the a of imanic, acute by the suffix accent, was dropped, so anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ — अनुदात्तस्य च यत्रोदात्तलोपः (anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ) — Pā. 6-1-161 makes the ending ṭā acute; the m is lost as a Vedic usage. — amanyamānān — manyante jānanti iti manyamānāḥ, "those who know"; root mana jñāne, laṭ, śānac by laṭaḥ śatṛśānacau; divādibhyaḥ śyan — दिवादिभ्यः श्यन् (divādibhyaḥ śyan) — Pā. 3-1-69; man + ya + āna, the augment muk by āne muk: manyamāna; accusative plural manyamānān; in the Saṃhitā dīrghād aṭi samānapāde gives ru for the n, and atrānunāsikaḥ… the nasalisation of the preceding vowel (neither sūtra is numbered in the print). Rik 9 ends here (|| 9 ||).

न ये दि॒वः पृ॑थि॒व्या अन्त॑मा॒पुर्न मा॒याभि॑र्धनदां॒ प॒र्यभू॑वन् । युजं॒ वज्रं॑ वृष॒भश्च॑क्र॒ इन्द्रो॒ निर्ज्योति॑षा॒ तम॑सो॒ गा अ॑दुक्षत् ॥ १० ॥

Pada-pāṭha the first line at the foot of p. 42

युजम् । वज्रम् । वृषभः । चक्रे । इन्द्रः । निः । ज्योतिषा । तमसः । गाः । अधुक्षत् ॥ १० ॥

na | ye | divaḥ | pṛthivyāḥ | antam | āpuḥ | na | māyābhiḥ | dhana-dām | pari-abhūvan || yujam | vajram | vṛṣabhaḥ | cakre | indraḥ | niḥ | jyotiṣā | tamasaḥ | gāḥ | adhukṣat || 10 ||

(The print gives परिऽअभूवन् (pari-abhūvan) as one Pada word. The Pada's last word has dh ("adhukṣat") while the Saṃhitā has "adukṣat"; the bhāṣya explains this below as the Vedic non-application of the bhaṣ substitution in the Saṃhitā.)

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya p. 43, in full; numerals zoom-checked

ये जलविशेषा दिवो द्युलोकात्पृथिव्या अन्तं भूमेः स्थानं नापुर्न प्राप्ताः । मेघरूपमापन्नेन वृत्रेण निरुद्धत्वात् । अत एव भूमिप्राप्त्यभावाद्धनदां धनप्रदां भूमिं मायाभिः सस्योपकारादिभिः कर्मभिर्न पर्यभूवन् । परितो न व्याप्ताः । जलपानसस्याभिवृद्ध्याद्युपकारं न चक्रुरित्यर्थः । तदानीमयमिन्द्रो मेघभेदनाय वज्रं युजं स्वहस्तयुक्तं चक्रे । ततो ज्योतिषा द्योतमानेन वज्रेण तमस अन्धकाररूपान्मेघाद्गा गमनशीलान्युदकानि निरधुक्षत् । निःशेषेण दुग्धवान् । मेघं भित्त्वा जलं वृष्टवानित्यर्थः ॥ दिवः । ऊडिदमिति षष्ठ्या उदात्तत्वम् । आपुः । आप्लृ व्याप्तौ । लिट्युसि रूपम् । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । पर्यभूवन् । अत्रापि यच्छब्दस्यानुषङ्गान्निघाताभावः । युजम् । युजिर् योगे । ऋत्विगित्यादिना क्विन् । अनित्यमागमशासनमिति वचनान्नुमभावः । अधुक्षत् । दुह प्रपूरणे । लुङि शल इगुपधादनिटः क्सः । पा. ३-१-४५ । इति च्लेः क्सादेशः । दादेर्धातोर्घः । पा. ८-२-३२ । इति घत्वम् । एकाचो बश इत्यादिना । पा. ८-३-३७ । भष्भावः । संहितायां भष्भावाभावश्छान्दसः ॥ ॥ २ ॥

ye jalaviśeṣā divo dyulokātpṛthivyā antaṃ bhūmeḥ sthānaṃ nāpurna prāptāḥ | megharūpamāpannena vṛtreṇa niruddhatvāt | ata eva bhūmiprāptyabhāvāddhanadāṃ dhanapradāṃ bhūmiṃ māyābhiḥ sasyopakārādibhiḥ karmabhirna paryabhūvan | parito na vyāptāḥ | jalapānasasyābhivṛddhyādyupakāraṃ na cakrurityarthaḥ | tadānīmayamindro meghabhedanāya vajraṃ yujaṃ svahastayuktaṃ cakre | tato jyotiṣā dyotamānena vajreṇa tamasa andhakārarūpānmeghādgā gamanaśīlānyudakāni niradhukṣat | niḥśeṣeṇa dugdhavān | meghaṃ bhittvā jalaṃ vṛṣṭavānityarthaḥ ‖ divaḥ | ūḍidamiti ṣaṣṭhyā udāttatvam | āpuḥ | āplṛ vyāptau | liṭyusi rūpam | yadvṛttayogādanighātaḥ | paryabhūvan | atrāpi yacchabdasyānuṣaṅgānnighātābhāvaḥ | yujam | yujir yoge | ṛtvigityādinā kvin | anityamāgamaśāsanamiti vacanānnumabhāvaḥ | adhukṣat | duha prapūraṇe | luṅi śala igupadhādaniṭaḥ ksaḥ | pā. 3-1-45 | iti cleḥ ksādeśaḥ | dāderdhātorghaḥ | pā. 8-2-32 | iti ghatvam | ekāco baśa ityādinā | pā. 8-3-37 | bhaṣbhāvaḥ | saṃhitāyāṃ bhaṣbhāvābhāvaśchāndasaḥ ‖ ‖ 2 ‖ As printed: "तमस अन्धकार…" (for तमसोऽन्धकार…); "पा. ८-३-३७" in the bhāṣya [sic: the middle digit is the 3-glyph; the same sūtra is printed 8-2-37 on p. 46; the usual number is 8-2-37]; the closing numeral is printed "॥ २ ॥" [sic, for १०].

Translation: "Those particular waters which did not reach (nāpuḥ) the end, the place, of the earth from the heaven (divaḥ), because they were held back by Vṛtra, who had taken the form of a cloud. For that very reason, since they did not reach the earth, they did not pari-abhūvan — enclose all round — the earth, the dhanadām, giver of wealth, by māyābhiḥ — works helpful to the crops and so on: that is, they did not do the benefit of drinking-water, the increase of the crops, and the like. Then this Indra, for the splitting of the cloud, yujaṃ cakre — took in his own hand — the thunderbolt. Then, with the thunderbolt that shone with light (jyotiṣā), tamasaḥ — from the cloud, which has the nature of darkness — he nir adhukṣat — milked out completely — the gāḥ, the flowing waters: that is, he split the cloud and rained down the water." (The grammatical tail: divaḥ — the genitive acute by ūḍidam…; āpuḥ — root āplṛ, liṭ with us; not unaccented because of yat; paryabhūvan — here too no loss of accent, because the word yat is carried over; yujam — root yujir, kvin by ṛtvig…; no num by "the rule on augments is not universal"; adhukṣat — root duh, luṅ, ksa for cli by Pā. 3-1-45, gh by Pā. 8-2-32, bhaṣ by ekāco baśaḥ…; in the Saṃhitā the absence of bhaṣ is Vedic.)

Pratipadārtha — "ye — (when Vṛtra, in the form of a cloud, had shut up the mid-region) which streams of water; divaḥ — from the mid-region; pṛthivyāḥ — of the earth; antam — the place; na āpuḥ — did not reach (and); dhanadām — the earth that gives wealth; māyābhiḥ — by works that make the crops grow; na paryabhūvan — did not spread and pervade (then); vṛṣabhaḥ — the one who makes the rain fall; indraḥ — Indra; vajram — the thunderbolt-weapon; yujaṃ cakre — took up in his hand; (afterwards) jyotiṣā — with the shining thunderbolt; tamasaḥ — from the dark cloud; gāḥ — those streams of water; niḥ adhukṣat — milked out completely (drove them out)."

original p. 44

Bhāvārtha — "(O Indra, you are the remover of the people's troubles.) Formerly the asura Vṛtra, in the form of a cloud, shut up the whole mid-region. He stopped all the streams of water that would come to the earth from the mid-region. All the crops that give wealth to people perished. There was no water even to drink. Then you took your thunderbolt in your hand. With its radiance you made the stream of water fall from the cloud, dark enough to pervade even the mid-region."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 44) — "When the waters did not descend upon the ends of the earth and did not overspread, with its productions. the wealth-giver ( Indra ) the showerer, grasped his bolt and with its brightness milked out the waters from the darkness." Printed so, with the full stop after "productions"; the better scan reads "productions" clearly — the earlier "produetions" [sic] was a misreading.

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 44 — "Formerly the asura Vṛtra, who was in the form of a cloud, held back the rain that was to fall from the heavenly world (the mid-region) on to the earth; as a result there was no water on the earth, and no crops either, and wealth, food and the like did not arise. Therefore Indra, taking up his shining thunderbolt and striking the asura Vṛtra, caused rain to come on the earth: that is the main idea." — māyābhiḥ = sasyopakāribhiḥ karmabhiḥ: "by works that help the crops to grow. The word māyā has many meanings; we have explained them earlier. Here māyābhiḥ means 'by bold deeds' [Kannada sāsahakṛtyagaḷinda]" the Kannada gloss differs from the bhāṣya's; reported as printed. — gāḥ = gamanaśīlāny udakāni: "waters, water."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 44–46, grammar pages — noted briefly; numerals zoom-checked: divaḥ — after div, the "genitive singular jas" [sic: as printed, for ṅas]; ūḍidampadādyappumraidyubhyaḥ — ऊडिदम्पदाद्यप्पुम्रैद्युभ्यः (ūḍidampadādyappumraidyubhyaḥ) — Pā. 6-1-171: after ūṭ, idam, the substitutes pad etc. prescribed by paddannomās…, ap, pum, rai, div — one-syllabled and final-acute — a non-sarvanāmasthāna ending is acute.

original p. 45

āpuḥ — root āplṛ vyāptau, liṭ, jhi; parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatusus… — Pā. 3-4-82 gives us; doubling; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, applied by resort to the jāti view or by splitting the sūtra (yogavibhāga), drops the p of the reduplicate; savarṇadīrgha; ru, visarga; no total anudātta because of the connection with yat. — paryabhūvan — bhū sattāyām, the preverb pari, luṅ (as printed), third person plural; ye in the first foot is connected with paryabhūvan of the second: "for the reason stated in the first foot, ye na dhanadāṃ māyābhiḥ paryabhūvan" is the construction; so here too, owing to the connection with yat, there is no total anudātta. — yujam — root yujir yoge; ṛtvigdadhṛksragdiguṣṇigañcuyujikruñcāṃ ca — ऋत्विग्दधृक्स्रग्दिगुष्णिगञ्चुयुजिक्रुञ्चां च (ṛtvigdadhṛksragdiguṣṇigañcuyujikruñcāṃ ca) — Pā. 3-2-59: kvin after these roots, some operations coming by nipātana: kvin after yaj with ṛtu as upapada; doubling and final acute for dhṛṣ; kvin in the object-sense and am for sṛj; kvin in the object-sense for diś; kvin after snih with ut, the preverb's last letter dropped and s → ṣ; kvin after añc with a sup-ending upapada; and kvin after yuj without upapada — all established by nipātana. Accusative singular am: yuj + am; yujer asamāse — युजेरसमासे (yujer asamāse) — Pā. 7-1-71 would give num to yuj outside a compound before a sarvanāmasthāna ending, but by the paribhāṣā anityam āgamaśāsanam the num does not come. — adhukṣat — root duha prapūraṇe, luṅ–tip; cli luṅi — च्लि लुङि (cli luṅi) — Pā. 3-1-43; śala igupadhād aniṭaḥ ksaḥ — शल इगुपधादनिटः क्सः (śala igupadhād aniṭaḥ ksaḥ) — Pā. 3-1-45: after a root ending in a śal sound (ś ṣ s h), with i/u/ṛ penultimate and without iṭ, cli is replaced by ksa; the aṭ augment: aduh + sa + t; dāder dhātor ghaḥ — दादेर्धातोर्घः (dāder dhātor ghaḥ) — Pā. 8-2-32, read as dādeḥ dhātoḥ ghaḥ, with hoḍhaḥ bringing down haḥ, and jhali, padasya, ante continued; dādeḥ is repeated (āvṛtti, "saying twice what was said once", as kamalāni kamalāni means "fine lotuses"), so "dādeḥ" means "a root beginning with d at the time of instruction"; some repeat dhātoḥ instead; thus, before a jhal and at the end of a word, the h of a root beginning with d at the time of instruction is replaced by gh

original p. 46

— so gh: adugh + s + t; ekāco baśo bhaṣ jhaṣantasya sadhvoḥ — एकाचो बशो भष् झषन्तस्य स्ध्वोः (ekāco baśo bhaṣ jhaṣantasya sadhvoḥ) — Pā. 8-2-37 (here printed 8-2-37): before s or dhv, and at the end of a word, the baś (b g ḍ d) of a one-vowelled root-part ending in a jhaṣ is replaced by the bhaṣ (bh gh ḍh dh); here s follows, dugh is treated as one-vowelled by vyapadeśivadbhāva, and it ends in a jhaṣ, so its baś d becomes dh: adhugh-s-t; k for gh by cartva; ādeśapratyayayoḥ — आदेशप्रत्यययोः (ādeśapratyayayoḥ) — Pā. 8-3-59 gives ṣ for s: adhukṣat. In the Saṃhitā the bhaṣ change does not come, by Vedic usage, i.e. there is no dh. Rik 10 ends here (|| 10 ||).

आपो जलान्यस्येन्द्रस्य स्वधामन्नं व्रीह्यादिरूपमनुलक्ष्याक्षरन् । मेघाद्वृष्ट्वा अभवन् । तदानीमयं वृत्रो नाव्यानां नावा तरणयोग्यानां बह्वीनामपां मध्ये आ समन्तादवर्धत । वृद्धिं प्राप्तः । प्रभूतजले वर्तमानोऽपि न ममार । किन्त्वभिवृद्ध एव । तदानीमिन्द्रः सध्रीचीनेन सहगच्छता मनसा युक्तं तं वृत्रमोजिष्ठेनातिबलयुक्तेन हन्मना हननसाधनेन वज्रेणाभि द्यून् कतिचिद्दिवसानभिलक्ष्याहन् । तेषु दिवसेषु हतवान् । जलमध्ये पतितस्यापि वृत्रस्य मनो यत्रेन्द्रस्तिष्ठति तत्रैव सह गच्छति तादृशमभिज्ञाय स हतवानित्यर्थः ॥ अक्षरन् । क्षर संचलने । नाव्यानाम् । नावा तार्याणाम् । नौवयोधर्मेत्यादिना । पा. ४-४-९१ । यत् । वान्तो यि प्रत्यये । पा. ६-१-७९ । इत्यावादेशः । अनाव इति पर्युदासात् । पा. ६-१-२१३ । तित्स्वरितमिति प्रत्ययस्य स्वरितत्वम् । सध्रीचीनेन । सहाञ्चतीति सध्र्यङ् । सहस्य सध्रिः । पा. ६-३-९५ । इति सध्र्यादेशः । विभाषाञ्चेरदिक्स्त्रियाम् । पा. ५-४-८ । इति स्वार्थे खप्रत्ययः । तस्यायन्नित्यादिना ईनादेशः । अच इत्यकारलोपे चाविति दीर्घत्वम् । खादेशस्योपदेशिवद्वचनादीकार उदात्तः । ओजिष्ठेन । ओजोऽस्यास्तीत्योजस्वी । अस्मायामेधेति विनिः । तत आतिशायनिक इष्ठन् । विन्मतोर्लुगिति विनो लुक् । टेरिति टिलोपः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । हन्मना । हन्यतेऽनेनेति हन्म । अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्त इति दृशिग्रहणात्करणेऽपि मनिन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । तृतीयैकवचनेऽल्लोपे प्राप्ते न संयोगाद्वमन्तात् । पा. ६-४-१३७ । इति प्रतिषेधः ॥ ॥ ११ ॥

āpo jalānyasyendrasya svadhāmannaṃ vrīhyādirūpamanulakṣyākṣaran | meghādvṛṣṭvā abhavan | tadānīmayaṃ vṛtro nāvyānāṃ nāvā taraṇayogyānāṃ bahvīnāmapāṃ madhye ā samantādavardhata | vṛddhiṃ prāptaḥ | prabhūtajale vartamāno 'pi na mamāra | kintvabhivṛddha eva | tadānīmindraḥ sadhrīcīnena sahagacchatā manasā yuktaṃ taṃ vṛtramojiṣṭhenātibalayuktena hanmanā hananasādhanena vajreṇābhi dyūn katiciddivasānabhilakṣyāhan | teṣu divaseṣu hatavān | jalamadhye patitasyāpi vṛtrasya mano yatrendrastiṣṭhati tatraiva saha gacchati tādṛśamabhijñāya sa hatavānityarthaḥ ‖ akṣaran | kṣara saṃcalane | nāvyānām | nāvā tāryāṇām | nauvayodharmetyādinā | pā. 4-4-91 | yat | vānto yi pratyaye | pā. 6-1-79 | ityāvādeśaḥ | anāva iti paryudāsāt | pā. 6-1-213 | titsvaritamiti pratyayasya svaritatvam | sadhrīcīnena | sahāñcatīti sadhryaṅ | sahasya sadhriḥ | pā. 6-3-95 | iti sadhryādeśaḥ | vibhāṣāñceradikstriyām | pā. 5-4-8 | iti svārthe khapratyayaḥ | tasyāyannityādinā īnādeśaḥ | aca ityakāralope cāviti dīrghatvam | khādeśasyopadeśivadvacanādīkāra udāttaḥ | ojiṣṭhena | ojo 'syāstītyojasvī | asmāyāmedheti viniḥ | tata ātiśāyanika iṣṭhan | vinmatorlugiti vino luk | ṭeriti ṭilopaḥ | nittvādādyudāttatvam | hanmanā | hanyate 'neneti hanma | anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti dṛśigrahaṇātkaraṇe 'pi manin | nittvādādyudāttatvam | tṛtīyaikavacane 'llope prāpte na saṃyogādvamantāt | pā. 6-4-137 | iti pratiṣedhaḥ ‖ ‖ 11 ‖

Translation: "The waters (āpaḥ) of this Indra, having in view svadhām — food, in the form of rice and the like — akṣaran — flowed: having rained from the cloud they came into being. Then this Vṛtra, in the midst of the many waters nāvyānām — fit to be crossed by boat — ā avardhata — grew all round, attained increase; though he was in plenty of water he did not die, but only grew. Then Indra, with hanmanā — the instrument of killing, the thunderbolt — ojiṣṭhena, endowed with the greatest strength, abhi dyūn — having marked out some days — ahan, struck that Vṛtra, joined with a sadhrīcīna mind, one that 'goes along with'; he killed him on those days. The sense is: the mind of Vṛtra, even when he had fallen into the midst of the water, goes along to wherever Indra stands; knowing it to be such, he killed him." (The grammatical tail: akṣaran — root kṣar, to move; nāvyānām — "to be crossed by boat", yat by nauvayodharma…, Pā. 4-4-91; āv by vānto yi pratyaye, Pā. 6-1-79; because of the exclusion "not after nau" (Pā. 6-1-213) no initial acute, and the suffix is svarita by titsvaritam; sadhrīcīnena — sadhryañc, sadhri for saha by Pā. 6-3-95, kha in the self-sense by Pā. 5-4-8, īna for it, loss of a by acaḥ, lengthening by cau, the ī acute because the substitute of kha counts as taught originally; ojiṣṭhena — ojasvin by asmāyāmedhā…, then iṣṭhan of excellence, vin dropped, ṭi dropped, initial acute as nit; hanmanā — manin in the instrument sense also, by the word dṛśi in anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante; initial acute; the loss of a in the instrumental is barred by na saṃyogād vamantāt, Pā. 6-4-137.)

Pratipadārtha — "āpaḥ — water; asya — Indra's; svadhām anu — for the sake of rice and the like, which serve as food; akṣaran — flowed (then); nāvyānām — of streams that can be travelled only by boat (brimming over); madhye — in the midst; avardhata — (Vṛtra) grew on all sides; (then) indraḥ — Indra; sadhrīcīnena — following Indra himself out of hatred; manasā — with a mind; joined; tam — that Vṛtra; ojiṣṭhena — very strong; hanmanā — with the thunderbolt-weapon, the means for killing; abhi dyūn — having watched for some days; ahan — killed."

Bhāvārtha — "In the sacrifice, even while the currents of the rivers flowed so abundantly — for the increase of rice and other grains that please Indra — that one could move about on them only by boat, Vṛtra grew in the midst of those currents.

original p. 48

Then Indra, noting the mind of that one which followed himself, killed that Vṛtra with his strong and destructive thunderbolt."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 48) — "According to his (Indra's) wish the waters flowed to provide food, but the demon (Vritra) grew in strength in the midst of waters so deep as to be navigable. Indra, with his collected wisdom and with his most mighty thunderbolt slew him in the course of time."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), pp. 48–49 — svadhām: "Though Yāska has given two kinds of meaning for the word svadhā — 'water' (Ni. 2 24 as printed [the hyphen is not visible; zoom-checked]) and 'food' (Ni. 3-9, zoom-checked) — the bhāṣyakāra has adopted here only the sense 'food'." — akṣaran = kṣara sañcalane: "movement; here the sense is 'flowing in the form of a stream'." — avardhata: "Though Vṛtra was in the midst of the water (in the circle of the clouds) he did not die; the idea is that he grew more and more and attained prosperity." — nāvyānām = nāvā taraṇayogyānām: "so much water that it can be crossed only by boat or dug-out; i.e. in the midst of abundant water." — sadhrīcīnena = saha gacchatā manasā | samastena buddhicāturyeṇa: "with one-pointedness of mind, i.e. with a mind steadied — fixed on that very thing — a mind fixed on the destruction of the asura Vṛtra, 'with his collected wisdom &c.' [the print's English]. The bhāṣyakāra adds the word yuktam to this word and uses it as an attribute of the asura Vṛtra. That is not quite proper. We give as examples some ṛks in which the word is used —"

सध्रीचीनेन मनसाविवेनन् तमित्सखायं कृणुते समत्सु ॥ (ऋ. सं. ४-२४-६) अस्माभिरिन्द्र सखिभिर्हुवानः सध्रीचीनो मादयस्वा निषद्य ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-११२-३) चक्राथे हि सध्र्य१ङ्नाम भद्रं सध्रीचीना वृत्रहणा उत स्थः ॥ (ऋ. स. १-१०८-३) सध्रीचीना पथ्या३ सा विषूची महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. ३-५५-१५)

ojiṣṭhena — ojo 'syāstīty ojasvī: "endowed with great strength." — hanmanā — hananasādhanena vajreṇa: "with the thunderbolt-weapon, the means for destroying." — abhi dyūn: "observing some days, waiting for the time — such meanings may be given."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 49–51, grammar pages — noted briefly; numerals zoom-checked: nāvyānām — nāvā tāryāḥ nāvyāḥ, teṣām, "fit to be crossed by a boat"; nauvayodharmaviṣamūlamūlasītātulābhyas tāryatulyaprāpyavadhyānāmyasamasamitasaṃmiteṣu — नौवयोधर्मविषमूलमूलसीतातुलाभ्यस्तार्यतुल्यप्राप्यवध्यानाम्यसमसमितसंमितेषु (nauvayodharmaviṣamūlamūlasītātulābhyas tāryatulyaprāpyavadhyānāmyasamasamitasaṃmiteṣu) — Pā. 4-4-91: after nau in the instrumental, yat in the sense "which can be crossed"; after vayas in the instrumental, yat in the sense "equal" (the word is used only of a friend, not of an enemy); likewise after dharma, viṣa, mūla, mūlya, sītā, tulā in the senses prāpya, vadhya, ānāmya, sama, samita, saṃmita: mūla is the capital a merchant invests, ānāmya the share he keeps for himself, i.e. profit; whatever money one gives, so much is "mūlya" in common usage; sītā is the tip of the plough, and "agreeing with it" means levelled, without pits and mounds; saṃmita means well weighed. With yat after nau: nau + ya; vānto yi pratyaye — वान्तो यि प्रत्यये (vānto yi pratyaye) — Pā. 6-1-72 as printed [sic: a flat-footed 7 and a curled 2, zoom-checked; the bhāṣya on p. 47 prints 6-1-79, the usual number] gives av/āv for o/au before a y-initial suffix: āv; yato 'nāvaḥ — यतोऽनावः (yato 'nāvaḥ) — Pā. 6-1-213: a two-vowelled word ending in the suffix yat, not after nau, has initial acute; when the nañ goes with the verb it is a prasajya-pratiṣedha, when with the second member a paryudāsa; since "other than the word nau" is a paryudāsa, no initial acute comes here, and by titsvaritam a svarita comes. — sadhrīcīnena — saha añcati iti sadhryañc; by ṛtvigdadhṛk… kvin after the root añc with a sup-ending upapada; sahasya sadhriḥ — सहस्य सध्रिः (sahasya sadhriḥ) — Pā. 6-3-95: sadhri for saha before añc ending in v-suffix or a suffix that is not heard; sadhri + añc, yaṇ: sadhryañc (the printed p. 50 begins inside this gloss on Pā. 6-3-95);

original p. 50

(sadhrīcīnena, continued) aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti — अनिदितां हल उपधायाः क्ङिति (aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti) — Pā. 6-4-24 drops the n; vibhāṣāñcer adikstriyām — विभाषाञ्चेरदिक्स्त्रियाम् (vibhāṣāñcer adikstriyām) — Pā. 5-4-8: kha optionally in the self-sense after a stem ending in añc, when not denoting a direction and not feminine; āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ… — Pā. 7-1-2 gives īn for it: sadhryac + īna; acaḥ — अचः (acaḥ) — Pā. 6-4-138 drops the a of añc (already without its n), a part of the bha-stem; cau — चौ (cau) — Pā. 6-3-138 lengthens the preceding aṇ before añc thus reduced: sadhrīcīna; by the vārtika āyannādiṣūpadeśivadbhāvo vaktavyaḥ — आयन्नादिषूपदेशिवद्भावो वक्तव्यः (āyannādiṣūpadeśivadbhāvo vaktavyaḥ) — Pā. 7-1-2-1, the īn substitute counts as present at the time of instruction, so the ī is acute by the suffix accent; without this, after the initial acute had come with the naming of the suffix, the substitute coming in the place of an accentless consonant such as kh would be accentless, and a syllable without accent cannot be pronounced; so the undesired accent of anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam would have to come.
