त्रिः । अश्विना । सिन्धुऽभिः । सप्तमातृऽभिः । त्रयः । आऽहावाः । त्रेधा । हविः । कृतम् । तिस्रः । पृथिवीः । उपरि । प्रवा । दिवः । नाकम् । रक्षेथे इति । द्युऽभिः । अक्तुऽभिः । हितम् ॥ ८ ॥

triḥ | aśvinā | sindhu-bhiḥ | saptamātṛ-bhiḥ | trayaḥ | ā-hāvāḥ | tredhā | haviḥ | kṛtam | tisraḥ | pṛthivīḥ | upari | pravā | divaḥ | nākam | rakṣethe iti | dyu-bhiḥ | aktu-bhiḥ | hitam || 8 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya pp. 108–109, in full; numerals zoom-checked

हे अश्विना सप्तमातृभिः । इमं मे गङ्गे । ऋग्वे. १०-७५-५ । इत्यादि मन्त्रोक्ताः सप्तसंख्याका गङ्गाद्या नद्यो मातर उत्पादिका येषां जलविशेषाणां ते सप्तमातरः । तैः सिन्धुभिः स्यन्दनस्वभावैर्जलैर्वसतीवरीनामभिस्त्रिः सोमाभिषवः कृत इति शेषः । तथा चान्यत्र ब्राह्मणे समाम्नातम् । अष्टौ कृत्वोऽभिषुणोति एकादश कृत्वो द्वितीयं द्वादश कृत्वस्तृतीयमिति । तै. सं. ६-४-५-१ । आहावा यथोक्तजलयुक्तस्य सोमस्याधारभूताः कूपसदृशास्त्रयस्त्रिसंख्याका द्रोणकलशाधवनीयपूतभृदाख्या निष्पन्ना इति शेषः । तेषु त्रिषु पात्रविशेषेषु त्रेधा त्रिभिः प्रकारैः सवनत्रयगतैर्हविष्कृतम् । सोमाख्यं हविः संपादितं द्रव्यं वर्तत इति शेषः । तिस्रः पृथिवीरुपरि त्रिभ्यः पृथिव्यादिलोकेभ्य ऊर्ध्वं प्रवा प्रवन्तौ गच्छन्तौ युवां दिवो नाकं द्युलोकसंबन्धिनमादित्यं रक्षेथे । कीदृशं नाकम् । द्युभिरहोभिरक्तुभी रात्रिभिश्च हितं स्थापितम् । अहनि सूर्य उदेति रात्रावस्तं गच्छतीत्येवमहोरात्राभ्यां सूर्यो व्यवस्थाप्यत इत्यर्थः ॥ सप्तमातृभिः । बहुव्रीहिस्वरः । आहावाः । निपानमाहावः । पा. ३-३-७४ । इत्याङ्पूर्वाद्ध्वयतेरप्प्रत्ययः संप्रसारणं वृद्धिश्च निपातनात् । थाथादिनोत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । प्रवा । च्युङ् प्लुङ् गतौ । प्रवेते गच्छत इति प्रवौ । पचाद्यच् । सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । नाकम् । नास्मिन्नकमस्तीति नाकः । नभ्राण्नपादित्यादिना नञः प्रकृतिभावः । द्युभिः । ऊडिदमित्यादिना प्राप्तस्य विभक्त्युदात्तत्वस्य दिवो झल् । पा. ६-१-१८२ । इति प्रतिषेधः ॥

he aśvinā saptamātṛbhiḥ | imaṃ me gaṅge | ṛgve. 10-75-5 | ityādi mantroktāḥ saptasaṃkhyākā gaṅgādyā nadyo mātara utpādikā yeṣāṃ jalaviśeṣāṇāṃ te saptamātaraḥ | taiḥ sindhubhiḥ syandanasvabhāvairjalairvasatīvarīnāmabhistriḥ somābhiṣavaḥ kṛta iti śeṣaḥ | tathā cānyatra brāhmaṇe samāmnātam | aṣṭau kṛtvo 'bhiṣuṇoti ekādaśa kṛtvo dvitīyaṃ dvādaśa kṛtvastṛtīyamiti | tai. saṃ. 6-4-5-1 | āhāvā yathoktajalayuktasya somasyādhārabhūtāḥ kūpasadṛśāstrayastrisaṃkhyākā droṇakalaśādhavanīyapūtabhṛdākhyā niṣpannā iti śeṣaḥ | teṣu triṣu pātraviśeṣeṣu tredhā tribhiḥ prakāraiḥ savanatrayagatairhaviṣkṛtam | somākhyaṃ haviḥ saṃpāditaṃ dravyaṃ vartata iti śeṣaḥ | tisraḥ pṛthivīrupari tribhyaḥ pṛthivyādilokebhya ūrdhvaṃ pravā pravantau gacchantau yuvāṃ divo nākaṃ dyulokasaṃbandhinamādityaṃ rakṣethe | kīdṛśaṃ nākam | dyubhirahobhiraktubhī rātribhiśca hitaṃ sthāpitam | ahani sūrya udeti rātrāvastaṃ gacchatītyevamahorātrābhyāṃ sūryo vyavasthāpyata ityarthaḥ ‖ saptamātṛbhiḥ | bahuvrīhisvaraḥ | āhāvāḥ | nipānamāhāvaḥ | pā. 3-3-74 | ityāṅpūrvāddhvayaterappratyayaḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ vṛddhiśca nipātanāt | thāthādinottarapadāntodāttatvam | pravā | cyuṅ pluṅ gatau | pravete gacchata iti pravau | pacādyac | supāṃ sulugityākāraḥ | nākam | nāsminnakamastīti nākaḥ | nabhrāṇnapādityādinā nañaḥ prakṛtibhāvaḥ | dyubhiḥ | ūḍidamityādinā prāptasya vibhaktyudāttatvasya divo jhal | pā. 6-1-182 | iti pratiṣedhaḥ ‖

(As printed: Ṛg. 10-75-5; Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-5-1; divo jhal printed Pā. 6-1-182 (the last glyph is the looped 2; the grammar on p. 111 prints 6-3-183). The bhāṣya runs onto p. 109 at "नाकं द्युलोकसंबन्धिनम्…".)

Translation: "O Aśvins, saptamātṛbhiḥ — by the seven mothers: the seven rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā named in the mantra 'imaṃ me gaṅge' (Ṛg. 10-75-5), the mothers, the producers of those particular waters. Sindhubhiḥ — with the flowing waters, named vasatīvarī, the soma pressing has been done triḥ, three times (the sentence is to be completed so). And so in another Brāhmaṇa it is handed down: 'Eight times he presses; the second, eleven times; the third, twelve times' (Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-5-1). Āhāvāḥ — [the vessels] that hold the soma with the water so described, like wells, three in number, called droṇakalaśa, ādhavanīya, pūtabhṛt, are ready. In these three particular vessels, tredhā — in three ways, belonging to the three pressings — the oblation (havis) called soma has been made. Tisraḥ pṛthivīḥ upari — above the three worlds, earth and the others — pravā — you two, who go forward — divo nākam — the sun belonging to the heavenly world — rakṣethe protect. What sort of sun? Dyubhiḥ — by days — aktubhiḥ — by nights — hitam, established: the sun rises in the day, goes down at night; so the sun is regulated by day and night."

original p. 109

(The grammatical tail, transcribed above: saptamātṛbhiḥ — bahuvrīhi accent; āhāvāḥ — ap after hve with ā, saṃprasāraṇa and vṛddhi by nipātana in nipānam āhāvaḥ, Pā. 3-3-74; final acute of the later member by thātha…; pravā — root pru "to go", "the two who go", ac of the pacādi class, ā by supāṃ suluk…; nākam — "in which there is no aka (pain)", the nañ kept by nabhrāṇnapāt…; dyubhiḥ — the ending's acute, due by ūḍidam…, barred by divo jhal.)

Pratipadārtha — "aśvinā — O Aśvin deities; saptamātṛbhiḥ — by the seven rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā, which are the sources of streams (the mothers of the flow); sindhubhiḥ — [by those] flowing waters named vasatīvarī; triḥ — [the soma juice has been] pressed three times; āhāvāḥ — [vessels] like the well [for the one who is to drink soma]; trayaḥ — three [vessels called droṇakalaśa, dhavanīya, pūtabhṛt, are ready]; tredhā — in three ways; haviḥ kṛtam — the soma oblation has been prepared; tisraḥ — three; pṛthivīḥ upari — above the earth and the other worlds; pravā — [you two] who travel; dyubhiḥ — by days; aktubhiḥ — by nights; hitam — regulated; divaḥ — of the heavenly world; nākam — the sun; rakṣethe — you protect."

Bhāvārtha — "O Aśvin deities, you travel over the three worlds, protecting the sun of the heavenly world, who is established so as to make day and night. For you we have performed the soma pressing with sacred water brought from the seven rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā. The soma offering has been prepared in the three vessels like wells, droṇakalaśa, dhavanīya and pūtabhṛt. Come and enjoy it."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 109) — "Aswins, thrice the three jars are filled with the seven mothered streams for you and in three ways the oblations is prepared ; rising above the three worlds you keep the [printed as a raised word] sun steady in the sky, who is established for both night and day." Printed so, with "oblations is prepared" [sic].

original p. 110

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), pp. 110–111 - saptamātṛbhiḥ — "in the mantra 'imaṃ me gaṅge' stated in the Ṛgveda (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-75-5) the seven rivers named Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī, Śutudri, Paruṣṇī, Asikni, Marudvṛdhā are addressed here as the seven mothers." - sindhubhiḥ = syandanasvabhāvair jalaiḥ: "by waters." - āhāvāḥ — "the three vessels in which the soma juice is held: droṇakalaśa, dhavanīya, pūtabhṛt. Ordinarily these are made of wood." - divo nākam — "the peak of heaven, the summit of heaven, a very high place in the mid-region. Here the bhāṣyakāra has explained the word nāka as the sun. In regard to the word nāka Yāska says:"

स्वः । पृश्निः । नाकः । गौः । विष्टपम् । नभः ॥ इति षट् साधारणानि दिवश्चादित्यस्य च ॥ (नि. २-१३) नाक आदित्यो भवति । नेता रसान्, नेता भासाम्, ज्योतिषां प्रणयः ॥ (नि. ३-१४)

svaḥ | pṛśniḥ | nākaḥ | gauḥ | viṣṭapam | nabhaḥ || iti ṣaṭ sādhāraṇāni divaś cādityasya ca || (ni. 2-13) nāka ādityo bhavati | netā rasān, netā bhāsām, jyotiṣāṃ praṇayaḥ || (ni. 3-14)

"The six words beginning with svaḥ (among them the word nāka) are words denoting the common senses 'heaven' and 'sun'; and 'nāka is the name of Āditya — because [he is] the leader of the rasa, i.e. of water, who draws water by his rays and makes it fall as rain; or the leader of light, the chief support, who illuminates the whole world through his rays; therefore Sūrya is called nāka'. The expressions divaḥ nākam in this sense occur in many places in the Ṛgveda:"

सहस्रधारेव ते समस्वरन् दिवो नाके मधुजिह्वा असश्चतः ॥ (ऋ. सं. ९-७३-४)

sahasradhāreva te samasvaran divo nāke madhujihvā asaścataḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. 9-73-4)

"and so on: many examples may be given." Untranslated in the source; the gloss, editorial and tentative: "like [a stream] of a thousand streams they sounded together, in the vault of heaven, the honey-tongued, unfailing"; the reference zoom-checked, 9-73-4 replaces 9-62-4. - dyubhiḥ aktubhiḥ — "by days and by nights; this sense [is shown in]:"

द्युभिरक्तुभिः परि पातमस्मानरिष्टेभिरश्विना सौभगेभिः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११२-२५)

original p. 111

वि द्यामेषि रजस्पृथ्वहा मिमानो अक्तुभिः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-५०-७)

dyubhir aktubhiḥ pari pātam asmān ariṣṭebhir aśvinā saubhagebhiḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-25) vi dyām eṣi rajas pṛthv ahā mimāno aktubhiḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. 1-50-7)

"and so on: many examples may be given." My gloss, tentative: "protect us by days and nights, O Aśvins, with unharmed good fortunes"; "you go through heaven, the wide mid-region, measuring out days with nights". Both references zoom-checked.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā p. 111, grammar page — noted briefly; numerals zoom-checked - āhāvāḥ: nipānam āhāvaḥ — निपानमाहावः — Pā. 3-3-74: when the sense "a drinking-place" is meant, the suffix ap after the root hve with the preverb ā, with saṃprasāraṇa (the v becoming u) and vṛddhi, is given by nipātana; ā + hve + a; after saṃprasāraṇa, saṃprasāraṇāc ca — संप्रसारणाच्च (no number printed), the earlier form: ā + hu + a, vṛddhi, āv for au by eco 'yavāyāvaḥ — एचोऽयवायावः (no number printed): ā + hāv + a, āhāva; since the suffix ends in ap, thāthaghañktājabitrakāṇām — थाथघञ्क्ताजबित्रकाणाम् — Pā. 6-2-144: a word ending in a suffix tha, āth, ghañ, kta, ac, ap or itra, standing after a gati or a kāraka, is final-acute. - pravā: root cyuṅ plugṅ gatau; pravete = gacchataḥ "the two who go"; the suffix ac of the pacādi group by nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ — Pā. 3-1-134; guṇa, āv-substitution; the dual au replaced by ā by supāṃ sulug…; savarṇadīrgha; single-substitute accent. - nākam: na akam asminn iti nākam: ka is happiness, āka = unhappiness (duḥkha); the place without unhappiness is nāka. The n of the nañ would be lost by nalopo nañaḥ; but prakṛtibhāva is specially laid down by nabhrāṇnapānnavedānāsatyānamucinakulanakhanapuṃsakanakṣatranakranāsikāsu prakṛtyā — Pā. 6-3-75 (the print's abridgement "nabhrāṇ… nakranākeṣu prakṛtyā") — so the n is not lost. - dyubhiḥ: after div, bhis; diva ut — दिव उत् (diva ut) — Pā. 6-1-131: in the pada-final case the last letter of div becomes u; so v → u; yaṇ; anudāttau suppitau — अनुदात्तौ सुप्पितौ (no number printed) would make the ending unaccented; this is overridden by ūḍidaṃ… (the print opens "(Pā. Sū." but gives no number), which would make the ending after div acute; but divo jhal — दिवो झल् — Pā. 6-3-183 as printed [sic: for 6-1-183; the bhāṣya prints 6-1-182] prohibits acute for a jhal-initial ending after div; hence, by anudāttau suppitau, the ending remains unaccented. Rik 8 ends here (|| 8 ||); a tailpiece ornament follows. This is the first of the two Triṣṭup ṛks of the sūkta, per the introduction on p. 71.

original pp. 112–116

Rik 9

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

क्व१ त्री च॒क्रा त्रि॒वृतो॒ रथ॑स्य॒ क्व१ त्रयो॑ व॒न्धुरो॒ ये सनी॑ळाः । क॒दा योगो॑ वा॒जिनो॒ रास॑भस्य॒ येन॑ य॒ज्ञं नास॑त्योपया॒थः ॥ ९ ॥ [accent ?]

kva1 trī cakrā́ trivṛ́to ráthasya kvá1 tráyo vandhúro yé sánīḷāḥ | kadā́ yógo vājíno rā́sabhasya yéna yajñáṃ nā́satyopayātháḥ || 9 || [accent ?]

(As printed: after each kva stands the numeral ೧ (the Saṃhitā's sign for the independent svarita), with a svarita stroke above and an underline below it; the accent of kva is therefore not split onto the IAST letters. In line 1 the print shows no underline under ತ್ರಿ of trivṛto and no stroke over trayo: the marks given there follow the print where seen, [accent ?] for the rest of the line's marks as a whole; no underline is visible under the ಯೋ of yogo.)

Pada-pāṭha

क्व । त्री । चक्रा । त्रिऽवृतः । रथस्य । क्व । त्रयः । वन्धुरः । ये । सऽनीळाः । कदा । योगः । वाजिनः । रासभस्य । येन । यज्ञम् । नासत्या । उपऽयाथः ॥ ९ ॥

kva | trī | cakrā | tri-vṛtaḥ | rathasya | kva | trayaḥ | vandhuraḥ | ye | sa-nīḷāḥ | kadā | yogaḥ | vājinaḥ | rāsabhasya | yena | yajñam | nāsatyā | upa-yāthaḥ || 9 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya pp. 112–113, in full

हे नासत्यावश्विनौ त्रिवृतस्त्रिसंख्याकैरश्रिभिरुपेतस्य भवदीयस्य रथस्य । ईषाद्वयं पूर्वभागे संयुज्यते । सेयमेकाश्रिः । पृष्ठभागे वियुज्यते । तत्र कोणद्वयं संपद्यते । ईदृशस्य रथस्य संबन्धीनि त्री चक्रा त्रीणि चक्राणि क्व । कुत्र स्थितानीत्यस्माभिर्न दृश्यते । ये काष्ठविशेषाः सनीळाः । नीळं गृहसदृशं रथस्योपर्युपवेशस्थानम् । तेन सह वर्तन्त इति सनीळास्ते काष्ठविशेषा वन्धुरो नीडबन्धनाधारभूतास्त्रयोऽक्षेण सहिते द्वे ईषे इत्येवं त्रिसंख्याकाः क्व । कुत्र स्थिता इत्यस्माभिर्न ज्ञायते । वाजिनो बलवतो रासभस्य भवदीयाश्वस्थानीयस्य गर्दभस्य योगो रथे योजनं कदा । कस्मिन्काले निष्पन्नमित्यस्माभिर्न दृश्यते । येन चक्रत्रयनीडकाष्ठत्रयरासभयोजनसहितेन रथेन यज्ञमस्मदीयं यागस्थानमुपयाथो युवां प्राप्नुथः । तादृशस्य रथस्येति पूर्वत्रान्वयः ॥ त्री चक्रा । उभयत्रापि शेश्छन्दसि बहुलमिति शेर्लोपः । वन्धुरः । बन्धेरौणादिक उरप्रत्ययः । वत्वं छान्दसम् । स नीळाः । वोपसर्जनस्येति सभावः ॥

he nāsatyāvaśvinau trivṛtastrisaṃkhyākairaśribhirupetasya bhavadīyasya rathasya | īṣādvayaṃ pūrvabhāge saṃyujyate | seyamekāśriḥ | pṛṣṭhabhāge viyujyate | tatra koṇadvayaṃ saṃpadyate | īdṛśasya rathasya saṃbandhīni trī cakrā trīṇi cakrāṇi kva | kutra sthitānītyasmābhirna dṛśyate | ye kāṣṭhaviśeṣāḥ sanīḷāḥ | nīḷaṃ gṛhasadṛśaṃ rathasyoparyupaveśasthānam | tena saha vartanta iti sanīḷāste kāṣṭhaviśeṣā vandhuro nīḍabandhanādhārabhūtāstrayo 'kṣeṇa sahite dve īṣe ityevaṃ trisaṃkhyākāḥ kva | kutra sthitā ityasmābhirna jñāyate | vājino balavato rāsabhasya bhavadīyāśvasthānīyasya gardabhasya yogo rathe yojanaṃ kadā | kasminkāle niṣpannamityasmābhirna dṛśyate | yena cakratrayanīḍakāṣṭhatrayarāsabhayojanasahitena rathena yajñamasmadīyaṃ yāgasthānamupayātho yuvāṃ prāpnuthaḥ | tādṛśasya rathasyeti pūrvatrānvayaḥ ‖ trī cakrā | ubhayatrāpi śeśchandasi bahulamiti śerlopaḥ | vandhuraḥ | bandherauṇādika urapratyayaḥ | vatvaṃ chāndasam | sa nīḷāḥ | vopasarjanasyeti sabhāvaḥ ‖

(As printed: "वन्धुरो नीडबन्धन…" with ड, "स नीळाः" divided in the tail. The bhāṣya runs onto p. 113 at "…चक्रत्रयनीडकाष्ठत्रय…".)

Translation: "O Nāsatyas, Aśvins: of your chariot, which is trivṛt — furnished with three corners (aśri): the two shafts (īṣā) are joined at the front, and that [junction] is one corner; at the back they are separated, and there two corners are formed — of such a chariot, trī cakrā — the three wheels — where are they? Where they stand we cannot see. Those particular timbers sanīḷāḥ — [the nīḷa is the seat on the chariot, like a house, for sitting in] — those timbers which go with the nīḷa, vandhuraḥ, the supports for the fastening of the seat, three in number [two shafts with the axle, as I read]: where are they? We do not know where they stand. Vājinaḥ rāsabhasya — of your strong ass, standing in the place of a horse — yogaḥ, the yoking to the chariot: when? At what time it has been done we do not see. By that chariot — furnished with three wheels, three timbers for the seat, and the yoking of the ass — yajñam, our sacrifice, upayāthaḥ — you two reach our place of yoking [= arrival]: of such a chariot — the connection with what went before."

original p. 113

(The grammatical tail: trī cakrā — in both words the śi is dropped by śeś chandasi bahulam; vandhuraḥ — the Uṇādi suffix ura after bandh, the v Vedic; sanīḷāḥ — sa for saha by vopasarjanasya.)

Pratipadārtha — "nāsatyā — O Aśvin deities; yena — by which chariot; yajñam — to our place of sacrifice; upayāthaḥ — you come and arrive; trivṛtaḥ — [furnished] with three corners, triangular, of wood; rathasya — of the chariot; trī cakrā — three wheels; kva — where? ye — which timbers; sanīḷāḥ — with the seat, like a house, for sitting; vandhuraḥ — the supports for building [the seat]; trayaḥ — three [two shafts and one axle]; kva — where? (We do not see these); vājinaḥ — of the strong; rāsabhasya — [instead of a horse] of the ass; kadā — at what time; yogaḥ — [the ass] is yoked to your chariot (this we do not know)."

Bhāvārtha — "O Aśvin deities, we do not see any of the parts of your chariot. Where are the three wheels of your chariot, which is triangular with three corners? The two shafts and the axle, the supports for building the seat in the chariot where one sits as in a house: where are they? And at what time do you yoke your strong ass in place of a horse to your chariot? That also we do not know. We know only that you come in that chariot to our sacrificial place."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 113) — "Where are the wheels of the triangular car ? Where are the three beams with seats on them? when will you harness your powerful donkey (ass) to that car that you may come to this sacrifice.?" The better scan reads "sacrifice" — the earlier "sicrifice" [sic] was a misreading of the old scan; the stray full stop before the question mark is printed.

original p. 114

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), pp. 114–115

"In this mantra the ṛṣi has asked three questions: where are the three wheels of your chariot? where are the corners? when do you yoke the ass (in place of a horse) to your chariot? Though we do not know any of these, he prays that you sit in your chariot and come to our sacrificial ground."

  • trivṛtaḥ = trisaṃkhyākair aśribhir upetasya rathasya: "of a chariot furnished with three corners: with three-cornered, i.e. having three corners, a trangular cart [sic, the print's English]. It is said in the Veda that the chariot of the Aśvins is of this kind. The bhāṣyakāra has explained these three corners thus: 'īṣādvayaṃ pūrvabhāge saṃyujyate | seyam ekāśriḥ | pṛṣṭhabhāge viyujyate | tatra koṇadvayaṃ sampadyate | īdṛśasya rathasya sambandhīni trīṇi cakrāṇi kva ||' Here 'triangular' means: two upright pieces of timber (beams, in the print's English) are joined at the front, and that makes one corner; behind, another timber joins the ends of those two beams, and at the back there are two corners, at the two ends. In all, the three timbers make three corners. Three sides (beams) of the triangle form the three angles [the print's English]. Near each angle is one wheel below it, so that the chariot has three wheels in all. In the middle of these three wheels there is a seat-place called nīḷa, on which the Aśvins sit."

  • vandhuraḥ = "the seat of a chariot; the place for sitting in a chariot: seat in the chariot [the print's English]. In general the seat in the Aśvins' chariot is called tri-vandhura. Though the word in this ṛk is vandhura, the sense of tri-vandhura must be given. For examples we give here one or two ṛks that contain this word or the word tri-vandhura:"

अधि वां स्थाम वन्धुरे रथे दस्रा हिरण्यये ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१३९-४) यत्सीमञ्जन्ति पूर्व्यं हविर्भिरा वन्धुरेव तस्थतुर्दुरोणे ॥ (ऋ. सं. ३-१४-३) त्रिवन्धुरेण त्रिवृता सुपेशसा रथेना यातमश्विना ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१४७-३) त्रिवन्धुरेण त्रिवृता रथेन त्रिचक्रेण सुवृता यातमर्वाक् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११८-२)

adhi vāṃ sthāma vandhure rathe dasrā hiraṇyaye ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-139-4) yatsīmañjanti pūrvyaṃ havirbhirā vandhureva tasthaturduroṇe ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 3-14-3) trivandhureṇa trivṛtā supeśasā rathenā yātamaśvinā ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-147-3) trivandhureṇa trivṛtā rathena tricakreṇa suvṛtā yātamarvāk ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-118-2)

त्रिवन्धुरो मघवा विश्वसौभगः शं न आ वक्षद्द्विपदे चतुष्पदे ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१५७-३) स पप्रथानो अभि पञ्च भूमा त्रिवन्धुरो मनसा यातु युक्तः ॥ (ऋ. सं. ७-६९-२) रथो यो वां त्रिवन्धुरो हिरण्याभीशुरश्विना ॥ (ऋ. सं. ८-२२-५)

trivandhuro maghavā viśvasaubhagaḥ śaṃ na ā vakṣaddvipade catuṣpade ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-157-3) sa paprathāno abhi pañca bhūmā trivandhuro manasā yātu yuktaḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 7-69-2) ratho yo vāṃ trivandhuro hiraṇyābhīśuraśvinā ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 8-22-5)

"In many ṛks such as these the words vandhura and tri-vandhura are used. Though the word vandhura is used with reference to any deity, the word tri-vandhura is used only with reference to the Aśvin deities." All seven references zoom-checked. 1-147-3 is as printed (its middle-last glyph is the flat-footed 7); the others are as printed. The source leaves these ṛks untranslated. My glosses, editorial and tentative: "may we mount your seat, the golden chariot, O Dasras"; "whom they anoint, the ancient one, with oblations; the two stood as on a chariot-seat in the house"; "with the three-seated, three-cornered, well-shaped chariot come, O Aśvins"; "with the three-seated, three-cornered, three-wheeled, well-rolling chariot come hither"; "the three-seated, bountiful [chariot], of all good fortune, would bring us welfare for biped and quadruped"; "spreading over the five lands, the three-seated [chariot], yoked by thought, shall come"; "the three-seated chariot of yours, with golden reins, O Aśvins".

  • yogaḥ — "connection, joining, yoking; here the sense is yoking the horse (the ass) to the chariot."
  • vājino rāsabhasya — "vāji means horse; rāsabhasya means ass. Here the words vājino rāsabhasya mean yoking an ass in the place of yoking a horse to the chariot. It is the general convention (rūḍhi) that an ass is yoked to the chariot of the Aśvin deities. On this subject —"

तद्रासभो नासत्या सहस्रमाजा यमस्य प्रधने जिगाय ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११६-२) हरी ते युञ्जा पृषती अभूतामुपास्थाद्वाजी धुरि रासभस्य । (ऋ. सं. १-१६२-२१) यत्रा रथस्य बृहतो निधानं विमोचनं वाजिनो रासभस्य ॥ (ऋ. सं. ३-५३-५)

tadrāsabho nāsatyā sahasramājā yamasya pradhane jigāya ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-2) harī te yuñjā pṛṣatī abhūtāmupāsthādvājī dhuri rāsabhasya | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-162-21) yatrā rathasya bṛhato nidhānaṃ vimocanaṃ vājino rāsabhasya ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 3-53-5)

"— in ṛks such as these, and further in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā 4-2-1 [the middle glyph is a flat 2/7; read 2], the Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa 18-1, and the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 6-1-1-11; 6-3-1-23; 6-3-2-3; 6-4-4-3 and other mantras, the word rāsabha is used in the singular, so it becomes clear that the horse of the chariot of the Aśvin deities is a single ass." References zoom-checked. The source leaves the ṛks untranslated. My glosses, editorial and tentative: "then the ass, O Nāsatyas, won a thousand in the race, in Yama's contest"; "your two bays were yoked, the dappled ones; the swift one stood at the pole of the ass"; "where is the resting-place of the great chariot, the unyoking of the swift ass"; "yoke the ass to the strong-limbed chariot, O possessors of virile wealth".

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā p. 116, grammar page — noted briefly; numerals zoom-checked: - kva — kimo 't — किमोऽत् (kimo 't) — Pā. 5-3-12: after kim in the locative the suffix at; this is a prāgdiśīya suffix: those from prāg diśo vibhaktiḥ — प्राग्दिशो विभक्तिः (prāg diśo vibhaktiḥ) — Pā. 5-3-1 up to the sūtra dikśabdebhyaḥ… — Pā. 5-3-27 have the name vibhakti, so at is a vibhakti. Then by na vibhaktau tusmāḥ — न विभक्तौ तुस्माः (na vibhaktau tusmāḥ) — Pā. 1-3-4 the t-class, s and m in a vibhakti are not it, so the ban on it-status would apply; but because in idamas thamuḥ — इदमस्थमुः (idamas thamuḥ) — Pā. 5-324 as printed [for 5-3-24] the suffix is taught as thamu, though na vibhaktau would already keep its m from being it, the u added to prevent it-status is pointless and so shows that na vibhaktau is not constant; hence here the t is it and is dropped and a remains: kim + a; kv āti — क्वाति (kv āti) — Pā. 7-2-105: before the suffix at, kva replaces kim: kva + a; titsvaritam — तित्स्वरितम् (titsvaritam) — Pā. 6-1-185: a suffix with the marker t is svarita, so the a is svarita; ato guṇe gives pararūpa, and by sthānivadbhāva it stays svarita. - trī, cakrā — after tri and cakra, jas; jaśśasoḥ śiḥ gives śi; śi sarvanāmasthānam — शि सर्वनामस्थानम् (śi sarvanāmasthānam) — Pā. 1-1-42 gives it the sarvanāmasthāna name; napuṃsakasya jhalacaḥ gives num; sarvanāmasthāne ca… lengthens the penultimate; śeś chandasi bahulam — Pā. 6-1-70 drops the śi in the Veda; nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya drops the n. - vandhuraḥ — bandha bandhane, a kryādi root; after it the Uṇādi suffix ura; v for b by Vedic usage. - sanīḷāḥ — nīḷena saha vartante; tena saheti tulyayoge — तेन सहेति तुल्ययोगे (tena saheti tulyayoge) — Pā. 2-2-28: a bahuvrīhi; nīḷa is the seat on the chariot; vopasarjanasya — वोपसर्जनस्य (vopasarjanasya) — Pā. 6-3-82: in a bahuvrīhi sa replaces saha. Rik 9 ends here (|| 9 ||); a tailpiece ornament closes p. 116.

Rik 10

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

आ ना॑सत्या॒ गच्छ॑तं हू॒यते॑ ह॒विर्मध्वः॑ पिबतं मधु॒पेभि॑रा॒सभिः॑ । यु॒वोर्हि पूर्वं॑ सवि॒तोषसो॒ रथ॑मृ॒ताय॑ चि॒त्रं घृ॒तवं॑त॒मिष्य॑ति ॥ १० ॥

ā́ nāsatyā gácchataṃ hūyáte havír mádhvaḥ pibataṃ madhupébhir āsábhiḥ | yuvór hi pū́rvaṃ savitóṣaso rátham ṛtā́ya citráṃ ghṛtávaṃtam íṣyati || 10 ||

Pada-pāṭha

आ । नासत्या । गच्छतम् । हूयते । हविः । मध्वः । पिबतम् । मधुऽपेभिः । आसऽभिः ॥ युवोः । हि । पूर्वम् । सविता । उषसः । रथम् । ऋताय । चित्रम् । घृतऽवन्तम् । इष्यति ॥ १० ॥

ā | nāsatyā | gacchatam | hūyate | haviḥ | madhvaḥ | pibatam | madhu-pebhiḥ | āsa-bhiḥ || yuvoḥ | hi | pūrvam | savitā | uṣasaḥ | ratham | ṛtāya | citram | ghṛtavantam | iṣyati || 10 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya the first half, to the point where the leaf ends; the rest follows on p. 118

हे नासत्यावश्विनाविह कर्मण्या गच्छतम् । अत्रास्माभिर्हविर्हूयते । युवां च मधुपेभिर्मधुरद्रव्यपानयुक्तैरासभिर्भवदीयैरास्यैर्मध्वो मधुरद्रव्याणि हवींषि पिबतम् । सविता सूर्य उषसः पूर्वमुषःकालात्पुरा युवयोरश्विनोः सम्बन्धिनं रथमृतायास्मद्यज्ञार्थमिष्यति हि । प्रेरयति खलु । कीदृशम् । चित्रं पूर्वोक्तैश्चक्रत्रयादिभिर्विचित्रं घृतवन्तमक्षाञ्जनसाधनेन घृतेनोपेतम् ॥ [grammar of gacchatam, pibatam, hūyate, madhvaḥ, madhupebhiḥ, āsabhiḥ begins at the foot of p. 117 and continues on p. 118]

he nāsatyāv aśvināv iha karmaṇyā gacchatam | atrāsmābhir havir hūyate | yuvāṃ ca madhupebhir madhuradravyapānayuktair āsabhir bhavadīyair āsyair madhvo madhuradravyāṇi havīṃṣi pibatam | savitā sūrya uṣasaḥ pūrvam uṣaḥkālāt purā yuvayor aśvinoḥ sambandhinaṃ ratham ṛtāyāsmadyajñārtham iṣyati hi | prerayati khalu | kīdṛśam | citraṃ pūrvoktaiś cakratrayādibhir vicitraṃ ghṛtavantam akṣāñjanasādhanena ghṛtenopetam ||

Translation: "O Nāsatyas, Aśvins, come iha karmaṇi — to this rite. Here, by us, the oblation is poured. And you two, with your mouths madhupebhiḥ āsabhiḥ — mouths that drink sweet substances (madhuradravya) — madhvaḥ pibatam — drink the sweet oblations. Savitā, the sun, before the dawn (uṣasaḥ pūrvam) iṣyati — sends — your chariot, the Aśvins' chariot, ṛtāya, for the sake of our sacrifice. What sort? Citram — variegated (vicitram) by the wheels and so forth described before; ghṛtavantam — furnished with ghṛta, ghee, the means of greasing the axle [as I read akṣāñjana-; the print is clear enough on the other words]."

Rik 10 — end of the bhāṣya grammar, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, English, Special Topics, grammar (pp. 118–120, PDF 132–134)

End of the grammar within the bhāṣya characterized: yuvoḥ — "explained already under yuvor hi yantram" (Rik 1); iṣyati — root iṣa gatau; śyan is nit, so the root's first syllable is acute, and hi ca (no sūtra number printed in the bhāṣya) bars the lowering of the verb after hi.

Pratipadārtha — "nāsatyā — O Aśvin deities (come here for the sake of our sacrifice); āgacchatam — graciously come; haviḥ — the oblation; hūyate — is being offered; madhupebhiḥ — [with mouths] able to drink sweet liquid (able to enjoy tasting it); āsabhiḥ — with mouths; madhvaḥ — our sweet oblations; pibatam — drink; savitā — the Sun; uṣasaḥ pūrvam — before the dawn-time; yuvoḥ — your; citram — wonderful (by its three wheels and other extraordinary parts); ghṛtavantam — furnished with oil (to be put into the hole that holds the axle-rod, so that the wheels turn well); ratham — chariot; ṛtāya — for our sacrifice (for your coming to our sacrifice); iṣyati hi — sends, does he not?"

Bhāvārtha — "O Aśvin deities, kindly come to our sacrifice; we offer you sweet oblations. Drink this oblation with your mouths that are always drinking sweet liquid. For this very purpose Sūrya sends your chariot to you even before the dawn. That chariot is furnished with the three wheels and other wonderful parts, and with the oil that lets the wheels turn smoothly."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 118) — "Nasatyas, come to the sacrifice ; the oblation is offered ; drink the soma juice with your mouths relishing its sweet savour ; before the dawn Savitri ( Sun ) sends forth your wonderful and well-oiled chariot to the sacrifice" .

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), pp. 118–119 - pūrvaṃ uṣasaḥ — "before the dawn-time: that is, in the sacrifice, after midnight until the dawn-time they recite the Āśvina-kratu hymns during the recitation of the prātaranuvāka mantras. The ṛṣi prays that [the Aśvins] come to the sacrificial ground at the time those mantras are being recited, before the dawn, in order to receive them." - ṛtāya = yajñāya: "Yāska explains the word ṛta as satyaṃ vā yajñaṃ vā (Ni. 4-19) — 'truth or sacrifice'; here the sense 'sacrifice' is given." - citram = pūrvoktaiś cakratrayādibhiś citram: "a wonderful chariot with the three wheels and the rest as described before. Ordinarily a chariot has four wheels, and the chariot is square; but the Aśvins' chariot is triangular and has three wheels, so it is not an ordinary chariot but a wonderful one." - ghṛtavantam = akṣāñjanasādhanena ghṛtenopetam: "so that the wheels turn properly, it is the custom to put grease in the axle-hole and in the hole between the wheels. In the same way, here, it is a chariot in which, in place of grease, ghee has been applied to the axles and the wheels turn smoothly."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 119–120, PDF 133–134 — grammar pages, noted briefly - gacchatam (p. 119): root gamḷ gatau; loṭ, second-person dual thas, replaced by tam by tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ — तस्थस्थमिपां तांतंतामः — (Pā. 3-4-101); gam + tam, śap; iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ — इषुगमियमां छः — (Pā. 7-3-77) gives ch for the m; tuk by che ca — छे च (che ca) — (Pā. 6-1-73); ścutva, stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ — स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः — (Pā. 8-4-40) giving cch; the loṭ-substitute tam is lasārvadhātuka and stands after śap, which is anupadeśa; tiṅ is accented [anudātta] by tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāt… (Pā. 6-1-186), and the root's accent remains. The page goes on to explain that the meaning "come to the sacrifice and drink the oblation" calls for the particle ca to be understood after āgacchatam, "nāsatyā āgacchataṃ pibatam ca"; since the word ca is not actually used, cādilope vibhāṣā — चादिलोपे विभाषा — (Pā. 8-1-63) is applied: when ca, vā, ha, aha, eva are dropped, the verb standing first in the sentence [gacchatam] does not become sarvānudātta; the sūtra's sense is that the grammar does not itself prescribe the dropping of cādi words, but where the sense of ca is felt from the context and the word is not used, it must be understood that it has been dropped. - hūyate (p. 119 end – p. 120): root hve̐ śabde, laṭ in the passive; laṭ is replaced by ta, with ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere — टित आत्मनेपदानां टेरे — (no number printed) giving e for the ṭi of the ending; hve + ya + te; sārvadhātuke yak — सार्वधातुके यक् — (Pā. 3-1-67) gives yak in the passive; vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti — वचिस्वपियजादीनां किति — (Pā. 6-1-15) gives saṃprasāraṇa, whence hu + ya + te; halaś ca — हलश्च — (Pā. 3-4-2, as printed; the lengthening rule halaḥ is Pā. 6-4-2) lengthens the vowel of a base that has saṃprasāraṇa before a final consonant-group; hūyate; the te is lasārvadhātuka and unaccented by tāsyanudāttenṅid…; the yak suffix makes the accent fall on its own ya [as the print says, yak is kit: yakpratyayasvareṇa udāttaḥ]. - madhvaḥ (p. 120): "madhu is derived, as I said before, by the Uṇādi sūtra phalipāṭi… (no number printed here); the word is neuter, but here it is used as masculine by vyatyaya: śas of the second case plural, madhu + as; by rule prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ — प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः — (Pā. 6-1-102) the long vowel of the first should result, but by Vedic usage here yaṇādeśa comes: madhvaḥ." - madhupebhiḥ: madhu pibantīti madhupāḥ, taiḥ; root pā pāne; with madhu as upapada the suffix ka after a root ending in ā, ātoʼnupasarge kaḥ — आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः — (Pā. 3-2-3); ātolopa iṭi ca — Pā. 6-4-64: loss of ā; pa is acute by the suffix-accent. - āsabhiḥ: after āsya, bhis; pad-dan-no-māsa-hṛn-niśa-…-śas-prabhṛtiṣu — पद्दन्नोमास्हृन्निशसन्… — (Pā. 6-1-63): āsan replaces āsya; n lost by na lopaḥ prātipadikāntasya — न लोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य — (Pā. 8-2-7). - yuvoḥ: "explained under yuvor hi yantram (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-34-1)". - iṣyati: root iṣa gatau, divādi; laṭ, tip; divādibhyaḥ śyan; śyan is nit, so hi ca — हि च (hi ca) — (Pā. 8-1-34) prevents the loss of accent and ñnityādir nityam — ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यम् — (Pā. 6-1-197) makes the first syllable acute. Rik 10 ends here (|| 10 ||).

original pp. 120–124

Rik 11

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

आ ना॑सत्या त्रि॒भिरे॑काद॒शैरि॒ह दे॒वेभि॑र्यातं मधु॒पेय॑मश्विना । प्रायु॒स्तारि॑ष्टं॒ नी रपां॑सि मृक्षतं॒ सेध॑तं॒ द्वेषो॒ भव॑तं सचा॒भुवा॑ ॥ ११ ॥

ā́ nāsatyā tribhír ekādaśáir ihá devébhir yātaṃ madhupéyam aśvinā | prāyus tā́riṣṭaṃ nī́ rápāṃsi mṛkṣataṃ sédhataṃ dvéṣo bhávataṃ sacābhúvā || 11 ||

Pada-pāṭha

आ । नासत्या । त्रिऽभिः । एकादशैः । इह । देवेभिः । यातम् । मधुऽपेयम् । अश्विना ॥ प्र । आयुः । तारिष्टम् । निः । रपांसि । मृक्षतम् । सेधतम् । द्वेषः । भवतम् । सचाऽभुवा ॥ ११ ॥

ā | nāsatyā | tri-bhiḥ | ekādaśaiḥ | iha | devebhiḥ | yātam | madhu-peyam | aśvinā || pra | āyuḥ | tāriṣṭam | niḥ | rapāṃsi | mṛkṣatam | sedhatam | dveṣaḥ | bhavatam | sacā-bhuvā || 11 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya the first half in full, the grammatical tail characterized; where the print is crowded [?] is marked

हे नासत्या असत्येनानृतेन रहिताव् अश्विनौ देवौ युवां त्रिभिरेकादशैः । ये देवासो दिव्येकादश स्थ । ऋग्वे. १-१३९-११ । इत्यादिमन्त्रप्रतिपादितैस्त्रिसंख्याकैरेकादशात्मकैर्वर्गत्रयगतैर्देवैः सह मधुपेयं सोमात्मकं मधुरद्रव्यपानमभिलक्ष्येहास्मिन्देवयजनदेश आ यातम् । आगच्छतम् । आयुरस्मदीयमायुष्यं प्रतारिष्टम् । प्रवर्धयतम् । रपांस्यस्मदीयानि पापानि निर्मृक्षतम् । निःशेषेण शोधयतम् । द्वेषो द्वेषकर्तॄन् सेधतम् । प्रतिषेधतम् । सचाभुवा अस्माभिः सहावस्थितौ भवतम् ॥

he nāsatyā asatyenānṛtena rahitāv aśvinau devau yuvāṃ tribhir ekādaśaiḥ | ye devāso divy ekādaśa stha | ṛgve. 1-139-11 | ity ādimantrapratipāditais trisaṃkhyākair ekādaśātmakair vargatrayagatair devaiḥ saha madhupeyaṃ somātmakaṃ madhuradravyapānam abhilakṣyehāsmin devayajanadeśa ā yātam | āgacchatam | āyur asmadīyam āyuṣyaṃ pratāriṣṭam | pravardhayatam | rapāṃsy asmadīyāni pāpāni nirmṛkṣatam | niḥśeṣeṇa śodhayatam | dveṣo dveṣakartṝn sedhatam | pratiṣedhatam | sacābhuvā asmābhiḥ sahāvasthitau bhavatam ||

Translation: "O Nāsatyas, Aśvins, free of falsehood and untruth: with tribhir ekādaśaiḥ — the three elevens: 'you gods who are eleven in heaven' (Ṛg. 1-139-11) and so on in the mantras — the gods of three groups, each of eleven, come, together with them, iha, here, to this place of the worship of the gods (devayajana), with a view to the madhupeya — the drinking of the sweet substance, soma. Āyuḥ — our lifetime — pra tāriṣṭam — extend. Rapāṃsi — our sins — nir mṛkṣatam — cleanse completely. Dveṣaḥ — those who hate — sedhatam — ward off. Sacābhuvā — be together with us."

Grammar within the bhāṣya pp. 121–122, characterized: tribhiḥ, ekādaśaiḥ (ekādaśānāṃ pūraṇaiḥ, the suffix ḍaṭ in the ordinal sense, tasya pūraṇe ḍaṭ [Pā. 5-2-48]); madhupeyam (root pā, yat after a vowel-final root, ac-ending roots by aco yat [no number printed in the bhāṣya], ī for ā by īdyati [Pā. 6-4-65], yato nāvaḥ initial-acute rule, the compound madhu ca tat peyam ca, accent of the later member of a kṛt-compound); tāriṣṭam (root tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ; luṅ in the sense of a prayer, Vedic; cli → sic, the iṭ augment, with vṛto vā [Pā. 7-2-38] on the length of the augment, barred by sici ca parasmaipadeṣu [Pā. 7-2-40]; the Vedic absence of aṭ; ādiḥ sico 'nyatarasyām, Pā. 6-1-187, for the initial acute; the print adds that tāriṣṭam and mṛkṣatam are not lowered, by the understood but unused ca, as with gacchatam above); mṛkṣatam (root mṛśa āmarśane; chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ, luṅ in the sense of loṭ; śala igupadhād aniṭaḥ kṣaḥ — Pā. 3-1-45; kṣa is it-marked, no iṭ, no guṇa); sedhatam (root ṣidhu gatyām; here the plain root has the sense of "preventing" because it is understood with prati; loṭ in the prayer sense, śap pit so unaccented; tiṅ [tāsyanudāttenṅid…] so the root's accent stands); dveṣaḥ (anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante — vic in the agent sense, "[those] who make hatred"); bhavatam (the word dveṣaḥ is in another sentence and so bhavatam [being the sentence's first verb] is not lowered; a rule is cited from the vārtika that yuṣmad-asmad-substitutes come only in the same sentence, Pā. 8-1-18-5 as printed); sacābhuvā (sacā is an indeclinable of the meaning of saha; Yāska: 'sacā sahety artha iti' (Ni. 5-5); sacā bhavate iti sacābhūḥ, kvip; oḥ supi — ओः सुपि — Pā. 6-4-83 would give yaṇ, but na bhūsudhiyoḥ — न भूसुधियोः — Pā. 6-4-85 forbids the yaṇ-substitution for bhū and sudhī; the dual ending replaced by ā by supāṃ sulug…)."

Pratipadārtha — "nāsatyā — [O two] free of untruth; aśvinā — O Aśvin deities; tribhir ekādaśaiḥ devebhiḥ — with the thrice-eleven, i.e. thirty-three, gods; madhupeyam — for [the sake of drinking] the sweet and drinkable soma juice; iha — to this place of our sacrifice; ā yātam — come; āyuḥ — our lifetime; pra tāriṣṭam — increase; rapāṃsi — our sins; niḥ mṛkṣatam — wash well, make pure; dveṣaḥ — those who hate us (our enemies); sedhatam — keep off; sacābhuvā — being with us; bhavatam — be."

Bhāvārtha — "O Aśvin deities, you never speak untruth. Kindly come to this place of our sacrifice with the thirty-three gods, to drink the sweet soma juice. Increase our lives, wash away our sins and make us pure, and keep off our enemies. Be always with us."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 122) — "Come hither, O Nasatyas, with the thrice eleven gods to drink the sweet Soma ; prolong our lives, efface our faults ; ward off our enemies and be ever with us·" the print ends with a raised dot where a full stop is expected.

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), pp. 123–124

tribhir ekādaśaiḥ — "The meaning of this ṛk is clear. Tribhir ekādaśaiḥ means 'thrice eleven', or thirty-three. In the Ṛgveda, and in the other Vedas here and there, it is stated that there are thirty-three gods. In some ṛks it is said that one group of eleven gods dwells on the earth, another group of eleven in the mid-region, and a third group of eleven in heaven."

ये देवासो दिव्येकादश स्थ पृथिव्यामध्येकादश स्थ । अप्सुक्षितो महिनैकादश स्थ ते देवासो यज्ञमिमं जुषध्वम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१३९-११)

ye devāso divy ekādaśa stha pṛthivyām adhy ekādaśa stha | apsukṣito mahinaikādaśa stha te devāso yajñam imaṃ juṣadhvam || (ṛ. saṃ. 1-139-11)

"The idea here is: 'Let the eleven gods who are in heaven, the eleven who are on earth, and the eleven who are in the mid-region (apaḥ = mid-region, Ni. 2-10) come to this sacrifice and accept the oblation.' And:"

श्रुष्टीवानो हि दाशुषे देवा अग्ने विचेतसः । तान्रोहिदश्व गिर्वणस्त्रयस्त्रिंशतमा वह ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-४५-२) पत्नीवतस्त्रिंशतं त्रींश्च देवाननुष्वधमा वह मादयस्व ॥ (ऋ. सं. ३-६-९) त्रीणि शता त्री सहस्राण्यग्निं त्रिंशच्च देवा नव चासपर्यन् ॥ (ऋ. सं. ३-९-९)

śruṣṭīvāno hi dāśuṣe devā agne vicetasaḥ | tān rohidaśva girvaṇas trayastriṃśatam ā vaha || (ṛ. saṃ. 1-45-2) patnīvatas triṃśataṃ trīṃś ca devān anuṣvadham ā vaha mādayasva || (ṛ. saṃ. 3-6-9) trīṇi śatā trī sahasrāṇy agniṃ triṃśac ca devā nava cāsaparyan || (ṛ. saṃ. 3-9-9)

Untranslated in the source. My glosses, editorial and tentative: 1.45.2 "for the giver the gods, O Agni, are attentive [?], wise: bring those thirty-three, O red-horsed, lover of songs"; 3.6.9 "bring the thirty-three gods with their wives, and rejoice according to [their] custom [?]"; 3.9.9 "three hundred, three thousand, thirty and nine gods served Agni". The reference numerals are zoom-checked: 1-45-2, 3-6-9, 3-9-9. "Besides these ṛks, in the Yajurveda — Taittirīya Saṃhitā 1-4-10-1, Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 4-5-7-2 and other [texts] — the number of the gods is likewise said to be thirty-three. In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa these thirty-three gods are given as the Vasus 8, the Rudras 11, the Ādityas 12, and Dyāvāpṛthivī 2 — in all thirty-three; but that division must be understood as a separate matter. The notion that in each of the three worlds — earth, mid-region, heaven — there are eleven gods, thirty-three in all, is the one specially seen in the Ṛgveda. The statement in the Purāṇas and elsewhere that there are thirty-three koṭi gods may rest on [a misreading of] what is said in the Ṛgveda. In the Viṣṇu Purāṇa too [the count is given as] Vasus 8, Rudras 11, Ādityas 12, Prajāpati 1, the vaṣaṭkāra 1 — in all thirty-three gods."

madhupeyam = "the drinking of soma juice that is sweet like honey."

pra tāriṣṭam = tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ | pravardhayatam — "let there be increase."

rapāṃsi = asmadīyāni pāpāni — "our sins [the print adds the English: our sins, our faults or errors &c]. On this word Yāska says 'rapo ripram iti pāpanāmanī bhavataḥ' — the two words rapaḥ and ripram are names of sin." No Nirukta number is printed here.

nir mṛkṣatam = mṛśa āmarśane | niḥśeṣeṇa śodhayatam — "cleanse fully, wipe away [sins], and so on."

sedhatam = ṣidhu gatyām — "though the root ṣidh has the sense of motion, the bhāṣyakāra says that here, being joined with the preverb prati, it has the sense prati-ṣidh = 'prevent' (pratiṣedhatam): 'keep off, obstruct'."

sacābhuvā = sacety ayaṃ nipātaḥ sahaśabdasamānārthaḥ | sāhāyyārthaṃ asmābhiḥ sahāvasthitau — "here sacā is [said in the Kannada to be] an upasarga; its sense is saha, 'with'; so sacābhuvā means 'staying with [us]': be with us, near us, for our protection."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā p. 124, PDF 138 — grammar page, noted briefly; begun, to continue on p. 125 - tribhiḥ: ṣaṭtricaturbhyo halādiḥ — षट्त्रिचतुर्भ्यो हलादिः — (Pā. 6-1-179): an ending beginning with a consonant, after ṣaṭ, tri or catur, is acute; so bhis is acute. - ekādaśaiḥ: ekādaśānāṃ pūraṇāḥ, taiḥ; the aṃśa (part) that completes the number eleven; tasya pūraṇe ḍaṭ — तस्य पूरणे डट् — (Pā. 5-2-48): after a word denoting a number, in the sixth case, the suffix ḍaṭ comes when the completer of that number is meant. - madhupeyam: pātum yogyam peyam; aco yat — अचो यत् — (Pā. 3-1-97): after a root ending in a vowel the suffix yat; pā + ya; īdyati — ईद्यति — (Pā. 6-4-65): before yat, an ā [of a root] becomes ī; then guṇa by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ — Pā. 7-3-84; yato 'nāvaḥ — यतोऽनावः — (Pā. 6-1-213): a word ending in the suffix yat — other than nau — and having two syllables is first-syllable acute; hence peya is first-syllable acute; madhu ca tat peyam ca is a karmadhāraya; gatikārakopapadāt kṛt — Pā. 6-2-139: the accent of the later member, being a kṛt, is retained.

Rik 11 — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā, continued and concluded (pp. 125–127, PDF 140–142; grammar pages, noted briefly)

Kannada prose with sūtras quoted; numerals zoom-checked against the better scan. The twelfth ṛk is the second Triṣṭup of the sūkta, per the introduction on p. 71.

  • tāriṣṭam (p. 125): root tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ; the two l-tenses liṅ and loṭ are taught only in the sense of a prayer; here luṅ appears in the prayer sense, Vedically; parasmaipada, second-person dual thas, replaced by tam by tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ (no number printed here); cli in the luṅ, then sic for it by cleḥ sic — च्लेः सिच् (cleḥ sic) — (no number printed): tṝ + s + tam; ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ — आर्धधातुकस्येड्वलादेः — Pā. 7-2-35: the augment iṭ for sic, as its first part; the print then works through vṛto vā — वृतो वा — Pā. 7-2-38 (which takes in the roots vṛ(ñ), vṛ, ṛt-final bases), graho 'liṭi dīrghaḥ — ग्रहोऽलिटि दीर्घः — (no number printed) (lengthening of the augment) and sici ca parasmaipadeṣu — सिचि च परस्मैपदेषु — Pā. 7-2-40, which forbids that lengthening before sic in parasmaipada for roots in ṛ — "here iṭ is present after tṝ, a root in ṛ"; bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi — बहुलं छन्दस्यमाङ्योगेऽपि — Pā. 6-4-75: the words māṅ-connection and api mean that in the Veda the augments aṭ and āṭ are not constantly present, even where māṅ is connected — hence no aṭ here; ṛta iddhātoḥ — ऋत इद्धातोः — Pā. 7-1-100 is set aside by the vṛddhi of sici vṛddhiḥ parasmaipadeṣu — सिचि वृद्धिः परस्मैपदेषु — Pā. 7-2-1; uraṇ raparaḥ; tār + iṣ + tam; ṣ by ādeśapratyayayoḥ; ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ: tāriṣṭam. "Here the sense of ca — tāriṣṭaṃ mṛkṣataṃ ca — is understood, though not used; since the ca has been dropped, cādilope vibhāṣā — चादिलोपे विभाषा — (explained under the previous ṛk) forbids the lowering of the first verb, and by tiṅ ṅatiṅaḥ it is not wholly unaccented; and ādiḥ sicoʼnyatarasyām — आदिः सिचोऽन्यतरस्याम् — Pā. 6-1-187 gives the first syllable of a sic-ending word the acute, optionally: thus ādyudātta."
  • mṛkṣatam (pp. 125–126): root mṛśa āmarśane, tudādi ("touching"); here, with the preverb niḥ, the sense is "cleansing"; chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ — छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिटः — Pā. 3-4-6: in the Veda luṅ, laṅ, liṭ are used optionally in the senses of all tenses — here for loṭ; thas → tam; mṛś + cli + tam; śala igupadhād aniṭaḥ kṣaḥ — शल इगुपधादनिटः क्सः — Pā. 3-1-45 (śal = ś, ṣ, s, h; ik = i, u, ṛ, ḷ; "upadhā" is the letter before the last; a root so characterised, without the augment iṭ, takes ksa for cli, k being an it); so mṛś + sa + tam; ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt — Pā. 7-2-10: no iṭ, the root being counted among the anudāttet roots in the mnemonic verse kṛśir-daṃśi-diśī-dṛśṛ-mṛś ("mṛś is among them"); bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge — as above: no aṭ; the root ends in ś; ś → ṣ by vraścabhrasjasṛjamṛjayajarājabhrājacchaśāṃ ṣaḥ — Pā. 8-2-36; mṛṣ + s + tam; ṣaḍhoḥ kassi — षढोः कः सि — Pā. 8-2-41: ṣ → k before s: mṛk + sa + tam. "In the Veda-bhāṣya it is written ṣatva-kutve; it would be correct to write ṣatva-katve". Then ādeśapratyayayoḥ turns s into ṣ: mṛkṣatam.
  • sedhatam (p. 126): root ṣidha gatyām, "to go"; "the form ṣidhu is not found in the present Dhātupāṭha"; with the preverb prati it means "to ward off" (pratiṣedha); the preverbs are only indicators (dyotaka), i.e. words that make the force of a verb evident; "so, even though there is no indicator, the sense that appears when prati is joined to ṣidh is the one meant here". Vidhinimantraṇāmantraṇādhīṣṭasaṃpraśnaprārthaneṣu liṅ — विधिनिमन्त्रणामन्त्रणाधीष्टसंप्रश्नप्रार्थनेषु लिङ् — (Pā. 3-3-161) and loṭ ca — लोट् च — (Pā. 3-3-162): loṭ in the sense of a prayer; second-person dual thas, śap; ṣ → s [as the page says, the ṣa of the root's initial]; loṭo laṅvat; tasthasthamipāṃ…: tam; śap is a non-taught (anupadeśa) element, so tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāt… (no number printed here) makes the lasārvadhātuka unaccented, and pit-ness of śap does the same; anudāttaṃ sarvam apādādau — अनुदात्तं सर्वमपादादौ — (Pā. 8-1-18): everything is unaccented except at the beginning of a foot — but the verb stands at the beginning of the fourth foot, so this does not apply; alternatively tiṅ ṅatiṅaḥ — तिङ्ङतिङः — (Pā. 8-1-28): a tiṅ after a non-tiṅ word is unaccented, and here sedhatam stands after the tiṅ mṛkṣatam, so it is not unaccented; dhātoḥ (Pā. 6-1-162) keeps the root's own acute.
  • dveṣaḥ (p. 126 end): root dviṣa aprītau, adādi; anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante — अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्ते — (Pā. 3-2-75): manin, kvanip, vanip, vic come after other roots too; so vic in the agent sense.
  • bhavatam (p. 127): root bhū, loṭ, second-person dual: "there are two sentences: 'sedhataṃ dveṣaḥ' (ward off those who hate) and 'sacābhuvā bhavatam' (be with us). For the lowering [nighāta] to come, the cause and the thing caused must lie in one sentence, as the rule samānavākye nighāte yuṣmadasmadādeśā vaktavyāḥ — समानवाक्ये निघाते युष्मदस्मदादेशा वक्तव्याः — (Pā. 8-1-18-5 as printed, a vārtika) teaches. Here, for bhavatam to be lowered, the word dveṣaḥ before it would have to be its cause; but that word lies in another sentence; so there is no sarvānudātta, and the root's accent stands."
  • sacābhuvā: Yāska in the Nirukta (Ni. 5-5): sacā sahety arthaḥ; sacā bhavataḥ iti sacābhuvau, suffix kvip; after sacā bhū the nominative dual au; oḥ supi — ओः सुपि — (Pā. 6-4-83): before a vowel-initial sup, a base whose last [dhātu] syllable is u/ū — with a preceding non-conjunct — takes yaṇ; here the ban na bhūsudhiyoḥ — न भूसुधियोः — (Pā. 6-4-84 as printed; for 6-4-85) stops the yaṇ for bhū, sudhī; then aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau — अचि श्नुधातुभ्रुवां य्वोरियङुवङौ — (Pā. 6-4-77): before a vowel-initial suffix a base ending in śnu, a dhātu ending in i/u, and bhrū takes iyaṅ/uvaṅ; so sacābhuv + au, and supāṃ sulug… gives ā for au. Rik 11 ends here (|| 11 ||).
original pp. 127–131

Rik 12

Saṃhitā-pāṭha As printed, the first half ends in सुवीरं with anusvara.

आ नो॑ अश्विना त्रि॒वृता॒ रथे॑ना॒र्वाञ्चं॑ र॒यिं व॑हतं सु॒वीरं॑ । शृ॒ण्वन्ता॑ वा॒मव॑से जोहवीमि वृ॒धे च॑ नो भवतं॒ वाज॑सातौ ॥ १२ ॥

ā́ no aśvinā trivṛ́tā ráthenārvā́ñcaṃ rayíṃ vahataṃ suvī́raṃ | śṛṇvántā vām ávase johavīmi vṛdhé ca no bhavataṃ vā́jasātau || 12 ||

Pada-pāṭha

आ । नः । अश्विना । त्रिऽवृता । रथेन । अर्वाञ्चम् । रयिम् । वहतम् । सुऽवीरम् ॥ शृण्वन्ता । वाम् । अवसे । जोहवीमि । वृधे । च । नः । भवतम् । वाजऽसातौ ॥ १२ ॥

ā | naḥ | aśvinā | tri-vṛtā | rathena | arvāñcam | rayim | vahatam | su-vīram || śṛṇvantā | vām | avase | johavīmi | vṛdhe | ca | naḥ | bhavatam | vāja-sātau || 12 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya the first half in full, the grammatical tail characterized

हे अश्विना त्रिवृता रथेन अप्रतिहतगतित्वात् त्रिषु लोकेषु वर्तमानेन रथेन सह नोऽस्माकमर्वाञ्चमभिमुखं सुवीरं शोभनैर्वीर्यैः पुत्रभृत्यादिभिरुपेतं रयिं धनमा वहतम् । आनीय प्रापयतम् । शृण्वन्तास्मदीयस्तुतिं शृण्वन्तौ वां युवामवसेऽस्मद्रक्षणार्थं जोहवीमि । आह्वयामि । नोऽस्माकं वाजसातौ संग्रामे । वाजसातौ महाधन इति संग्रामनामसु पाठात् । वृधे वर्धनाय च भवतम् ॥

he aśvinā trivṛtā rathena apratihatagatitvāt triṣu lokeṣu vartamānena rathena saha no 'smākam arvāñcam abhimukhaṃ suvīraṃ śobhanair vīryaiḥ putrabhṛtyādibhir upetaṃ rayiṃ dhanam ā vahatam | ānīya prāpayatam | śṛṇvantāsmadīyastutiṃ śṛṇvantau vāṃ yuvām avase 'smadrakṣaṇārthaṃ johavīmi | āhvayāmi | no 'smākaṃ vājasātau saṃgrāme | vājasātau mahādhana iti saṃgrāmanāmasu pāṭhāt | vṛdhe vardhanāya ca bhavatam ||

Translation: "O Aśvins, together with your trivṛt chariot — which, its course being unobstructed, travels in the three worlds — bring (ā vahatam) to us arvāñcam, towards us, suvīram — furnished with good heroic men, sons, servants and the like — rayim, wealth. Bring it and cause us to obtain it. Śṛṇvantā — you who hear our praise — vām — you — I call avase, for our protection, johavīmi — I invoke. Naḥ vājasātau — for us, vājasātau — in battle [saṃgrāma], since vājasātau is read in the lists of words for 'battle', 'mahādhana' — for our success, vṛdhe ca bhavatam — and be for our increase."

Grammar within the bhāṣya p. 128, characterized: suvīram (śobhanā vīrā yasya, a bahuvrīhi, with the first-member accent of vīravīryau ca); śṛṇvantā (root śru śravaṇe, laṭ, śatṛ; śruvaḥ śṛ ca — Pā. 3-1-74 — śṛ in place of śru, śnu for śap; huśnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke — yaṇ; the dual in ā by supāṃ sulug…); johavīmi (root hve̐ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; yaṅ with luk; yaṅluky abhyastasya ca — Pā. 6-1-33 as cited — the saṃprasāraṇa; yaṅo vā — Pā. 7-3-94 — the optional īṭ); vṛdhe (sampadādibhyaḥ kvip); vājasātau (root ṣaṇu dāne, ktin; titutra… — the ban on iṭ; janasana… — the ā; accent of the first member of a bahuvrīhi).

Pratipadārtha — "aśvinā — O Aśvin deities; trivṛtā rathena — [with the chariot] that moves without obstruction in the three worlds; naḥ — our; arvāñcam — directed towards us; suvīram — endowed with good sons and servants; rayim — wealth; ā vahatam — bring; śṛṇvantā — those who listen to our praises; vām — you two; avase — for the sake of our protection; johavīmi — I call; naḥ — to us; vājasātau — in battle; vṛdhe ca — and for our success (for victory); bhavatam — be."

Bhāvārtha — "O Aśvin deities, your chariot can move through the three worlds without any obstruction. Coming with it, give us wealth together with a good line of descendants, and listen to our praise with favour. Therefore I call on you for our protection. In the time of our battle, be the ones who win us victory."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 129) — "Sitting in your chariot that traverses the three worlds, bring us plenty of wealth accompanied by valiant progeny ; I call upon you both for protection, listen to me and give us victory ( encouragement ) in battle·" .

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 129 - trivṛtā = apratihatagatitvāt triṣu lokeṣu vartamānena: "there is no obstruction to the travel of these deities; the meaning is that they can move in all three worlds, earth, mid-region and heaven." - śṛṇvantā = asmadīyāṃ stutiṃ śṛṇvantau: "those who listen attentively to the hymns and so on that we make." - avase = asmadrakṣaṇārtham: "for our protection." - vṛdhe ca no bhavatam: "for our growth, or for encouraging us — you strive." - vājasātau — "since vājasātau is read among the forty-six words for 'battle', raṇaḥ, vivāk and the rest (no Nirukta number printed), this word means in the battle — the battle we have with our enemies."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 130–131, PDF 144–145 — grammar pages, noted briefly - suvīram (p. 130): śobhanāḥ vīrāḥ yasya saḥ, a bahuvrīhi — "[the wealth] with good heroes"; vīravīryau ca — वीरवीर्यौ च — (Pā. 6-2-120): in a bahuvrīhi the words vīra, vīrya after su are first-syllable acute; vīra is from vīra vikrāntau (the tenth class [as read: of the tenth group]) with the ac suffix of the pacādi kind; citaḥ — चितः — (no number printed) gives it the natural final acute. - śṛṇvantā: root śru śravaṇe, 5th class; laṭ; laṭaḥ śatṛśānacau, śatṛ; śruvaḥ śṛ ca — श्रुवः शृ च — (Pā. 3-1-74): śṛ is substituted for śru, and śnu for śap; śnu by atideśa is ṅit, so no guṇa; with the vowel-initial at as cause, aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ… — Pā. 6-4-77 would apply, but huśnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke — हुश्नुवोः सार्वधातुके — (Pā. 6-4-82 as printed; for 6-4-87) gives yaṇ for the u of a base ending in śnu, or of a dhātu having several vowels and preceded by a conjunct [as the print explains], before a vowel-initial sārvadhātuka, overriding the uvaṅ; the accusative dual in ā. - johavīmi: root hve̐ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; dhātor ekāco… — yaṅ; yaṅo 'ci ca (no number printed) — luk of yaṅ; abhyastasya ca — अभ्यस्तस्य च — (Pā. 6-1-33): saṃprasāraṇa of hve in the reduplicate, where the cause of the abhyasta-name follows; doubling, shortening of the reduplicate, kuhoś cuḥ (no number printed) giving ju-hu; guṇo yaṅluktoḥ — गुणो यङ्लुकोः — (Pā. 7-4-82): guṇa for the reduplicate even when yaṅ is present or has been dropped; jo-hu; laṭ first person singular mip, śap with luk; yaño vā — यङो वा — (Pā. 7-3-94): īṭ for a pit sārvadhātuka beginning with a consonant after yaṅ-ending bases, optionally — hence the augment; guṇa, āv-substitution. The print adds that after a yaṅ-ending base only the ātmanepada is regular; yet johavīmi is parasmaipada — Vedic usage. - vṛdhe: root vṛdhu vṛddhau; sampadādibhyaḥ kvip: vṛdh, a kṛdanta; the fourth singular ṅe. - vājasātau (pp. 130–131): root ṣaṇu dāne, ṣ → s by dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ; striyāṃ ktin; titutratathasisusarakaseṣu ca — तितुत्रतथसिसुसरकसेषु च — (Pā. 7-2-9): no iṭ for these ten kṛt suffixes; janasanakhanāṃ sañjhaloḥ — जनसनखनां सञ्झलोः — (Pā. 6-4-42): ā in place of the n of these three roots when san or a jhal-initial kit/ñit suffix follows; savarṇadīrgha: sāti. Vājānām = of strength; sātiḥ = giving: "that in which there is the giving of strengths", a bahuvrīhi, hence the first-member accent. Rik 12 ends here (|| 12 ||).

Close of Sūkta 34

The sūkta has 12 Riks (printed pp. 71–131; PDF 85–146), as the heading on p. 72 states ("ṛks 1–12"). On the metre, the introduction (p. 71) says the ninth and twelfth ṛks are Triṣṭup and the rest Jagatī, whereas the heading's metre line (p. 72) prints Jagatī for 1–8, 10, 11 and Triṣṭup for what is read as "9–12"; the two are recorded as printed, and the twelve ṛks as actually read are consistent with the introduction (Riks 9 and 12 as Triṣṭup). No closing note ("illige … sūktavu samāptavu") is printed at the end of the last grammar paragraph on p. 131, only a small ornament. Sūkta 35 (hvayāmy agnim) begins on the same leaf, printed p. 131 = PDF 146, under the large heading mūvattaidaneya sūktavu ("the thirty-fifth sūkta"); its Sanskrit introduction on that page reads "ekādaśarcam" (eleven ṛks) where the Kannada anuvāda reads "ten" [?]; both and the rest of that page are not translated here and belong to the next session. The contents table's page for the start of Sūkta 35 (p. 131) is thus confirmed.

Summary of the sūkta (from the Bhāvārthas): an invocation of the Aśvins, with the number three in almost every pāda — their thrice-daily coming to the pressings (Rik 1), the three-wheeled, three-pillared chariot used at Soma's wedding with Venā [Sūryā] (Rik 2), their threefold forgiving of faults, giving of food and guidance (Riks 3–4), the Sun's daughter in their chariot (Rik 5), the three kinds of healing herbs (Rik 6), their lying on the barhis and travelling to three altars (Rik 7), the three soma-vessels and the protection of the sun by day and night (Rik 8), the questions about the wheels and the ass of their chariot (Rik 9), the invitation to come before dawn and drink the offering (Rik 10), the prayer to come with the thirty-three gods and ward off enemies (Rik 11), and a closing prayer for wealth with heroic descendants and victory in battle (Rik 12).

Sūkta 35 — "hvayāmy agnim"

original p. 131

॥ ॐ ॥ — Thirty-fifth Sūkta Kannada title line: "mūvattaidaneya sūktavu" The upper third of this leaf is the end of the grammar of Sūkta 34 Rik 12, already written above; the sūkta begins below the ornament.

original p. 131

Sāyaṇa's introduction and the Kannada anuvāda

Sāyaṇa's introduction printed in Kannada script; checked on 300/450-dpi crops of the better scan

ह्वयाम्यग्निमित्येकादशर्चं पञ्चमं सूक्तम् । हिरण्यस्तूप ऋषिः । आद्या नवमी च जगतीच्छन्दस्के । शिष्टास्त्रिष्टुभः । कृत्स्नस्य सूक्तस्य सविता देवता । आद्यायां ह्वयाम्यग्निमित्यस्यामग्निमित्रावरुणरात्रिसवित्राख्या लिङ्गोक्तदेवताः । तथा चानुक्रान्तम् । ह्वयाम्येकादश सावित्रं नवमी जगत्याद्या च लिङ्गोक्तदैवतपादाश्रय इति । अभिप्लवषडहस्य चतुर्थेऽहनि वैश्वदेवशस्त्र इदं सूक्तं सावित्रं निविद्धानम् । तृतीयस्य त्र्यर्यमेति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । ह्वयाम्यग्निमस्य मे द्यावापृथिवी इति तिस्रः । आ. ७-७ । इति ॥

hvayāmy agnim ity ekādaśarcaṃ pañcamaṃ sūktam | hiraṇyastūpa ṛṣiḥ | ādyā navamī ca jagatīchandaske | śiṣṭās triṣṭubhaḥ | kṛtsnasya sūktasya savitā devatā | ādyāyāṃ hvayāmy agnim ity asyām agnimitrāvaruṇarātrisavitrākhyā liṅgoktadevatāḥ | tathā cānukrāntam | hvayāmy ekādaśa sāvitraṃ navamī jagaty ādyā ca liṅgoktadaivatapādāśraya iti | abhiplavaṣaḍahasya caturthe 'hani vaiśvadevaśastra idaṃ sūktaṃ sāvitraṃ nividdhānam | tṛtīyasya tryarymeti khaṇḍe sūtritam | hvayāmy agnim asya me dyāvāpṛthivī iti tisraḥ | ā. 7-7 | iti ||

Translation: "Hvayāmy agnim is the fifth sūkta, of eleven ṛks. The ṛṣi is Hiraṇyastūpa. The first and the ninth are in Jagatī metre; the rest are Triṣṭup. Savitṛ is the deity of the whole sūkta; in the first ṛk, hvayāmy agnim, the deities named by the words themselves (liṅgokta) are Agni, Mitra-Varuṇa, Night and Savitṛ. So the Anukramaṇikā: 'hvayāmy — eleven; Savitṛ-addressed; the ninth and the first are Jagatī; [the first has] the deities stated by the pādas.' This sūkta, a Sāvitra [hymn], is used (nividdhānam, as printed) in the Vaiśvadeva śastra on the fourth day of the Ābhiplava Ṣaḍaha. It is laid down in the section beginning 'tṛtīyasya tryaryamā' [as read] — 'hvayāmy agnim, asya me dyāvāpṛthivī — three [ṛks]' (Āś. 7-7)."

Anuvāda (Kannada): "Hvayāmy agnim is the fifth sūkta in the seventh anuvāka. In it there are ten [as printed; the Sanskrit above and the heading on p. 132 say eleven] ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Hiraṇyastūpa. Of the ṛks of this sūkta the first and the ninth are in the Jagatī metre; the remaining ṛks are in Triṣṭup. Savitṛ is the deity of the whole sūkta; in the first ṛk, those named in the ṛk — Agni, Mitrāvaruṇa, Rātri, and Savitṛ — are the deities. The Anukramaṇikā says 'hvayāmy ekādaśa sāvitraṃ navamī jagaty ādyā ca liṅgoktadaivatapādāśraya'. For the Vaiśvadeva-śastra mantras on the fourth day of the Ābhiplava-ṣaḍaha rite it is prescribed that this sūkta be recited; this is explained in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section beginning 'tṛtīyasya tryaryamā', in the sūtra 'hvayāmy agnim asya me dyāvāpṛthivī (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-32-1) iti tisraḥ' (Āś. 7-7)."

original p. 132

heading of Sūkta 35 and Rik 35.1

॥ ॐ ॥

सूक्त — ३५ ॥ मण्डल — १ ॥ अनुवाक — ७ ॥ सूक्त — ३५ ॥ ॥ अष्टक — १ ॥ अध्याय — ३ ॥ वर्ग — ६, ७ ॥ ॥ सूक्तदल्लिरुव ऋक्संख्यै १—११ ॥ ॥ ऋषिः — हिरण्यस्तूप आङ्गिरसः ॥ ॥ देवता — १. अग्निर्मित्रावरुणौ रात्री सविता । २—११. सविता ॥ ॥ छन्दः — १–९, जगती । २–८, १०, ११ त्रिष्टुप् ॥

sūkta 35 | maṇḍala 1 | anuvāka 7 | aṣṭaka 1 | adhyāya 3 | varga 6, 7 | ṛks 1–11 | ṛṣi: Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa | devatā: 1. Agni, Mitra-Varuṇa, Rātrī, Savitṛ; 2–11. Savitṛ | chandas: "1–9" (as printed) Jagatī; 2–8, 10, 11 Triṣṭup.

Translation of the heading: "Sūkta 35; Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 7; Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 3, Varga 6, 7; ṛks in the sūkta: 1–11; Ṛṣi: Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa; Deity: for Rik 1 Agni, Mitra-Varuṇa, Night and Savitṛ, for Riks 2–11 Savitṛ; Metre: Jagatī for what is printed as '1–9' (an enlarged slice shows a dash or comma between the two numerals — the introduction on p. 131 says Riks 1 and 9), Triṣṭup for 2–8, 10, 11." The heading is thus consistent with the introduction if the first group is read "1, 9".

Rik 1

Saṃhitā-pāṭha Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented

ह्वया॑म्य॒ग्निं प्र॑थ॒मं स्व॒स्तये॒ ह्वया॑मि मि॒त्रावरु॑णावि॒हाव॑से । ह्वया॑मि॒ रात्रीं॒ जग॑तो नि॒वेश॑नीं॒ ह्वया॑मि दे॒वं स॑वि॒तार॑मू॒तये॑ ॥ १ ॥

hváyāmy agníṃ prathamáṃ svastáye hváyāmi mitrā́váruṇāv ihā́vase | hváyāmi rā́trīṃ jágato nivéśanīṃ hváyāmi deváṃ savitā́ram ūtáye || 1 ||

Pada-pāṭha

ह्वयामि । अग्निम् । प्रथमम् । स्वस्तये । ह्वयामि । मित्रावरुणौ । इह । अवसे ॥ ह्वयामि । रात्रीम् । जगतः । निऽवेशनीम् । ह्वयामि । देवम् । सवितारम् । ऊतये ॥ १ ॥

hvayāmi | agnim | prathamam | svastaye | hvayāmi | mitrāvaruṇau | iha | avase || hvayāmi | rātrīm | jagataḥ | ni-veśanīm | hvayāmi | devam | savitāram | ūtaye || 1 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya the first half in full, the grammatical tail characterized

स्वस्तयेऽस्माकमविनाशाय । स्वस्तीत्यविनाशनाम । नि. ३-२१ । इति यास्कः । प्रथममादावग्निं ह्वयामि । इहास्मिन्कर्मण्यवसेऽस्मद्रक्षणाय मित्रावरुणौ ह्वयामि । जगतो जङ्गमस्य प्राणिजातस्य निवेशनीमुपवेशनहेतुभूतां रात्रीं रात्रिदेवतां ह्वयामि । जङ्गमाः सर्वे प्राणिनो दिवसे स्वस्वव्यापारान्कृत्वा स्वस्वगृहे रात्रावुपविशन्तीति प्रसिद्धम् । ऊतयेऽस्मद्रक्षणार्थं सवितारं देवं ह्वयामि ॥

svastaye 'smākam avināśāya | svastīty avināśanāma | ni. 3-21 | iti yāskaḥ | prathamam ādāv agniṃ hvayāmi | ihāsmin karmaṇy avase 'smadrakṣaṇāya mitrāvaruṇau hvayāmi | jagato jaṅgamasya prāṇijātasya niveśanīm upaveśanahetubhūtāṃ rātriṃ rātridevatāṃ hvayāmi | jaṅgamāḥ sarve prāṇino divase svasvavyāpārān kṛtvā svasvagṛhe rātrāv upaviśantīti prasiddham | ūtaye 'smadrakṣaṇārthaṃ savitāraṃ devaṃ hvayāmi ||

Translation: "Svastaye — for our imperishableness, our welfare; 'svasti' is a word for 'imperishable' (Ni. 3-21), so Yāska. First, at the outset, I invoke Agni. Here, in this rite, for our protection I invoke Mitra and Varuṇa. Jagataḥ niveśanīm — the Night, the night-deity, who is the cause of settling down for the moving world, the whole class of living creatures — I invoke; it is well known that all moving creatures, having done their own works by day, settle down in their own homes at night. Ūtaye — for our protection I invoke the god Savitṛ."

Grammar within the bhāṣya p. 133, characterized: mitrāvaruṇau (a dvandva of two divine names; devatādvandve ca (no number in the bhāṣya) — the substitute ānaṅ for the end of the first member; na lopaḥ prātipadikāntasya; and the same-named rule on the accent, devatādvandve ca, keeps the natural accent of both members); rātrīm (rātreś cājasoḥ — Pā. 4-1-31 — ṅīp, except before jas and as); niveśanīm (niviśante 'syām iti niveśanī; lyuṭ by karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca; ṅīp by the ṭiḍḍhāṇañ… rule [Pā. 4-1-15]); ūtaye (root av, ktin; ū in place of v and the penultimate, by jvaratvarasrivyavimavām…; the ktin is acute by the rule ūtiyūtijūti… [as printed]).

Pratipadārtha — "prathamam — first; svastaye — so that we may not be destroyed (for our welfare); agnim — the deity Agni; hvayāmi — I call (praying); iha — in this sacrificial rite; avase — for our protection; mitrāvaruṇau — Mitra and Varuṇa; hvayāmi — I call; jagataḥ — for the moving world; niveśanīm — the giver of rest; rātrīm — the goddess of night; hvayāmi — I call; ūtaye — for protection; savitāraṃ devam — the Sun-god; hvayāmi — I call."

Bhāvārtha — "In this sacrifice I first invoke Agni, the guardian of our welfare, and then Mitra and Varuṇa, the protectors. For the keeping of our peace I invoke the goddess of night, who gives rest to the whole moving world; and for our protection I invoke the Sun-god, the protector of the world."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 133) — "I invoke Agni first for our welfare ; I invoke Mitra and Varuna in this sacrifice for protection ; I invoke Night whobr ings [sic] rest to the world ; I invoke the divine Savitri for my protection·" the print ends with a raised dot where a full stop is expected.

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 134 - "Although Savitṛ alone is the deity of this sūkta, in the first ṛk the deities Agni, Mitra-Varuṇa and Night are praised in the form of a preface, and then Savitṛ." - svastaye = svastyayanāya: "svasti is a name for the imperishable. Yāska explains: 'svastīty avināśanāma | avināśino 'rthasya nāma | astiḥ ayam abhipūjitaḥ supūrvaḥ san ucyate su-asti = svasti' (no Nirukta number printed here) — svasti is [su + asti], the word asti ('is') honoured by the prefix su; so it means what does not perish, what is auspicious, and so on." Translation of the Nirukta sentence editorial and tentative. - mitrāvaruṇau — "Mitra and Varuṇa are connected with day and night. In the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa it is said 'maitraṃ vā ahaḥ | vāruṇī rātriḥ' — Mitra is the form of the day, Varuṇa the form of the night." The reference is not printed here. - rātrīṃ jagato niveśanīm — "By day all living beings are engaged in their several works; at night they seek rest from their dealings and the like. Hence the meaning here is: the Night, who gives rest to the creatures that are in the world." - devaṃ savitāram — "devam means shining, glowing with radiance — bright, shining &c. [the print's English]; savitāram means Savitṛ, the Sun. Ordinarily the word deva stands with the word savitṛ as its adjective."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 134–, PDF 148–, grammar pages — noted briefly; begun, to continue on p. 135 - mitrāvaruṇau: mitraś ca varuṇaś ca, a dvandva; both words name deities; devatādvandve ca — देवताद्वन्द्वे च — (Pā. 6-3-25 as printed; for 6-3-26): in a dvandva of divine names a substitute is made in the end of the first member before the second; then nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya — Pā. 8-2-7 — for the n; and devatādvandve ca — (Pā. 6-2-141): in a dvandva of divine names both members keep their natural accent, so the accent which each had before the compound stays. Mitra is masculine and, as a base, final-acute; varuṇa ends in the Uṇādi suffix unan (kṛvṛdāribhya unan — Uṇ. 3-53), which is nit, so by the nit rule the first syllable of varuṇa is acute. - rātrīm: root rā dāne [and śadḷ śātane]; the Uṇādi sūtra rāśadibhyāṃ triṣ — राशदिभ्यां त्रिष् — (Uṇ. 4-50[?]; the last digit 7 or 2, undecided) gives triṣ; the suffix is pit, so anudāttau suppitau; then rātreś cājasoḥ — (Pā. 4-1-31): ṅīp is not made before jas, as [na jasi ajasi, tasmin — the print analyses the compound ajasau thus]; here the i… the page ends mid-sentence; it continues on p. 135.

Rik 1 — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā, continued and concluded (p. 135, PDF 150; grammar page, noted briefly)

  • rātrīm (concluded): in the Veda ṅīp comes after the word rātri even where the case is not jas [or as] — that ṅīp is itself anudātta; rātri + ī, the i of rātri is lost by yasyeti ca — यस्येति च — (no number printed), so rātrī is first-syllable acute; then am, with ami pūrvaḥ — अमि पूर्वः — (no number printed) giving pūrvarūpa; the single substitute standing in place of an unaccented vowel and an acute one takes the accent of the nearer, and by udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ — उदात्ताद् अनुदात्तस्य स्वरितः — (no number printed) the ī is svarita.
  • niveśanīm: niviśante 'syām — "in which they settle"; karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca — करणाधिकरणयोश्च — (Pā. 3-3-117): lyuṭ after a root in the sense of instrument or locus — here locus (adhikaraṇa = support); root viśa praveśane with ni; viś + yu; yuvor anākau — युवोरनाकौ — (Pā. 7-1-1) gives ana for yu; laghūpadha-guṇa; ni + veśana; lyuṭ is ṭit, so ṅīp by ṭiḍḍhāṇañdvayasajdaghnañmātrac… — टिड्ढाणञ्द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रच्तयप्ठक्ठञ्कञ्क्वरपः — (Pā. 4-1-15): after a base ending in a that has at its end any of the ṭit-suffixes etc. which is not subordinate, ṅīp appears when the feminine is meant; niveśan + ī, loss of a.
  • ūtaye: root ava rakṣaṇe, ktin; jvaratvarasrivyavimavāmupadhāyāś ca — ज्वरत्वरस्रिव्यविमवामुपधायाश्च — (Pā. 6-4-20) gives ūṭh for the v and the penultimate; ūtiyūtijūti… — ऊतियूतिजूति… — (Pā. 3-3-97) makes ktin acute. The print then discusses ekaḥ pūrvaparayoḥ — एकः पूर्वपरयोः — (Pā. 6-1-84) with the vārtika "vyākaraṇe 'pi hy anyatra dvayoḥ sthāninor eka ādeśaḥ" and the Mahābhāṣya on jvaratvara… ("here, in the jvaratvara sūtra, one substitute stands in place of two substituends"), and the other view in the Bhāṣya ("इह तावत् ज्वरत्वरस्रिव्यविमवामुपधायाश्चेति । स्यान्द्वावूठौ नास्ति दोषः । सवर्णदीर्घत्वेन सिद्धम्" — iha tāvat jvaratvarasrivyavimavām upadhāyāś ceti | syān dvāv ūṭhau nāsti doṣaḥ | savarṇadīrghatvena siddham — "here, in jvaratvara…, there may be two ūṭh substitutes: no fault, it is achieved by the lengthening of like vowels") that there are two substitutes for the two substituends, made good by savarṇadīrgha. Rik 1 ends here (|| 1 ||).
original pp. 135–139

Rik 2

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

आ कृष्णेन॒ रज॑सा॒ वर्त॑मानो निवे॒शय॑न्न॒मृतं॒ मर्त्यं॑ च । हि॒र॒ण्यये॑न सवि॒ता रथे॒ना दे॒वो या॑ति॒ भुव॑नानि॒ पश्य॑न् ॥ २ ॥

ā kṛṣṇena rájasā vártamāno niveśáyann amṛ́taṃ mártyaṃ ca | hiraṇyáyena savitā́ rathenā́ devó yāti bhúvanāni páśyan || 2 ||

Pada-pāṭha

आ । कृष्णेन । रजसा । वर्तमानः । निऽवेशयन् । अमृतम् । मर्त्यम् । च ॥ हिरण्ययेन । सविता । रथेन । आ । देवः । याति । भुवनानि । पश्यन् ॥ २ ॥

ā | kṛṣṇena | rajasā | vartamānaḥ | ni-veśayan | amṛtam | martyam | ca || hiraṇyayena | savitā | rathena | ā | devaḥ | yāti | bhuvanāni | paśyan || 2 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

सविता सूर्यः कृष्णेन रजसा कृष्णवर्णेन लोकेन । कृष्णं कृष्यतेर्निकृष्टो वर्णः । नि. २-२० । इति यास्कः । लोका रजांस्युच्यन्ते । नि. ४-१९ । इति च । अन्तरिक्षलोको हि सूर्यगमनात्पुरा कृष्णवर्णो भवति । तेनान्तरिक्षमार्गेण वर्तमानः पुनःपुनरागच्छन् अमृतं देवं मर्त्यं मनुष्यं च निवेशयन् स्वस्वस्थाने ऽवस्थापयन् । यद्वा । अमृतं मरणरहितं प्राणं मरणसहितं शरीरं च निवेशयन् । तथा चारण्यककाण्डे अमर्त्यो मर्त्येना सयोनिरित्येतस्य मन्त्रभागस्य व्याख्यानरूपे ब्राह्मणे यथोक्तोऽर्थोऽवगम्यते । मर्त्यानि हीमानि शरीराण्यमृतैषा देवता । ऐ. आ. २-१-८ । इति । यथोक्तगुणोपेतः सविता देवो भुवनानि सर्वान्लोकान्पश्यन् अवेक्षमाणः प्रकाशयन्नित्यर्थः । हिरण्ययेन सुवर्णनिर्मितेन रथेना याति । अस्मत्समीपमागच्छति ॥

savitā sūryaḥ kṛṣṇena rajasā kṛṣṇavarṇena lokena | kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣyater nikṛṣṭo varṇaḥ | ni. 2-20 | iti yāskaḥ | lokā rajāṃsy ucyante | ni. 4-19 | iti ca | antarikṣaloko hi sūryagamanāt purā kṛṣṇavarṇo bhavati | tenāntarikṣamārgeṇa vartamānaḥ punaḥ punar āgacchan amṛtaṃ devaṃ martyaṃ manuṣyaṃ ca niveśayan svasvasthāne 'vasthāpayan | yadvā | amṛtaṃ maraṇarahitaṃ prāṇaṃ maraṇasahitaṃ śarīraṃ ca niveśayan | tathā cāraṇyakakāṇḍe amartyo martyenā sayonir ity etasya mantrabhāgasya vyākhyānarūpe brāhmaṇe yathokto 'rtho 'vagamyate | martyāni hīmāni śarīrāṇy amṛtaiṣā devatā | ai. ā. 2-1-8 | iti | yathoktaguṇopetaḥ savitā devo bhuvanāni sarvān lokān paśyan avekṣamāṇaḥ prakāśayann ity arthaḥ | hiraṇyayena suvarṇanirmitena rathenā yāti | asmatsamīpam āgacchati ||

Translation: "Savitṛ — Sūrya — kṛṣṇena rajasā, by the dark-coloured world: 'kṛṣṇa, from the root kṛṣ, is a base [lowly] colour' (Ni. 2-20), so Yāska; and 'the worlds are called rajāṃsi' (Ni. 4-19). For the mid-region, before the sun's going, is dark in colour. Moving through that path of the mid-region, coming again and again, niveśayan — establishing, each in its own place — amṛtam, the immortal god, and martyam, the mortal man. Or: establishing the deathless vital breath and the mortal body. And so in the Brāhmaṇa that explains the mantra portion 'amartyo martyenā sayoniḥ' in the Āraṇyaka section the meaning as stated is understood: 'These bodies are mortal; this deity is immortal' (Ai. Ā. 2-1-8). Savitṛ the god, endowed with the stated qualities, bhuvanāni paśyan — looking on, regarding all the worlds, i.e. illuminating them — hiraṇyayena, with a chariot made of gold, ā yāti — comes to our neighbourhood."

Grammar within the bhāṣya p. 136, characterized: amṛtam (mṛtaṃ maraṇaṃ nāsty asya, a bahuvrīhi with nañ: jaramaramitramṛtāḥ — the later member [mṛta] takes the first-syllable acute); martyam (marte bhavam; bhave chandasi — yat; yato 'nāvaḥ — first syllable acute); hiraṇyayena (mayaṭ, with loss of the m by nipātana, under ṛtvyavāstvyavāstvamādhvīhiraṇyayāni chandasi [Pā. 6-4-175]; the suffix-accent after the loss of a by yasyeti ca); bhuvanāni (root bhū sattāyām; the Uṇādi sūtra bhūdhūsūbhrasjibhyaś chandasi [Uṇ. 2-80] — suffix kyun; ana for yu; uvaṅ; the first syllable is acute as nit).

Pratipadārtha — "devaḥ — the shining; savitā — the deity Savitṛ; kṛṣṇena — [by that which is] full of darkness; rajasā — through the region of the sky (by the sky-path); ā vartamānaḥ — moving again and again; amṛtam — the deathless gods; martyam — and men who are subject to death; niveśayan — setting (in the place of their duties); hiraṇyayena — made of gold; rathena — in a chariot; [seated]; bhuvanāni — the various worlds; paśyan — looking at (illuminating); ā yāti — comes near to us."

Bhāvārtha — "Savitṛ, who gives light to all the worlds, moving again and again in the dark expanse of the sky, sets all the gods and men in the places of their duties. Seated in a chariot made of gold, he comes near us, looking upon the many worlds and making them bright."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 137) — "Travelling through dark space (firmament) arousing martals [sic] and immortals, the divine Savitri come [sic] in his golden chariot beholding the several worlds·" the print ends with a raised dot.

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 137 - "It is the custom to use this ṛk, at the time of the saṃdhyā prayer, as the mantra for offering the arghya addressed to the Sun. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā the word satyena stands in place of kṛṣṇena." - kṛṣṇena rajasā = kṛṣṇavarṇena lokena: "before sunrise the darkness is spread everywhere. The Sun moves through the worlds [the mid-region and the rest] that are full of that darkness and drives the darkness away. Kṛṣṇena means 'covered with darkness'. Rajasā means 'by the path of the world' (Ni. 4-19)." - amṛtaṃ, martyam — "amṛta means the gods, who are free of death; martya means men, who are subject to death." - niveśayan — "causing the darkness of the night-time to depart, he sets the gods and the men to their own undertakings: such is the sense." The Special Topics of this ṛk and its grammar page continue on p. 138, to be viewed next.

Rik 2 — Special Topics concluded and grammar (pp. 138–139, PDF 153–154; grammar page, noted briefly)

Special Topics, continued from p. 137 - hiraṇyayena = suvarṇanirmitena: "made of gold. It is a convention to describe the chariot of the Sun, or of Savitṛ, as golden: since at sunrise and at sunset the Sun is covered with shining reddish rays (like the colour of gold), the ṛṣis describe the Sun's chariot as golden."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā - amṛtam: na vidyate mṛtaṃ yasya saḥ — "he who has no death"; this overrides bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. 6-2-1) by nañjor jaramaramitramṛtāḥ — नञ्जोर्जरमरमित्रमृताः — (Pā. 6-2-116): the words jara, mara, mitra, mṛta after nañ in a bahuvrīhi are first-syllable acute. - martyam: the Uṇādi sūtra hasimṛgṛṇvāmidamilūpūdhūrvibhyas tan — हसिमृग्रिण्वामिदमिलूपूधूर्विभ्यस्तन् — (Uṇ. 3-366): after the ten roots hase hasane, mṛṅ prāṇatyāge, gṝ nigaraṇe, iṇ gatau, vā gatigandhanayoḥ, amu gatyādiṣu, damu upaśame, lūñ chedane, pūñ pavane, dhurvī hiṃsāyām the suffix tan; titutratathasi… bars the iṭ; guṇa, raparatva: marta, "the earth-world"; tatra bhavo martyaḥ — "born there is martya"; the Tattvabodhinī says that digādibhyo yat — दिगादिभ्यो यत् — (Pā. 4-3-54) is applicable since digādi is an open list (ākṛtigaṇa); or, bhave chandasi — भवे छन्दसि — (Pā. 4-4-110) gives yat in the sense "born in" after a word in the seventh case; yato 'nāvaḥ — Pā. 6-1-213 — makes it first-syllable acute. - hiraṇyayena: ṛtvyavāstvyavāstvamādhvīhiraṇyayāni chandasi — ऋत्व्यवास्त्व्यवास्त्वमाध्वीहिरण्ययानि छन्दसि — (Pā. 6-4-175): after the word ṛtu in the sense of "born in it" the suffix yat and yaṇ-substitution are given by nipātana; after vāsu, yat and añ together, yaṇ; after madhu in the feminine, añ and yaṇ; and hiraṇyasya vikāraḥ, "the product of gold", takes mayaṭ — here the m of mayaṭ is lost by nipātana: hiraṇya + aya; the a of hiraṇya is lost by yasyeti ca (Pā. 6-4-148); aya is first-syllable acute by the suffix-accent (ādyudāttaś ca). The print adds that the Kaumudī-author states a loss of the word mas, i.e. the group m + a, in this view, so that hiraṇya + ya would arise and yasyeti ca would be expected; since the loss of m is asiddha, it must be handled by the maxim aṅgavṛtte punarvṛttāv avidhiḥ; the lengthening that would arise by akṛtsārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ must also be handled; the Veda-bhāṣya, on the ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-7-2 (middle digit the flat-footed 7), follows the same method; ekādeśa udāttena… (no number printed) is cited to say that the single substitute is acute. - bhuvanāni: root bhū sattāyām; the Uṇādi sūtra bhūsūdhūbhrasjibhyaś chandasi — भूसूधूभ्रस्जिभ्यश्छन्दसि — (Uṇ. 2-239 as printed here; the bhāṣya cites 2-80) gives kyun after bhū sattāyām, ṣūṅ prāṇiprasave, dhūñ kampane, bhrasja pāke; the yu of the suffix stays and ana replaces it; aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ… — Pā. 6-4-77 — uvaṅ; the suffix is nit, so the first syllable is acute. Rik 2 ends here (|| 2 ||).

original pp. 139–142

Rik 3

Saṃhitā-pāṭha As printed, the first half ends in हरिभ्यां with anusvara.

याति॑ दे॒वः प्र॒वता॒ यात्यु॒द्वता॒ याति॑ शु॒भ्राभ्यां॑ यज॒तो हरि॑भ्यां । आ दे॒वो या॑ति सवि॒ता प॑रा॒वतोऽप॒ विश्वा॑ दुरि॒ता बाध॑मानः ॥ ३ ॥

yā́ti deváḥ pravátā yā́ty udvátā yā́ti śubhrā́bhyāṃ yajató háribhyāṃ | ā devó yāti savitā́ parāváto 'pa víśvā duritā́ bā́dhamānaḥ || 3 ||

Pada-pāṭha

याति । देवः । प्रऽवता । याति । उत्ऽवता । याति । शुभ्राभ्याम् । यजतः । हरिऽभ्याम् ॥ आ । देवः । याति । सविता । पराऽवतः । अप । विश्वा । दुःऽइता । बाधमानः ॥ ३ ॥

yāti | devaḥ | pra-vatā | yāti | ut-vatā | yāti | śubhrābhyām | yajataḥ | hari-bhyām || ā | devaḥ | yāti | savitā | parā-vataḥ | apa | viśvā | duḥ-itā | bādhamānaḥ || 3 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

देवो दीप्यमानः सविता प्रवता प्रवणवता मार्गेण याति । गच्छति । तथोद्वतोत्कृष्टेनोर्ध्वदेशयुक्तेन मार्गेण याति । उदयानन्तरम् आ मध्याह्नमूर्ध्वो मार्गः । ततस्तत उपरि आ सायं प्रवणो मार्ग इति विवेकः । तथा यजतो यष्टव्यः स देवः शुभ्राभ्यां श्वेताभ्यां हरिभ्यामश्वाभ्यां याति । देवयजनदेशे गच्छति । सविता देवो विश्वा दुरिता सर्वाणि पापान्यप बाधमानो विनाशयन् परावतो दूरदेशात् । परावत इति दूरनामसु पठितत्वात् । तादृशाद्द्युलोकादायाति । यागदेश आगच्छति ॥
