devo dīpyamānaḥ savitā pravatā pravaṇavatā mārgeṇa yāti | gacchati | tathodvatotkṛṣṭenordhvadeśayuktena mārgeṇa yāti | udayānantaram ā madhyāhnam ūrdhvo mārgaḥ | tatas tata upari ā sāyaṃ pravaṇo mārga iti vivekaḥ | tathā yajato yaṣṭavyaḥ sa devaḥ śubhrābhyāṃ śvetābhyāṃ haribhyām aśvābhyāṃ yāti | devayajanadeśe gacchati | savitā devo viśvā duritā sarvāṇi pāpāny apa bādhamāno vināśayan parāvato dūradeśāt | parāvata iti dūranāmasu paṭhitatvāt | tādṛśād dyulokād āyāti | yāgadeśa āgacchati ||

Translation: "The shining god Savitṛ goes (yāti) by pravatā, a path with a slope [downward]; likewise he goes by udvatā, a path that is raised, with an upward region. After the rising, up to midday, the path is upward; thence on, up to evening, the path is a downward slope: that is the distinction. And yajataḥ — he who is to be worshipped — that god goes with śubhrābhyāṃ haribhyām, two white horses; he goes to the place of the sacrifice to the gods. Savitṛ the god, viśvā duritā apa bādhamānaḥ — warding off, destroying all sins — parāvataḥ, from a distant place (parāvataḥ being read in the lists of names for 'far') — comes from such a heaven: he comes to the place of the rite."

Grammar within the bhāṣya p. 140, characterized: pravatā (root vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau; asmāt prapūrvāt kvip — kvip after it with pra; the nasal dropped by the vārtika gamādīnām iti vaktavyam [Pā. 6-4-40-1], then tuk — tatas tuk; the accent of the later member of a kṛt-compound); udvatā ("with ut before the root vana, the same process"); yajataḥ (bhṛmṛdṛśi… [Uṇ. 3-110]; yajateḥ karmaṇi atac); viśvā duritā (in both words the śi is lost by śeś chandasi bahulam).

Pratipadārtha — "devaḥ — the shining Savitṛ; udvatā — by the path that goes upward (from sunrise up to midday); pravatā — by the path that goes downward (from midday up to evening); yāti — goes (moves about); yāti — moves; yajataḥ — he who is worthy of worship; śubhrābhyām — with two bright; haribhyām — horses; yāti — moves; devaḥ — the shining; savitā — Savitṛ; viśvā — all; duritā — sins; apa bādhamānaḥ — destroying; parāvataḥ — from a distant place; ā yāti — comes (graciously to this sacrificial ground)."

Bhāvārtha — "The shining Savitṛ's movement is by an upward way from sunrise to midday, and by a downward way from midday to evening. Everywhere he moves, mounted on a chariot drawn by two bright horses. Worthy of worship, he comes to this sacrificial ground from afar, destroying all sins."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 141) — "The divine Savitri travels by an upward path ; then he travels by a downward path ; deserving worship he journeys with two white horses ; he comes hither from a distance removing all sins (of true worshippers)" no full stop in the print.

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 141 - "When the Sun rises, he rises in the east in the lower part of the mid-region; then, towards midday, he comes to the middle of the mid-region — a high place; and then, as evening approaches, descending downward, he sets in the west. This very matter is stated in this ṛk." - pravatā = prakarṣeṇa gacchatā: "going swiftly; by the lower [downward] path." - udvatā = ūrdhvadeśayuktena mārgeṇa: "by an upward path." - śubhrābhyāṃ haribhyām: "with two clear or bright horses; that is, [Savitṛ is] seated in a chariot to which two bright horses are yoked." - parāvataḥ — "from afar." - viśvā duritā bādhamānaḥ — "driving off all troubles or sins."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā p. 141, PDF 155 — grammar page, noted briefly; begun, to continue on p. 142 - pravatā: the root vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau is read in the Dhātupāṭha; gamaḥ kvau — गमः क्वौ — (Pā. 6-4-40): the nasal of gam is lost before kvip; the vārtika gamādīnām iti vaktavyam — "[it must be said that] this is for the gamādi [roots]" — so that the rule for the nasal of gam alone is not enough, and the loss of the nasal before kvip must be taught for many other roots; the verse "uktānuktadurūktānāṃ cintā vārttikaṃ matam" — "a vārtika is held to be the consideration of what is said, not said, or ill said" — is cited for the vārtika's character; then for van + kvip the n is lost by this vārtika; hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk — ह्रस्वस्य पिति कृति तुक् — (Pā. 6-4-71 as printed; for 6-1-71): after the p of kvip is it, a kṛt that is pit … the page breaks off here and continues on p. 142.

Rik 3 — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā, concluded (p. 142, PDF 157; grammar page, noted briefly)

  • pravatā (concluded): after the tuk the form is pravat; the preverb pra + the third-case singular ṭā; in pravat the va is acute by the root's accent; once the compound with the preverb is made, gatikārakopapadāt kṛt — गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत् — (Pā. 6-2-139) lets the accent of the later member, the kṛdanta, stand.
  • udvatā: "here the preverb ut stands in place of pra; the rest of the process is as before."
  • yajataḥ: root yaja devapūjāyām; bhṛmṛdṛśiyajiparvipacyamitamināmidayibhyo 'tac — भृमृदृशियजिपर्विपच्यमितमिनमिदयिभ्योऽतच् — (Uṇ. 3-390 as printed here; the bhāṣya cites 3-110): atac after yaj: yajata.
  • viśvā duritā: viśvāni duritāni, second-case plural; the śi from jaśśasoḥ śiḥ is dropped by śeś chandasi bahulam — (Pā. 6-1-70); by the sarvanāmasthāna status the augment num had come and the lengthening of the penultimate; after the luk the n is lost. Rik 3 ends here (|| 3 ||).
original pp. 142–146

Rik 4

Saṃhitā-pāṭha As printed, the first half ends in बृहन्तं with anusvara.

अ॒भीवृ॑तं॒ कृश॑नैर्वि॒श्वरू॑पं॒ हिर॑ण्यशम्यं यज॒तो बृ॒हन्तं॑ । आस्था॒द्रथं॑ सवि॒ता चि॒त्रभा॑नुः कृ॒ष्णा रजां॑सि॒ तवि॑षीं॒ दधा॑नः ॥ ४ ॥

abhī́vṛtaṃ kṛ́śanair viśvárūpaṃ híraṇyaśamyaṃ yajató bṛhántaṃ | āsthād ráthaṃ savitā́ citrábhānuḥ kṛṣṇā́ rájāṃsi táviṣīṃ dádhānaḥ || 4 ||

Pada-pāṭha

अभिऽवृतम् । कृशनैः । विश्वऽरूपम् । हिरण्यऽशम्यम् । यजतः । बृहन्तम् ॥ आ । अस्थात् । रथम् । सविता । चित्रऽभानुः । कृष्णा । रजांसि । तविषीम् । दधानः ॥ ४ ॥

abhi-vṛtam | kṛśanaiḥ | viśva-rūpam | hiraṇya-śamyam | yajataḥ | bṛhantam || ā | asthāt | ratham | savitā | citra-bhānuḥ | kṛṣṇā | rajāṃsi | taviṣīm | dadhānaḥ || 4 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

सविता रथमास्थात् । आस्थितवान् । आरूढवानित्यर्थः । कीदृशम् । अभीवृतम् अभितो वर्तमानम् । तथा कृशनैर्विश्वरूपं सुवर्णेन नानारूपम् । कृशनं लोहमिति सुवर्णनामसु पाठात् । क्वचित्सुवर्णनिर्मितगजपङ्क्तिः क्वचिदश्वपङ्क्तिः क्वचिन्मनुष्यपङ्क्तिरित्येवं बहुरूपत्वम् । हिरण्यशम्यम् अश्वानां स्कन्धेषु रथयोजनवेलायां नियन्तुं प्रक्षेप्यमाणाः शङ्कवः शम्याः । ताः सुवर्णमय्यो रथे वर्तन्ते । बृहन्तं प्रौढम् । कीदृशः सविता । यजतो यष्टव्यः । चित्रभानुर्विविधरश्मियुक्तः कृष्णा रजांसि अन्धकारयुक्ततया कृष्णवर्णान् लोकानुद्दिश्य तमोनिवारणार्थं तविषीं बलं स्वकीयं प्रकाशरूपं दधानः ॥

savitā ratham āsthāt | āsthitavān | ārūḍhavān ity arthaḥ | kīdṛśam | abhīvṛtam abhito vartamānam | tathā kṛśanair viśvarūpaṃ suvarṇena nānārūpam | kṛśanaṃ loham iti suvarṇanāmasu pāṭhāt | kvacit suvarṇanirmitagajapaṅktiḥ kvacid aśvapaṅktiḥ kvacin manuṣyapaṅktir ity evaṃ bahurūpatvam | hiraṇyaśamyam aśvānāṃ skandheṣu rathayojanavelāyāṃ niyantuṃ prakṣepyamāṇāḥ śaṅkavaḥ śamyāḥ | tāḥ suvarṇamayyo rathe vartante | bṛhantaṃ prauḍham | kīdṛśaḥ savitā | yajato yaṣṭavyaḥ | citrabhānur vividharaśmiyuktaḥ kṛṣṇā rajāṃsi andhakārayuktatayā kṛṣṇavarṇān lokān uddiśya tamonivāraṇārthaṃ taviṣīṃ balaṃ svakīyaṃ prakāśarūpaṃ dadhānaḥ ||

Translation: "Savitṛ ratham āsthāt — has mounted the chariot. What sort? Abhīvṛtam — encircled all round; and kṛśanair viśvarūpam — many-formed with gold ('kṛśana' = iron/metal, being read among the names of gold): in places a row of elephants made of gold, in places a row of horses, in places a row of men — thus the many forms. Hiraṇyaśamyam — the pegs (śaṅku) that are thrust on the shoulders of the horses, at the time of yoking the chariot, to restrain them, are śamyāḥ; those, made of gold, are in the chariot. Bṛhantam — large, grand. What sort of Savitṛ? Yajataḥ — worthy of worship; citrabhānuḥ — with rays of many kinds; kṛṣṇā rajāṃsi — [looking] to the worlds which are dark-coloured through being full of darkness; taviṣīm — his own strength in the form of light, dadhānaḥ — bearing, for the removal of that darkness."

Grammar within the bhāṣya p. 143, characterized: abhīvṛtam (abhito vartata ity abhīvṛt; root vṛtu vartane; kvip; the lengthening of the first member by nahivṛtivṛṣivyadhi… [Pā. 6-3-116]); viśvarūpam (viśvāni rūpāṇi yasyāsau; bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām — the first-member final-acute here, by vyatyaya, even without a name); hiraṇyaśamyam (haryate gatikāntyoḥ — haryateḥ kanyan hira ca [Uṇ. 5-44]: the suffix kanyan and the substitution hiran for the root; initial-acute by the nit accent; first-member accent of a bahuvrīhi); āsthāt (root ṣṭhā, luṅ, sic dropped by gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu); kṛṣṇā (root kṛṣ in the sense of colour; the Uṇādi sūtra kṛṣer varṇe [Uṇ. 3-4] — the suffix nak; śi dropped by śeś chandasi bahulam); taviṣīm (the root tavati from the sautra list; the Uṇādi suffix iṣac [tavater ṇid vā, Uṇ. 1-49], ṭit, so ṅīp; first-syllable accent by vyatyaya, to be seen as of the vṛṣādi class); dadhānaḥ (śānac; abhyastānām ādiḥ — first-syllable acute).

Pratipadārtha — "yajataḥ — worthy of worship; citrabhānuḥ — endowed with rays of many colours; savitā — Savitṛ; kṛṣṇā rajāṃsi — the worlds filled with darkness (in order to destroy their darkness); taviṣīm — his own strength in the form of light; dadhānaḥ — bearing; abhīvṛtam — surrounded; kṛśanaiḥ viśvarūpam — of many forms, with pictures of elephants and others made of gold; hiraṇyaśamyam — having golden pegs (and [thereby] beautiful); bṛhantam — large; ratham — the chariot; āsthāt — has mounted."

Bhāvārtha — "The Savitṛ-deity, worthy of worship, shining with rays of many colours and destroying the darkness of the dark worlds by his own splendour, has mounted his chariot: a lofty chariot, with a golden pole and pegs for yoking the horses, made of gold and the like, and adorned with all sorts of pictures."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 144) — "The adorable Savitri of beautiful splendour having power to disperse darkness from the world has mounted his chariot decorated with many kinds of golden ornaments and furnished with great golden yokes·" .

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 144 - "In this ṛk the ṛṣi describes the chariot of the Sun. The Sun's chariot has golden [front beams — the Kannada word is mūkīmara, as printed]; and the chariot has been made with all kinds of golden ornaments, so that it is delightful with the many pictures all round it — rows of elephants, rows of horses and the like, made of gold. The Savitṛ has mounted such a shining chariot." - abhīvṛtaṃ kṛśanaiḥ viśvarūpam — "encircled all round with ornaments made of gold and the other metals, and furnished with pictures of many kinds, and so on." - hiraṇyaśamyam = aśvānāṃ skandheṣu rathayojanavelāyāṃ niyantuṃ prakṣepyamāṇāḥ śaṅkavaḥ śamyāḥ | suvarṇamayyo rathe vartante: "a chariot furnished with golden [front-beams] meant for yoking horses" [the Kannada gloss, as printed; the śamyā is the yoke-pin of the bhāṣya's own explanation]. - citrabhānuḥ = atiprakāśayuktaḥ — "possessing great brightness, of beautiful spendour [the print's English, sic]." - kṛṣṇā rajāṃsi — "worlds with darkness. Before the Sun rises, all the worlds are full of darkness; the Sun rises and lights the worlds with brightness." - taviṣīṃ dadhānaḥ — "making brightness by his own power."

Rik 4 — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (pp. 145–146, PDF 160–161; grammar pages, noted briefly)

Numerals zoom-checked against the better scan.

  • abhīvṛtam (p. 145): abhito vartate = abhīvṛt; root vṛtu vartane after the preverb abhi; kvip ca (no number printed) gives kvip, and the augment tuk would yield vṛt; nahivṛtivṛṣivyadhiruciṣahitaniṣu kvau — नहिवृतिवृषिव्यधिरुचिसहितनिषु क्वौ — (Pā. 6-3-116): before roots ending in kvip, the first member is lengthened: abhi → abhī.
  • viśvarūpam: viśvāni rūpāṇi yasya saḥ — "a chariot having many kinds of forms"; bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām — बहुव्रीहौ विश्वं संज्ञायाम् — (Pā. 6-2-106): when a name is shown, the first member viśva is final-acute; "although no name is shown here, being Vedic this rule operates by vyatyaya even without one".
  • hiraṇyaśamyam: root haryate gatikāntyoḥ; haryateḥ kanyan hirac — हर्यतेः कन्यन् हिरच् — (Uṇ. 5-722 as printed here — the first digit after the hyphen a flat-footed 7; the bhāṣya cites 5-44): kanyan after the root harya, with hir substituted for the root; the c is it and lost, the a is only for pronunciation; in the suffix k and n are it, leaving ya: hir + ya = hiraṇya; aṭkupvāṅ… (no number printed) turns n into ṇ; by the nit accent it is first-syllable acute; śamyāḥ are pegs for yoking horses; hiraṇyāḥ śamyā yasmin saḥ, a bahuvrīhi, first-member accent.
  • āsthāt: root ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau, ṣ → s; luṅ, tip, loss of the i, cli, sic, aṭ: ā-asthā + s + t; gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu — गातिस्थाघुपाभूभ्यः सिचः परस्मैपदेषु — (Pā. 2-4-77): luk for sic after these; "by gā is meant the gā substituted for iṇ by iṇo gā luṅi — इणो गा लुङि — (Pā. 2-4-45), and by pā the root pā pāne"; hence luk of sic; aṭ; the preverb ā.
  • kṛṣṇā: kṛṣer varṇe — कृषेर्वर्णे — (Uṇ. 3-284 as printed here; the bhāṣya cites 3-4): when colour is meant, nak after kṛṣ; kṛṣ + na; raṣābhyāṃ no ṇaḥ samānapade — रषाभ्यां नो णः समानपदे — (Pā. 8-4-1): n → ṇ; the word is neuter; śas → śi; śeś chandasi bahulam — (Pā. 6-1-70): luk of the śi; the augment num, the lengthening of the penultimate and the loss of n occur.
  • taviṣīm: the root tava is established by usage, not in the sūtra-list; tavater ṇid vā — तवतेर्णिद्वा — (Uṇ. 1-48 as printed here; the bhāṣya cites 1-49): after tav the suffix ṭiṣac; tav + iṣa; the suffix is ṭit, so ṅīp by ṭiḍḍhāṇañdvayasaj… (Pā. 4-1-15); as a cit suffix it should be final-acute by citaḥ saprakṛter bahvakajartham — चितः सप्रकृतेर्बह्वकजर्थम् — (Pā. 6-1-163), "properly"; but placing the word in the vṛṣādi group, vṛṣādīnāṃ ca — वृषादीनां च — (Pā. 6-1-203), it is first-syllable acute.
  • dadhānaḥ (p. 146): root ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ, laṭ; laṭaḥ śatṛśānacau, śānac; juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ — जुहोत्यादिभ्यः श्लुः — (Pā. 2-4-75) ślu for śap; ślau — श्लौ — (Pā. 6-1-10) doubling: dhā-dhā-āna; hrasvaḥ — ह्रस्वः — (Pā. 7-4-59) shortens the reduplicate; abhyāse carca — अभ्यासे चर्च — (Pā. 8-4-54): in the reduplicate jhal → car and jaś, so dh → d by similarity of place; ubhe abhyastam — उभे अभ्यस्तम् — (Pā. 6-1-5): both [the repeated parts] are called abhyasta; abhyastānām ādiḥ — (Pā. 6-1-189) — first-syllable acute. Rik 4 ends here (|| 4 ||).
original pp. 146–150

Rik 5

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

वि जना॑ञ्छ्या॒वाः शि॑ति॒पादो॑ अख्य॒न्रथं॒ हिर॑ण्यप्रउगं॒ वह॑न्तः । शश्व॒द्विशः॑ सवि॒तुर्दैव्य॑स्योपस्थे॒ विश्वा॒ भुव॑नानि तस्थुः ॥ ५ ॥ [accent ?]

vi jánāñ chyāvā́ḥ śitipā́do akhyan ráthaṃ híraṇyaprauugaṃ váhantaḥ | śaśvad víśaḥ savitúr daívyasyopasthe víśvā bhúvanāni tasthuḥ || 5 || [accent ?]

Pada-pāṭha

वि । जनान् । श्यावाः । शितिऽपादः । अख्यन् । रथम् । हिरण्यऽप्रउगम् । वहन्तः ॥ शश्वत् । विशः । सवितुः । दैव्यस्य । उपऽस्थे । विश्वा । भुवनानि । तस्थुः ॥ ५ ॥

vi | janān | śyāvāḥ | śiti-pādaḥ | akhyan | ratham | hiraṇya-prauugam | vahantaḥ || śaśvat | viśaḥ | savituḥ | daivyasya | upa-sthe | viśvā | bhuvanāni | tasthuḥ || 5 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

श्यावा एतन्नामकाः सूर्यस्याश्वाः । श्यावाः सवितुरिति निघण्टावुक्तत्वात् । ते च शितिपादः श्वेतैः पादैरुपेता हिरण्यप्रउगं रथस्य मुखमीषयोरग्रं युगबन्धनस्थानं प्रउगमित्युच्यते । तच्चात्र सुवर्णमयम् । तद्युक्तं रथं वहन्तो जनान्प्राणिनो व्यख्यन् । विशेषेण प्रकाशितवन्त इत्यर्थः । शश्वत् सर्वदा विशः प्रजा दैव्यस्येतरदेवसम्बन्धिनः सवितुः प्रेरकस्य सूर्यस्योपस्थे समीपस्थाने तस्थुः । स्थितवत्यः । न केवलं प्रजाः किं तर्हि विश्वा भुवनानि सर्वे च लोकाः प्रकाशाय सूर्यसमीपे तस्थुः ॥

śyāvā etannāmakāḥ sūryasyāśvāḥ | śyāvāḥ savitur iti nighaṇṭāv uktatvāt | te ca śitipādaḥ śvetaiḥ pādair upetā hiraṇyaprauugaṃ rathasya mukham īṣayor agraṃ yugabandhanasthānaṃ prauugam ity ucyate | tac cātra suvarṇamayam | tadyuktaṃ rathaṃ vahanto janān prāṇino vyakhyan | viśeṣeṇa prakāśitavanta ity arthaḥ | śaśvat sarvadā viśaḥ prajā daivyasyetaradevasambandhinaḥ savituḥ prerakasya sūryasyopasthe samīpasthāne tasthuḥ | sthitavatyaḥ | na kevalaṃ prajāḥ kiṃ tarhi viśvā bhuvanāni sarve ca lokāḥ prakāśāya sūryasamīpe tasthuḥ ||

Translation: "Śyāvāḥ — the horses of Sūrya who bear this name ('śyāvāḥ savituḥ' being so stated in the Nighaṇṭu). They, śitipādaḥ — furnished with white feet — bearing a chariot with a hiraṇyaprauuga, a golden front-yoke (the front of the chariot, the tip of the two shafts, the place for fastening the yoke is called prauuga; here it is made of gold) — janān — the creatures — vi akhyan — brightened especially. Śaśvat, always, viśaḥ — the people — [being] those of Savitṛ, the daivya, belonging to the other gods, the impeller Sūrya — upasthe, in his lap, in a near place — tasthuḥ, stood. Not only the people: viśvā bhuvanāni, all the worlds, too, stood near the Sun for light."

Grammar within the bhāṣya p. 147, characterized: śitipādaḥ (śitayaḥ śvetavarṇāḥ pādā yeṣām te; supāṃ sulug… — jas → su; or śitiḥ "white as crystal", sa iva pādo yeṣām; pādasya lopo 'hastyādibhyaḥ — पादस्य लोपोऽहस्त्यादिभ्यः — (Pā. 5-4-138): the final of the pāda at the end of such a compound is lost, since upamānāt is carried on there; pāda is first-syllable acute as of the vṛṣādi group; śiter nityābahvajbahuvrīhāv abhasat — (Pā. 6-2-138) the later member keeps its natural accent); akhyan (root khyā, luṅ, cli → aṅ by the rule asyativaktikhyātibhyo 'ṅ); hiraṇyaprauugam (a bahuvrīhi, first-member accent); vahantaḥ (śap is pit so unaccented; śatṛ and the lasārvadhātuka accent keep the root's); daivyasya (tasyedam — devād yañañau — (Pā. 4-1-85), yañ after deva by prāgdīvyatīya; vṛddhi by taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ; first-syllable acute by ñnityādir nityam); upasthe (ātaś copasarge kaḥ; the ā lost by ātolopa iṭi ca; first-member final accent as of marudvṛdhādi).

Pratipadārtha — "śitipādaḥ — with white-coloured feet; śyāvāḥ — the horses of Savitṛ named Śyāva; hiraṇyaprauugam — with a golden [front part, the Kannada mūkī]; ratham — the chariot; vahantaḥ — carrying; janān — beings; vi akhyan — have lit up well; śaśvat — always; viśaḥ — the people (and); viśvā bhuvanāni — all the worlds also; daivyasya — belonging to the other gods; savituḥ — of Savitṛ, the impeller of the world; upasthe — near; tasthuḥ — have stood."

Bhāvārtha — "The horses of the Sun, named Śyāva, carry the chariot with the golden [front-yoke]. With their radiance they light up the whole world of beings. The people and the rest, and all the worlds as well, have stood near the shining Savitṛ, the impeller of the world." The source's English translation, the Special Topics and the grammar of Rik 5 follow on p. 148 and later pages, to be viewed next.

Rik 5 — English, Special Topics and grammar (pp. 148–150, PDF 163–165)

English Translation (the source's own, p. 148) — "Savitri' s horses with white legs harnessed to his chariot with a golden yoke have manifested light to mankind for all people and all the worlds are ever in the presence of the divine Savitri." Printed so, with "Savitri' s" and "harnessed .to" [sic] spacing.

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 148 - śyāvāḥ — "the horses of the Sun are named śyāvāśva. Although śyāva means a horse of dark colour, in the third ṛk of this sūkta [it is a slip for the fifth] the Sun's horses are said to be of a shining white-footed colour; since here śitipādaḥ — 'white feet' (with white legs, the print's English) — is stated, the colour of the horses must be śyāma, brown [the print's English]." - hiraṇyaprauugam = rathasya mukhamīṣayor agraṃ yugabandhanasthānaṃ prauugam ity ucyate: "prauuga means the place at the front of the chariot where the [front beam] joins the chariot; the root part of the [front beam]. It will be golden. This word is used in mantras such as the Taittirīya Saṃhitā 5-4-11-1-2 (as printed), the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1-1-2-9; 3-5-3-4. Pra-uga is apparently equivalent to prayuga, denoting the fore part of the pole of the cart, the part in front of the yoke [the print's English]." - śitipādaḥ = śitayaḥ śvetavarṇāḥ pādā yeṣāṃ te śitipādāḥ: "those with white legs." - daivyasya = itaradevasambandhinaḥ savituḥ, prerakasya sūryasya: "[Savitṛ] who is related to the other gods, or the Sun who impels the other gods — so the bhāṣyakāra says. But the meaning divi sambandhino daivyaḥ — 'what belongs to heaven, i.e. is in heaven (in the mid-region)' — fits well."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 148–150, PDF 163–165 — grammar pages, noted briefly - śitipādaḥ (p. 148–149): śitiḥ = white; śitayaḥ = white; pādāḥ = feet; yeṣāṃ te — a bahuvrīhi; "if so analysed, the form śitipādāḥ is regular"; here supāṃ sulug… gives su for jas, so that śitipādaḥ in the plural has the same form as in the singular — "this is one way"; another way is by saptamyupamānapūrvapadasya … vācyo vā cottarapadalopaḥ (as printed) — a bahuvrīhi in which the second member is dropped: śitipāda iva pādo yeṣāṃ te, "those whose feet are like crystal-feet" — [the bhāṣya says śitiḥ śvetavarṇaḥ sphāṭikādiḥ sa iva pādo yeṣāṃ te] — and pādasya lopo 'hastyādibhyaḥ — पादस्य लोपोऽहस्त्यादिभ्यः — (Pā. 5-4-38 as printed; for 5-4-138): the a of the word pāda at the end of a compound is lost after a word in the sense of the comparison, other than hastin and the like; hence śitipād, and jas after it; vṛṣādīnāṃ ca — (Pā. 6-1-203): pāda is first-syllable acute; śiter nityābahvajbahuvrīhāv abhasat — शितेर्नित्याबह्वज्बहुव्रीहावभसत् — (Pā. 6-2-138): in a bahuvrīhi after śiti, the later member — one that always has more than two vowels [as the print explains] and is other than the word bhasat — keeps its natural accent. - akhyan (p. 149): root khyā prakathane, luṅ; cli; asyativaktikhyātibhyo 'ṅ — अस्यतिवक्तिख्यातिभ्योऽङ् — (Pā. 3-1-52): aṅ for cli; the augment aṭ; jhi → ant: a-khyā + a + anti; ato lopa iṭi ca — (Pā. 6-4-64) drops the ā; itaś ca — (Pā. 3-4-100) the i of the ending; the loss of the final t [conjunct-final loss, saṃyogāntalopa]. - hiraṇyaprauugam: hiraṇyam = golden, prauugam = the place where the pole is fastened, yasya saḥ — a bahuvrīhi; haryateḥ kanyan hirac — (Uṇ. 5-722 as printed, as on p. 145) gives hiraṇya; by nit the accent is first-syllable; the bahuvrīhi then keeps the first-member accent: that same accent remains. - daivyasya (p. 149): after the root div, the pacādi-suffix ac, giving deva; devād yañañau — देवाद्यञञौ — (Pā. 4-1-85-3, as printed; a vārtika): after deva in the sixth case, in the prāgdīvyatīya senses, the suffixes yañ and añ; in the Aṣṭādhyāyī the meanings from prāgdīvyatoṇ — प्राग्दीव्यतोऽण् — (Pā. 4-1-83) up to tena dīvyati khanati jayati jitam — तेन दीव्यति खनति जयति जितम् — (Pā. 4-4-2) are called prāgdīvyatīya. Tasyedam — तस्येदम् — (Pā. 4-3-120) is one of those; here yañ is added; deva + jas, yañ, being a taddhitānta it has the name prātipadika and the sup is lost by luk; devasyedam; taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ — तद्धितेष्वचामादेः — (Pā. 7-2-117): vṛddhi of the first vowel before a ñit/ṇit taddhita, so e → ai; yasyeti ca drops the a of deva [as the print says]: daivya; the sixth case daivyasya; ñnityādir nityam gives the first-syllable acute. - upasthe (p. 150): ātaś copasarge kaḥ — आतश्चोपसर्गे कः — (Pā. 3-1-136): after a root ending in ā, with a preverb as upapada, the suffix ka; "in the sūtra supi sthaḥ the Śekhara says: idaṃ kevalopasargeṇa ātaś copasarga ity eva siddhe karmaṇy upapade 'pi na, āto 'nupa— ity ārambhāt — this [rule] is not for the case with a preverb alone, since that is already achieved by ātaś copasarge, nor for an object as upapada, because āto 'nupasarge… is begun" ("so it is said"; hence supi sthaḥ does not apply where only a preverb is present); upa + sthā + a; ato lopa iṭi ca — (Pā. 6-4-64): the ā is lost before a kit/ñit ārdhadhātuka suffix beginning with a vowel and before iṭ. Rik 5 ends here (|| 5 ||).

original pp. 150–154

Rik 6

Saṃhitā-pāṭha Reading note, written after viewing the Pada: the Saṃhitā prints the nasalised "-ām̐" in "upasthām̐"; the Pada's upa-sthā shows the base, the nasalisation being the Vedic rule noted in the grammar below. The last word is printed "cikētat" in the Saṃhitā and Pada alike.

ति॒स्रो द्यावः॑ सवि॒तुर्द्वा उ॒पस्थाँ॒ एका॑ य॒मस्य॒ भुव॑ने विरा॒षाट् । आ॒णिं न रथ्य॑म॒मृताधि॑ तस्थुरि॒ह ब्र॑वीतु॒ य उ॒ तच्चिके॑तत् ॥ ६ ॥

tisró dyā́vaḥ savitúr dvā upásthām̐ ékā yamásya bhúvane virāṣā́ṭ | āṇíṃ na ráthyam amṛ́tā́dhi tasthur ihá bravītu yá u tác cíketat || 6 ||

Pada-pāṭha

तिस्रः । द्यावः । सवितुः । द्वा । उपऽस्था । एका । यमस्य । भुवने । विराषाट् ॥ आणिम् । न । रथ्यम् । अमृता । अधि । तस्थुः । इह । ब्रवीतु । यः । ऊं इति । तत् । चिकेतत् ॥ ६ ॥

tisraḥ | dyāvaḥ | savituḥ | dvā | upa-sthā | ekā | yamasya | bhuvane | virāṣāṭ || āṇim | na | rathyam | amṛtā | adhi | tasthuḥ | iha | bravītu | yaḥ | ūṃ iti | tat | cikētat || 6 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

द्यावः स्वर्गोपलक्षिताः प्रकाशमाना लोकास्तिस्रस्त्रिसंख्याकाः सन्ति । तत्र द्वौ लोकौ सवितुः सूर्यस्योपस्था समीपस्थाने वर्तेते । द्युलोकभूलोकयोः सूर्येण प्रकाशितत्वात् । एका मध्यमा भूमिरन्तरिक्षलोको यमस्य भुवने पितृपतेर्गृहे विराषाट् । विरान् गन्त्यॄन् सहते । प्रेताः पुरुषा अन्तरिक्षमार्गेण यमलोके गच्छन्तीत्यर्थः । अमृतामृतानि चन्द्रनक्षत्रादीनि ज्योतींषि जलानि वाधि तस्थुः । सवितारमधिगम्य स्थितानि । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । रथ्यमाणिं न । रथाद्वहिरक्षच्छिद्रे प्रक्षिप्तः कीलविशेष आणिरित्युच्यते । रथसम्बन्धिनमाणिमधिगम्य यथा रथस्तिष्ठति तद्वत् । यस्तु मानवस्तत्सवितृरूपं चिकेतत् जानाति स मानव इहास्मिन्विषये ब्रवीतु । कथयतु । केनापि वक्तुमशक्यः सवितुर्महिमेत्यर्थः ॥

dyāvaḥ svargopalakṣitāḥ prakāśamānā lokās tisras trisaṃkhyākāḥ santi | tatra dvau lokau savituḥ sūryasyopasthā samīpasthāne vartete | dyulokabhūlokayoḥ sūryeṇa prakāśitatvāt | ekā madhyamā bhūmir antarikṣaloko yamasya bhuvane pitṛpater gṛhe virāṣāṭ | virān gantṝn sahate | pretāḥ puruṣā antarikṣamārgeṇa yamaloke gacchantīty arthaḥ | amṛtāmṛtāni candranakṣatrādīni jyotīṃṣi jalāni vādhi tasthuḥ | savitāram adhigamya sthitāni | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | rathyam āṇiṃ na | rathād vahir akṣacchidre prakṣiptaḥ kīlaviśeṣa āṇir ity ucyate | rathasambandhinam āṇim adhigamya yathā rathas tiṣṭhati tadvat | yas tu mānavas tat savitṛrūpaṃ cikētat jānāti sa mānava ihāsmin viṣaye bravītu | kathayatu | kenāpi vaktum aśakyaḥ savitur mahimety arthaḥ ||

Translation: "The dyāvaḥ — the shining worlds, indicated by the word 'heaven' — are tisraḥ, three in number. Of these, two worlds are upasthā — near — Savitṛ, the Sun: for heaven and earth are lit by the Sun. Ekā — the one, the middle earth, the mid-region — is virāṣāṭ — the one that carries — in yamasya bhuvane, in Yama's world, the house of the lord of the fathers: it overcomes (sahate) virān, those who go (gantṝn); that is, the dead go by the mid-region path to Yama's world. Amṛtā — the imperishable luminaries, the moon, the stars and the rest, or waters — adhi tasthuḥ — rest, having come to Savitṛ. The illustration: rathyam āṇiṃ na — a peg of a particular kind, driven into the hole in the axle outside the chariot, is called āṇi; as the chariot stands by reliance on its āṇi, so [they rest on Savitṛ]. But whichever man cikētat — [should] know that form of Savitṛ — let that man iha bravītu, in this matter speak, declare: Savitṛ's greatness cannot be told by anyone."

Grammar within the bhāṣya p. 151, characterized: tisraḥ (the ending is acute by tisṛbhyo jasaḥ [Pā. 6-1-166]); dvā (dvau, with āv-substitution and the loss of the v by lopaḥ śākalyasya); upasthā (the seventh-case ending replaced by āc — the vārtika āṅyājayārāṃ copasaṃkhyānam [M. 7-1-39-1]; prakṛtibhāva by ajo 'nunāsikaś chandasi [Pā. 6-1-126]); virāṣāṭ (vṛñ varaṇe, the suffix ka in the sense of ghañ [vārtika, Pā. 3-3-58-4], in the object sense; the Vedic i-substitution by bahulaṃ chandasi [Pā. 7-1-103]; chandasi sahaḥ [Pā. 3-2-63] gives ṇvi; saheḥ sāḍaḥ saḥ [Pā. 8-3-56] — the ṣatva, and the lengthening of the first member by anyeṣām api dṛśyate; "tathā sati vriyanta [?] iti virāḥ", so virān sahate); rathyam (rathasyedam; yat by rathād yat [Pā. 4-3-121]; initial-acute by yato 'nāvaḥ); amṛtā (śi lost by śeś chandasi bahulam); cikētat (root kita jñāne, leṭ, the augment aṭ; the i of the ending lost by itaś ca; ślu for śap, the root being juhotyādi-like; laghūpadha-guṇa; anudātte ca [Pā. 6-1-190], first-syllable acute of the abhyasta; and because of the connected word yaḥ the verb is not lowered, yadvṛttayogād anighātaḥ).

Pratipadārtha — "dyāvaḥ — the worlds beginning with heaven; tisraḥ — three (are there); dvā — the two, heaven and earth; savituḥ — of Savitṛ; upasthā — near [in the lap]; ekā — the one in the middle, the mid-region; yamasya — of Yama; bhuvane — in the world; virāṣāṭ — capable of bearing those who go (the dead); rathyam — of the chariot; āṇiṃ na — as the pin [that holds the axle-hole]; amṛtā — the imperishable masses of light, the moon, stars and the rest; adhi tasthuḥ — rest [on Savitṛ]; yaḥ — whichever man; tat — this nature of Savitṛ; cikētat — if he knows well; iha — in this matter; bravītu — let him describe."

Bhāvārtha — "Of the three worlds — heaven, earth, mid-region — heaven and earth are both near the Sun. The mid-region in the middle is the way for the dead to Yama's world. As a chariot rests upon the pin of its axle, the imperishable light-bearers, the moon, the stars and the rest, rest upon this Savitṛ. The nature of this Savitṛ cannot be grasped by man; if anyone does know it, let him describe the superhuman nature of the deity Savitṛ."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 152) — "There are three heavens ( three worlds ) two are in the proximity of the Savitri ; the remaining one leads men to Yama 's abode ; the immortal stars depend upon Savitri as a car upon the pin of the axle· Let him who knows the greatness of Savitri say so·" Printed so, with raised dots for full stops.

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 152 - tisro dyāvaḥ — "three heavens, that is, the earth-world, the mid-region world and the heaven-world." - savitur dvā upasthā — "since the Sun, staying in heaven, lights the earth, the heaven and the earth are said to be near the Sun." - yamasya bhuvane virāṣāṭ = pretāḥ puruṣā antarikṣamārgeṇa yamaloke gacchanti: "since dead people (or their souls) go to Yama's world by way of the third world, the mid-region, the mid-region is called the way to Yama's world." - āṇiṃ na — "the pins fixed in the holes at the ends of the chariot's axle, so that the wheels, as they turn, may not fall off. If these pins were not there, the wheels and the chariot would not move properly and would fall. Hence, as the pins are the support of the chariot and its wheels, the Sun, by giving light to the worlds of earth and heaven, is the support: such is the meaning." - amṛtā = amṛtāni candranakṣatrādīni jyotīṃṣi jalāni vā: "amṛta means 'not perishing', 'always existing'. Here the luminaries — the moon, the stars and the other lights — or waters that do not perish." - iha bravītu ya u tac cikētat — "let a man who knows this matter say it: that is, since this matter is exceedingly secret or deep, it is not known to anyone."

Rik 6 — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (pp. 153–154, PDF 168–169; grammar pages, noted briefly)

Kannada prose with sūtras quoted; the numerals are small and a number is given only where it could be read, otherwise the rule is named and left unnumbered.

  • tisraḥ (p. 153): tricaturoḥ striyāṃ tisṛcatasṛ — त्रिचतुरोः स्त्रियां तिस्वृचतस्वृ — [the print: tisṛ, catasṛ replace tri, catur in the feminine]; the substitute is final-acute by sthānivadbhāva; tisṛ + jas; aci ra ṛtaḥ — अचि र ऋतः — the ṛ of tisṛ/catasṛ becomes r before a vowel-initial ending; tisr + as; the yaṇ standing for an acute vowel would be svarita by udāttayaṇo hal-pūrvāt; as an exception to that comes tisṛbhyo jasaḥ — तिसृभ्यो जसः — the jas after tisṛ is acute; the plural "jasaḥ" in the sūtra is explained like the plural in ṛnnebhyo ṅīp, as a looseness of expression (śabdabāhulya): hence the ending is acute.
  • dvā: in the Saṃhitā a vowel follows (the u of upasthā), so dvau takes āv by eco 'yavāyāvaḥ — एचोऽयवायावः; lopaḥ śākalyasya — लोपः शाकल्यस्य —: by the opinion of Śākalya a word-final y/v preceded by a/ā is lost before a vowel: here v is lost; this loss is asiddha, so no vowel-sandhi follows.
  • upasthā: upa — "near" — tiṣṭhataḥ "those who stand": ātaś copasarge kaḥ — आतश्चोपसर्गे कः — gives ka; loss of ā; the seventh-case dual os; under supāṃ sulug… the print cites the vārtika āṅyājayārāṃ copasaṃkhyānam, that āṅ, ayāc, ayār are three substitutes of sup, so os → āṅ; upastha + ā, savarṇadīrgha; antādivac ca — अन्तादिवच्च — the single substitute counts as the end of the former and the beginning of the latter, quoted with the Śekhara-kāra's remark that the technical states (base, suffix etc.) of the elements remain after the single substitution; ajo 'nunāsikaś chandasi — in the Veda an ā-ending [here: the substitute āc] takes nasalisation and prakṛtibhāva: hence the Saṃhitā's upasthām̐.
  • virāṣāṭ: virān sahate — "[it] bears those who go"; vṛṅ varaṇe: grahavṛdṛniścigamaś ca — ग्रहवृदृनिश्चिगमश्च — (ap) and the Mahābhāṣya's remark on ghañarthe kavidhānam sthāsnāvyadhihaniyudhy… — "the suffix ka is prescribed in the sense of ghañ": the roots there named are examples, not a complete list, since ka may follow other roots too; with the sense of an action-noun and of an agent other than the agent of ghañ the ka here has the sense of an object; vṛ + a; bahulaṃ chandasi — i and u appear variably, so ṛ → ir with raparatva; vir + a, the suffix kit, so no guṇa; virān sahate iti virāṣāṭ: root ṣaha marṣaṇe, dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ; chandasi sahaḥ — छन्दसि सहः — ṇvi after sah when a sup-word is the upapada; ato 'ta upadhāyāḥ — vṛddhi; cuṭū and upadeśe 'janunāsika it give the it-names to ṇ, i; ver apṛktasya — loss of the v [of ṇvi]; anyeṣām api dṛśyate — lengthening of the first member: virāsāh; su lost by halṅyābbhyo…; hoḍhaḥ — हो ढः — h → ḍh; jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte; sahes sāḍaḥ — सहेः साडः — the ṣatva; carva: virāṣāṭ.
  • rathyam (p. 154): rathasyedam; rathād yat — रथाद्यत् — yat after the sixth-case form of ratha in the sense "this belongs to"; yasyeti ca drops the a; yato 'nāvaḥ — यतोऽनावः — first-syllable acute (two vowels).
  • cikētat: root kita jñāne; leṭ, tip, śap; kit + a + ti; itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu — loss of the i of the ending; leṭo 'ḍāṭau — the augment aṭ; juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ — śap → ślu; ślau — doubling; the final t of the reduplicate dropped; laghūpadha-guṇa; kuhoś cuḥ — k → c: cikētat. "In the Dhātupāṭha now at hand the reading is ki jñāne; then the augment t must be called Vedic." Anudātte ca (Pā. 6-1-190): the first syllable of the abhyasta is acute before an unaccented lasārvadhātuka; because the word yaḥ is connected, the verb is not lowered (yadvṛttayogād anighātaḥ). Rik 6 ends here (|| 6 ||).
original pp. 155–158

Rik 7

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

वि सु॑प॒र्णो अन्तरि॑क्षाण्यख्यद्गभीरवे॑पा असु॑रः सुनीथः । [accent ?] क्वे॑दानीं॒ सूर्यः कश्चि॒के॑त॒ कत॒मां द्यां॒ रश्मिरस्या त॑तान ॥ ७ ॥ [accent ?]

ví suparṇó antárikṣāṇy akhyad gabhīrávepā ásuraḥ sunīthaḥ | [accent ?] kvedānīṃ sū́ryaḥ kaś ciketa kátamā́ṃ dyāṃ ráśmir asyā́ tatāna || 7 || [accent ?]

Pada-pāṭha

वि । सुऽपर्णः । अन्तरिक्षाणि । अख्यत् । गभीरऽवेपाः । असुरः । सुऽनीथः ॥ क्व । इदानीम् । सूर्यः । कः । चिकेत । कतमाम् । द्याम् । रश्मिः । अस्य । आ । ततान ॥ ७ ॥

vi | su-parṇaḥ | antarikṣāṇi | akhyat | gabhīra-vepāḥ | asuraḥ | su-nīthaḥ || kva | idānīm | sūryaḥ | kaḥ | ciketa | katamām | dyām | raśmiḥ | asya | ā | tatāna || 7 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

सुपर्णः शोभनपतनः सूर्यस्य रश्मिः । सुपर्णा इति पञ्चदश रश्मिनामानीति तन्नामसु पठितत्वात् । अन्तरिक्षाण्यन्तरिक्षोपलक्षितानि लोकत्रयस्थानानि व्यख्यत् । विशेषेण ख्यापितवान् प्रकाशितवान् । कीदृशो रश्मिः । गभीरवेपा गम्भीरकम्पनः । रश्मेः प्रकम्पनं चलनं केनापि द्रष्टुमशक्यमित्यर्थः । असुरः सर्वेषां प्राणदः । तथा चान्यत्राम्नायते । सर्वेषां भूतानां प्राणानादायोदेतीति । सुनीथः सुनयनः शोभनप्रापणः । मार्गप्रकाशनेनाभीष्टदेशं प्रापयतीत्यर्थः । तादृशरश्मियुक्तः सूर्य इदानीं रात्रौ क्व कुत्र वर्तते । तदेतद्रहस्यं कश्चिकेत को जानाति । न कोऽपीत्यर्थः । अस्य सूर्यस्य रश्मिः कतमां द्यामा ततान । कं द्युलोकं रात्रौ व्याप्तवान् । एतदपि को जानाति ॥

suparṇaḥ śobhanapatanaḥ sūryasya raśmiḥ | suparṇā iti pañcadaśa raśminamānīti tannāmasu paṭhitatvāt | antarikṣāṇy antarikṣopalakṣitāni lokatrayasthānāni vy akhyat | viśeṣeṇa khyāpitavān prakāśitavān | kīdṛśo raśmiḥ | gabhīravepā gambhīrakampanaḥ | raśmeḥ prakampanaṃ calanaṃ kenāpi draṣṭum aśakyam ity arthaḥ | asuraḥ sarveṣāṃ prāṇadaḥ | tathā cānyatrāmnāyate | sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ prāṇān ādāyodetīti | sunīthaḥ sunayanaḥ śobhanaprāpaṇaḥ | mārgaprakāśanenābhīṣṭadeśaṃ prāpayatīty arthaḥ | tādṛśaraśmiyuktaḥ sūrya idānīṃ rātrau kva kutra vartate | tad etad rahasyaṃ kaś ciketa ko jānāti | na ko 'pīty arthaḥ | asya sūryasya raśmiḥ katamāṃ dyām ā tatāna | kaṃ dyulokaṃ rātrau vyāptavān | etad api ko jānāti ||

Translation: "Suparṇaḥ — [the one] with a beautiful flight — a ray of Sūrya ('suparṇāḥ' being read among the fifteen names of the ray in the lists of such names). Antarikṣāṇi — the three-world regions known by the name of the mid-region — vy akhyat — he made known specially, illuminated. What sort of ray? Gabhīravepāḥ — of deep quivering; the sense is that the quivering and movement of the ray cannot be seen by anyone. Asuraḥ — giver of life to all: as it is handed down elsewhere, 'taking the lives of all beings he rises' [?]. Sunīthaḥ — good-leading, good-conducting: by lighting the way he brings [a man] to the desired place. The Sun, who has such a ray, kva idānīm — where is he now, at night? That secret, kaḥ ciketa — who knows? No one, is the sense. Asya raśmiḥ katamāṃ dyām ā tatāna — what heaven has this Sun's ray spread over? What heaven-world has it pervaded at night? That too, who knows?"

Grammar within the bhāṣya pp. 155–156, characterized: suparṇaḥ (nañsubhyām — after su, a bahuvrīhi's later member is final-acute); gabhīravepāḥ (root ṭuvepṛ kampane, the Uṇādi suffix asun; a bahuvrīhi with first-member accent); asuraḥ (asu kṣepaṇe — "he throws away enemies", the Uṇādi suffix uran [āser uran, as read]; nit, so first-syllable acute; or "asūn rāti", "he gives breaths"; ātonupasarge kaḥ); sunīthaḥ (ṇīñ prāpaṇe; hanikuṣinīramikāśibhyaḥ kthan [Uṇādi, as read]; the accent as in thādi-suffixed words, the final syllable acute — prādisamāse thāthādinottarapadāntodāttatvam); idānīm (idamaḥ — idaṃśabdāt saptamyarthe dānīṃ ca [Pā. 5-3-18] — the suffix dānīm, the augment iś [in the print: igama], the substitution iśī for idam); sūryaḥ (root ṣū preraṇe; suvati iti sūryaḥ; by rājasūyasūryamṛṣodyarucyakupyakṛṣṭapacyāvyathyāḥ the suffix kyap with the rut augment is irregularly given; the suffix being unaccented, the first syllable has the root's acute); ciketa (root kita jñāne, liṭ); katamām (kiñjātīyām — vā bahūnāṃ jātiparipraśne ḍatamac [Pā. 5-3-93, as read]: ḍatamac after kim; ḍit, so loss of ṭi; cita, hence final-acute).

Pratipadārtha — "gabhīravepāḥ — having a deep quiver (vibration); asuraḥ — life-giving; sunīthaḥ — leading [one] well to the desired place; suparṇaḥ — [the ray] that spreads so well; sūryakiraṇa — the Sun's ray; antarikṣāṇi — the three worlds, the mid-region and the rest; vi akhyat — has lit up well; idānīm — now (in the night); sūryaḥ — the Sun (who has that ray); kva — where is he? kaḥ ciketa — who can know (no one can); asya — of the Sun; raśmiḥ — the ray; katamām dyām — which heaven; ā tatāna — has spread over (no one can know this)."

Bhāvārtha — "The ray of the Sun, which gives life to all, lit up all the three worlds at midday and guided everyone. At the time of sunset it was pleasing and gladdening by its deep tremble. But where is that same Sun, with his ray, wandering now, in the night? No man can say which heavens he is lighting."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 156) — "Suparna (ray of the sun) is quivering, life-giving and directed (towards the earth); It has illminated [sic] tbe [sic] (three) aerial regions· Where is surya (sun) now ? who knows to what heaven his rays have extended now ?" Printed so, with a raised dot after "regions" and a stray semicolon-spacing; "directed (towards the earth)" is the source's own insertion.

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), pp. 156–157 - suparṇaḥ — "since the word suparṇa is read among the fifteen names of the ray beginning 'bhedayaḥ kiraṇāḥ' (Ni. 2-15, as read), suparṇa means a ray of the Sun." - gabhīravepāḥ = gambhīrakampanaḥ: "deeply quivering. To the eye the Sun's rays appear to quiver as they pass through the atmosphere; hence the ṛṣi describes the Sun's rays as quivering." - asuraḥ = asu kṣepaṇe | asyati śatrūn ity asuraḥ | yadvā | asūn prāṇān rāti dadātīty asuraḥ: "the word asura is an adjective of suparṇa. The bhāṣyakāra gives it two senses: because it throws away enemies — because the Sun's ray puts away darkness — the Sun's ray is called asura; or asu is breath, and rā is the root meaning 'to give': it gives, by producing the food that living beings most need, the means of protecting their breaths, hence asura; life giving vital breath [the print's English]." - kva idānīṃ sūryaḥ — "In the daytime everyone sees the Sun shining; but at evening the Sun sets and rises again the next morning, and this too is known to people. But the ṛṣi, wondering where the Sun is in the period between his setting and his rising on the next day, that is, at night, asks this question in amazement. Since people did not know in those times how the movements of the earth, and day and night, come about, this matter may well have appeared marvellous." - kaś ciketa katamāṃ dyāṃ raśmir asyā tatāna — "at night, over what region (what other heaven) do the Sun's rays spread and make light? Who among men is able to know it? — so, struck with wonder, the ṛṣi asks himself, in praise of the unfathomable greatness of the Sun."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā p. 157, PDF 172 — grammar page, noted briefly; begun, to continue on p. 158 - suparṇaḥ: śobhanaṃ parṇaṃ patanaṃ yasya saḥ — "he whose flight [lit. leaf-wing] is beautiful", a bahuvrīhi; nañsubhyām — नञ्सुभ्याम् — (Pā. 6-2-172): the later member after nañ or su in a bahuvrīhi is final-acute, so parṇa is final-acute. - gabhīravepāḥ: ṭuvepṛ kampane; the Uṇādi asun, of the oṇādika group; gabhīraṃ vepo yasya saḥ, a bahuvrīhi; the first-member accent of the compound applies; gabhīra is final-acute. - asuraḥ: root asu kṣepaṇe; asyati ity asuraḥ — āser uran — आसेरुरन् — (Uṇ. 1-42): uran after asu; the suffix is nit, hence first-syllable acute; "another way of derivation can also be given" the page ends here; continues on p. 158.

Rik 7 — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā, concluded (p. 158, PDF 173; grammar page, noted briefly)

Numerals zoom-checked; rules whose printed number was not re-read are left unnumbered.

  • asuraḥ (concluded): second way: asūn = breaths, rāti = gives — "he gives his breaths", that is, he who sacrifices his own life in battle; the root rā with asu as upapada, and ātonupasarge kaḥ — आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः — (Pā. 3-2-3) the suffix ka; loss of the ā.
  • sunīthaḥ: root ṇīñ prāpaṇe; hanikuṣinīramikāśibhyaḥ kthan — हनिकुषिनीरमिकाशिभ्यः क्थन् — (Uṇ. 2-159): after five roots, han hiṃsāgatyoḥ, kuṣa niṣkarṣe, ṇīñ prāpaṇe, ramu krīḍāyām, kāśṛ dīptau, the suffix kthan; ṇo naḥ — णो नः — (Pā. 6-1-65) the initial ṇ of the root becomes n beforehand; ni + tha, the suffix being kit there is no guṇa; kugatiprādayaḥ — a prādi compound with su; thāthaghañktājabitrakāṇām (Pā. 6-2-144) — the word ending in such a suffix after a gati or an upapada is final-acute.
  • idānīm: dānīṃ ca — दानीं च — (Pā. 5-3-18) a time-denoting idam, in the seventh case, takes the suffix dānīm in its own sense; idam + ṅi + dānīm; the ṅi, as part of a taddhitānta base, is lost by supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ (Pā. 2-4-71); idama iś — इदम इश् — (Pā. 5-3-3) iś replaces idam before a suffix of the prāgdiśīya class; iś is śit, so by anekālśit sarvasya — अनेकाल्शित्सर्वस्य — it replaces the whole of idam; iś + dānīm; by the suffix-accent dā is acute.
  • sūryaḥ: root ṣū preraṇe; suvati = prerayati — "he who impels people to their several works"; rājasūyasūryamṛṣodyarucyakupyakṛṣṭapacyāvyathyāḥ — the suffix kyap with the augment rut is irregularly (nipātana) given in this rule; ṣ → s; kyap is pit, so unaccented, and sū keeps the root's accent.
  • ciketa: root kita jñāne, juhotyādi; liṭ; liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya — doubling: kit + kit; the final t of the reduplicate lost; k → c; ci + kit; laghūpadha-guṇa; liṭ → ta; the print remarks that the form with e instead of what liṭas tajhayor eśirec (Pā. 3-4-81) teaches is Vedic.
  • katamām: vā bahūnāṃ jātiparipraśne ḍatamac — वा बहूनां जातिपरिप्रश्ने डतमच् — the Mahābhāṣya rejects the words jātiparipraśne as unnecessary; when one is to be chosen among many, ḍatamac after kim, yat, tat; ḍit, so the ṭi (im) is lost, leaving atama; ka + tama; the suffix is cit, so the word is final-acute. Rik 7 ends here (|| 7 ||).
original pp. 159–160

Rik 8

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

अ॒ष्टौ व्य॑ख्यत्क॒कुभः॑ पृथि॒व्यास्त्री ध॒न्व योज॑ना स॒प्त सिन्धू॑न् । हि॒र॒ण्या॒क्षः स॑वि॒ता दे॒व आगा॒द्दध॒द्र॑त्ना दा॒शुषे॒ वार्या॑णि ॥ ८ ॥

aṣṭáu vy akhyat kakúbhaḥ pṛthivyā́s trī dhánva yójanā saptá síndhūn | hiraṇyākṣáḥ savitā́ devá āgād dádhad ratnā dāśúṣe vā́ryāṇi || 8 ||

Pada-pāṭha

अष्टौ । वि । अख्यत् । ककुभः । पृथिव्याः । त्री । धन्व । योजना । सप्त । सिन्धून् ॥ हिरण्यऽअक्षः । सविता । देवः । आ । अगात् । दधत् । रत्ना । दाशुषे । वार्याणि ॥ ८ ॥

aṣṭau | vi | akhyat | kakubhaḥ | pṛthivyāḥ | trī | dhanva | yojanā | sapta | sindhūn || hiraṇya-akṣaḥ | savitā | devaḥ | ā | agāt | dadhat | ratnā | dāśuṣe | vāryāṇi || 8 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

पृथिव्याः सम्बन्धिनीरष्टौ ककुभः प्राच्याद्याश्चतस्रो दिश आग्नेय्याद्याश्चतस्रो विदिश इत्येवमष्टौ दिशो व्यख्यत् । सविता प्रकाशितवान् । तथा योजना प्राणिनः स्वस्वभोगेन योजयितॄन्धन्व अन्तरिक्षोपलक्षितान् त्री त्रिसंख्याकान् पृथिव्यादिलोकान् सप्त सिन्धून् गङ्गादिनदीः समुद्रान्वा सविता व्यख्यत् । हिरण्याक्षः हितरमणीयचक्षुर्युक्तो हिरण्मयाक्षो वा सविता देव आगात् । इहागच्छतु । किं कुर्वन् । दाशुषे हविर्दत्तवते यजमानाय वार्याणि वरणीयानि रत्नानि दधत् । प्रयच्छन् ॥

pṛthivyāḥ sambandhinīr aṣṭau kakubhaḥ prācyādyāś catasro diśa āgneyyādyāś catasro vidiśa ity evam aṣṭau diśo vy akhyat | savitā prakāśitavān | tathā yojanā prāṇinaḥ svasvabhogena yojayitṝn dhanva antarikṣopalakṣitān trī trisaṃkhyākān pṛthivyādilokān sapta sindhūn gaṅgādinadīḥ samudrān vā savitā vy akhyat | hiraṇyākṣaḥ hitaramaṇīyacakṣur yukto hiraṇmayākṣo vā savitā deva āgāt | ihāgacchatu | kiṃ kurvan | dāśuṣe havir dattavate yajamānāya vāryāṇi varaṇīyāni ratnāni dadhat | prayacchan ||

Translation: "The eight kakubhaḥ of the earth — the four directions beginning with the east, and the four intermediate directions beginning with the south-east: thus the eight directions — Savitṛ vy akhyat, illuminated. Likewise yojanā — [the worlds that] join the creatures each to their own enjoyment; dhanva, marked by the mid-region; trī, three in number, the worlds, earth and the rest; and the sapta sindhūn — the seven rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā, or the seas — Savitṛ made known. Hiraṇyākṣaḥ — having eyes that are good and pleasing, or having golden eyes — Savitṛ the god āgāt — let him come here. Doing what? To dāśuṣe — the sacrificer who has given the oblation — dadhat, bestowing vāryāṇi, choice, desirable ratnā, gems."

Grammar within the bhāṣya pp. 159–160, characterized: akhyat (khyātelṛjyasyativaktītyādi — cli → aṅ); trī (śi lost by śeś chandasi bahulam); dhanva (rivi ravi dhavi gatyarthāḥ; the nasal augment for an idit root; the Uṇādi suffix kanin [kanin yuvṛṣitakṣarājidhanvidyupratidivaḥ]; the sup ending replaced by luk; na lopaḥ; nit, so first-syllable acute); yojanā (yojayanti prāṇina upabhogeneti yojanāni — "that which join creatures by enjoyment"; lyu by the nandyādi rule; ṇer aniṭi — loss of ṇi; śi lost); hiraṇyākṣaḥ (hiraṇmayāny akṣīṇi yasya, a bahuvrīhi; bahuvrīhau sakthyakṣṇoḥ svāṅgāt ṣac — Pā. 5-4-113 — the compound-final suffix ṣac); āgāt (eteluṅo gā luṅi — gā substituted for i; gātisthā… — luk of sic; Pā. 2-4-45 cited for gā); dadhat (śatṛ; nābhyastācchatuḥ — no num; śnābhyastayor ātaḥ — loss of ā; abhyastānām ādiḥ); dāśuṣe (dāśvān sāhvān mīḍhvāṃś ca — kvasu by nipātana; in the fourth singular vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam; śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca — ṣatva); vāryāṇi (vṛñ sambhaktau; ṛhaloṇyat; ādyudātta as in īḍavandavṛśaṃsaduhāṃ ṇyataḥ).

Pratipadārtha — "savitā — the deity Savitṛ; pṛthivyāḥ — of the earth; aṣṭau kakubhaḥ — the eight directions (four directions and four intermediate directions); yojanā — joining the living beings to their experience of their dealings; dhanva — containing the mid-region; trī — the three worlds beginning with earth; sapta sindhūn — the seven rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā (or the seven seas); vi akhyat — he lit up well; hiraṇyākṣaḥ — golden-eyed (or having eyes that are beneficial and pleasing); devaḥ — the shining Savitṛ; dāśuṣe — to the sacrificer who gives the oblation; vāryāṇi — desired gems; dadhat — giving; āgāt — let him come here."

Bhāvārtha — "The shining Savitṛ lit up the eight directions of the earth, the three worlds, earth and the others, that join beings to their several dealings and experiences, and the seven rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā, as also the seven seas, with his rays. His eyes are made of gold; they are beneficial to all, and pleasing. May Savitṛ, bright and golden-eyed, come to this sacrificial ground, granting the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice and gives the oblation the riches he desires."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 160) — "He has lighted up the eight quarters (points) of the earth, the three regions of living beings and the seven rivers (or seven Seas); may the golden-eyed Savitri come hither bestowing upon the offerer of the oblation, desirable riches·" .

Rik 8 — Special Topics and grammar (pp. 161–163, PDF 176–178; grammar pages, noted briefly)

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 161 - aṣṭau kakubhaḥ pṛthivyāḥ — "the eight directions: the four, east, west, south, north, and the four intermediate directions, south-east, south-west, north-west, north-east — together eight directions. Eight points of the Horizon [the print's English]." - trī — "the three worlds, earth, mid-region and heaven." - sapta sindhūn — "the seven rivers, Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī, Śutudrī, Paruṣṇī, Asiknī, Vitastā, or the seven seas." Vitastā stands here where the list at Rik 6 of Sūkta 34 gave Marudvṛdhā; recorded as printed. - hiraṇyākṣaḥ = hitaramaṇīyacakṣur yuktaḥ | athavā hiraṇmayāny akṣiṇī yasyāsau hiraṇyākṣaḥ: "one who has eyes pleasant to look at, beautiful; or one with eyes as beautiful as gold." - vāryāṇi = varaṇīyāni: "wished for by all, needed by all, desirable &c. [the print's English]."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā - akhyat (p. 161): "explained in the fifth mantra of this same sūkta" (Rik 5 above). - trī: after tri in the neuter, śas, replaced by śi, which has the name sarvanāmasthāna; the augment num; the lengthening of the penultimate; trīn + śi; by śeś chandasi bahulam the śi is dropped, and the n is lost. - dhanva: the root rivi ravi dhavi, with the sense of going, idit; idito num dhātoḥ — the augment num gives dhanv; kanin yuvṛṣitakṣarājidhanvidyupratidivaḥ — (Uṇ. 1-154) — the suffix kanin after these roots; dhanv + an; supāṃ sulug…: luk of the śas; nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya: loss of n; kanin is nit, so the first syllable is acute. - yojanā (pp. 161–162): root yujir yoge; yojayanti ("they join [creatures to their enjoyments]") — yojayatīti yojanā; nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ — the suffix lyu; yuvor anākau — ana for yu; ṇer aniṭi — loss of ṇi before an ārdhadhātuka without iṭ; laghūpadha-guṇa; after the stem yojana, śas, replaced by śi, and the loss of śi etc. as before. - hiraṇyākṣaḥ (p. 162): hiraṇyāny akṣīṇi yasya saḥ — "he who has golden eyes"; the form is hiraṇyākṣan [before the suffix]; bahuvrīhau sakthyakṣṇoḥ svāṅgāt ṣac — बहुव्रीहौ सक्थ्यक्ष्णोः स्वाङ्गात्षच् — the suffix ṣac, a compound-final (samāsānta) and taddhita, after a bahuvrīhi ending in sakthi or akṣi which denotes a svāṅga ("own limb"). The print then gives the definition of svāṅga in a verse:

अद्रवं मूर्तिमत्स्वाङ्गं प्राणिस्थमविकारजम् । अतत्स्थं तत्र दृष्टं च तेन चेत्तत्तथायुतम् ॥

adravaṃ mūrtimat svāṅgaṃ prāṇistham avikārajam | atatsthaṃ tatra dṛṣṭaṃ ca tena cet tat tathāyutam ||

"A non-fluid, bodily thing located in a living being and not born of a change [is svāṅga]; and also that which is not located there but is seen there, if it is likewise joined with it." Translation editorial and tentative; the verse is read as printed. The Kannada explains the three marks: it must be a non-liquid (adrava) thing of solid form (mūrtimat) belonging to the living being from its nature, not arising from a change; and the second mark covers what is no longer in a living being but was once, as hair lying in the street (the print's example: sukeśī rathyā), or what is joined in the manner of one in a living being, as the breasts of an image. Here the eye (akṣi) is a body-part and so svāṅga; hiraṇyākṣin + a; nastaddhite — नस्तद्धिते — the ṭi of an aṅga ending in n and bearing the name bha is lost before a taddhita suffix: so in is lost; the final syllable acute. - āgāt: iṇ gatau, luṅ; iṇo gā luṅi — before luṅ, gā replaces iṇ; gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu: luk of sic; loss of the i of tip by itaś ca. - dadhat (pp. 162–163): root ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ, laṭ, śatṛ; śap → ślu; doubling: dhā + dhā + at; hrasvaḥ: the reduplicate is shortened; abhyāse carca: dh → d of the reduplicate; śnābhyastayor ātaḥ — the ā of a base in śnā or an abhyasta base is lost before a kit/ñit sārvadhātuka suffix (here śatṛ, treated as ñit): so dadh + at; nābhyastācchatuḥ — no num for śatṛ after an abhyasta; since supi follows, ugidacām… would give num, but it is prevented; loss of the ending [su]; ubhe abhyastam — the two repeated parts together are abhyasta; abhyastānām ādiḥ: first-syllable acute. - dāśuṣe (p. 163): dāśvān sāhvān mīḍhvāṃś ca — दाश्वान्साह्वान्मीढ्वांश्च — the forms are irregular: dāś dāne with kvasu, with the absence of doubling and of iṭ by nipātana (against liṭi dhātoḥ…); in sāhvān the root ṣaha marṣaṇe, parasmaipada, with kvasu, no doubling, no iṭ, and lengthened penultimate; in mīḍhvān the root miha secane, with kvasu, lack of doubling and of iṭ; after dāśvas the fourth singular ṅe: dāśvas + e; vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam — the v of a base ending in vas [with the name bha] becomes u, with pūrvarūpa; dāśus + e; ādeśapratyayayoḥ — s that is part of a suffix → ṣ; the print adds that in śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca the roots [śās, vas, ghas, sī…] are meant by association, not the suffix, so the ṣatva of that rule cannot arise here — "the sense is clear in the Śekhara and similar works". - vāryāṇi: vṛñ sambhaktau; ṛhaloṇyat — ऋहलोर्ण्यत् — ṇyat after a root ending in ṛ or in a consonant; vṛ + ya; aco ñṇiti — vṛddhi: vārya; īḍavandavṛśaṃsaduhāṃ ṇyataḥ — ईडवन्दवृशंसदुहां ण्यतः — the first syllable of a word in ṇyat from these roots is acute; the sūtra names vṛ, not vṛñ, so — since vṛñ would otherwise take kyap by ētisstuśāsvṛdṛjuṣaḥ kyap — the vārtika vṛñaḥ grahaṇaṃ kartavyam ("vṛñ must be taken in") is cited; and in īḍavanda… the word vṛ is held to mean the root vṛñ; otherwise ṇyat would not apply. Rik 8 ends here (|| 8 ||). The ninth ṛk is the second Jagatī of the sūkta, per the introduction on p. 131.

original pp. 163–165

Rik 9

Saṃhitā-pāṭha As printed, several expected underlines — after अपामीवां, बाधते, वेति, कृष्णेन — are absent; only the marks seen are given.

हिर॑ण्यपाणिः सवि॒ता विच॑र्षणिरु॒भे द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी अ॒न्तरी॑यते । अपामी॑वां बाध॑ते वेति सूर्य॑म॒भि कृष्णेन॒ रज॑सा॒ द्यामृ॑णोति ॥ ९ ॥

híraṇyapāṇiḥ savitā́ vícarṣaṇir ubhé dyā́vāpṛthivī́ antárīyate | apā́mīvāṃ bā́dhate veti sū́ryam abhí kṛṣṇena rájasā dyā́m ṛṇoti || 9 ||

Pada-pāṭha

हिरण्यऽपाणिः । सविता । विऽचर्षणिः । उभे इति । द्यावापृथिवी इति । अन्तः । ईयते ॥ अप । अमीवाम् । बाधते । वेति । सूर्यम् । अभि । कृष्णेन । रजसा । द्याम् । ऋणोति ॥ ९ ॥

hiraṇya-pāṇiḥ | savitā | vi-carṣaṇiḥ | ubhe iti | dyāvāpṛthivī iti | antaḥ | īyate || apa | amīvām | bādhate | veti | sūryam | abhi | kṛṣṇena | rajasā | dyām | ṛṇoti || 9 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

हिरण्यपाणिः सुवर्णमयहस्तयुक्तः । यद्वा । यजमानेभ्यो दातुं हिरण्यं हस्ते धृतवान् । विचर्षणिर्विविधदर्शनयुक्तः । विचर्षणिः पश्यतीत्यर्थः । विचर्षणिर्विश्वचर्षणिरिति तन्नामसु पाठात् । सविता देव उभे द्यावापृथिवी अन्तः उभयोर्लोकयोर्मध्य ईयते । गच्छति । अमीवां रोगादिबाधामप बाधते । सम्यग्निराकरोति । तथा । सूर्यं वेति गच्छति । यद्यपि सवितृसूर्ययोरेकदेवतात्वं तथापि मूर्तिभेदेन गन्तृगन्तव्यभावः । कृष्णेन तमसः कर्षकेण निवर्तकेन रजसा तेजसा द्यामाकाशमभ्यृणोति । सर्वतो व्याप्नोति ॥

hiraṇyapāṇiḥ suvarṇamayahastayuktaḥ | yadvā | yajamānebhyo dātuṃ hiraṇyaṃ haste dhṛtavān | vicarṣaṇir vividhadarśanayuktaḥ | vicarṣaṇiḥ paśyatīty arthaḥ | vicarṣaṇir viśvacarṣaṇir iti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | savitā deva ubhe dyāvāpṛthivī antaḥ ubhayor lokayor madhya īyate | gacchati | amīvāṃ rogādibādhām apa bādhate | samyag nirākaroti | tathā | sūryaṃ veti gacchati | yadyapi savitṛsūryayor ekadevatātvaṃ tathāpi mūrtibhedena gantṛgantavyabhāvaḥ | kṛṣṇena tamasaḥ karṣakeṇa nivartakena rajasā tejasā dyām ākāśam abhyṛṇoti | sarvato vyāpnoti ||

Translation: "Hiraṇyapāṇiḥ — having golden hands; or, holding gold in his hand to give to the sacrificers. Vicarṣaṇiḥ — endowed with varied seeing, i.e. 'he sees': since vicarṣaṇiḥ, viśvacarṣaṇiḥ is read in the lists of such names. Savitṛ the god īyate, goes, antaḥ, in the midst of the two worlds, ubhe dyāvāpṛthivī. Amīvām — the affliction of disease and the like — apa bādhate, he drives away completely. Likewise sūryaṃ veti — he goes to Sūrya: although Savitṛ and Sūrya are one deity, there is yet the relation of goer and goal, by a difference of form. Kṛṣṇena rajasā — with the radiance that draws away, that removes, the darkness — dyām, the sky, abhi ṛṇoti, he pervades on all sides."

Grammar within the bhāṣya p. 164, characterized: dyāvāpṛthivī (divasaś ca pṛthivyām — the word ca carries dyāvā as the substitute of div before pṛthivī in a dvandva of deity-names; devatādvandve ca gives both members their natural accent; the rule on a following unaccented second member does not bar it); īyate (īṅ gatau; the tiṅ is lowered by tiṅ ṅatiṅaḥ); bādhate ca vā iti (the sense of ca is understood though the word ca is not used, so by cādilope vibhāṣā the lowering [nighāta] is not applied); veti (vī gatiprajanakāntyasanakhādaneṣu; śap lost by adādi; tip is pit, so unaccented and the root's accent stays; though sūryam is a second-case word, the tiṅ [veti] stands after it, so there is no lowering of the verb); ṛṇoti (ṛṇu gatau, tanādi; of the tanādi roots only kṛ takes guṇa, as śali… ut-ness; so no guṇa here).

Pratipadārtha — "hiraṇyapāṇiḥ — with golden hands (or holding gold in the hand, to give it to the sacrificer); vicarṣaṇiḥ — of varied seeing (able to look at what has been, is, and will be); savitā — the Savitṛ deity; ubhe dyāvāpṛthivī — of the two worlds, earth and mid-region; antaḥ — in the middle; īyate — moves about; amīvām — the afflictions of disease and the like; apa bādhate — destroys completely; sūryam — to the Sun's neighbourhood; veti — goes; kṛṣṇena — [that which] removes darkness; rajasā — with radiance; dyām — the sky; abhi ṛṇoti — pervades all round."

Bhāvārtha — "The Savitṛ deity's hands are of gold, or he always holds gold in his hand to give to the sacrificer. He can see everything, and can behold past, future and present. This Savitṛ moves in the middle of the two worlds, earth and mid-region. He destroys completely disease and troubles of that kind. He goes also to the neighbourhood of the Sun, who is of a different form from himself; and with his divine radiance, which removes the darkness, he pervades the whole sky."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 165) — "The golden-handed, all seeing Savitri travels between heaven and earth, dispels diseases, approaches the sun, and ascends the heaven through the dark regions of space·" .

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 165 begun; continued on p. 166 - hiraṇyapāṇiḥ = suvarṇamayahastayuktaḥ | yadvā | yajamānebhyo dātuṃ hiraṇyaṃ haste dhṛtavān: "one who has golden hands, or one who holds gold in his hand in order to give it to sacrificers. We have explained this word in detail in Ṛgveda Saṃhitā Part 3, pages 75 and 76." - vicarṣaṇiḥ = viśeṣeṇa draṣṭā athavā viśvasya bhuvanasya draṣṭā: "the one who sees specially, or who sees the whole universe. There is nothing that is not seen by the Sun's eye; that is, the sense is that the Sun's rays pervade the whole world." The rest of the Special Topics and the grammar of Rik 9 follow on p. 166 and later pages, to be viewed next.

Rik 9 — Special Topics concluded and grammar (pp. 166–168, PDF 181–183; grammar pages, noted briefly)

Special Topics, continued from p. 165 (p. 166) - ubhe dyāvāpṛthivī antar īyate — "below the earth, above heaven: [he] moves between these worlds, by the path of the mid-region; such is the meaning." - amīvām apa bādhate — "one who destroys disease and the like. It is the opinion of the physicians that the Sun's rays have the power to remove many illnesses. On this matter the ṛk:"

हृद्रोगं मम सूर्य हरिमाणं च नाशय । (ऋ. सं. १-५०-११)

hṛdrogaṃ mama sūrya harimāṇaṃ ca nāśaya | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-50-11)

"— 'destroy my heart-disease and my jaundice, O Sūrya' — so Praskaṇva, the ṛṣi of that sūkta, prays to the Sun. That the Sun's light is indispensable to the life of living beings and of plants, and that without the Sun beings and plants could not live on the earth, even ordinary people know well." Translation of the ṛk editorial and tentative; reference 1-50-11 zoom-checked. - sūryam abhi — "Here the bhāṣyakāra says 'yady api savitṛsūryayor ekadevatātvaṃ tathāpi mūrtibhedena gantṛgantavyabhāvaḥ' (he is both the goer and the goal by a difference of form); that is, though Sūrya and Savitṛ are one deity, by a difference of form one may be said to go to the neighbourhood of the other: this is the reconciliation he offers. In explaining the word sūrya Yāska says 'sūryaḥ sarter vā suvater vā svīryater vā' (no Nirukta number printed). Of these three explanations, svīryater vā means su-pūrvasya vā īrayater gatyarthasya — 'one who moves well, or swiftly'. If this sense is taken in this ṛk, it will be right to say that the Sun, moving swiftly in the mid-region, goes towards the world of heaven." Translation of the Nirukta quotation editorial and tentative. - kṛṣṇena rajasā — "the mid-region through which the Sun travels is full of darkness. The Sun lights up everything by his own light."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā - dyāvāpṛthivī (pp. 166–167): dyauś ca pṛthivī ca, a dvandva; divasaś ca pṛthivyām — दिवसश्च पृथिव्याम् — the ca carries on the preceding rule's divo dyāvā, so dyāvā is the substitute of div [the print notes the svarita-announcement, svaritatvapratijñā, so divaḥ continues]; in a dvandva with pṛthivī as second member, div is replaced by divas or dyāvā; here dyāvā, which is first-syllable acute by nipātana; devatādvandve ca — देवताद्वन्द्वे च — in a dvandva of deity-names both members keep their natural accent together, i.e. the accent they had before stays; the print adds that there is no vyatyāsa of this [i.e. no reversal]. Pṛthivī: pratheḥ ṣivan saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca — प्रथेः षिवन् संप्रसारणं च — [Uṇ. 1-[?]] — after prath prakhyāne the suffix ṣivan, with saṃprasāraṇa of the base: pṛthivi; ṣiddhaurādibhyaś ca — ṅīṣ; the word is final-acute by the suffix; the pṛ is unaccented by the śeṣa-nighāta; the print then argues that the prohibition notarapade 'nudāttādau — नोत्तरपदेऽनुदात्तादौ — (the rule that a second member beginning with an unaccented syllable stops the natural accent of both members) might be thought to apply, but that rule itself says apṛthivīrudrapūṣamanthiṣu — "except for pṛthivī, rudra, pūṣan, manthin" — so it does not apply here, where pṛthivī is the second member. - īyate (p. 167): root īṅ gatau, 4th class; the root is ṅit, so anudāttaṅita ātmanepadam — the ātmanepada; laṭ → ta; ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere gives e; divādibhyaḥ śyan; kṅiti ca bars guṇa; tiṅ ṅatiṅaḥ makes the verb wholly unaccented. - amīvām: root amu roge; śīvayeśajihvāgrīvāpyāmīvāḥ — (Uṇ. 1-153) — the suffix van, with the augment īṭ, irregularly; ṭāp; accusative singular am, pūrvarūpa. - bādhate: "although the sense of ca is understood — 'he destroys disease, and goes to the Sun, though of a different form' — the word ca is not used; so by cādilope vibhāṣā there is a prohibition of the wholly-unaccented accent of the verb." - veti: root vī gatiprajanakāntyasanakhādaneṣu; laṭ, tip, śap; ādiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ: luk of śap; guṇa; tip is pit and so unaccented; the root's own accent stays; this is the second tiṅanta of the sentence, so cādilope is not applicable; but since it stands after the tiṅanta bādhate, the lowering by tiṅ ṅatiṅaḥ does not arise (it requires a non-tiṅ before). - ṛṇoti (pp. 167–168): root ṛṇu gatau, tanādi; laṭ, tip; tanādikṛñbhya uḥ — तनादिकृञ्भ्य उः — the suffix u; with this u as the cause laghūpadha-guṇa would arise; the teachers Ātreya, Āpiśali and others, by saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ (Paribhā. 95), hold that guṇa does not arise in the tanādi; by their opinion no guṇa here. Or, following bahulam etannidarśanam, the root ṛ is read in the svādi class, and svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ gives the śnu of the vikaraṇa, an apit sārvadhātuka and so ṅit; kṅiti ca prevents guṇa; the result is ṛṇoti. Rik 9 ends here (|| 9 ||).

Rik 10

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

हिर॑ण्यहस्तो॒ असु॑रः सुनी॒थः सु॑मृळी॒कः स्ववाँ॑ यात्व॒र्वाङ् । अ॒प॒सेध॑न्र॒क्षसो॑ यातु॒धाना॒नस्था॑द्दे॒वः प्र॑तिदो॒षं गृ॑णानः ॥ १० ॥

híraṇyahasto ásuraḥ sunītháḥ sumṛḷīkáḥ svávām̐ yātv arvā́ṅ | apasédhan rakṣáso yātudhā́nān ásthād deváḥ pratidoṣáṃ gṛṇānaḥ || 10 || As printed, no underline is seen under णा of गृणानः. Reading note, written after viewing the Pada on the same page: the Saṃhitā's "svavām̐ yātv arvāṅ" is the Pada's sva-vān | yātu | arvāṅ joined by sandhi, with the Vedic nasalised ām̐ before a vowel-initial word.

Pada-pāṭha

हिरण्यऽहस्तः । असुरः । सुऽनीथः । सुऽमृळीकः । स्वऽवान् । यातु । अर्वाङ् ॥ अपऽसेधन् । रक्षसः । यातुऽधानान् । अस्थात् । देवः । प्रतिऽदोषम् । गृणानः ॥ १० ॥

hiraṇya-hastaḥ | asuraḥ | su-nīthaḥ | su-mṛḷīkaḥ | sva-vān | yātu | arvāṅ || apa-sedhan | rakṣasaḥ | yātu-dhānān | asthāt | devaḥ | prati-doṣam | gṛṇānaḥ || 10 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

हिरण्यहस्तोऽसुरः प्राणदाता सुनीथः सुष्ठु नेता । प्रशस्य इत्यर्थः । सुनीथः पाक इति प्रशस्यनामसु पाठात् । सुमृळीकः सुष्ठु सुखयिता स्ववान् धनवान् अर्वाङ् अभिमुखः कर्मदेशे गच्छतु । किंचायं देवः प्रतिदोषं प्रतिरात्रि गृणानः स्तूयमानोऽस्थात् । स्थितवान् । किं कुर्वन् । रक्षसो बाधकत्वेन रक्षणनिमित्तभूतान् । रक्षो रक्षितव्यमस्मादिति यास्कः । नि. ४-१८ । यातुधानानसुरानपसेधन् निराकुर्वन् ॥

hiraṇyahasto 'suraḥ prāṇadātā sunīthaḥ suṣṭhu netā | praśasya ity arthaḥ | sunīthaḥ pāka iti praśasyanāmasu pāṭhāt | sumṛḷīkaḥ suṣṭhu sukhayitā svavān dhanavān arvāṅ abhimukhaḥ karmadeśe gacchatu | kiṃcāyaṃ devaḥ pratidoṣaṃ pratirātri gṛṇānaḥ stūyamāno 'sthāt | sthitavān | kiṃ kurvan | rakṣaso bādhakatvena rakṣaṇanimittabhūtān | rakṣo rakṣitavyam asmād iti yāskaḥ | ni. 4-18 | yātudhānān asurān apasedhan nirākurvan ||

Translation: "Hiraṇyahastaḥ — golden-handed; asuraḥ — the giver of life; sunīthaḥ — good leader, i.e. praiseworthy, since sunīthaḥ is read among the names for 'praiseworthy'; sumṛḷīkaḥ — the one who gives good happiness; svavān — possessed of wealth: let him come arvāṅ — facing us, to the place of the rite. Moreover this god, being praised every night (pratidoṣam), asthāt — has stood [here]. Doing what? Rakṣasaḥ — [driving away those] who, by being injurers, are the occasion for [our] need of protection ('rakṣas, that from which [one] must be protected', so Yāska, Ni. 4-18); yātudhānān, the asuras — apasedhan, keeping off, driving away."

Grammar within the bhāṣya p. 169, characterized: "hiraṇyahasta and the like are as before"; sumṛḷīkaḥ (suṣṭhu mṛḷīkaṃ sukhaṃ yasyāsau, nañsubhyām — final-acute of the later member); svavān (svam asyāsti; matup, with m → v by mādupadhāyāḥ (iti vatvam); the n in the Saṃhitā becomes ru by dīrghād aṭi samānapāde, the ā is nasalised by āto 'ṭi nityam, and the ru becomes y (ror yatvam, yalopaś ca)); apasedhan (ṣidhu gatyām; śap pit so unaccented; śatṛ and the lasārvadhātuka accent keeps the compound's later member's natural accent); rakṣasaḥ (rakṣa pālane; the Uṇādi asun; or rakṣyate 'neneti rakṣaḥ, "strength", karaṇe 'sun; the loss of the possessive suffix is Vedic; accent by the suffix); yātudhānān (yata nikāropaskārayoḥ — "to oppose, to prepare"; the Uṇādi suffix; yātanā — torments — dhīyante eṣu, "in whom torments are placed"; adhikaraṇe lyuṭ; the accent of what precedes a lit suffix); asthāt (gātisthā… luk of sic); pratidoṣam (prati in the sense of repetition, with an avyayībhāva: "night by night"); gṛṇānaḥ (gṝ śabde; laṭ in the passive, śānac; śnā by vyatyaya; the shortening of ṛ (pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ); final-acute by cit).

Pratipadārtha — "hiraṇyahastaḥ — golden-handed (or holding gold in the hand to give to the sacrificer); asuraḥ — life-giver; sunīthaḥ — praiseworthy because he leads [one] to the desired place by showing the way; sumṛḷīkaḥ — full of great delight (or giving joy); svavān — Savitṛ, the wealthy; arvāṅ — facing the sacrificial place (let him walk); devaḥ — the god Savitṛ; pratidoṣam — every night; gṛṇānaḥ — being praised; rakṣasaḥ — the injurious; yātudhānān — the rākṣasas; apasedhan — warding off and driving away; asthāt — he stands [at the sacrificial place]."

Bhāvārtha — "The hands of the Savitṛ deity are of gold; or he always holds gold in his hand to give to the sacrificer. He gives breath to all living beings. By showing light to all and guiding them, he gives joy to all. May such a rich Savitṛ walk towards the sacrificial ground — for at the sacrificial place the injury done by the rākṣasas is great. If one praises the Savitṛ deity well every night, he, pleased by that praise, stands at the sacrificial ground and, driving off the injuring rākṣasas, remains there."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 170) — "May the golden-handed Savitri, the excellent guide, the giver of happiness and possessor of riches come to this sacrifice ; praised by men he drives off the harmful Rukshasas every night·" Printed so, with "Rukshasas" and a raised dot after "night".

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 170 begun; continued on p. 171 - hiraṇyahastaḥ — "its meaning and derivation are the same as those of the word hiraṇyapāṇiḥ." - asuraḥ = asuṃ prāṇaṃ rāti dadātīty asuraḥ | prāṇadātā: "the giver of breath, who protects the breath: life giving [the print's English]." - sunīthaḥ — suṣṭhu netā praśasya ity arthaḥ: "a leader, an excellent one, one worthy of praise; among the ten words for 'praiseworthy' beginning asremāḥ, anemāḥ [as printed] the word sunīthaḥ is read; so sunīthaḥ means praiseworthy." - sumṛḷīkaḥ = suṣṭhu sukhayitā — "the one who makes happiness." - svavān = svam asyāstīti svavān | dhanavān — "he who has wealth." - apasedhan = nirākurvan — "contemning, driving away, shunning, and so on." - rakṣaḥ = rakṣanty anena iti rakṣo balam | rakṣo rakṣitavyam asmād iti yāskaḥ (Ni. 4-18): "one who protects, or one who is able to protect from the rākṣasas and the like." - yātudhānān — "In general this word means rākṣasas, those who roam at night; asuras are also meant; but its exact sense is: one who works by spells — a spell-man, a sorcerer, a magician (mantragāra, māṭagāra, māyagāra); Sorcerer, Wizard, magician [the print's English]. We give one or two examples:"

अयोदंष्ट्रो अर्चिषा यातुधानानुप स्पृश जातवेदः समिद्धः । (ऋ. सं. १०-८७-२) उतान्तरिक्षे परि याहि राजन् जम्भैः सं धेह्यभि यातुधानान् । (ऋ. सं. १०-८७-३)

ayodaṃṣṭro arciṣā yātudhānān upa spṛśa jātavedaḥ samiddhaḥ | (ṛ. saṃ. 10-87-2) utāntarikṣe pari yāhi rājan jambhaiḥ saṃ dhehy abhi yātudhānān | (ṛ. saṃ. 10-87-3) Untranslated in the source. My gloss, editorial and tentative: "O Jātavedas, kindled, iron-fanged, touch the yātudhānas with your flame"; "and in the mid-region too, O king, go round; set your jaws on the yātudhānas".) (The list of examples continues on p. 171, to be viewed next.

Rik 10 — Special Topics concluded and grammar (pp. 171–173, PDF 186–188; grammar pages, noted briefly)

Special Topics, continued from p. 170 (p. 171) — the list of examples for yātudhānān, two more ṛks:

इह प्र ब्रूहि यतमः सो अग्ने यो यातुधानो य इदं कृणोति । (ऋ. सं. १०-८७-७) तस्याग्ने पृष्टीर्हरसा शृणीहि त्रेधा मूलं यातुधानस्य वृश्च । (ऋ. सं. १०-८७-७)

iha pra brūhi yatamaḥ so agne yo yātudhāno ya idaṃ kṛṇoti | (ṛ. saṃ. 10-87-7) tasyāgne pṛṣṭīr harasā śṛṇīhi tredhā mūlaṃ yātudhānasya vṛśca | (ṛ. saṃ. 10-87-7)

Mine and tentative: "here tell, O Agni, which one he is, the yātudhāna who does this"; "break his ribs with your heat, O Agni; cut the root of the yātudhāna in three ways". Both references are printed 10-87-7, as printed. "And the word yātudhāna is also used in the Atharvaveda (AV 1-7-1; 4-3-4; 6-13-3; 6-32-2; 7-70-2; 19-46-2 [?]), the Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā 37-14, the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā 8-7, the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 7-4-1-9 and other mantras." - pratidoṣam = pratirātrāṇi — "every night, on the night of every day." - gṛṇānaḥ = gṝ śabde — stūyamānaḥ: "one who is being praised."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā - svavān (p. 171): svam eṣām asti — tadasyāstyasminn iti matup; māduparadhāyāś ca matorvo 'yavādibhyaḥ — मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः — the m of matup becomes v after a base ending in a or having m or a as penultimate [the print explains the compound rule in two ways] and not belonging to the yavādi group; sva ends in a, so svavat; su; asaṃtasya cādhātoḥ — असन्तस्य चाधातोः — the penultimate vowel is lengthened before a sarvanāmasthāna ending, of a base not a dhātu ending in at; the augment num (ugidacām…); svavān + su, halṅyābbhyo… — loss of su; saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ: loss of the t; this loss, being asiddha, does not allow the loss of n; in the Saṃhitā, dīrghād aṭi samānapāde turns the n into ru; āto 'ṭi nityam — ā nasalised; bhobhago 'gho 'pūrvasya yo 'śi — ru → y; lopaḥ śākalyasya — loss of the y. - apasedhan (p. 172): root ṣidha gatyām, "1st class, 47th root; 48, ṣidhū śāstre māṅgalye ca; ṣidhu saṃrāddhau, the 119[?]th root (last digit 2 or 7), 4th class; in the present Dhātupāṭha ṣidha gatyām is not found"; laṭ, śatṛ, śap, laghūpadha-guṇa: sedhat; su; num by ugit; sedhan + su; halṅyādilopa, loss of the t; the preverb apa; śap is pit and śatṛ is lasārvadhātuka, so both unaccented; after the compound with apa, the later member keeps its natural accent (kṛdutarapadaprakṛtisvara). - rakṣasaḥ: root rakṣa pālane, 1st class; the Uṇādi suffix asin in the sense of apādāna: rakṣanty asmāt — "those from whom protection is [needed]", i.e. the occasion for protection; or rakṣyate 'nena — rakṣaḥ, in the sense of instrument, the Uṇādi asun: "strength": one who is protected by yātu is thus protected; without strength protection cannot be done; so rakṣaḥ = strength; rakṣo 'syāsti = rakṣasvin, "powerful"; asmāyāmedhāsrajo viniḥ — the suffix vin, whose luk is Vedic: rakṣasaḥ, rakṣasvinaḥ, "powerful ones"; the a of as is acute by the suffix-accent; had asun been intended, the first syllable would have been acute. - yātudhānān: root yata nikāropaskārayoḥ, 1st class; satyāpapāśarūpavīṇātūlaślokasenālomatvacavarmavarṇacūrṇacurādibhyo ṇic — the suffix ṇic in its own sense; after it, the Uṇādi suffix u in the verbal-noun sense; loss of ṇi; upadhā-vṛddhi: yātu, "torment, harassment"; yātavo dhīyante eṣu — "in whom torments are placed"; karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca — lyuṭ after dhā in the locus sense: ana; yātudhā + ana; lit — the syllable before the lit is acute; savarṇadīrgha; single-substitute accent. - asthāt: the print has "asmāt" at this entry and says it is explained in the eighth mantra of this sūkta; evidently a misprint for asthāt (see Rik 8: gātisthā… luk of sic). - pratidoṣam (pp. 172–173): doṣā = night; the phrase doṣāṃ prati; prati compounded with doṣā: avyayaṃ vibhaktisamīpasamṛddhivṛddhyarthābhāvātyayāsampratiśabdaprādurbhāvapaścādyathānupūrvyayaugapadyasādṛśyasampattisākalyāntavacaneṣu — an indeclinable in any of these senses (case-sense, proximity, prosperity…) compounds with a subanta, and it is avyayībhāva; here yathā-sense; the four senses of yathā are yogyatā (fitness), vīpsā (repetition), padārthānativṛtti (not exceeding) and sādṛśya (likeness); here vīpsā: "vīpsā means vyāpti, relating fully; when vīpsā is shown in a sentence, doubling comes by nityavīpsayoḥ; but in a compound the vīpsā is already expressed and so no doubling — so Kaiyaṭa says on a rule [the word printed hayavarāṭ]"; avyayībhāvaś ca — neuter; hrasvo napuṃsake prātipadikasya — shortening; nāvyayībhāvād ato 'm tv apañcamyāḥ — after an avyayībhāva ending in a the sup is replaced by am (not luk), except the fifth case; amipūrvaḥ: pūrvarūpa: pratidoṣam. - gṛṇānaḥ (p. 173): root gṝ śabde, kryādi; laṭ in the passive, śānac; kryādibhyaḥ śnā — śnā as the vikaraṇa: gṛ + nā + āna; the root's vowel is shortened [the print: pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ]; ṛvarṇān nasya ṇatvaṃ vācyam (vārtika): n → ṇ; cita: final-acute. Rik 10 ends here (|| 10 ||).
