दिवा॑ चि॒त्तमः॑ कृण्वन्ति प॒र्जन्ये॑नोदवा॒हेन॑ । यत्पृ॑थि॒वीं व्यु॒न्दन्ति॑ ॥ ९ ॥

divā cit tamaḥ kṛṇvanti parjanyenodavāhena | yat pṛthivīṃ vyundanti || 9 ||

Pada-pāṭha

दिवा । चित् । तमः । कृण्वन्ति । पर्जन्येन । उद-वाहेन । यत् । पृथिवीम् । वि-उन्दन्ति ॥ ९ ॥

divā | cit | tamaḥ | kṛṇvanti | parjanyena | uda-vāhena | yat | pṛthivīm | vi-undanti || 9 || The bhāṣya of Rik 9 begins on p. 317, not yet written.

Rik 38.9, continued from p. 317; the Saṃhitā and Pada are above

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

ते मरुत उदवाहेनोदकधारिणा पर्जन्येन मेघेन सूर्यमाच्छाद्य दिवा चिदहन्यपि तमः कृण्वन्ति । अन्धकारं कुर्वन्ति यद्यदा पृथिवीं भूमिं व्युन्दन्ति । विशेषेण क्लेदयन्ति । तदानीमतिवृष्टिकाले तमः कुर्वन्तीति पूर्वत्रान्वयः ॥ उदवाहेन । उदकानि वहतीत्युदवाहः । कर्मण्यण् । मेघविशेषस्येयं सञ्ज्ञा । उदकस्योदः सञ्ज्ञायां । पा. ६-३-५७ । इत्युदकशब्दस्योदभावः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । व्युन्दन्ति । उन्दी क्लेदने । रुधादित्वात् श्नम् । श्नान्नलोपः । पा. ६-४-२३ । इति नलोपः । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः ॥

te maruta udavāhenodakadhāriṇā parjanyena meghena sūryam ācchādya divā cid ahany api tamaḥ kṛṇvanti | andhakāraṃ kurvanti yad yadā pṛthivīṃ bhūmiṃ vyundanti | viśeṣeṇa kledayanti | tadānīm ativṛṣṭikāle tamaḥ kurvantīti pūrvatrānvayaḥ || udavāhena | udakāni vahatīty udavāhaḥ | karmaṇy aṇ | meghaviśeṣasyeyaṃ sañjñā | udakasyodaḥ sañjñāyāṃ | pā. 6-3-57 | ity udakaśabdasyodabhāvaḥ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | vyundanti | undī kledane | rudhāditvāt śnam | śnān nalopaḥ | pā. 6-4-23 | iti nalopaḥ | yadvṛttayogād anighātaḥ ||

Translation: "Those Maruts, with the udavāha — the water-bearing parjanya, the cloud — covering the sun, divā cit, even by day, tamaḥ kṛṇvanti, make darkness, make gloom, yad, when they pṛthivīm vyundanti, drench the earth, specially wet it. The sense is to be connected with what precedes: at that time, in the time of excessive rain, they make darkness. Udavāhena: 'udakāni vahati', that which carries waters; the suffix aṇ with an object [as upapada]; this is the name of a particular cloud; by udakasyodaḥ saṃjñāyām (Pā. 6-3-57) uda for the word udaka; the accent of the first member of a compound ending in a kṛt. Vyundanti: root undī kledane; śnam because of the rudhādi class; by śnān nalopaḥ (Pā. 6-4-23) the n is lost; no nighāta because of the connection with yat."

Pratipadārtha — "(marutaḥ — the Maruts) yat — when; pṛthivīm — the earth; vyundanti — they drench, so that it is filled as if with rushing water (when, before that); udavāhena — bearing water; parjanyena — with the cloud; divā cit — even by day; tamaḥ kṛṇvanti — they make darkness."

Bhāvārtha — "Before the Maruts drench the earth with a flood of rain, they make darkness even by day with the cloud that bears water."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 317) — "Even in the day they create darkness with the water-bearing cloud when they drench the earth."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 317 — "When black clouds fill the atmosphere, the darkness [is there] even in the daytime. At such a time the Maruts make the rain pour and make the earth wet with water: such is the main intention."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 317–319 — grammar pages, characterized - kṛṇvanti: "explained in the earlier mantra Rik 7." - udavāhena: root vaha prāpaṇe; "udakāni vahati, so udavāhaḥ": karmaṇy aṇ — कर्मण्यण् — (Pā. Sū. 3-2-1): when a word in the case of the object is upapada, the suffix aṇ comes after the root. The print adds that the analysing sentence is of two kinds, laukika and alaukika: the laukika is what everyone uses in the world; the alaukika is the one used only by grammarians, separating base and suffix for the purposes of the śāstra. In the laukika sentence one says udakāni vahati; in the alaukika one has udaka + as + vah + aṇ, where the genitive-case ending, not the accusative, is what is wanted, because a word ending in a kṛt is not used in the laukika sentence; by kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛti — कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति — (Pā. Sū. 2-3-65) the sixth case-ending comes after the word that expresses the agent or the object of a kṛt-base; hence the sixth case after udaka. Ata upadhāyāḥ — अत उपधायाः — (printed "Pā. Sū. 7-1-91" as read, the last two digits faint [?]; for 7-2-116): vṛddhi of the short a of the penultimate before a ñit/ṇit suffix: vah → vāh; udaka + as + vāha. Tatropapadaṃ saptamīstham — तत्रोपपदं सप्तमीस्थम् — (Pā. Sū. 3-1-92): the word in the locative-sense in the dhātvadhikāra is the upapada; upapadam atiṅ — उपपदमतिङ् — (Pā. Sū. 2-2-19) compound with a word that is not a verb: a tatpuruṣa; supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ — सुपो धातुप्रातिपदिकयोः — (printed "Pā. Sū" with no number) the loss of as: udakavāha; udakasyodaḥ saṃjñāyām — उदकस्योदः सञ्ज्ञायाम् — (Pā. Sū. 6-3-57): in a name the udaka of the first member becomes uda (here a name for a cloud). The final syllable of vāha, a kṛt, is acute by the suffix; after the compound gatikārakopapadāt kṛt — गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत् — (no number printed) gives the accent of the first member to the whole, so by kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara the same accent remains. - vyundanti: the prefix vi; root undī kledane, rudhādi; laṭ, jhi, the substitute ant; rudhādibhyaḥ śnam — रुधादिभ्यः श्नम् — (Pā. Sū. 3-1-78) śnam after the last vowel of the root: vi + und + śna + anti; śnān nalopaḥ — श्नान्नलोपः — (Pā. Sū. 6-4-23) the n of śnam is lost; śnasor allopaḥ — श्नसोरल्लोपः — (printed "Pā. Sū. 7-4-111" [as printed; for 6-4-111]) the a of śna is lost before a kit/ṅit sārvadhātuka; vi → vy by yaṇ: vyundanti. As yat pṛthivīm gives the connection with yat, yadvṛttān nityam — यद्वृत्तान्नित्यम् — prohibits the verb's being wholly unaccented. Rik 9 ends here (|| 9 ||).

Saṃhitā-pāṭha p. 319 = PDF 334 of the better scan; Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented

अध॑ स्व॒नान्म॒रुतां॒ विश्व॒मा सद्म॒ पार्थि॑वम् । अरे॑जन्त॒ प्र मानु॑षाः ॥ १० ॥

adha svanān marutāṃ viśvam ā sadma pārthivam | arejanta pra mānuṣāḥ || 10 ||

Pada-pāṭha

अध । स्वनात् । मरुताम् । विश्वम् । आ । सद्म । पार्थिवम् । अरेजन्त । प्र । मानुषाः ॥ १० ॥

adha | svanāt | marutām | viśvam | ā | sadma | pārthivam | arejanta | pra | mānuṣāḥ || 10 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

मरुतां सम्बन्धिनः स्वनादध ध्वनेर्गर्जनरूपादनन्तरं पार्थिवं पृथिवीसम्बन्धि विश्वं सद्म सर्वं गृहमा समन्तादरेजतेति शेषः । तथा मानुषा गृहवर्तिनो मनुष्या अपि प्रारेजन्त । प्रकर्षेण कम्पितवन्तः ॥ अध । छान्दसं ध्त्वं । सद्म । षद्लृ विशरणगत्यवसादनेषु । अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्ते इति मनिन् । पार्थिवं । पृथिव्याः सम्बन्धि । पृथिव्या ञाञौ । पा. ४-१-८४ [?] । इति प्राग्दीव्यतीयोऽञ्प्रत्ययः । ञित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं । अरेजन्त । रेजृ कम्पने ॥ १६ ॥

marutāṃ sambandhinaḥ svanād adha dhvaner garjanarūpād anantaraṃ pārthivaṃ pṛthivīsambandhi viśvaṃ sadma sarvaṃ gṛham ā samantād arejateti śeṣaḥ | tathā mānuṣā gṛhavartino manuṣyā api prārejanta | prakarṣeṇa kampitavantaḥ || adha | chāndasaṃ dhtvaṃ | sadma | ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu | anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante iti manin | pārthivaṃ | pṛthivyāḥ sambandhi | pṛthivyā ñāñau | pā. 4-1-85 | iti prāgdīvyatīyo 'ñpratyayaḥ | ñittvād ādyudāttatvaṃ | arejanta | rejṛ kampane || 16 ||

Translation: "Adha — then, after the svanāt, the sound [belonging to the Maruts], their sound in the form of thunder — pārthivam, belonging to the earth — viśvam sadma, every house — ā, all round, arejata ['shook': so the remainder is supplied]. Likewise mānuṣāḥ, men dwelling in houses, prārejanta — shook greatly. Adha: the dha [for tha] is Vedic. Sadma: root ṣadḷ in the senses of dissolving, going, sinking; manin by anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante. Pārthivam: 'belonging to the earth'; the suffix añ of the prāgdīvyatīya group after pṛthivī by the vārttika pṛthivyā ñāñau [Pā. 4-1-85]; being ñit it is first-syllable acute. Arejanta: root rejṛ kampane."

Pratipadārtha — "marutām — of the Maruts; svanād adha — immediately upon the sound in the form of thunder; pārthivam — belonging to the earth-world; viśvaṃ sadma — every house too; ā (arejata) — shook all round (even so); mānuṣāḥ — all the men (who dwell in the houses) too; prārejanta — trembled completely."

Bhāvārtha — "Through the clouds, as soon as the Maruts' sound in the form of thunder comes, every house dwelling on the earth shakes. In the same way all the people who live in those houses tremble completely."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 320) — "At the roaring of the Maruts, every house on the earth shakes and men also greatly tremble."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 320 - svanāt — "when rain falls with a sound, or with thunder, the wind blows violently, with sound, and terribly." - arejanta — "even houses shake, unable to bear the blow of the wind. People, drenched by the rain-water and struck by the blows of the wind, walk shivering with the cold: this is the sense. In the earlier ṛks, and in this ṛk, there is a description of the first monsoon rain [muṅgāru maḷe] that comes together with hail, lightning and black clouds."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 320–321 — grammar page, noted briefly - adha: the tha of the word atha has become dha by Vedic usage. - sadma: root ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu; by dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ the s; anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante — अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्ते — [Pā. Sū. 3-2-75]: the four suffixes manin, kvanip, vanip, vic are seen after roots also [other than the ones taught]; so manin; the suffix being nit, the print says pratyayānta ādyudātta ("the end of the suffix: first-syllable acute") — as printed. - pārthivam: prath prakhyāne; pratheḥ ṣivan saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca — प्रथेः षिवन् सम्प्रसारणं च — [U. Sū. 1-148, as printed]: the suffix ṣivan after prath, with saṃprasāraṇa of the r, giving ṛ: pṛthiv-; ṣidgaurādibhyaś ca — षिद्गौरादिभ्यश्च — [Pā. Sū. 4-1-41]: ṅīṣ after a root with indicatory ṣ and after the gaurādi group: pṛthivī; pṛthivyā ñāñau — the vārttika [Pā. Sū. 4-1-85-2, as printed]: in the prāgdīvyatīya senses the suffixes ñ and añ come after the word pṛthivī; so añ: pṛthivī + a; yasyeti ca the loss of ī; taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ — तद्धितेष्वचामादेः — [Pā. Sū. 7-2-117]: when a ñit or ṇit suffix follows, the first vowel of the base takes vṛddhi: ṛ → ār: pārthiva; the taddhita suffix is ñit; ñnityādir nityam — ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यम् — (no number printed) gives the first-syllable acute; accusative singular. - arejanta: rejṛ kampane; laṅ, jha; jho 'ntaḥ the substitute ant; śap; the augment aṭ. Rik 10 ends here (|| 10 ||).

मरु॑तो वीळुपा॒णिभि॑श्चि॒त्रा रोध॑स्वती॒रनु॑ । या॒तेमखि॑द्रयामभिः ॥ ११ ॥

maruto vīḷupāṇibhiś citrā rodhasvatīr anu | yātem akhidrayāmabhiḥ || 11 ||

Pada-pāṭha

मरुतः । वीळुपाणिऽभिः । चित्राः । रोधस्वतीः । अनु । यात । ईम् । अखिद्रयामऽभिः ॥ ११ ॥

marutaḥ | vīḷupāṇi-bhiḥ | citrāḥ | rodhasvatīḥ | anu | yāta | īm | akhidrayāma-bhiḥ || 11 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

हे मरुतो यूयं वीळुपाणिभिर्दृढहस्तैः सहिताः सन्तो रोधस्वतीरनु कूलयुक्ता नदीरनुलक्ष्याखिद्रयामभिरखिन्नगमनैर्यातेम् । गच्छतैव ॥ मरुतः । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वं । वीळुपाणिभिः । वीळ्विति बलनाम । वीळु ज्यौत्नमिति [?] तन्नामसु पाठात् । तेन च तद्वाल्लक्ष्यते । वीळवश्च ते पाणयश्च । समासस्येत्यन्तोदात्तत्वं । रोधस्वतीः । रुधिर् आवरणे । रुणद्धि स्रोत इति रोधः कूलं । रोधः कूलं निरुणद्धि स्रोतः । नि. ६-१ । इत्युक्तत्वात् । असुनो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं । तद्युक्ता रोधस्वत्यः । मादुपधाया इति मतुपो वत्वं । उगितश्चेति ङीप् । मतुब्ङीपोः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वेऽसुनः स्वर एव शिष्यते । यात । या प्रापणे । अदादित्वाच्छपो लुक् । ईम् । चादयोऽनुदात्ता इत्यनुदात्तत्वं । गुण एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्त इत्याद्युदात्तत्वं । अखिद्रयामभिः । खिद दैन्ये । स्पायितञ्चीत्यादिना रक् । खिद्रं यान्तीति खिद्रयामानः । न खिद्रयामानोऽखिद्रयामानः । त्रैः । अव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥

he maruto yūyaṃ vīḷupāṇibhir dṛḍhahastaiḥ sahitāḥ santo rodhasvatīr anu kūlayuktā nadīr anulakṣyākhidrayāmabhir akhinnagamanair yātem | gacchataiva || marutaḥ | āmantritādyudāttatvaṃ | vīḷupāṇibhiḥ | vīḷv iti balanāma | vīḷu jyautnam iti [?] tannāmasu pāṭhāt | tena ca tadvāl lakṣyate | vīḷavaś ca te pāṇayaś ca | samāsasyety antodāttatvaṃ | rodhasvatīḥ | rudhir āvaraṇe | ruṇaddhi srota iti rodhaḥ kūlaṃ | rodhaḥ kūlaṃ niruṇaddhi srotaḥ | ni. 6-1 | ity uktatvāt | asuno nittvād ādyudāttatvaṃ | tadyuktā rodhasvatyaḥ | mād upadhāyā iti matupo vatvaṃ | ugitaś ceti ṅīp | matub-ṅīpoḥ pittvād anudāttatve 'sunaḥ svara eva śiṣyate | yāta | yā prāpaṇe | adāditvāc chapo luk | īm | cādayo 'nudāttā ity anudāttatvaṃ | guṇa ekādeśa udāttenodātta ity ādyudāttatvaṃ | akhidrayāmabhiḥ | khida dainye | spāyitañcī ty ādinā rak | khidraṃ yāntīti khidrayāmānaḥ | na khidrayāmāno 'khidrayāmānaḥ | traiḥ | avyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ||

Translation: "O Maruts, you, accompanied by vīḷupāṇibhiḥ, strong hands, rodhasvatīr anu, along the rivers that have banks, akhidrayāmabhiḥ, with unwearied goings, yātem — go indeed. Vīḷupāṇibhiḥ — vīḷu is a name for strength, since it is read among its names [vīḷu … as read, doubtful [?]]; and by it its possessors are indicated; they are strong and they are hands [or: those whose hands are strong]; the accent is final by samāsasya. Rodhasvatīḥ — root rudhir āvaraṇe: 'ruṇaddhi srotaḥ', that which checks the stream is rodhaḥ, the bank; as is said, 'rodhaḥ kūlaṃ niruṇaddhi srotaḥ' (Ni. 6-1); since the suffix asun is nit the first syllable is acute; the rivers that have them are rodhasvatyaḥ; mādupadhāyāḥ gives va for matup; ṅīp by ugitaś ca; because matup and ṅīp are pit they are unaccented, so only the accent of asun remains. Yāta — root yā prāpaṇe; the śap elided because of the adādi class. Īm — particles such as ca are unaccented. Akhidrayāmabhiḥ — root khida dainye; the suffix rak by spāyitañci-…: 'khidraṃ yānti', those who go in weakness; na khidrayāmāna, the unwearied; the accent of the first member as an indeclinable."

Pratipadārtha — "marutaḥ — O Maruts (you); vīḷupāṇibhiḥ — having capable hands; citrāḥ — charming (from being filled with trees and creepers of many kinds); rodhasvatīḥ anu — along the rivers that have banks; akhidrayāmabhiḥ — with goings that have no hindrance; yātam — go about, certainly."

Bhāvārtha — "O Maruts, with strong hands (vṛdha-hasta; the print adds 'pādagaḷinda ?', 'with feet?', with its own question mark), go along the rivers with their banks, charming from being full of trees and creepers of many kinds, without hindrance."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 322) — "Maruts with strong hands (legs ?) come along the beautiful banks of the rivers with unbroken speed." The Special Topics of Rik 11 begin at the foot of p. 322 and continue on p. 323; not yet written.

Rik 38.11, continued from the foot of p. 322

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), pp. 322–323 - vīḷupāṇibhiḥ = vṛdhahastaiḥ [as read; the second word of the gloss is printed with a doubtful letter [?]] — "the word pāṇi indicates the sense 'hand', but here the sense 'feet' seems called for; for here the going of the Maruts is spoken of, and since people and creatures move by their feet, it is impossible to say that they go with the hands. The ṛṣi's intention may be 'feet'. On this point, in the ṛk सेदग्निरग्नीँ रत्यस्त्वन्यान् यत्र वाजी तनयो वीळुपाणिः । sed agnir agnīm̐ ratyas tv anyān yatra vājī tanayo vīḷupāṇiḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-1-14, as printed) — the word pāṇi has to be taken in the sense of 'feet'." Reference numerals and the text of the quotation as printed, with doubt; the quotation is left untranslated by the source. Mine and tentative: "that Agni [goes] beyond other fires, where the vigorous steed, the offspring, is strong-footed" — the gloss is uncertain, as the Sanskrit is crowded [?]. - rodhasvatīḥ — "rivers with banks: that is, river-banks, the sides of rivers." - akhidrayāmabhiḥ = akhinnayāmabhiḥ — "with unbroken goings, with unobstructed movements." The source adds in English: "with unobstructed or unbroken progress."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 323–324 — grammar pages, characterized - vīḷupāṇibhiḥ: among the names of strengths in the Nirukta (Niru. 2-9-14, as printed) vīḷu [the print has vīḍu here] is read; therefore it means "strength". If only that sense were taken, the connection with pāṇi would be blocked; so, by implication (lakṣaṇā), the sense "possessing strength" is taken: "with strong hands". The print compares gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣaḥ ("a cowherd village on the Gaṅgā"), where the literal sense is blocked and gaṅgā is taken as "the bank of the Gaṅgā"; and says that here too, as the sense given in the Nirukta is blocked, implication must be relied upon. Viśeṣaṇaṃ viśeṣyeṇa bahulam — विशेषणं विशेष्येण बहुलम् — [Pā. Sū. 2-1-57]: a qualifier compounds with its qualified noun of the same case; it is a tatpuruṣa, and by tatpuruṣaḥ samānādhikaraṇaḥ karmadhārayaḥ — तत्पुरुषः समानाधिकरणः कर्मधारयः — [Pā. Sū. 1-2-42] it is called karmadhāraya; by samāsasya — समासस्य — [Pā. Sū. 6-1-223] the last syllable of the compound is acute. - rodhasvatīḥ: root rudhir āvaraṇe (rudhādi), "āvaraṇa" meaning stopping — stopping what? From the sense, the flow: "ruṇaddhi, so rodhaḥ"; the sentence rodhaḥ kūlaṃ niruṇaddhi srotaḥ (Ni. 6-1) means "rodhaḥ is the bank, because it stops the stream". By this Nirukta passage the sense stated before is confirmed. Sarvadhātubhyo 'sun — सर्वधातुभ्योऽसुन् — [U. Sū. printed "4-6-28" as read; middle and last groups doubtful [?]]: asun; rudh + as; pugantalaghūpadhasya ca [Pā. Sū. 7-3-86] gives guṇa; asun is nit, so the end of the suffix is acute [as printed: pratyayānta ādyudātta]; "rodhaḥ belongs to these [rivers]" — tad asyāsty asminn iti matup — तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप् — [Pā. Sū. 5-2-94]; rodhas + mat, rodhas ends in as; mādupadhāyāś ca matorvo 'yavādibhyaḥ — मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः — [Pā. Sū. 8-2-9]: after a word that ends in m or a/ṛ or has m, a as penultimate [the print's wording is crowded], the m of matup becomes v: rodhasvat; the u of matup is an indicatory letter, so it is ugit; ugitaś ca — उगितश्च — [Pā. Sū. 4-1-6]: ṅīp in the feminine after a ugit base; matup and ṅīp are both pit and so unaccented, by anudāttau suppitau — अनुदात्तौ सुप्पितौ (no number printed). - yāta: yā prāpaṇe, adādi, loṭ, tha; the ta substitute by tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ; adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ — अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शपः (no number printed) the śap is elided; because the word is at the beginning of a pāda it is not wholly unaccented; the ta is acute by the suffix accent. - īm: this is in the cādi group; by cādayo 'nudāttāḥ — चादयोऽनुदात्ताः — [Phi. Sū. 84, as printed] it is unaccented; in the Saṃhitā yāta + īm by ād guṇaḥ — आद्गुणः — [Pā. Sū. 6-1-87]: when a or ā is followed by a vowel of a different kind, guṇa is the single substitute: so in place of the gutturo-palatal ā and ī the gutturo-palatal e, which has the guṇa name, comes: yātem; since this single substitute has come in place of an acute and an unaccented vowel, by ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ it is acute. - akhidrayāmabhiḥ: khida dainye; the suffix rak by spāyitañci-… — the print says this sūtra was given in full in the eighth ṛk of this very sūkta [see Rik 8]; "yā prāpaṇe: khidraṃ yānti, those who go in weakness: khidrayāmānaḥ"; anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante gives manin; na khidrayāmānaḥ, a nañ-compound; nalopo nañaḥ — नलोपो नञः (no number printed) the loss of the n of nañ [before a vowel]; the accent of the first member as an indeclinable. Rik 11 ends here (|| 11 ||).

original pp. 324–327

Rik 12

Saṃhitā-pāṭha p. 324 foot = PDF 339 of the better scan; Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented

स्थि॒रा वः॑ सन्तु ने॒मयो॒ रथा॒ अश्वा॑स एषाम् । सुसं॑स्कृता अ॒भी॑शवः ॥ १२ ॥

sthirā vaḥ santu nemayo rathā aśvāsa eṣām | susaṃskṛtā abhīśavaḥ || 12 ||

Pada-pāṭha

स्थिराः । वः । सन्तु । नेमयः । रथाः । अश्वासः । एषाम् । सुऽसंस्कृताः । अभीशवः ॥ १२ ॥

sthirāḥ | vaḥ | santu | nemayaḥ | rathāḥ | aśvāsaḥ | eṣām | su-saṃskṛtāḥ | abhīśavaḥ || 12 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

हे मरुत एषां वो युष्माकं नेमयो रथचक्रवलययः स्थिराः सन्तु । तथा रथा अश्वासोऽश्वाश्च स्थिराः सन्तु । अभीशवोऽङ्गुलयः । अभीशवो दीधितय इति तन्नामसु पाठात् । सुसंस्कृता अश्वबन्धनरज्जुपरिग्रहणे स्वलङ्कृताः सावधानाः सन्तु ॥ सुसंस्कृताः । सम्पूर्वात्करोतेः कर्मणि क्तः । सम्पर्युपेभ्यः । पा. ६-१-१३७ । इति सुट् । पुनः सुशब्देन प्रादिसमासेऽव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । अभीशवः । अभिपूर्वादश्नोतेः कृवापाजीत्यादिना उण् । वर्णव्यत्ययेनाकारस्यैकारः । उक्तं च । वर्णागमो वर्णविपर्ययश्च । का. ६-३-१०९ । इति । अभीशवोऽभ्यश्नुवते कर्माणीति निरुक्तं । नि. ३-९ ॥

he maruta eṣāṃ vo yuṣmākaṃ nemayo rathacakravalayayaḥ sthirāḥ santu | tathā rathā aśvāso 'śvāś ca sthirāḥ santu | abhīśavo 'ṅgulayaḥ | abhīśavo dīdhitaya iti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | susaṃskṛtā aśvabandhanarajjuparigrahaṇe svalaṅkṛtāḥ sāvadhānāḥ santu || susaṃskṛtāḥ | sampūrvāt karoteḥ karmaṇi ktaḥ | samparyupebhyaḥ | pā. 6-1-137 | iti suṭ | punaḥ suśabdena prādisamāse 'vyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | abhīśavaḥ | abhipūrvād aśnoteḥ kṛvāpājī ty ādinā uṇ | varṇavyatyayenākārasyaikāraḥ | uktaṃ ca | varṇāgamo varṇaviparyayaś ca | kā. 6-3-109 | iti | abhīśavo 'bhyaśnuvate karmāṇīti niruktaṃ | ni. 3-9 ||

Translation: "O Maruts, eṣām — of these — vaḥ — your — nemayaḥ, the rims of the chariot-wheels, sthirāḥ santu, let them be firm. Likewise let the rathāḥ, chariots, and aśvāsaḥ, horses, be firm. Abhīśavaḥ — the fingers ('abhīśavaḥ is [read as] dīdhitayaḥ', since it is read among the names of these [fingers]). Susaṃskṛtāḥ — let them be well adorned and attentive in the holding of the ropes that bind the horses. Susaṃskṛtāḥ: from kṛ after sam, kta in the passive; by samparyupebhyaḥ [Pā. 6-1-137] the augment suṭ; then, in the compound with su as a prādi compound, the accent of the first member as an indeclinable. Abhīśavaḥ: from aś with abhi, the Uṇādi uṇ by kṛvāpāji-…; a → ai [as printed: akārasyaikāraḥ] by varṇavyatyaya; as is said: 'the addition of a letter and the transposition of letters' (Kāśikā on Pā. 6-3-109); the Nirukta says 'abhīśavo: they pervade the works' (Ni. 3-9, as printed)."

Pratipadārtha — "eṣāṃ vaḥ — (O Maruts) of these, your; nemayaḥ — the outer rims of the chariot wheels; sthirāḥ — firm; santu — let them be (so); rathāḥ — chariots; aśvāsaḥ — horses (let them be steady); abhīśavaḥ — (your) fingers [printed ugurugaḷu (also in the Bhāvārtha) — which would mean 'nails'; as printed]; susaṃskṛtāḥ — (fit to hold the bridles of the horses) adorned and well-trained (let them be)."

Bhāvārtha — "O Maruts, let the outer rims of your chariot-wheels be firm. Let your chariots and your horses be steady. Let your fingers [printed as in the pratipadārtha], graceful as befits your strength, have adornments fit for holding the bridles of the horses, and be skilled."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 325) — "May the fellies of your wheels be firm ; may your chariots and their horses be steady and your fingers well-skilled in holding the reins."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 326 - nemayaḥ — "the outer rims of the wheels of a chariot." The source adds in English: "the fellies of a chariot wheel ; the outer rims of the wheels." "The word nemi is read in many ṛks of the Ṛgveda:" (the six quotations follow in the print, left untranslated by the source; Devanagari and IAST from the print, reference numerals as printed, and glosses editorial and tentative): 1. सेदु राजा क्षयति चर्षणीनामरान्न नेमिः परि ता बभूव ॥ — sed u rājā kṣayati carṣaṇīnām arān na nemiḥ pari tā babhūva (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-32-15) — "that king rules over the peoples; like a rim [round] spokes, he has encompassed all these" (editorial and tentative). 2. यत्सीमनु क्रतुना विश्वथा विभुररान्न नेमिः परिभूरजायथाः — yat sīm anu kratunā viśvathā vibhur arān na nemiḥ paribhūr ajāyathāḥ (printed "Ṛ. Sū. 1-141-9") — the print reads as given; "…by [your] will, everywhere pervasive, like a rim [round] spokes you were born encompassing" (editorial, very tentative: the Sanskrit is uncertain [?]). 3. परि विश्वानि काव्या नेमिश्चक्रमिवाभवत् । — pari viśvāni kāvyā nemiś cakram ivābhavat (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-5-3) — "he encompassed all the poetic works as a rim a wheel" (editorial and tentative). 4. अग्ने नेमिररां इव देवाँस्त्वं परिभूरसि । — agne nemir arām̐ iva devām̐s tvaṃ paribhūr asi (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-13-6) the print has āgne — "Agni, as a rim [round] spokes, you encompass the gods" (editorial and tentative). 5. आ व इन्द्रं पुरुहूतं नमे गिरा नेमिं तष्टेव सुद्र्वम् । [?] — ā va indraṃ puruhūtaṃ name girā nemiṃ taṣṭeva sudrvam [?] (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-32-20, as printed) — the last word is printed sadvram and is uncertain: "I bow to Indra, much invoked, with a song, as a carpenter [bends] a rim" (editorial, very tentative). 6. तं नेमिमृभवो यथा नमस्व सहूतिभिः ॥ — taṃ nemim ṛbhavo yathā namasva sahūtibhiḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-75-5, as printed) — "bow to him, as the Ṛbhus [bend] a rim, with joint invocations" (editorial, very tentative). "etc. This nemi is made of a hard wood called sadru [as printed] and bent." - susaṃskṛtāḥ — "well-trained [cennāgi paḷagida]." English added by the source: "well-trained, well-skilled &c." - abhīśavaḥ — "abhīśu also has the senses 'arm' (Ni. 3-8) and 'ray' (Ni. 2-15, as printed); but since the word abhīśavaḥ is read among the twenty-two names of the fingers beginning with agruvaḥ aṅgyaḥ, the commentator has taken for abhīśavaḥ in this ṛk the sense 'fingers'."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā p. 326, begun; the rest on p. 327 not yet written - susaṃskṛtāḥ: root ḍukṛñ karaṇe; with the prefix sam, kta in the senses of object etc. by niṣṭhā [Pā. Sū. 3-2-102]; saṃ + kṛ + ta; by saṃparibhyāṃ karotau bhūṣaṇe — सम्परिभ्यां करोतौ भूषणे — [Pā. Sū. 6-1-137] the augment suṭ for kṛ after the prefixes sam, pari in the sense of ornament; the print then says that the vṛttikāras read samparyupebhyaḥ [as in the bhāṣya], which is not agreeable to the Mahābhāṣya; by suṭkāt pūrvaḥ — सुट्कात्पूर्वः — [Pā. Sū. 6-1-135] and the Mahābhāṣya's statement "saṃparibhyām iti naiṣā pañcamī | kā tarhi | tṛtīyā" [as read]; "some…" continued on p. 327.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 38.12, continued p. 327, PDF 341 — grammar page, noted briefly - susaṃskṛtāḥ, concluded: the print goes on to say that in the sūtra upāt pratiyatnavaikṛtavākyādhyāhāreṣu [as read, crowded [?]] the word ca is read, so that even with the prefix upa the augment suṭ is established in the senses of ornament and of relation, and that the vṛttikāras explain in the Bhāṣya tradition the point of the reading upa; the Śekhara [commentator] does not accept this: the passage of the Śekhara "some do not allow suṭ after upāt [or pra] in the senses of ornament and relation, and do not read ca" is quoted to make the earlier points clear. This passage is very crowded; only its drift is given. - abhīśavaḥ: aśū vyāptau, with the prefix abhi; kṛvāpājimisvadisādhyaśūbhya uṇ — कृवापाजिमिस्वदिसाध्यशूभ्य उण् — [U. Sū. 1-1]: the suffix uṇ after the root aś; pṛṣodarādīni yathopadiṣṭam — पृषोदरादीनि यथोपदिष्टम् — [Pā. Sū. 6-3-109]: the Kāśikā authors say "the addition of a letter, the transposition of letters, and two other [processes], the change and the loss of a letter — [these are] the five kinds, in which a root is joined with its sense in excess: so says the Nirukta"; here a change of the vowel into an i-form has come. The Kaumudī gives examples: "haṃsaḥ from addition of a letter, siṃhaḥ from transposition of letters, gūḍhotmā from change of a letter, pṛṣodaram from loss of a letter"; in the bahuvrīhi gūḍha ātmā yasya saḥ a u has come in place of the ā, so this is an example of change of letter, not of transposition; therefore here it is proper to say that the change into the form of i has come. Abhīśavaḥ abhyaśnuvate karmāṇi (Ni. 3-9, as printed): "the things that get works, i.e. do them": it is well known that the hands do works; therefore abhīśavaḥ means hands; the Nirukta author means that, as said before, this form is established from the root aś. Rik 12 ends here (|| 12 ||).

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

हे ऋत्विक्समूह तना तनया देवतास्वरूपं प्रकाशयन्त्या गिरा वाचा ब्रह्मणस्पतिं मन्त्रस्य हविर्लक्षणस्यान्नस्य वा पालकं मरुद्गणमग्निं दर्शतं दर्शनीयं मित्रं न मित्रमपि जरायै स्तोतुमच्छाभिमुख्येन वद । ब्रूहि ॥ अच्छ । निपातस्य चेति संहितायां दीर्घत्वं । वद । द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङ इति संहितायां दीर्घः । तना । तनु विस्तारे । तनोति देवतामाहात्म्यं विस्तारयतीति तना । पचाद्यच् । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं । तृतीयाया डादेशः । गिरा । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । ब्रह्मणः । षष्ठ्याः । पतिपुत्रेति संहितायां सत्वं ॥

he ṛtvik-samūha tanā tanayā devatāsvarūpaṃ prakāśayantyā girā vācā brahmaṇaspatiṃ mantrasya havirlakṣaṇasyānnasya vā pālakaṃ marudgaṇam agniṃ darśataṃ darśanīyaṃ mitraṃ na mitram api jarāyai stotum acchābhimukhyena vada | brūhi || accha | nipātasya ceti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghatvaṃ | vada | dvyaco 'tastiṅa iti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghaḥ | tanā | tanu vistāre | tanoti devatāmāhātmyaṃ vistārayatīti tanā | pacādyac | vṛṣāditvād ādyudāttatvaṃ | tṛtīyāyā ḍādeśaḥ | girā | sāvekāca iti vibhakter udāttatvaṃ | brahmaṇaḥ | ṣaṣṭhyāḥ | patiputreti saṃhitāyāṃ satvaṃ ||

Translation: "O company of priests, tanā — with tanayā, speech that sets out the nature of the deities — girā, with speech, brahmaṇaspatim — the protector of the mantra, or of the food whose mark is the oblation, the host of the Maruts — and agnim — and Agni — darśatam, beautiful to see — mitram na, [and] also Mitra [as a friend] — jarāyai, to praise, accha, facing [them], vada, speak, say. Accha: in the Saṃhitā the lengthening by nipātasya ca. Vada: in the Saṃhitā the long vowel by dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ. Tanā: root tanu vistāre: 'tanoti', one that spreads the greatness of the deity, is tanā; the suffix ac of the pacādi class; because of its belonging to the vṛṣādi class the first syllable is acute; the substitute ḍā for the instrumental. Girā: the ending is acute by sāvekāca. Brahmaṇaḥ: genitive; in the Saṃhitā the s by patiputra…."

Pratipadārtha — "tanā — (O priests, [with speech] fit to describe the nature of the deities) capable of describing; girā — with speech; brahmaṇaspatim — the host of the Maruts, protectors of the mantra and also of the food in the form of the oblation; agnim — Agni too; darśatam — the beautiful one; mitram — Mitra; jarāyai — in order to praise; acchā — facing [those deities]; vada — speak clearly (the praise)."

Bhāvārtha — "O priests! With words fit to describe their nature, standing facing the host of the Maruts, who protect both the mantra and the food in the form of oblation, and Agni, and Mitra of beautiful form, together with that deity, recite your praises clearly."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 328) — "Sing forth in uninterrupted speech in order to glorify Brahmanaspati (or the Maruts, lords of prayer or of the Sacrificial food) and Agni as well as the handsome Mitra."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 329 - acchā vada = ābhimukhyena vada — "speak, praising particularly." - tanā = tanayā, devatāsvarūpaṃ prakāśayantyā — "that which spreads, or that which makes known the nature of the deities." - jarāyai = stotum — "in order to praise." - brahmaṇaḥ patim — "brahma means praise, and also food. Brahmaṇaspati means the host of the Maruts who are lords over praise or over food: so the commentator has explained. If one wishes, one may explain this word also as the deity named Brahmaṇaspati." - darśatam = darśanīyam — "beautiful to look at."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 329–, grammar pages, characterized; the long page 330 is very crowded - acchā: a nipāta; nipātasya ca — निपातस्य च — [Pā. Sū. 6-3-136]: in a mantra a nipāta takes the long vowel: so the long vowel. - vada: vada vyaktāyāṃ vāci; loṭ, sip, the substitute hi; śap: vad + a + hi; ato heḥ — अतो हेः — [Pā. Sū. 6-4-105]: hi is elided after a short a; dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ — द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङः — [Pā. Sū. 6-3-135]: in a mantra the a of a tiṅ-word that has two vowels is lengthened: so the long vowel. - tanā: root tasu [print; = tanu] vistāre, the first root of the tanādi class; "tanoti = spreads"; spreads what? — "the greatness of the deity", which is suited to the context; the Vedabhāṣya says "tanoti (the greatness of the deity) vistārayatīti tanā". Nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ — नन्दिग्रहिपचादिभ्यो ल्युणिन्यचः — [Pā. Sū. 3-1-134]: by the paribhāṣā yathāsaṃkhyam anudeśaḥ samānām the senses are: lyu after nandi etc., ṇini after grahi etc., ac after pacādi; when ac comes after tan in the pacādi sense: tan + a = tana. This belongs to the vṛṣādi group; vṛṣādīnāṃ ca — वृषादीनां च — [Pā. Sū. 6-1-203]: the vṛṣādi is an ākṛtigaṇa, a group not wholly enumerated; the print explains that the words are listed only as examples (kṛtyā — avayavaviśeṣeṇa gaṇyate = parigaṇyate), so a word whose first-syllable acute is not otherwise established is to be taken, by looking at the kind of word, as belonging to the group; hence tana is first-syllable acute. The instrumental singular: supāṃ sulug…, the substitute ḍā, the ḍ an indicatory letter; loss, tana + ā; by the power of the ḍit the ṭi, the a of tana, is lost: tan + ā = tanā. - girā: root gṝ nigaraṇe; kvip ca gives kvip; ṛta id dhātoḥ — ऋत इद्धातोः — [Pā. Sū. 7-1-100]: for the ṛ of a root-final ṛ the substitute i, and the r follows: gir; instrumental singular ṭā: gir + ā = girā; in the locative plural sup, gīrṣu is the form; halica — हलि च — [Pā. Sū. 8-2-77]: before a consonant the penultimate ik of a root ending in r or v is lengthened [rule from the eighth adhyāya]. The print then argues at length, concerning the sāvekāca sūtra (sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ — सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिर्विभक्तिः — [Pā. Sū. 6-1-168]) and the Bhāṣya's discussion of whether su, in the sūtra, means the nominative singular or the locative plural, quoting the Bhāṣya (p. 330): सावितिकिमिदं प्रथमैकवचनस्यग्रहणमाहोस्वित्सप्तमीबहुवचनस्य, कुतस्सन्देहः । समानोनिर्देशः । सप्तमीबहुवचनस्यग्रहणम् । कथं ज्ञायते ? । (sāv iti kim idaṃ prathamaikavacanasya grahaṇam āhosvit saptamībahuvacanasya, kutas sandehaḥ | samāno nirdeśaḥ | saptamībahuvacanasya grahaṇam | kathaṃ jñāyate? | — "'sau': is the nominative singular meant here, or the locative plural? Whence the doubt? The wording is the same. The locative plural is meant. How is it known?"), followed by a sentence citing the sūtra on go, śvan etc. (not transcribed; its sūtra name is crowded) and the example of the participle of yā, yān, yātsu, yātā. Continued on p. 331, below.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 38.13, continued pp. 331–332, PDF 346–347 — large grammar pages, characterized in outline; the print is very crowded and its argument is not reproduced - girā, continued: the long discussion of the sāvekāca sūtra goes on. The print argues about the sense of su in the Bhāṣya's question "kim idaṃ prathamaikavacanasya grahaṇam āhosvit saptamībahuvacanasya" and of the word ekācaḥ in the sūtra: if ekācaḥ were not said, the ending in rājñā would be acute, since it follows rājan; with it, the rule applies to the ending after a base that is monosyllabic in the form that has the case ending; examples discussed are rājñā, dvābhyām, dos (doṣabhyām, dorbhyām), keṣu, kābhyām, abhiḥ, eṣām, keṣu, āsu + eṣu, with the interplay of sthānivadbhāva and of the question whether the rule is to take account of the form (rūpagrahaṇa) or not, and with the remark that in the world the ending is acute, while in the Veda the unaccented (sarvānudātta) forms are to be explained by Vedic usage. Only the drift; the page is too crowded to transcribe, and the details may contain slips. - brahmaṇaḥ: patiputrapṛṣṭhapārapadapayaspoṣeṣu — पतिपुत्रपृष्ठपारपदपयस्पोषेषु — [Pā. Sū. 8-3-53]: when words such as pati follow, the visarga belonging to a genitive becomes s; so in the Saṃhitā the visarga becomes s. Rik 13 ends here (|| 13 ||).

Pada-pāṭha

मिमीहि । श्लोकम् । आस्ये । पर्जन्यः । इव । ततनः । गाय । गायत्रम् । उक्थ्यम् ॥ १४ ॥

mimīhi | ślokam | āsye | parjanyaḥ | iva | tatanaḥ | gāya | gāyatram | ukthyam || 14 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

हे ऋत्विक्समूह आस्ये स्वकीयमुखे श्लोकं स्तोत्रं मिमीहि । निर्मितं कुरु । तं च श्लोकं ततनः । विस्तारय । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । पर्जन्य इव । यथा मेघो वृष्टिं विस्तारयति तद्वत् । उक्थ्यं शस्त्रयोग्यं गायत्रं गायत्रीच्छन्दस्कं सूक्तं गाय । पठ ॥ मिमीहि । माङ् माने । जौहोत्यादिकः । व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं । भृञामित्यभ्यासस्येत्वं । आस्ये । असु क्षेपणे । अस्यते क्षिप्यतेऽस्मिन्नित्यास्यं । कृत्यल्युटो बहुलं । पा. ३-३-११३ । इत्यधिकरणे ण्यत् । तित्स्वरितमिति स्वरितत्वं । ततनः । तनु विस्तारे । लेटि सिपि बहुलं छन्दसीति विकरणस्य श्लुः । लेटोऽडाटावित्यडागमः । इतश्च लोप इतीकारलोपः । गायत्रं । गायत्र्याः सम्बन्धि तस्येदमित्यण् । यद्वा । गायतस्त्रायत इति गायत्रं । आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः ॥

he ṛtviksamūha āsye svakīyamukhe ślokaṃ stotraṃ mimīhi | nirmitaṃ kuru | taṃ ca ślokaṃ tatanaḥ | vistāraya | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | parjanya iva | yathā megho vṛṣṭiṃ vistārayati tadvat | ukthyaṃ śastrayogyaṃ gāyatraṃ gāyatrīchandaskaṃ sūktaṃ gāya | paṭha || mimīhi | māṅ māne | jauhotyādikaḥ | vyatyayena parasmaipadaṃ | bhṛñām ity abhyāsasyetvaṃ | āsye | asu kṣepaṇe | asyate kṣipyate 'smin ity āsyaṃ | kṛtyalyuṭo bahulaṃ | pā. 3-3-113 | ity adhikaraṇe ṇyat | titsvaritam iti svaritatvaṃ | tatanaḥ | tanu vistāre | leṭi sipi bahulaṃ chandasīti vikaraṇasya śluḥ | leṭo 'ḍāṭāv ity aḍāgamaḥ | itaś ca lopa itīkāralopaḥ | gāyatraṃ | gāyatryāḥ sambandhi tasyedam ity aṇ | yadvā | gāyatas trāyata iti gāyatraṃ | āto 'nupasarge kaḥ ||

Translation: "O company of priests, in your own mouth (āsye) ślokam, a praise-song, mimīhi — compose, make it. And tatanaḥ — spread that śloka. The example: parjanya iva — as a cloud spreads the rain, so. Gāya — sing, recite — gāyatram, the sūkta in the Gāyatrī metre, ukthyam, fit for the śastra. Mimīhi: root māṅ māne, of the juhotyādi class; parasmaipada by vyatyaya; the i in the reduplicate by bhṛñām it. Āsye: root asu kṣepaṇe; 'in which it is thrown': āsyam; by kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam [Pā. 3-3-113] the suffix ṇyat in the locative sense; the svarita by tit svaritam. Tatanaḥ: root tanu vistāre; leṭ, sip; by bahulaṃ chandasi the vikaraṇa is elided; the augment aṭ by leṭo 'ḍāṭau; the loss of i by itaś ca lopaḥ. Gāyatram: 'belonging to the Gāyatrī' — the suffix aṇ by tasyedam; or: 'gāyataḥ trāyate', that which protects the singer — gāyatram, the suffix ka by * āto 'nupasarge kaḥ*."

Pratipadārtha — "āsye — in your mouth; ślokam — the praise-song; mimīhi — compose; (taṃ ca śloke — that praise-song); parjanya iva — as Parjanya spreads the water by sending down rain; tatanaḥ — spread it out and sing; ukthyam — fit for praise; gāyatram — the sūkta that stands in the Gāyatrī metre; gāya — recite."

Bhāvārtha — "Composing the praise-song in your mouth, sing it out and spread it as Parjanya sends down rain and spreads the water. Recite the sūkta in the Gāyatrī metre that is fit for praise."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 333) — "Compose a verse in your mouth, spread it out like a cloud spreading rain ; chant that verse like a verse of Gayatri metre."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 333 - mimīhi — "compose, make; compose." (the source adds the English "compose"). - śloka — "praise, sūkta, sentence. Because the word śloka is read among the fifty-seven names of speech beginning with dhārā (Ni. printed "2-23"; first digit a curled ೨), śloka means a sentence in the form of praise." - parjanya iva tatanaḥ — "as rain falls on the earth and the water spreads over every place, spread out the praise-sentence you have composed: this is the intention." - gāyatraṃ ukthyam — "ukthya means: recite the śastra-mantras, the ṛks of the Gāyatrī metre that praise the deities: so the sense."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 334–335 — grammar pages, characterized - mimīhi: root māṅ māne, of the juhotyādi class; it is ñit, so by anudāttañita ātmanepadam — अनुदात्तङित आत्मनेपदम् — [Pā. Sū. 1-3-12] the ātmanepada would be proper, but the parasmaipada comes instead by vyatyayo bahulam — व्यत्ययो बहुलम् — [Pā. Sū. 3-1-85]; loṭ, madhyama singular sip; serhyapicca — सेर्ह्यपिच्च — [Pā. Sū. 3-4-87] the substitute hi; since apicca ("not pit") is said, sārvadhātukam apit — सार्वधातुकमपित् — [Pā. Sū. 1-2-4] makes a non-pit sārvadhātuka ṅit; śap → ślu by juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ; ślau — श्लौ — [Pā. Sū. 6-1-10] doubling: mā-mā + hi; hrasvaḥ — ह्रस्वः — [Pā. Sū. 7-4-59] shortens the reduplicate; bhṛñām it — भृञामित् — [Pā. Sū. 7-4-76] gives i to the reduplicate; alo 'ntyasya — अलोऽन्त्यस्य — [Pā. Sū. 1-1-52] — a substitute taught for a ṣaṣṭhī-word goes to its final letter, so the i goes to the last letter of the reduplicate; the print then discusses the paribhāṣā nānarthake 'lo 'ntyavidhir anabhyāsavikāre [Paribhā. 106], saying that the alo 'ntyasya rule does not operate where the substitute is meaningless, except in the change of a reduplicate, which here applies; mi + mā + hi; īhalyaghoḥ — ईहल्यघोः — [Pā. Sū. 6-4-113]: the ā of śnā and of a reduplicated base becomes ī before a kit/ṅit sārvadhātuka beginning with a consonant: mimīhi. Since it stands at the beginning of a pāda, the wholly-unaccented rule does not apply; hi is acute by the suffix accent. - āsye: root asu kṣepaṇe: "asyate = kṣipyate asminn ity āsyam": "the things to be eaten are thrown into this" is the analytical sentence. Kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam — कृत्यल्युटो बहुलम् — [Pā. Sū. 3-3-113]: the kṛtya suffixes (the adhikāra of kṛtyāḥ, Pā. 3-1-95 [as printed]) and lyuṭ come variously, i.e. in senses other than those in which they are prescribed; the suffix ṇyat, prescribed by ṛhaloṇ ṇyat [Pā. Sū. 3-1-124] in the senses of state and passive, comes by bahulagrahaṇa in the sense of the locus too; ata upadhāyāḥ — अत उपधायाः — [Pā. Sū. 7-2-116] gives the ā by vṛddhi; as + ya = āsya; tit svaritam — तित्स्वरितम् — [Pā. Sū. 6-1-185]: "the print says that 'antaḥ' of the sūtra karṣātvato ghañanta udāttaḥ (no number printed) is carried forward": the last vowel of the suffix, a tit one, is svarita: so the a of the suffix is svarita. - tatanaḥ: tanu vistāre; liḍarthe leṭ — लिङर्थे लेट् — [Pā. Sū. 3-4-7]: in the senses in which liṅ is prescribed, in the sūtras vidhinimantraṇāmantraṇa… (no number printed) and hetuhetumator liṅ (no number printed), in the Veda leṭ comes; in its place madhyama singular sip; leṭo 'ḍāṭau — लेटोऽडाटौ — [Pā. Sū. 3-4-94] the augment aṭ; itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu — इतश्च लोपः परस्मैपदेषु — [Pā. Sū. 3-4-97] loss of the i; bahulaṃ chandasi [Pā. Sū. 2-4-76] śap → ślu, doubling: tan + tan + as; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ — loss of the n of the reduplicate; tatanas; the s becomes ru, then visarga. - gāyatram: "gāyatryā idam"; tasyedam — तस्येदम् — [Pā. Sū. 4-3-120]: after a base ending in a ṣaṣṭhī-word, in the sense of "this is his", the aṇ and the other of the "big five" suffixes, and the chādi suffixes, come. According to the Śekhara author the tasyedam is just the statement of the desired sense; śeṣe is carried forward: "upayuktād anyaḥ śeṣaḥ" — the senses other than those already used are called śeṣa; those ending with the fourth case [apatyādi caturthyantāḥ] were stated before; the suffixes aṇ and the rest come in the sense "this is his" after a base that has the sandhi of a kṛta. By implication, an ṛ-word of the same kind is a base for the base; the print then argues over prātipadika and whether the sixth-case ending must be taken, relying on ghakālatāneṣu kālanāmnaḥ — घकालतनेषु कालनाम्नः — [Pā. Sū. 6-3-17], where tarap and tamap as taddhita suffixes follow and the aluk of the locative is prescribed, and so on; the conclusion being that the taddhita suffix comes even with the sup intervening, as the Śekhara author thinks, so that here the sixth case is taken: gāyatrī + a; yasyeti ca the loss of ī. [This passage is very crowded; the drift only.] The second analysis: root gai śabde, then laṭ, śatṛ; śap and āy substituted, gāyat, gāyataḥ: "trāyate" — root trai pālane; ādeca upadeśe 'śiti — आदेच उपदेशेऽशिति — [Pā. Sū. 6-1-45] ā for the ai; ato 'nupasarge kaḥ — आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः — [Pā. Sū. 3-2-3] the suffix ka after a root ending in ā when no prefix; trā + a; āto lopa iṭi ca — आतो लोप इटि च — [Pā. Sū. 6-4-64] the loss of the ā; gāyat + tra = gāyatra; one t is lost by Vedic usage; accusative singular am; gāyatra + am; ami pūrvaḥ — अमि पूर्वः — [Pā. Sū. 6-1-107] the prior form: gāyatram. Rik 14 ends here (|| 14 ||).

Rik 15

Saṃhitā-pāṭha p. 336 = PDF 351 of the better scan; Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented

वन्द॑स्व मारु॑तं ग॒णं त्वे॒षं प॑न॒स्युम॒र्किण॑म् । अ॒स्मे वृ॒द्धा अ॑सन्नि॒ह ॥ १५ ॥

vandasva mārutaṃ gaṇaṃ tveṣaṃ panasyum arkiṇam | asme vṛddhā asann iha || 15 ||

Pada-pāṭha

वन्दस्व । मारुतम् । गणम् । त्वेषम् । पनस्युम् । अर्किणम् । अस्मे इति । वृद्धाः । असन् । इह ॥ १५ ॥

vandasva | mārutam | gaṇam | tveṣam | panasyum | arkiṇam | asme iti | vṛddhāḥ | asan | iha || 15 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

हे ऋत्विक्संघ मारुतं मरुत्सम्बन्धिनं गणं समूहं वन्दस्व । नमस्कुरु स्तुहि वा । कीदृशं गणं । त्वेषं दीप्तं पनस्युं स्तुतियोग्यं अर्किणमर्चनोपेतं । अस्मे अस्माकमिहास्मिन्कर्मणि वृद्धा आसन् । मरुतः प्रवृद्धा भवन्तु ॥ वन्दस्व । वदि अभिवादनस्तुत्योः । आदुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः । पनस्युं । पन च इति स्तुत्यर्थो धातुः । असुन् । पनः स्तोत्रमात्मन इच्छतीति पनस्युः । सुप आत्मनः क्यच् । क्याच्छन्दसीत्युप्रत्ययः । आर्किणं । ऋच स्तुतौ पुंसि सञ्ज्ञायामिति घः । अर्कोऽस्यास्तीत्यर्की । अत इनिठनौ । असन् । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुगभावः । इतश्च लोप इतीकारलोपः । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः ॥ १७ ॥

he ṛtviksaṃgha mārutaṃ marutsambandhinaṃ gaṇaṃ samūhaṃ vandasva | namaskuru stuhi vā | kīdṛśaṃ gaṇaṃ | tveṣaṃ dīptaṃ panasyuṃ stutiyogyaṃ arkiṇam arcanopetaṃ | asme asmākam ihāsmin karmaṇi vṛddhā āsan | marutaḥ pravṛddhā bhavantu || vandasva | vadi abhivādanastutyoḥ | ād upadeśāl lasārvadhātukānudāttatve dhātusvaraḥ | panasyuṃ | pana ca iti stutyartho dhātuḥ | asun | panaḥ stotram ātmana icchatīti panasyuḥ | supa ātmanaḥ kyac | kyāc chandasīty u pratyayaḥ | ārkiṇaṃ | ṛca stutau puṃsi sañjñāyām iti ghaḥ | arko 'syāstīty arkī | ata iniṭhanau | asan | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo lugabhāvaḥ | itaś ca lopa itīkāralopaḥ | tiṅ atiṅa iti nighātaḥ || 17 ||

Translation: "O company of priests, mārutam gaṇam, the host belonging to the Maruts, vandasva — salute, or praise. What is the host like? Tveṣam — shining; panasyum — fit for praise; arkiṇam — endowed with worship. Asme — of us, iha, in this rite, vṛddhā asan — let them be grown: let the Maruts be grown. Vandasva: root vadi, in the senses of salutation and praise; the root accent, because the la-substitute sārvadhātuka is unaccented after a root with an acute [? as printed: ād upadeśāl…]. Panasyum: the root pana [read with ca] in the sense of praise; the suffix asun; 'panaḥ', praise, 'ātmana icchati', one who desires it for himself, is panasyuḥ; kyac after a sup in the sense of desiring for oneself (supa ātmanaḥ kyac); the suffix u after kya by kyāc chandasi. Ārkiṇam: the root ṛca stutau; the suffix gha by puṃsi saṃjñāyāṃ ghaḥ prāyeṇa; 'arko 'syāstīti arkī', one that has the arka; by ata iniṭhanau the suffix ini. Asan: by bahulaṃ chandasi the śap is not elided; the loss of i by itaś ca lopaḥ…; the verb is unaccented by tiṅ atiṅaḥ."

Pratipadārtha — "tveṣam — one with brilliance; panasyum — fit to be praised; arkiṇam — one worthy of worship; mārutaṃ gaṇam — the host of the Maruts; vandasva — salute, or praise; asme — our; iha — in this sacrificial rite; vṛddhā asan — let those Marut-deities be increased (let them shine forth)."

Bhāvārtha — "O priests! Salute, or praise, the Marut-deities, who are full of brilliance, fit to be praised, and worthy of worship. In this sacrificial rite of ours may the Maruts be increased, and may our sacrifice be carried through in all its parts."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 337) — "Glorify the host of Maruts, brilliant, deserving of praise and adoration; may they be pleased in this our worship."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 337 - panasyum — "panaḥ is only stotra; one who desires it for himself is panasyuḥ: one who longs for praise, deserving praise, fit to be praised." - arkiṇam — "ṛca stutau; arka is mantra; 'arko mantro bhavati', says Yāska (Ni. 5-4). Arka means mantra, stotra. 'arko 'syāstīti arkī', that which has a stotra: one who is praised with the stotra, one fit for praise." - asme = asmākam — "our; in the Ṛgveda, in many places, the word asme is used in place of asmākam." - vṛddhā asan = pravṛddhā bhavatu — "let them be increased: that is, let them be praised, let them shine."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 337–339 — grammar pages, characterized - vandasva: root vadi abhivādanastutyoḥ, idit; idito num dhātoḥ — इदितो नुम् धातोः (no number printed) the augment num; ātmanepada; loṭ, madhyama singular thās; thāsaḥ se — थासः से (no number printed) the substitute se; savābhyāṃ vāmau — सवाभ्यां वामौ (no number printed) va for the e; śap; being pit it is unaccented; the printed argument that sva is a sārvadhātuka standing for la, and about whether the śap that follows is a-ending or p-ending in the upadeśa (anekāntā anubandhāḥ — "indicatory letters are not [parts]", Paribhā. 4 — so the p is not part of śap, which counts as a-ending in the upadeśa); then the sūtra printed only as tāsyanudāttet, (abbreviated in the print) gives the unaccented sva, so the root accent alone stands. - panasyum: paṇa vyavahāre stutau ca, first class; the root is read here also with pana ca in the sense of praise; sarvadhātubhyo 'sun — सर्वधातुभ्योऽसुन् — [U. Sū. printed "4-6-28" as read, as in Rik 11; middle and last groups doubtful [?]]: asun: panas; "panaḥ = praise; ātmana icchati = he wants it for himself": supa ātmanaḥ kyac — सुप आत्मनः क्यच् — [Pā. Sū. 3-1-8]: kyac after a sup-ending word in the sense of wishing for oneself, optionally; hence panasya; kyāc chandasi — क्याच्छन्दसि — [Pā. Sū. 3-2-170]: the kya word allows (kyac-kyaṣ-kyaṅ, all three) the suffix u after the kya-ending base in the Veda, in senses such as habitual disposition; so panasyu: "one who naturally desires praise of himself". - arkiṇam: ṛca stutau, tudādi; puṃsi saṃjñāyāṃ ghaḥ prāyeṇa — पुंसि सञ्ज्ञायां घः प्रायेण — [Pā. Sū. 4-3-118 as printed; for 3-3-118] the suffix gha; its gh has the indicatory-letter name; ṛc + a; cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ — चजोः कु घिण्ण्यतोः — [Pā. Sū. 7-3-52]: k for c and j before ghit, ṇit, yat; guṇa of the penultimate: ṛ → ar; arka: the worship that is made with stotra is taken here; "arkaḥ asya asti": for the sense "this has it", ata ini-ṭhanau — अत इनिठनौ — [Pā. Sū. 5-2-115]: after a base ending in a the suffixes ini and ṭhan in the sense of matup: so ini. Although the Mahābhāṣya has the sūtra एकाक्षरात्कृतो जातेः सप्तम्यां च न तौ स्मृतौ (ekākṣarāt kṛto jāteḥ saptamyāṃ ca na tau smṛtau, printed as Pā. Sū. 5-2-115-2) — ini and ṭhan do not come after a base with one syllable, one ending in a kṛt suffix, or a word denoting a species, or in the sense of the locative — the print says: arka is a kṛt-ending word, so how can ini come after it? Not so: the Bhāṣya's examples are svavān (single-syllable), kārakavān (kṛtaḥ), vṛkṣavān (jāteḥ), daṇḍavān ("in this hall there are staves", locative); the print answers that arka here is kṛdanta but not a species-word, so the prohibition does not apply; the clause is only for the most part (prāyika); in some places it does not apply, so the prohibition is not applied here. The page is very crowded; this is a summary and may contain slips. The word iti in the sūtra tad asyāsty asminn iti matup is to be connected with each, which shows that the sense of worldly usage is meant (iti śabdo laukikīṃ vivakṣāṃ manusārayati); so ini etc. come sometimes after a kṛdanta too, e.g. kāryī, as the vṛttikāra and others hold. - āsan at the top of p. 339: as bhuvi, adādi; by bahulaṃ chandasi the śap is not elided [in this case]; leṭ, jhi; the substitute ant; by itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu the loss of the i; by saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ — संयोगान्तस्य लोपः — the loss of the final consonant [the print has ś ("śge lopa"), as printed [sic]]; tiṅ atiṅaḥ gives the wholly-unaccented form. Rik 15 ends here (|| 15 ||).

End of Sūkta 38. After the grammar of Rik 15, at the top of printed p. 339, a flourish closes the sūkta; unlike the close of Sūkta 37, there is no printed closing sentence ("illige … sūktavu pūrṇavu") on the page. Below it begins Sūkta 39 (pra yad itthā, "the thirty-ninth sūkta", title line mūvattombhattaneya sūktavu, Anuvāka 8, fourth sūkta; ten Riks; ṛṣi Kaṇva Ghaura; Maruts; the Prāgātha [bṛhatī–satobṛhatī] metre — as read from the Kannada introduction at the foot of p. 339); its introduction and Rik 1 are not yet written and belong to the next session.

Summary of Sūkta 38. Fifteen Riks to the Maruts, all written in full. They open with a prayer that the Maruts take up the sacrificers as a father his son (Rik 1), ask where they are, where their treasures are (Riks 2–3), say that were they mortal their praiser would be immortal (4), and pray that the praiser not be negligent and not tread the road of Yama (5) and that Nirṛti, with craving, perish (6); then describe their rain, with lightning and thunder, in the desert and over the houses (Riks 7–10), their journey along the banks of rivers (11) and the firmness of their chariots (12); the last three Riks (13–15) turn to the priests, bidding them sing, compose and praise the host of the Maruts. The doubtful parts are the many reference numerals, the heavily crowded grammar pages, and the passages named in the flags below.

prayad itthety daśarcaṃ caturthaṃ sūktam | ghoraputrasya kaṇvasyārṣam | maruddevatākaṃ | yujaḥ satobṛhatyaḥ | ayujo bṛhatyaḥ | pra yad daśa prāgāthaṃ tv ity anukramaṇikā | gato viniyogaḥ ||

Translation: "Pra yad itthā — the fourth sūkta [of the anuvāka], of ten ṛks; the seer's work of Kaṇva, the son of Ghora; its deity is the Maruts; the even-numbered [ṛks] (yujaḥ) are Satobṛhatī; the odd-numbered (ayujaḥ) are Bṛhatī. The Anukramaṇikā [says]: 'pra yad daśa prāgātham tu' ('pra yad: ten [ṛks], but prāgātha'). The application (viniyoga) has been stated [before]." Translation tentative. The page also carries, above the title, the end of Sūkta 38's grammar, "… || 15 ||" [printed ೧೫].

Anuvāda (Kannada), p. 339 — "Pra yad itthā is the fourth sūkta in the eighth anuvāka. In it there are ten ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Kaṇva, the son of Ghora; the deities are the Maruts. Prāgātha is the metre: the even-numbered ṛks are in the Satobṛhatī metre, the odd-numbered ṛks in the Bṛhatī metre. What the Anukramaṇikā says is 'pra yad daśa prāgātham' [as read]. The viniyoga has been stated already."

हे धूतयः स्थावरादीनां कम्पनकारिणो मरुतो यद्यदा मानं मननीयं युष्मद्बलं परावतो दूरात् । आरे परावत इति दूरनामसु पाठात् । इत्थास्मादन्तरिक्षात्प्रास्यथ भूमौ प्रक्षिपथ । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । शोचिर्न तेज इव । यथा सूर्यस्य तेजोऽन्तरिक्षाद्भूमौ प्रक्षिप्यते तद्वत् । तदानीं यूयं कस्य यजमानस्य क्रत्वा क्रतुना सङ्गच्छध्व इति शेषः । तथा कस्य यजमानस्य वर्पसा स्तोत्रेण सङ्गच्छध्वे । कं यजमानमुद्दिश्य याथ । देवयजनदेशे गच्छथ । कं ह कं खलु यजमानमनुगृह्णीथेति शेषः ॥ इत्था । थाहेतौ च च्छन्दसि । पा. सू. ५-३-२६ । इतीदंशब्दात्प्रकारवचने थाप्रत्ययः । यदि तत्रेदंशब्दस्य नानुवृत्तिस्तर्हि थमुप्रत्ययान्तादिदंशब्दादुत्तरस्या विभक्तेर्व्यत्ययेन सुपां सुलुगिति डादेशः । प्रथमपक्षे प्रत्ययस्वरः । द्वितीयपक्षे तूदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरः । अस्यथ । असु क्षेपणे । अदुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वे श्यनो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । क्रत्वा । जसादिषु छन्दसि वा वचनं । पा. सू. ७-३-१०९-१ । इति नाभावस्य विकल्पितत्वादभावः । वर्पसा । वृङ् सम्भक्तौ । वृङ्शीङ्भ्यां रूपस्वाङ्गयोः पुक्च । उ. ४-२०० । इत्यसुन् । तत्सन्नियोगेन पुगागमश्च । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं । अत्र रूपाभिधायिना वर्पस्शब्देन देवतास्वरूपप्रकाशकं स्तोत्रं लक्ष्यते । क्रतुना साहचर्यात् ॥

he dhūtayaḥ sthāvarādīnāṃ kampanakāriṇo maruto yad yadā mānaṃ mananīyaṃ yuṣmadbalaṃ parāvato dūrāt | āre parāvata iti dūranāmasu pāṭhāt | itthāsmād antarikṣāt prāsyatha bhūmau prakṣipatha | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | śocir na teja iva | yathā sūryasya tejo 'ntarikṣād bhūmau prakṣipyate tadvat | tadānīṃ yūyaṃ kasya yajamānasya kratvā kratunā saṅgacchadhva iti śeṣaḥ | tathā kasya yajamānasya varpasā stotreṇa saṅgacchadhve | kaṃ yajamānam uddiśya yātha | devayajanadeśe gacchatha | kaṃ ha kaṃ khalu yajamānam anugṛhṇīteti śeṣaḥ || itthā | thāhetau ca cchandasi | pā. sū. 5-3-26 | itīdaṃśabdāt prakāravacane thāpratyayaḥ | yadi tatredaṃśabdasya nānuvṛttis tarhi thamupratyayāntād idaṃśabdād uttarasyā vibhakter vyatyayena supāṃ sulug iti ḍādeśaḥ | prathamapakṣe pratyayasvaraḥ | dvitīyapakṣe tūdāttanivṛttisvaraḥ | asyatha | asu kṣepaṇe | adupadeśāl lasārvadhātukānudāttatve śyano nittvād ādyudāttatvaṃ | yadvṛttayogād anighātaḥ | kratvā | jasādiṣu chandasi vā vacanaṃ | pā. sū. 7-3-109-1 | iti nābhāvasya vikalpitatvād abhāvaḥ | varpasā | vṛṅ sambhaktau | vṛṅśīṅbhyāṃ rūpasvāṅgayoḥ puk ca | u. 4-200 | ity asun | tatsanniyogena pugāgamaś ca | nittvād ādyudāttatvaṃ | atra rūpābhidhāyinā varpasśabdena devatāsvarūpaprakāśakaṃ stotraṃ lakṣyate | kratunā sāhacaryāt ||

Translation: "O dhūtayaḥ, shakers of fixed things and the like — Maruts — yad, when, mānam, your estimable strength, parāvataḥ, from afar (since āre, parāvataḥ are read among the names of 'far'), itthā, asmād antarikṣāt, from this atmosphere, prāsyatha, you cast, you throw down to the earth. The example: śocir na — like light: as the light of the sun is thrown from the atmosphere to the earth, so. Then, kasya, with which sacrificer's kratu, rite, do you meet — so the remainder is to be supplied — and, with which sacrificer's varpas, praise, are you united? Kam yātha — aiming at which sacrificer do you go to the place of the divine rite? Kam ha — whom indeed do you favour? so the remainder."

Translation of the grammatical tail characterized; numerals zoom-checked: Itthā — by thāhetau ca chandasi (Pā. Sū. 5-3-26) the suffix thā, in the sense of manner, after the word idam; if the word idam is not carried over there, then, after a base ending in tham, the case-ending of the word idam is given the substitute ḍā by vyatyaya, via supāṃ sulug…; in the first alternative the accent is that of the suffix, in the second the accent that follows the disappearance of an acute. Asyatha — root asu kṣepaṇe; the unaccentedness of the sārvadhātuka after a root with an acute, and since śyan is nit, the first syllable is acute; no nighāta because of the connection with yat. Kratvā — by the vārttika jasādiṣu chandasi vā vacanam (Pā. Sū. 7-3-109-1) the nā-substitute is optional, so here it does not occur. Varpasā — root vṛṅ sambhaktau; the Uṇādi suffix asun with the augment puk (U. 4-200; this font's ಙ has a ಜ-like shape, as in ṅīṣ and ṅas on p. 349, so the roots read vṛṅ, śīṅ); because it is nit the first syllable is acute; "here by the word varpas, which denotes form, the praise that reveals the nature of the deity is meant, by association with kratu."

Pratipadārtha — "dhūtayaḥ — (O Maruts) you who make even immovable things tremble; marutaḥ — O Maruts; yat — when; mānam — your worshipful strength; parāvataḥ — from a very distant region; itthām — from this atmosphere; śocir na — as the sun sends out its rays; prāsyatha — you spread [your strength] over the earth; kasya — of which sacrificer; kratvā — [by the rite] to which will you go? kasya — of which sacrificer; varpasā — by the praise [will you be satisfied]; kam — aiming at which sacrificer; yātha — do you go to the place of sacrifice? kam ha — whom indeed [will you favour]?"

Bhāvārtha — "O Maruts, who have the strength to make fixed things tremble: as the rays of the sun fall from the atmosphere and spread out to all the world, your worshipful power spreads from the atmosphere to all the worlds. Now to the sacrifice of which sacrificer will you go? By whose praise will you be satisfied? Aiming at which sacrificer do you go to the place of sacrifice? Whom will you favour?"

Page 342 (better scan PDF 357)

English Translation (the source's own, p. 342) — "O Maruts, you make all things tremble ; you direct your awful power downwards from afar, as light descends from the heaven ; by whose worship, by whose praise are you attracted ? To what place of sacrifice or to whom indeed do you repair ?"

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 342 - "The sense of this ṛk begins abruptly [toḍakāgiruvudu]. The power of the Marut-deities is boundless. It spreads over the earth like the rays of the sun, falling downward from the atmosphere very far away. O Marut-deities who have such power: now to whose place of sacrifice will you go? To favour whom will you go? — this is the main intention. In this intention, when the ṛṣi asks 'where have you gone?', there must have been a calm state, without thunder and without rain; and therefore he asks where the Marut-deities have gone. Earlier, in the 35th sūkta, 7th ṛk [printed ೩೫, ೭], the ṛṣi Hiraṇyastūpa, at night-time, addressing Savitṛ (the Sun), asked a question of this very kind: 'Where is the sun now? What world is he lighting?' When the visible Sun, Maruts and other deities are not seen at an unusual time, astonished questions such as 'Where do they go? Where are they now?' are natural." - parāvataḥ — "since the word parāvataḥ is read among the five names of 'far' beginning with āke, parāke (Ni. 3-20), parāvataḥ means 'from afar'. The sense is that the wind blows from very far away in the atmosphere." - śocir na — "'like a brilliant thing': that is, as the light of the sun comes to the earth from very far: so the intention of the example." - varpasā = stotreṇa — vṛṅ sambhaktau — "by praise." - dhūtayaḥ = sthāmādīnāṃ kampanakāriṇaḥ — "those who, by the power of their strength, make shake [make sway] fixed things such as houses, and trees and the like."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā p. 342 foot, begun; the rest on p. 343 not yet written - pra: upasargāś cābhivarjam — उपसर्गाश्चाभिवर्जम् — (Phi. Sū. 82, as printed: ಲ then a curled ೨, not ೦): the prefixes, except abhi, are first-syllable acute; so pra is ādyudātta. Continued on p. 343.

Page 343 (better scan PDF 358)

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 39.1, continued p. 343, old-scan PDF 357 — grammar page, noted briefly - itthā: thā hetau ca chandasi — था हेतौ च छन्दसि — (Pā. Sū. 5-3-26): the suffix thā in the senses of cause and manner after idam and kim, in the Veda; the print explains that idam comes by carry-over (anuvṛtti) from the sūtra idamas thamuḥ — इदमस्थमुः — and kim from kimaś ca — किमश्च —; "the idam is carried over, since in the Veda the words kim and idam are in question"; idam + thā; idam iś — इदम इश् — would give iś in its place, but it is barred by etetau rathoḥ — एतेतौ रथोः — (Pā. Sū. 5-3-4): before a prāgdīvyatīya suffix beginning with r or th, idam gets the substitutes eta and it: it; it + thā = itthā. The print adds that if one does not accept this carry-over, one takes, by idamas thamuḥ (Pā. Sū. 5-3-24; the number is printed at this second mention), idam + thamu ("itthamu") and gives the ending following it the substitute ḍā by supāṃ sulug…, with loss of the ṭi: itthā. In the first alternative the word is final-acute by the suffix accent; in the second the ending is acute by anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ — अनुदात्तस्य च यत्रोदात्तलोपः — (no number printed), so again final-acute. - asyatha: root asu kṣepaṇe, divādi; loṭ, madhyama tha [as the print says]; divādibhyaḥ śyan — दिवादिभ्यः श्यन् — (no number printed): śyan; by the paribhāṣā anekāntā anubandhāḥ the root's accentual status is that of an adupadeśa; the la-substitute sārvadhātuka after it is unaccented by tāsyanudāttetṅidupadeśalasārvadhātukam anudāttam, and śyan being nit, the word ending in the suffix is first-syllable acute; because of the connection with yat there is no wholly-unaccented form. - kratvā: jasādiṣu chandasi vā vacanam prāṅṇau caṅy upadhāyāḥ — जसादिषु छन्दसि वा वचनं प्राङ्णौ चङ्युपधायाः — the vārttika (Pā. Sū. 7-3-109-1): in this section the operations laid down up to ṇau caṅy upadhāyāḥ are optional in the Veda; so āṅo nāstriyām — आङो नास्त्रियाम् — the nā-substitute for the instrumental ṭā — does not come; the yaṇ substitution: kratu + ā = kratvā. - varpasā: vṛṅ śīṅbhyāṃ rūpasvāṅgayoḥ puk ca — वृङ् शीङ्भ्यां रूपस्वाङ्गयोः पुक्च — (U. Sū., no number printed here): after the roots vṛṅ and śīṅ, in the senses "form" and "own limb", the suffix asun, and the augment puk in the base; vṛp + as, guṇa of the light penultimate: varpas; instrumental singular. "Here the word rūpa ['form'] is by implication to be taken as 'praise that reveals the form', because of the association with the word kratu." Rik 1 ends here (|| 1 ||).

हे मरुतो व आयुधा युष्माकमायुधानि पराणुदे शत्रूणामपनोदनाय स्थिरा सन्तु स्थिराणि भवन्तु । उतापि च प्रतिष्कभे शत्रूणां प्रतिबन्धाय वीळु सन्तु । दृढानि सन्तु । युष्माकं तविषी बलं पनीयसी अतिशयेन स्तोतव्यं भवतु । मायिनोऽस्मासु छद्मचारिणो मर्त्यस्य मनुष्यस्य शत्रोर्मा । बलं मा भवतु ॥ स्थिरा । आयुधा । उभयत्र शेश्छन्दसि बहुलमिति शेर्लोपः । पराणुदे । णुद प्रेरणे । सम्पदादिलक्षणः क्विप् । उपसर्गादसमासेऽपि । पा. ८-४-१४ । इति णत्वं । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । वीळु । सुपां सुलुगिति विभक्तेर्लुक् । ईषाअक्षादित्वात्प्रकृतिभावः । पा. ६-१-१२७-२ । प्रतिष्कभे । स्कन्भुः सौत्रो धातुः । सम्पदादिलक्षणो भावे क्विप् । अनिदितामिति नलोपः । पनीयसी । पनतिः स्तुत्यर्थः । अस्मादौणादिकः कर्मण्यसुन् । तत ईयसुनि टेरिति टिलोपः । उगितश्चेति ङीप् । ईयसुनो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं । मायिनः । मायाशब्दस्य व्रीह्यादिषु पाठात् व्रीह्यादिभ्यश्चेति मत्वर्थीये इनिः ॥

he maruto va āyudhā yuṣmākam āyudhāni parāṇude śatrūṇām apanodanāya sthirā santu sthirāṇi bhavantu | utāpi ca pratiṣkabhe śatrūṇāṃ pratibandhāya vīḷu santu | dṛḍhāni santu | yuṣmākaṃ taviṣī balaṃ panīyasī atiśayena stotavyaṃ bhavatu | māyino 'smāsu chadmacāriṇo martyasya manuṣyasya śatror mā | balaṃ mā bhavatu || sthirā | āyudhā | ubhayatra śeś chandasi bahulam iti śer lopaḥ | parāṇude | ṇuda preraṇe | sampadādilakṣaṇaḥ kvip | upasargād asamāse 'pi | pā. 8-4-14 | iti ṇatvaṃ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | vīḷu | supāṃ sulug iti vibhakter luk | īṣāakṣāditvāt prakṛtibhāvaḥ | pā. 6-1-127-2 | pratiṣkabhe | skanbhuḥ sautro dhātuḥ | sampadādilakṣaṇo bhāve kvip | anidit ām iti nalopaḥ | panīyasī | panatiḥ stutyarthaḥ | asmād auṇādikaḥ karmaṇy asun | tata īyasuni ṭer iti ṭilopaḥ | ugitaś ceti ṅīp | īyasuno nittvād ādyudāttatvaṃ | māyinaḥ | māyāśabdasya vrīhyādiṣu pāṭhāt vrīhyādibhyaś ceti matvarthīye iniḥ ||

Translation: "O Maruts, vaḥ āyudhā, your weapons — parānude, in order to thrust away enemies — sthirā santu, let them be firm. Uta — and — pratiṣkabhe, in order to check enemies, vīḷu santu, let them be strong, stout. Yuṣmākam taviṣī, your strength, let it be panīyasī, extremely praiseworthy; and the strength of the martyasya, the mortal, the man who is an enemy, māyinaḥ, deceitful towards us, going about in disguise — mā, let it not be. Sthirā, āyudhā: in both the loss of śi by śeś chandasi bahulam. Parānude: root ṇuda preraṇe; kvip of the sampadādi class; ṇatva by upasargād asamāse 'pi (Pā. 8-4-14); the accent of the first member of a compound ending in a kṛt. Vīḷu: loss of the ending by supāṃ sulug…; prakṛtibhāva because [the word] is in the īṣā-akṣādi [list] (Pā. 6-1-127-2). Pratiṣkabhe: skambhu is a sautra root; kvip in the abstract sense; the loss of n by anidit ām…. Panīyasī: the root pana in the sense of praise; from it the Uṇādi asun in the passive sense; then īyasun, loss of the ṭi; ṅīp by ugitaś ca; īyasun is nit so the first syllable is acute. Māyinaḥ: since māyā is read in the vrīhyādi group, the suffix ini in the sense of matup by vrīhyādibhyaś ca."

Pratipadārtha — "marutaḥ — O Maruts; vaḥ — your; āyudhā — weapons; parānude — for driving away the enemies; sthirā — firm; santu — let them be; uta — and; pratiṣkabhe — for checking the enemies too; vīḷu — let them be strong; yuṣmākam — your; taviṣī — strength; panīyasī — let it be extremely praiseworthy; māyinaḥ — [him who] deceives (us); martyasya — of the enemy in human form; mā — let [his strength] not be [praiseworthy]."

Bhāvārtha — "O Maruts, may your weapons be firm for driving away our powerful enemies. May they be strong for checking them. May your strength be worthy of praise. May the enemy in human form, who deceives us, be without strength."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 345) — "May your weapons be steady, may they be strong to drive away or resist the enemy ; may your strength merit praise, not that of a treacherous mortal."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 345 - parānude — "ṇuda preraṇe: in the matter of opposing enemies." - vīḷu — "vīḍu: firmly, steady." (English as printed: "steady"). - pratiṣkabhe = śatrūṇāṃ pratibandhāya — "for the checking of enemies." - taviṣī = balam — "strength, power, capacity and the like." - panīyasī = panatiḥ stutyarthaḥ | atiśayena stotavyā bhavatu — "let it be worthy of much praise." - māyinaḥ = chadmacāriṇo manuṣyasya — "of a wicked man who deceives": the source adds "treacherous or vily [sic] person."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā p. 346 — grammar page, noted briefly - sthirā, āyudhā: in both words the loss of śi by śeś chandasi bahulam. - parānude: root ṇuda preraṇe; kvip by sampadādibhyaḥ kvip — सम्पदादिभ्यः क्विप् —; upasargād asamāse 'pi ṇopadeśasya — उपसर्गादसमासेऽपि णोपदेशस्य — (Pā. Sū. 8-4-14): the n of a root taught with ṇ, after the r and ṣ of a prefix, becomes ṇ, even without compounding; the print explains that the root ṇuda has ṇ at the beginning; the eight roots nard, nāṭ, nāth, nādh, nand, nakk, nṝ, nṛt are excepted from ṇopadeśa-hood (ṇopadeśās tv anarda-nāṭi-nāth-nādh-nand-nakka-nṝ-nṛtaḥ — णोपदेशास्त्वनर्द-नाटि-नाथ्-नाध्-नन्द्-नक्क-नॄ-नृतः —, zoom-checked); parānud takes the accent of the first member of a compound with a kṛt last member. - vīḷu: supāṃ sulug for the ending; in the Saṃhitā, in vīḷu + uta, prakṛtibhāva by īṣākṣādiṣu chandasi prakṛtibhāvam [ātram] (printed "Pā. S6-1-127", the Sū. run into the 6). - pratiṣkabhe: the root skambhu is not read in the present dhātupāṭha, but Pāṇini's sūtras use it: grasitaskabhita… (Pā. Sū. 7-2-34) has skabhita from the root skambhu ("skambhu rodhane"); kvip of the sampadādi class; anidito hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti — अनिदितां हल उपधायाः क्ङिति — (Pā. Sū. 6-4-24) loss of the nasal. - panīyasī: the root pana is read in the sense of praise; after it the Uṇādi asun in the passive sense; in the sense of excess, dvivacanavibhajyopapade tarabīyasunau — द्विवचनविभज्योपपदे तरबीयसुनौ — (no number printed) īyasun; ṭeḥ — टेः — (no number printed) loss of as; panīyas is ugit, so ugitaś ca — उगितश्च — (Pā. Sū. 6-3-45 [as printed; for 4-1-6]) gives ṅīp in the feminine; īyasun is nit, so the first syllable is acute. - māyinaḥ: vrīhyādibhyaś ca — व्रीह्यादिभ्यश्च — (Pā. Sū. 5-2-116): after the words in the vrīhyādi group the suffixes ini and ṭhan in the sense of matup; by anyebhya ubhayam ["both"] both suffixes come; and vini by asmāyāmedhāsrajo viniḥ — अस्मायामेधास्रजो विनिः — (printed abbreviated, "asmāyāmedhā—", no number); so the forms māyāvī, māyī, māyikaḥ; in the vrīhyādi group "vrīhi-māyā" is read. Rik 2 ends here (|| 2 ||).

हे नरो नेतारो मरुतो यद्यदा स्थिरं वसु पराहथ वृक्षादिकं पराहतं भग्नं कुरुथ । गुरु पाषाणादिकं गुरुत्वोपेतं वर्तयथ प्रेरयथ । तदानीं पृथिव्याः सम्बन्धिनो वनिनो वनवतो वृक्षान्वियाथन । वियुज्य मध्ये गच्छथ । अरण्यगतानां निबिडानां वृक्षाणां मध्ये यस्य कस्यापि वृक्षस्य भग्नत्वादितरवृक्षाणां परस्परवियोगेन प्रौढो मार्गो भवति । तथा पर्वतानामाशाः पर्वतपार्श्वदिशो वियाथन । वियुज्य गच्छथ ॥ हथ । हन हिंसागत्योः । अनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यादिना अनुनासिकलोपः । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । नरः । पादादित्वादामन्त्रितनिघाताभावः । वर्तयथ । अदुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वे णिचः स्वर एव शिष्यते । यच्छब्दानुषङ्गान्निघाताभावः । याथन । तप्तनप्तनथनाश्चेति थनादेशः ॥

he naro netāro maruto yad yadā sthiraṃ vasu parāhatha vṛkṣādikaṃ parāhataṃ bhagnaṃ kurutha | guru pāṣāṇādikaṃ gurutvopetaṃ vartayatha prerayatha | tadānīṃ pṛthivyāḥ sambandhino vanino vanavato vṛkṣān viyāthana | viyujya madhye gacchatha | araṇyagatānāṃ nibiḍānāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ madhye yasya kasyāpi vṛkṣasya bhagnatvād itaravṛkṣāṇāṃ parasparaviyogena prauḍho mārgo bhavati | tathā parvatānām āśāḥ parvatapārśvadiśo viyāthana | viyujya gacchatha || hatha | hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ | anudāttopadeśety ādinā anunāsikalopaḥ | yadvṛttayogād anighātaḥ | naraḥ | pādāditvād āmantritanighātābhāvaḥ | vartayatha | adupadeśāl lasārvadhātukānudāttatve ṇicaḥ svara eva śiṣyate | yacchabdānuṣaṅgān nighātābhāvaḥ | yāthana | tapta-nap-tana-thanāś ceti thanādeśaḥ ||

Translation: "O naraḥ, leaders, Maruts, yad, when, [a thing that is] sthiram, firm, [you] parā hatha — you break down, make felled and broken — trees and the like; guru, heavy things such as rocks, you vartayatha, make roll, set going. Then pṛthivyāḥ, belonging to the earth, vaninaḥ, forest trees, viyāthana — you go through, having parted [them]. Among the dense trees that have gone into the forest, through the breaking of some one tree or other, a broad way is made by the separation of the other trees from each other. Likewise parvatānām āśāḥ, the āśā of the mountains [the print reads parvatapārśvadiśaḥ, 'the regions of the mountains' flanks'] viyāthana — you go through, parting [them]. Hatha: root han hiṃsāgatyoḥ; the loss of the nasal by the rule beginning anudāttopadeśa…; no nighāta because of the connection with yat. Naraḥ: [not unaccented, since it is] at the beginning of a pāda, there is no āmantrita-nighāta. Vartayatha: [after the śap] the la-substitute sārvadhātuka is unaccented [after a root taught with a] (adupadeśāt…), so only the accent of ṇic remains; no nighāta because yat is to be supplied. Yāthana: the substitute thana by tapta-nap-tana-thanāś ca."

Pratipadārtha — "naraḥ — O leaders of men (Maruts); yat — when; sthiram — fixed, immovable (trees and the like); parā hatha — you roll down (and); guru — heavy objects (such as rocks); vartayatha — you cause to move (when); pṛthivyāḥ — belonging to the earth; vaninaḥ — forest trees; viyāthana — you go through, separating (just so); parvatānām — of mountains; āśāḥ — the directions [print: dikkugaḷannu] (of the narrow passes); vi (yāthana) — you go, separating."

Page 348 (better scan PDF 363)

Bhāvārtha — "O leaders, Marut-deities, you roll down firm trees and the like. You set heavy things such as rocks in motion. Breaking even the forest trees with your force, and parting the narrow mountain passes, you go about easily and freely."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 348) — "O leaders of men, (Maruts) whenever you move you demolist [sic] what is stable, scatter what is heavy, then make your way through the forest trees of earth and through the regious [sic] of the mountains."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 348 - Main intention — "When the Marut-deities move, nothing hinders them. On the earth they roll down, roots and all, the big, big trees that stand well grown and firm. Heavy things, houses and the like, are shaken by the blow of the wind. When they blow among clusters of densely grown forest trees on earth, they break many trees, make a way, and press on. In mountain regions too they make their way through narrow passes." - parā hatha — "hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ; bhagnaṃ kurutha: you break; you throw down." - naraḥ — "nominative plural of the ṛ-ending word nṛ: leaders, guides of men." - guru — "extremely heavy stones, houses and such things." - vi yāthana = viyujya madhye gacchatha — "...in a forest, among densely grown trees, since one tree or another has been broken, the other trees being separated from one another, a broad path comes to be: so the intention." - āśāḥ parvatānām — "the slopes of mountains, or the narrow-pass regions between the mountains."

Page 349 (better scan PDF 364)

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā p. 349 — grammar page, noted briefly; no sūtra numbers printed - hatha: han hiṃsāgatyoḥ; laṭ, tha; the śap elided; by anudāttopadeśa… the loss of the n; because of the connection with yat the verb is not wholly unaccented. - naraḥ: because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, the unaccented vocative of the eighth adhyāya does not apply. - vartayatha: śap is pit and so unaccented; the la-substitute sārvadhātuka after it is unaccented by tāsyanudāttet…, so the accent of ṇic remains; "the word yat of yat sthiram is to be connected here too", and by yadvṛttān nityam the wholly-unaccented form is prohibited. - yāthana: yā prāpaṇe, loṭ, madhyama tha → ta; tapta-nap-tana-thanāś ca gives thana. - vaninaḥ: "vanam eṣām asti": the suffix ini. - pṛthivyāḥ: the root prath + ṣivan; ṣidgaurādibhyaś ca gives ṅīṣ, acute; the genitive ending ṅas [the font's ಙ, ಜ-like], the yaṇ substitution; udāttayaṇo hal-pūrvāt gives the acute to the ending. Rik 3 ends here (|| 3 ||).
