हे रिशादसः शत्रुहिंसका मरुतोऽधिद्यवि द्युलोकस्योपरि वो युष्माकं शत्रुर्नहि विविदे । न च बभूव । तथा भूम्यामपि शत्रुर्न बभूव । हे रुद्रासो रुद्रपुत्रा मरुतो युष्माकमेकोनपञ्चाशत्संख्यानां भवतां युजा योगेन परस्परैकमत्येनाधृषे वैरिणां सर्वतो धर्षणाय तविषी बलं नू चित् क्षिप्रमेव तनास्तु । विस्तृता भवतु ॥ विविदे । विद सत्तायां । लिटि प्रत्ययस्वरः । द्यवि नहि विविदे भूम्यां च न हि विविद इति चशब्दार्थप्रतीतेश्चादिलोपे विभाषेति प्रथमायास्तिङ्विभक्तेर्निघातप्रतिषेधः । प्राथम्यं चानुषक्तक्रियापेक्षया । रिशादसः । रिश हिंसायां । रिशन्ति हिंसन्तीति रिशाः । इगुपधलक्षणः कः । तानदन्तीति रिशादसः । असुन् । आमन्त्रितनिघातः । युजा । युजिर् योगे । ऋत्विगित्यादिना क्विन् । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । रुद्रासः । रुद्रशब्देन तत्सम्बन्धिनो मरुतो लक्ष्यन्ते । आज्जसेरसुक् । नू चित् । ऋचि तुनुघेत्यादिना दीर्घः । आधृषे । ञिधृषा प्रागल्भ्ये । सम्पदादिलक्षणो भावे क्विप् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥

he riśādasaḥ śatruhiṃsakā maruto 'dhidyavi dyulokasyopari vo yuṣmākaṃ śatrur nahi vivide | na ca babhūva | tathā bhūmyām api śatrur na babhūva | he rudrāso rudraputrā maruto yuṣmākam ekonapañcāśatsaṃkhyānāṃ bhavatāṃ yujā yogena parasparaikamatyenādhṛṣe vairiṇāṃ sarvato dharṣaṇāya taviṣī balaṃ nū cit kṣiprameva tanāstu | vistṛtā bhavatu || vivide | vida sattāyāṃ | liṭi pratyayasvaraḥ | dyavi nahi vivide bhūmyāṃ ca na hi vivida iti caśabdārthapratīteś cādilope vibhāṣeti prathamāyās tiṅvibhakter nighātapratiṣedhaḥ | prāthamyaṃ cānuṣaktakriyāpekṣayā | riśādasaḥ | riśa hiṃsāyāṃ | riśanti hiṃsantīti riśāḥ | igupadhalakṣaṇaḥ kaḥ | tān adantīti riśādasaḥ | asun | āmantritanighātaḥ | yujā | yujir yoge | ṛtvigdadhṛksragdiguṣṇigañcuyujikruñcāṃ ca | pā. 3-2-59 [?] | iti kvin | sāvekāca iti vibhakter udāttatvaṃ | rudrāsaḥ | rudraśabdena tatsambandhino maruto lakṣyante | ājjaser asuk | nū cit | ṛci tunughety ādinā dīrghaḥ | ādhṛṣe | dhṛṣā prāgalbhye | sampadādilakṣaṇo bhāve kvip | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ||

Translation: "O riśādasaḥ, destroyers of enemies, Maruts — adhi dyavi, above the heaven-world, vaḥ, for you, an enemy nahi vivide, is not found; and there has not been one; likewise, on the earth also, an enemy has not been. O rudrāsaḥ, sons of Rudra, Maruts — of you who are forty-nine in number, yujā, by union, by agreement among one another, ādhṛṣe, for the overcoming of enemies on all sides, may [your] taviṣī, strength, nū cit, quickly indeed, tanā astu, be extended: be spread. Vivide: root vida sattāyām; the suffix accent in liṭ; [the verb is understood in both halves — 'dyavi nahi vivide, bhūmyāṃ ca na hi vivide' — because the sense of ca is perceived]; on the dropping of a cādi word, by vibhāṣā, for the first [of the pair] the prohibition of nighāta for the first verb-form (tiṅ-vibhakti); the first is 'first' in respect of the action understood. Riśādasaḥ: root riśa hiṃsāyām; 'riśanti, they injure': riśāḥ; the suffix ka by the rule of ik-penultimate roots; 'tān adanti', they eat them: riśādasaḥ; the suffix asun; unaccented as a vocative. Yujā: root yujir yoge; kvin by [the rule beginning] ṛtvig… (no number in the bhāṣya); the ending is acute by sāvekāca. Rudrāsaḥ: by the word rudra the Maruts connected with him are indicated; asuk by ājjaser asuk. Nū cit: the lengthening by ṛci tunughā…. Ādhṛṣe: root ñidhṛṣā prāgalbhye; kvip in the abstract sense of the sampadādi class; the accent of the first member in a compound ending in a kṛt."

Pratipadārtha — "riśādasaḥ — O destroyers of enemies, Maruts; adhi dyavi — in the heaven-world above; vaḥ — for you; śatruḥ — an enemy; na hi vivide — there is not [such] a one; bhūmyām — on the earth also; na babhūva — there has not been at all; rudrāsaḥ — O Maruts, sons of Rudra; yuṣmākam — of you (of forty-nine in number); yujā — by union; ādhṛṣe — for the overpowering of enemies on all sides; taviṣī — [your] strength; nū cit — quickly indeed; tanā astu — let it be extended."

Page 351 (better scan PDF 366)

Bhāvārtha — "O destroyers of enemies, Maruts, for you there is no room for an enemy, whether in heaven or on earth. O Maruts, sons of Rudra, may your joined strength, of you who are forty-nine in number, quickly increase for the destruction of enemies."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 351) — "O distroyers [sic] of the wicked, there exists no adversary of yours above heavens, nor upon this earth, O Sons of Rudras [sic], may four [sic] collective strength be quickly exerted to humble your enemies"

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 351 - riśādasaḥ — "riśa hiṃsāyām; riśanti hiṃsanti iti riśāḥ, enemies; tān adanti iti riśādasaḥ: the root riśa has the sense 'to injure'; those who injure are enemies; these are those who devour or destroy them; so riśādasaḥ: destroyers of enemies." - adhi dyavi = dyulokasyopari — "in the upper part of heaven, or even in the heaven that is above." - taviṣī — "strength, power." - tanā — "tanu vistāre, vistṛtā: let it be spread, that is, let it increase and grow. The word tanā is specially used in the Ṛgveda." - yujā = yogena parasparaikamatyena — "that the Maruts are forty-nine in number is said in the Purāṇas and elsewhere. In the Ṛgveda they are described in another way; see the explanation we wrote on the 1st ṛk of the 37th sūkta [printed ೩೭, ೧]." - rudrāsaḥ — "that the Maruts are the sons of Rudra is described in many places in the Ṛgveda; we have already explained this."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 351–353 — grammar pages, noted briefly - nahi: "abhāve nahy ano nāpi" — अभावे नह्यनो नापि — (Amara., A. Va.): nahi is one unbroken word, an indeclinable; by evādīnām antaḥ — एवादीनामन्तः — it may be said to be final-acute as belonging to the evādi group. Or, by saha supā — सह सुपा — (Pā. Sū. 2-1-4; p. 352), where saha is taken as a separate rule (yogavibhāga): a sup-ending word compounds with a competent sup-ending word; na and hi are compounded by this sūtra; samāsasya — समासस्य — (Pā. Sū. 6-1-223) the last syllable of the compound is acute; hence final-acute. - vaḥ: bahuvacanasya vasnasau — बहुवचनस्य वस्नसौ — (Pā. Sū. 8-1-21): for yuṣmākam, ending in the genitive plural, the unaccented substitute vas. - vivide: root vida sattāyām, divādi, ātmanepada; liṭ → eś for ṭe; the doubling, and the loss of the reduplicate's [consonant] ; no guṇa of the light penultimate: vivide. In the second half, "bhūmyāṃ ca na hi vivide", the sense of ca is understood though ca is not used; there is no verb in the second half of the ṛk, but the verb said before has to be repeated and joined with the second sentence; this brought-in verb is the second; the one in the mantra is the first; by cādilope vibhāṣā — चादिलोपे विभाषा — (Pā. Sū. 8-1-63), when a cādi word is dropped, the first of the two verbs is optionally not unaccented; so there is a prohibition of anudātta for the first. - na: being a nipāta, first-syllable acute. - riśādasaḥ: root riśa hiṃsāyām; "riśanti hiṃsanti iti riśāḥ": enemies who give injury; igupadhajñāprīkiraḥ kaḥ — इगुपधज्ञाप्रीकिरः कः — (Pā. Sū. 3-1-135): after roots with an ik as penultimate (ik = i u ṛ ḷ), and after jñā etc., the suffix ka; the suffix is kit, so no guṇa of the light penultimate; the root ad bhakṣaṇe: "riśān adanti", they eat enemies, that is, destroy them; sarvadhātubhyo 'sun — सर्वधातुभ्योऽसुन् — (U. Sū. 4-6-28, as printed) asun; the vocative is unaccented by the eighth-adhyāya rule. - yujā: yujir yoge; ṛtvigdadhṛksragdiguṣṇigañcuyujikruñcāṃ ca — ऋत्विग्दधृक्स्रग्दिगुष्णिगञ्चुयुजिक्रुञ्चां च — (Pā. Sū. 3-2-59): kvin; instrumental singular ṭā; by sāvekācaḥ… the ending is acute; yuj has one syllable in the locative plural yukṣu. - rudrāsaḥ: "rodayatīti rudraḥ": by rorer ṇiluk ca — रोरेर्णिलुक्च — (U. Sū. 2-179; the 7 is the flat-footed form, set beside a round-headed 2): after the root rudir aśruvimocane, ending in the ṇic suffix, the suffix rak, and the ṇic is elided: rudra; here by implication "belonging to Rudra", that is, the Maruts, are denoted by this word; jas with the augment asuk by ājjaser asuk. - nū: ṛci tunughamakṣutaṅkutroruṣyāṇām — ऋचि तुनुघमक्षुतङ्कुत्रोरुष्याणाम् — (Pā. Sū. 6-3-133; p. 353): in a mantra, with ṛg as a following upapada, these words take the long vowel: nū. - ādhṛṣe: the root ñidhṛṣā prāgalbhye [the grammar page prints ñi dṛṣā, with d]; sampadādibhyaḥ kvip in the abstract sense; compounded with āṅ; the accent of the first member in a compound ending in a kṛt. Rik 4 ends here (|| 4 ||).

पर्वतान्मेरुहिमवदादीन् प्रवेपयन्ति । मरुतः प्रकर्षेण कम्पयन्ति । वनस्पतीन् वटाश्वत्थादींश्च विञ्चन्ति । परस्परवियुक्तान्कुर्वन्ति । हे मरुतो देवासो देवाः सर्वया विशा प्रजया सहिता यूयं प्रो आरत । प्रकर्षेणैव सर्वतो गच्छत । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । दुर्मदा इव । यथा मदोन्मत्ताः स्वेच्छया सर्वतः क्रीडन्ति तद्वत् ॥ वेपयन्ति । टुवेपृ कम्पने । वेपमानान् प्रयुञ्जते । हेतुमण्णिच् । विञ्चन्ति । विचिर् पृथग्भावे । रुधादित्वात् श्नम् । श्नसोरल्लोप इत्यकारलोपः । वनस्पतीन् । वनानां पतयो वनस्पतयः । पारस्करादित्वात्सुट् । वनस्पतिशब्दावाद्युदात्तौ । उभे वनस्पत्यादिषु युगपदिति पूर्वोत्तरपदयोर्युगपत्प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । आरत । ऋ गतौ । लङि मध्यमबहुवचने बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुगभावः । यद्वा लुङ् । सर्त्तिशास्त्यर्तिभ्यश्च । पा. ३-१-५६ । इत्यङ् । आडजादीनामित्याडागमः । आटश्च । पा. ६-१-९० । इति वृद्धिः । देवासः । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वं । सर्वया । सर्वस्य सुपि । पा. ६-१-१९१ । इत्याद्युदात्तत्वं । विशा । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं ॥

parvatān meruhimavadādīn pravepayanti | marutaḥ prakarṣeṇa kampayanti | vanaspatīn vaṭāśvatthādīṃś ca viñcanti | parasparaviyuktān kurvanti | he maruto devāso devāḥ sarvayā viśā prajayā sahitā yūyaṃ pro ārata | prakarṣeṇaiva sarvato gacchata | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | durmadā iva | yathā madonmattāḥ svecchayā sarvataḥ krīḍanti tadvat || vepayanti | ṭuvepṛ kampane | vepamānān prayuñjate | hetumaṇṇic | viñcanti | vicir pṛthagbhāve | rudhāditvāt śnam | śnasor allopa ity akāralopaḥ | vanaspatīn | vanānāṃ patayo vanaspatayaḥ | pāraskarāditvāt suṭ | vanaspatiśabdāv ādyudāttau | ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapad iti pūrvottarapadayoḥ yugapat prakṛtisvaratvaṃ | ārata | ṛ gatau | laṅi madhyamabahuvacane bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo lugabhāvaḥ | yadvā luṅ | sartiśāstyartibhyaś ca | pā. 3-1-56 | ity aṅ | āḍajādīnām ity āḍāgamaḥ | āṭaś ca | pā. 6-1-90 | iti vṛddhiḥ | devāsaḥ | āmantritādyudāttatvaṃ | sarvayā | sarvasya supi | pā. 6-1-191 | ity ādyudāttatvaṃ | viśā | sāvekāca iti vibhakter udāttatvaṃ ||

Translation: "Parvatān — mountains such as Meru and Himavat — pra vepayanti: the Maruts make them shake greatly. Vanaspatīn — banyan, fig and other trees — vi viñcanti: they make them separated from one another. O Maruts, gods, with sarvayā viśā, with all your people, pro ārata, go forth: go greatly on all sides. The example: durmadā iva — as those drunk with intoxication sport on all sides at their own will, so. Vepayanti: root ṭuvepṛ kampane; the ṇic of the causative: they make [the mountains] shaking. Viñcanti: root vicir pṛthagbhāve; śnam because of the rudhādi class; loss of the a by śnasor allopaḥ. Vanaspatīn: 'vanānām patayaḥ'; the augment suṭ because of the pāraskarādi group; the words vana and pati are [each] first-syllable acute; both members keep their accent at the same time by ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapat. Ārata: root ṛ gatau; in laṅ second-person plural, by bahulaṃ chandasi the śap is not elided [as it otherwise would be]; or luṅ: aṅ by sartiśāstyartibhyaś ca (Pā. 3-1-56); the augment āṭ by āḍ ajādīnām; vṛddhi by āṭaś ca. Devāsaḥ: vocative, first-syllable acute. Sarvayā: first-syllable acute by sarvasya supi. Viśā: the ending acute by sāvekāca."

Pratipadārtha — "(marutaḥ — Maruts) parvatān — mountains such as Meru and Himavat; pravepayanti — they shake well; vanaspatīn — forest trees such as the banyan and the fig (grown close together); vi viñcanti — they make to be separate from one another; devāsaḥ marutaḥ — O Maruts, who are gods; sarvayā viśā — together with all your people; durmadā iva — as those full of intoxication wander and sport at will; pro ārata — wander freely all around."

Bhāvārtha — "The Marut-deities make the immovable mountains, Meru, Himavat and the like, shake well. They make the forest trees that grow close together be separated one from another. O Maruts, who are deities, you are free. As men intoxicated with ecstasy sport and wander at will, you too, together with your people, go all around, sporting and wandering."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 354) — "They make the mountains tremble ; They slit asunder the forest trees ; divine Maruts go wether [sic] you wlll [sic] with all your progeny like men in to vicated [sic]."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), pp. 354–355 - Main intention — "Because the power of the Maruts is boundless, they make the mountains shake. Trees and the like that have grown close together are struck by the wind's blow and become separate. O Marut-deities, together with all those in your group — as a man intoxicated moves, as his mind wishes, with no obstruction, so you, with no obstruction, move about at your will." - durmadā iva — "like men intoxicated by drinking an intoxicating substance, who, having no control of the mind, wherever they are, wander about there; or like those who, proud from arrogance and cunning, go about as their mind wishes, with regard to no one." - sarvayā viśā — "with all the people; here 'all the people' means the attendants of the Marut-deities, or the host of the Maruts, forty-nine in number, united."

Page 355 (better scan PDF 370)

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 355–356 — grammar pages, noted briefly - pra: upasargāś cābhivarjam [Phiṭ.]: first-syllable acute. - vepayanti: root ṭuvepṛ kampane, first class, ātmanepada: vepate in the present; "parvatāḥ vepante" means "the mountains shake"; the sense to be intended is that the Maruts make the mountains shake. Hetumati ca — हेतुमति च — (Pā. Sū. 3-1-26): hetu = the instigator; ṇic after roots when the action of an instigator is to be expressed; the Pāṇinīya sages' term hetu is for the one who is the instigator of the agent; vep + i; since the result goes to another, ṇicaś ca — णिचश्च — (Pā. Sū. 1-3-74) the ātmanepada does not come; parasmaipada, laṭ, jhi, ant, śap, guṇa and ay-substitution: vepayanti. - viñcanti: vicir pṛthagbhāve; jhi, ant; rudhādibhyaḥ śnam — रुधादिभ्यः श्नम् — (Pā. Sū. 3-1-78); vi-n-c + anti; śnasor allopaḥ — श्नसोरल्लोपः — (Pā. Sū. 6-4-111): the a of the suffix is lost before a kit or ṅit sārvadhātuka; naś cāpadāntasya jhali — नश्चापदान्तस्य झलि — (Pā. Sū. 8-2-24 [as printed; for 8-3-24]) anusvāra for n; anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ — अनुस्वारस्य ययि परसवर्णः — (Pā. Sū. 8-4-58) gives the homorganic nasal (ñ): viñcanti. - vanaspatīn: "vanānāṃ patayaḥ"; pāraskaraprabhṛtīni ca saṃjñāyām — पारस्करप्रभृतीनि च सञ्ज्ञायाम् — (Pā. Sū. 6-1-157; p. 356): the pāraskarādi words, in names, take suṭ; the group is open (ākṛtigaṇa); so suṭ comes to pati: vanaspati. The neuter word vana is first-syllable acute by nabviṣayasyāni saṃtasya — नब्विषयस्यानि संतस्य — (Phi. Sū. 26; spaced as printed); pāter ḍatiḥ — पातेर्डतिः — (U. Sū. 4-497; last digit flat-footed, read 7): the word pati with the suffix ḍati is first-syllable acute by the suffix accent; on compounding, by ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapat — उभे वनस्पत्यादिषु युगपत् — (Pā. Sū. 6-2-140): in the words of the vanaspatyādi group both first and last members have their own accent at the same time: so both members retain their accent. - ārata: ṛ gatau; laṅ, second-person plural tha → ta; since the root belongs to a ślu-taking class, śap would be elided, but by bahulaṃ chandasi (Pā. Sū. 2-4-76) it is not; ṛ + a + ta; the augment aṭ; sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ gives guṇa; ā + ar + ta; āṭaś ca — आटश्च — (Pā. Sū. 6-1-90) vṛddhi: ārata. Or: the root ṛ, luṅ, ta; cli; sartiśāstyartibhyaś ca — सर्तिशास्त्यर्तिभ्यश्च — (Pā. Sū. 3-1-56) aṅ for cli; ṛdṛśo 'ṅi guṇaḥ — ऋदृशोऽङि गुणः — (Pā. 8-4-16 [as printed; for 7-4-16]) guṇa; ar + a + ta; āḍ ajādīnām — आडजादीनाम् — (Pā. Sū. 6-4-72) the augment āṭ; ā + ar + a + ta; āṭaś ca: ārata. In the second alternative there is no trouble of resorting to Vedic usage; the form may be used in the world also; but by the first process the form is valid in the Veda only. - devāsaḥ: vocative plural; the augment asuk by ājjaser asuk; since it is at the beginning of the fourth pāda the eighth-adhyāya unaccentedness of the vocative does not apply; by āmantritasya ca — the sixth-adhyāya sūtra — it is first-syllable acute. - sarvayā: sarvasya supi — सर्वस्य सुपि — (Pā. Sū. 6-1-191): the first syllable of sarva is acute before a sup. - viśā: root viśa praveśane; kvip; instrumental singular ṭā; sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ — सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिर्विभक्तिः — (no number printed) gives the ending the acute [the print says ādyudātta here, apparently by slip]. Rik 5 ends here (|| 5 ||).

हे मरुतो रथेषु भवदीयेषु पृषतीर्बिन्दुयुक्ता मृगीरुपो सामीप्येनैवायुग्ध्वं । योजितवन्तः । प्रष्टिरेतत्संज्ञको वाहनत्रयमध्यवर्ती मृगविशेषो रोहितो मृगावान्तरजातिर्लोहितवर्णो वहति । रथं नयति । वो युष्माकं यामाय गमनाय पृथिवी चित् अन्तरिक्षमप्याश्रोत् । आभिमुख्येनाशृणोत् । अनुजानातीत्यर्थः । पृथिवीत्यन्तरिक्षनाम । पृथिवी भूः स्वयम्भ्विति तन्नामसु पाठात् । मानुषाः भूलोकवर्तिनः पुरुषा अबीभयन्त । स्वयं भीताः सन्तोऽन्येषामपि भीतिमुत्पादितवन्तः ॥ उपो इति निपातद्वयसमुदायात्मकमन्यन्निपातान्तरं । ओत् । पा. १-१-१५ । इति प्रगृह्यत्वं । आयुग्ध्वं । लुङि झलो झलि । पा. ८-२-२६ । इति सकारस्य लोपः । चोः कुरिति कुत्वं । रोहितः । रुहे रश्च लो वा । उ. ३-९४ । इतीतन्प्रत्ययान्तः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । यामाय । यमेर्भावे घञ् । कर्षात्वत इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते वृषादिषु पाठादाद्युदात्तत्वं । अश्रोत् । श्रु श्रवणे । बहुलं छन्दसीति विकरणस्य लुक् । अबीभयन्त । ञिभी भये । अस्माण्ण्यन्तात् लुङि भीस्म्योर्हेतुभये । पा. १-३-६८ । इत्यात्मने-

Translation of this part: "O Maruts, ratheṣu, in your chariots, pṛṣatīḥ, the spotted does — upo (upa + u) — you have yoked, close by. Praṣṭiḥ, [the animal] so named, standing in the middle of the three draught-animals, rohitaḥ, a sub-species (avāntarajāti) of deer, red-coloured, vahati, draws the chariot. Vaḥ yāmāya: for your going — pṛthivī cit, even the atmosphere — aśrot, heard, i.e. gave assent, so the sense. 'Pṛthivī' is a name of the atmosphere, since it is read among the names of it ('pṛthivī, bhūḥ, svayambhū' — the print runs them as svayambhv iti). Mānuṣāḥ, men living in the earth-world, abībhayanta: being themselves frightened, they caused fear to others also." The grammatical tail so far: upo is a further particle made up of the two particles; by ot [Pā. 1-1-15] it is pragṛhya [exempt from sandhi]; āyugdhvam: in luṅ, by jhalo jhali [Pā. 8-2-26] the loss of the s, k for c by coḥ kuḥ; rohitaḥ: from ruh, with the Uṇādi rule ruhe raś ca lo vā (U. 3-94), the suffix itan; because it is nit, first-syllable acute; yāmāya: ghañ in the abstract sense of yam; though the final acute would be due by karṣātvataḥ…, the word is read in the vṛṣādi group, so first-syllable acute; aśrot: root śru śravaṇe; the vikaraṇa elided by bahulaṃ chandasi; abībhayanta: root ñibhī bhaye, in the causative, in luṅ, ātmanepada by bhīsmyor hetubhaye [Pā. 1-3-68] — the sentence ends here at the foot of the page). (On p. 357 the Pada of Rik 6 is printed without a heading directly under the Saṃhitā.

Pratipadārtha — "(marutaḥ — O Maruts) ratheṣu — in your chariots; pṛṣatīḥ — female deer with spots in the form of dots; upo — joining them closely; ayugdhvam — you have yoked [to the yoke]; rohitaḥ — one of a red colour; praṣṭiḥ — the deer named praṣṭi (yoked in the middle of the three [draught-animals]); vahati — helps to draw [the chariot]; vaḥ — your; yāmāya — for [your] going; pṛthivī cit — the atmosphere also; ā aśrot — gives leave (room); mānuṣāḥ — men (at your going); abībhayanta — are afraid; and they cause fear to others as well."

Bhāvārtha — "O Maruts, you have yoked to your chariot the female deer with their spots. The red deer called praṣṭi, which is in the middle of them, draws your vehicle. Even the atmosphere gives room for your going. When they see your swift approach, men are not only afraid themselves, they cause fear to those who are with them."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 358) — "You have harnessed the spotted deer to your chariot ; the red deer yoked between them helps to drag the car ; the firmament makes way for you and men tremble through fear at your approach."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), pp. 358–359 - pṛṣatīḥ — "The Marut-deities do not yoke horses to their chariots. They yoke female deer with spots, called pṛṣatī. On this matter, in the passage in which Yāska in his Nirukta speaks of the vehicles of the deities: हरी इन्द्रस्य । रोहितोऽग्नेः । हरित आदित्यस्य । रासभावश्विनोः । अजाः पूष्णः । पृषत्यो मरुताम् । अरुण्यो गाव उषसः । श्यावाः सवितुः । विश्वरूपा बृहस्पतेः । नियुतो वायोरिति । (Ni. 2-28) harī indrasya | rohito 'gneḥ | harita ādityasya | rāsabhāv aśvinoḥ | ajāḥ pūṣṇaḥ | pṛṣatyo marutām | aruṇyo gāva uṣasaḥ | śyāvāḥ savituḥ | viśvarūpā bṛhaspateḥ | niyuto vāyor iti. Since this is said, the chariot-horses of the Marut-deities are pṛṣatīḥ, that is, two spotted does." [p. 359: eraḍu heṇṇu jiṅkegaḷu, "two female deer"] The passage is left untranslated by the source. Mine and tentative: "Indra's [are] the two bays; Agni's the red one; the Sun's the tawny ones; the Aśvins' two asses; Pūṣan's goats; the Maruts' spotted does; Uṣas's ruddy cows; Savitṛ's the dark-brown ones; Bṛhaspati's the many-formed ones; Vāyu's the Niyuts." The reference numeral, printed ೨-೨೮, is zoom-checked. - rohitaḥ — "among deer, a kind of red colour; another species of deer, belonging to the class of the spotted deer." - pṛthivī cit aśrot — "among the sixteen names of the atmosphere beginning with ambaram, viyat, the word pṛthivī is read; therefore pṛthivī here means the atmosphere, the path of the wind. Cit aśrot means 'anujānāti': gives permission, or gives room: so the intention."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 359–361 — grammar pages, characterized; numerals zoom-checked on the better scan, PDF 374–376 - upo: "upa and u, two particles; by ād guṇaḥ the guṇa comes and upo results; so a further, new particle, made up of the combination of two. Ot — ओत् — (Pā. Sū. 1-1-15): a particle ending in o is called pragṛhya: so says the Vedabhāṣya; but this name has no use here: plutapragṛhyā aci nityam — प्लुतप्रगृह्या अचि नित्यम् — (Pā. Sū. 6-1-125) prescribes prakṛtibhāva when a vowel follows; here no vowel follows, so the establishing of the pragṛhya name has no fruit." - ayugdhvam: yujir yoge; the ir has the name of an indicatory letter; luṅ, cli; irito vā — इरितो वा — (3-1-57, printed without "Pā. Sū."): after a root with indicatory ir, optionally aṅ for cli; here the option is not taken; cleḥ sic (no number printed): sic; the augment aṭ: a-yuj + s + dhvam; jhalo jhali — झलो झलि — (Pā. Sū. 8-2-26) the loss of s after a jhal before a jhal; coḥ kuḥ — चोः कुः — (Pā. Sū. 8-2-30) k for c even before a jhal and at the end of a word, so j → g: ayugdhvam. - rohitaḥ: ruha bījajanmani prādurbhāve ca; ruheraś ca lo vā — रुहेरश्च लो वा — (U. Sū. 3-374, as printed; the bhāṣya gives U. 3-94): after this root the suffix itan, with l optional for r; guṇa of the light penultimate; as the l-substitution is optional it does not come here; the suffix is nit, so first-syllable acute. - yāmāya: root yamu uparame; halaś ca — हलश्च — (Pā. Sū. 3-3-121) ghañ in the abstract sense; upadhāvṛddhi: yām + a; karṣātvato ghañ anta udāttaḥ — कर्षात्वतो घञोऽन्त उदात्तः — (Pā. Sū. 6-1-159): a ghañ-ending word from kṛṣ or from a root with an ā-ending [etc.] is final-acute: this would give final-acute to yāma; but that is set aside by vṛṣādīnāṃ ca — वृषादीनां च — (Pā. Sū. 6-1-203) and it is first-syllable acute. - aśrot: root śru śravaṇe; laṅ, tip; itaś ca gives the loss of i; the augment aṭ; śruvaḥ śṛ ca — श्रुवः शृ च — (Pā. Sū. 3-1-74) gives the śnu vikaraṇa [with the substitute śṛ]; by bahulaṃ chandasi (Pā. Sū. 2-4-73) luk of it; the paribhāṣā sanniyogaśiṣṭānām anyatarāpāye ubhayor apy apāyaḥ — सन्नियोगशिष्टानामन्यतरापाये उभयोरप्यपायः — (Paribhāṣā 88): when of two substitutes laid down together one is lost, both are lost; here the śnu vikaraṇa and the śṛ substitute are laid down by the same sūtra; as the vikaraṇa is lost, so is the śṛ substitution; sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ gives guṇa; in place of aśṛṇot, aśrot has come. - abībhayanta: root ñibhī bhaye; hetumati ca (Pā. Sū. 3-1-26): ṇic after the root for the sense of an instigator's action such as sending; after it luṅ; bhīsmyor hetubhaye — भीस्म्योर्हेतुभये — (Pā. Sū. 1-3-68; p. 360): ātmanepada when fear (or wonder, smaya, by implication) is caused by the instigator; and ṇicaś ca — णिचश्च — (Pā. Sū. 1-3-74) gives ātmanepada when the fruit goes to the agent; here the first sūtra applies; jha → ant; bhī + i + anta; aco ñṇiti (no number at this mention) vṛddhi: bhai + i + anta; then the print goes on at length: by bibheter hetubhaye (Pā. Sū. 6-1-56) an optional ā for the root bhī where fear arises from the instigator — not taken here since optional; by bhīyo hetubhaye ṣuk — भीयो हेतुभये षुक् — (Pā. Sū. 7-3-40) the augment ṣuk after the ī-ending root bhī with ṇic — would be obtained before the vṛddhi, but by the paribhāṣā āgamaśāstram anityam (Paribhāṣā 96) it is not; cli → caṅ by ṇiśridrusrubhyaḥ kartari caṅ — णिश्रिद्रुस्रुभ्यः कर्तरि चङ् — (Pā. Sū. 3-1-48); the discussion of ṇicy ac ādeśo na syād dvitve kartavye — णिच्यच आदेशो न स्याद्द्वित्वे कर्तव्ये — ("before ṇic, a vowel-substitute should not take place when doubling is to be done"; made known from the jaś-pratyāhāra in oḥ puyaṇjy apare — ओः पुयण्ज्यपरे — Pā. Sū. 7-4-80), whether the ṇic-loss is to be taken as sthānivat and the differing view of Vopadeva and others (uvarṇādeśa eva sthānivat syān nānyaḥ [as read]), settled by the Mahābhāṣya's remark on acikīrtat, with caṅi — चङि — (Pā. Sū. 6-1-11) for the doubling; aco ñṇiti (Pā. Sū. 7-2-115) for vṛddhi ai; ṇeraniṭi — णेरनिटि — (Pā. Sū. 6-4-51) for the loss of ṇic; eco 'yavāyāvaḥ — एचोऽयवायावः — (Pā. Sū. 6-1-78) ai → āy; hrasvaḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-4-59) for the reduplicate, and ṇau caṅy upadhāyā hrasvaḥ — णौ चङ्युपधाया ह्रस्वः — (7-4-1); sanvallaghuni caṅ pare 'nagloppe — सन्वल्लघुनि चङ्परे ऽनग्लोपे — (Pā. Sū. 7-4-93) and dīrgho laghoḥ — दीर्घो लघोः — (Pā. Sū. 7-4-94) giving the long ī of the reduplicate: bibhay + a + anta; the augment aṭ; pararūpa: abībhayanta. आ वो॑ म॒क्षू तना॑य॒ कं रुद्रा॒ अवो॑ वृणीमहे । गन्ता॑ नू॒नं नोऽव॑सा यथा॑ पु॒रेत्था कण्वा॑य बि॒भ्युषे॑ ॥ ७ ॥

ā́ vo makṣū́ tánāya káṃ rudrā ávo vṛṇīmahe | gántā nūnáṃ nó 'vasā yáthā purétthā káṇvāya bibhyúṣe || 7 ||

Pada-pāṭha

आ । वः । मक्षु । तनाय । कम् । रुद्राः । अवः । वृणीमहे । गन्त । नूनम् । नः । अवसा । यथा । पुरा । इत्था । कण्वाय । बिभ्युषे ॥ ७ ॥

ā | vaḥ | makṣu | tanāya | kam | rudrāḥ | avaḥ | vṛṇīmahe | ganta | nūnam | naḥ | avasā | yathā | purā | itthā | kaṇvāya | bibhyuṣe || 7 || The Saṃhitā prints makṣū and gantā long, the Pada makṣu and ganta short.

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

हे रुद्रा रुद्रपुत्रा मरुतः तनाय कमस्मदीयपुत्रार्थं मक्षु शीघ्रं वो युष्मदीयमवो रक्षणमावृणीमहे । सर्वतः प्रार्थयामहे । मक्ष्विति क्षिप्रनाम । नु मक्षु इति तन्नामसु पठितत्वात् । पुरा पूर्वस्मिन्काले कर्मान्तरेषु नोऽवसास्मदीयरक्षणेन निमित्तेन यूयं यथा प्राप्तवन्तः । इत्था अनेन प्रकारेण बिभ्युषे भीतियुक्ताय कण्वाय मेधाविने यजमानाय तदनुग्रहार्थं नूनं क्षिप्रं गन्त । प्राप्नुत ॥ मक्षु । ऋचि तुनुघमक्षुतञ्कुत्रोरुष्याणामिति दीर्घः । तनाय । तनोतीति तनः । पचाद्यच् । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं । यद्वा तनयशब्देऽय् इत्यस्य लोपश्छान्दसः । कमित्येतत्पादान्ते प्रयुज्यमानं पादपूरणं । शिशिरं जीवनाय कमितिवत् । उक्तं च । अथापि पादपूरणाः कमीमिद्वितीति । रुद्राः । रोदयन्तीति रुद्राः । रोदेर्णिलुक् च । उ. २-२२ । इति रक्प्रत्ययः । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वं । पादादित्वान्निघाताभावः । गन्त । लोटि बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । तप्तनबित्यादिना तबादेशः । अतः पित्त्वादनुनासिकलोपाभावः । बिभ्युषे । बिभेतेर्लिटः क्वसुः । वस्वेकाजाद्घसामिति नियमादिडभावः । चतुर्थ्येकवचने वसोः सम्प्रसारणमिति सम्प्रसारणं । परपूर्वत्वं । शासिवसिघसीनां चेति षत्वं ॥

he rudrā rudraputrā marutaḥ tanāya kam asmadīyaputrārthaṃ makṣu śīghraṃ vo yuṣmadīyam avo rakṣaṇam āvṛṇīmahe | sarvataḥ prārthayāmahe | makṣv iti kṣipranāma | nu makṣu iti tannāmasu paṭhitatvāt | purā pūrvasmin kāle karmāntareṣu no 'vasāsmadīyarakṣaṇena nimittena yūyaṃ yathā prāptavantaḥ | itthā anena prakāreṇa bibhyuṣe bhītiyuktāya kaṇvāya medhāvine yajamānāya tadanugrahārthaṃ nūnaṃ kṣipraṃ ganta | prāpnuta || makṣu | ṛci tunughamakṣutañkutroruṣyāṇām iti dīrghaḥ | tanāya | tanotīti tanaḥ | pacādyac | vṛṣāditvād ādyudāttatvaṃ | yadvā tanayaśabde 'y ity asya lopaś chāndasaḥ | kam ity etad ante prayujyamānaṃ pādapūraṇaṃ | śiśiraṃ jīvanāya kam itivat | uktaṃ ca | athāpi pādapūraṇāḥ kamīm id v itīti | rudrāḥ | rodayantīti rudrāḥ | roder ṇiluk ca | u. 2-22 | iti rakpratyayaḥ | āmantritādyudāttatvaṃ | pādāditvān nighātābhāvaḥ | ganta | loṭi bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | taptanabityādinā tabādeśaḥ | ataḥ pittvād anunāsikalopābhāvaḥ | bibhyuṣe | bibheter liṭaḥ kvasuḥ | vasvekājāddhasām iti niyamād iḍabhāvaḥ | caturthyekavacane vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam iti saṃprasāraṇaṃ | parapūrvatvaṃ | śāsivasighasīnāṃ ceti ṣatvaṃ ||

Translation: "O rudrāḥ, sons of Rudra, Maruts — for tanāya, for a son, our own offspring — kam [a filler] — makṣu, quickly — vaḥ avaḥ, your help, your protection, ā vṛṇīmahe, we ask for on all sides. 'Makṣu' is a name for 'quick', since it is read in its names [nu makṣu and so on]. Purā, formerly, on other occasions naḥ avasā, by the cause which is our protection, you came as [you did]; itthā, in the same way, bibhyuṣe, to the frightened kaṇva, the wise sacrificer, nūnam, quickly, ganta, come: arrive, for his favour. Makṣu: the lengthening by ṛci tunugha-…. Tanāya: 'tanoti', that which extends, tana; ac of the pacādi class; first-syllable acute from belonging to the vṛṣādi group; or, in the word tanaya, the loss of ay is Vedic. Kam: used at the end, a mere filler of the verse-foot, as in śiśiraṃ jīvanāya kam; and it is said 'athāpi pādapūraṇaḥ kamīm id iti'. Rudrāḥ: 'rodayanti', they make [enemies] weep; by the Uṇādi rule roder ṇiluk ca (U. 2-22) the suffix rak and loss of ṇic; first-syllable acute as a vocative; at the beginning of a pāda there is no nighāta. Ganta: śap elided in the loṭ by bahulaṃ chandasi; the substitute tap (tab-ādeśaḥ); so because the suffix is pit the loss of the nasal does not occur. Bibhyuṣe: from bhī, the suffix kvasu of the liṭ; no iṭ by the restriction vasvekājāddhasām; in the dative singular, saṃprasāraṇa of the vasu by vaso saṃprasāraṇam; parapūrvatva; ṣatva by śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca." Rik 7's Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, English, Special Topics and grammar begin on p. 363, below.

Rik 39.7, continued from p. 363

Pratipadārtha — "rudrāḥ — O Maruts, sons of Rudra; tanāye kam — for our sons; makṣu — promptly; vaḥ — your; avaḥ — protection; ā vṛṇīmahe — we ask for; purā — formerly, at the times of sacrifice; naḥ — our; avasā — for protection; yathā — in the way in which; [you came]; itthā — in the very same way; bibhyuṣe — to [him who is] afraid (from devotion); kaṇvāya — to the wise sacrificer, or to the ṛṣi Kaṇva, to favour [him]; nūnam — quickly; ganta — come."

Bhāvārtha — "O Maruts, sons of Rudra, we pray to you for the protection of our sons. Accepting our prayer, in the way in which you came formerly at our sacrifices for our protection, in the very same way now also, to favour the wise sacrificer who worships you full of fear and devotion — or the ṛṣi Kaṇva who is now praising you — come quickly here."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 363) — "O Sons of Rudra, we entreat your protection quickly for the sake of our progeny ; come quickly to the timid Kanwa ( or to the sacrificer ) as you came formerly for our protection."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 363 - makṣu — "among the twenty-six names of 'quick' beginning with nu, makṣu [maṅkṣu] is read; so makṣu means swiftly, at once." - tanāye = tanoti iti tanaḥ putraḥ — "for a son: that is, for the protection of offspring such as sons." - rudrāḥ = rudraputrāḥ — "the Maruts who are the sons of Rudra. Here, in place of the word rudriyāsaḥ, which speaks of sons of Rudra, the word rudrāḥ itself is used." - bibhyuṣe = bhītiyuktāya — "to one who is afraid; one who is afraid from another cause, the ṛṣi Kaṇva: [the Maruts] must protect him: this is the sense."

Page 364 (better scan PDF 379)

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā p. 364 — grammar page, noted briefly - makṣū: ṛci tunughamakṣutaṅkutroruṣyāṇām (Pā. Sū. 6-3-133): the long vowel for the word makṣu. - tanāya: "tanoti iti tanaḥ": root tanu vistāre, with ac of the pacādi class [pacādibhyo 'c]; "since it spreads the family, the word tana means son"; dative singular. The print adds that in the word tanaya either the middle ay or the final ya is lost — a process for which there is no teaching of the śāstra; the loss occurs by Vedic usage; in this alternative the well-known sense is taken; the derivation of the form is forced; in the first alternative [tana] the word tana is not well known in the sense "son"; vṛṣādīnāṃ ca gives the first-syllable acute to tana. - kam: "a word to be used for filling out a pāda, at the end of a pāda; in śiśiraṃ jīvanāyu kam also kam is used for filling out the verse. In the Nirukta 'athāpi pādapūraṇāḥ kamīm id iti' (Niru. 1-9), kam, īm and it and the like are said to be for filling out a pāda." - rudrāḥ: root rudir aśruvimocane, "rodayantīti rudrāḥ": the suffix rak by roder ṇiluk ca — रोदेर्णिलुक्च — (U. Sū. 2-179, as printed here; the bhāṣya gives U. 2-22; cf. Ṛk 4); ṇic lost; "here by implication the Maruts, sons of Rudra, are meant". The print adds that in the Śruti "so 'rodīd yad arodīt tad rudrasya rudratvam" — सोऽरोदीद्यदरोदीत्तद्रुद्रस्य रुद्रत्वम् — the word arodīt must be understood with the sense of the ṇic included, "he made to weep"; therefore some say that the derivation given has no conflict with the Śruti. - ganta: root gamḷ gatau; loṭ, madhyama plural tha, substitute ta; bahulaṃ chandasi elides śap; tapta-nap-tana-thanāś ca gives tap; this is pit, so sārvadhātukam apit makes no ṅit; therefore [by] anudāttopadeśa-vanati-tanotyādīnām anunāsikalopo jhali kṅiti (Pā. Sū. 6-4-37) the loss of the nasal m does not occur. - bibhyuṣe: root ñibhī bhaye; liṭ, kvasu by kvasuś ca; the doubling, the shortening and jaś; by the restriction vasvekājāddhasām — वस्वेकाजाद्घसाम् — iṭ does not come to vas (this restriction has been explained earlier); dative singular ṅe; by vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam the v of vas becomes u; by saṃprasāraṇāc ca the prior form; ādeśapratyayayoḥ: s → ṣ; the print says that śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca does not apply here, as has been shown earlier many times (anekāvarti) with reasons. Rik 7 ends here (|| 7 ||).

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

हे मरुतो यो यः कश्चिदभ्वः शत्रुर्युष्मेषितो युष्माभिः प्रेषितो मर्त्येषितो मारकैरन्यैर्वा प्रेषितः सन् नोऽस्मान्प्रति आ ईषते अभिमुख्येन प्राप्नोति । तं शत्रुं शवसान्नेन वि युयोत । विभक्तं कुरुत । तथौजसा बलेन वि युयोत । युष्माकाभिरूतिभिर्युष्मत्सम्बन्धिभी रक्षणैश्च वि युयोत ॥ युष्मेषितः । युष्माभिरिषितः । सुब्लुकि प्रत्ययलक्षणेन युष्मदस्मदोरनादेश इत्यात्वं । न च न लुमताङ्गस्येति प्रतिषेधः । इकोऽचि विभक्तौ । पा. ७-१-७३ । इत्यत्राज्ग्रहणेन तस्य पाक्षिकत्वोक्तेः । तृतीया कर्मणीति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । मर्त्येषितः । पूर्ववत् । अभ्वः । आभवतीत्यभ्वः । पृषोदरादित्वादभिमतरूपस्वरसिद्धिः । ईषते । ईष गतिहिंसादर्शनेषु । अदुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः । युयोत । यु मिश्रणामिश्रणयोः । लोण्मध्यमबहुवचने बहुलं छन्दसीति शपः श्लुः । तप्तनप्तनथनाश्चेति तबादेशः । पित्त्वाद्गुणः । युष्माकाभिः । युष्मत्सम्बन्धिनीभिः । तस्मिन्नणि च युष्माकास्माकौ । पा. ४-३-२ । इति युष्मच्छब्दस्य युष्माकादेशः । ङीब्वृद्धी छान्दसत्वान्न क्रियेते । ऊतिभिः । अवतेः क्तिनि ज्वरत्वरेत्यादिना ऊठ् । ऊतियूतीत्यादिना क्तिन उदात्तत्वं ॥

he maruto yo yaḥ kaścid abhvaḥ śatrur yuṣmeṣito yuṣmābhiḥ preṣito martyeṣito mārakair anyair vā preṣitaḥ san no 'smān prati ā īṣate abhimukhyena prāpnoti | taṃ śatruṃ śavasānnena vi yuyota | vibhaktaṃ kuruta | tathaujasā balena vi yuyota | yuṣmākābhir ūtibhir yuṣmatsambandhibhī rakṣaṇaiś ca vi yuyota || yuṣmeṣitaḥ | yuṣmābhir iṣitaḥ | sublluki pratyayalakṣaṇena yuṣmadasmador anādeśa ity ātvaṃ | na ca na lumatāṅgasyeti pratiṣedhaḥ | iko 'ci vibhaktau | pā. 7-1-73 | ity atrāgrahaṇena tasya pākṣikatvoktes | tṛtīyā karmaṇīti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | martyeṣitaḥ | pūrvavat | abhvaḥ | ābhavatīty abhvaḥ | pṛṣodarāditvād abhimatarūpasvarasiddhiḥ | īṣate | īṣa gatihiṃsādarśaneṣu | anupadeśāl lasārvadhātukānudāttatve dhātusvaraḥ | yuyota | yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ | loṇmadhyamabahuvacane bahulaṃ chandasīti śapaḥ śluḥ | tapta-nap-tana-thanāś ceti tabādeśaḥ | pittvād guṇaḥ | yuṣmākābhiḥ | yuṣmatsambandhinībhiḥ | tasminn aṇi ca yuṣmākāsmākau | pā. 4-3-2 | iti yuṣmacchabdasya yuṣmākādeśaḥ | jeb-bṛddhiś chāndasatvān na kriyete [?] | ūtibhiḥ | avateḥ ktini jvaratvarasrivy ety ādinā ūṭh | ūtiyūtī ty ādinā ktina udāttatvaṃ ||

Translation: "O Maruts, whoever it may be, abhvaḥ, an enemy, yuṣmeṣitaḥ, sent by you, or martyeṣitaḥ, sent by deadly others [men], who, being so sent, naḥ, towards us, ā īṣate, comes forward: taṃ, that enemy, śavasā, with food [the strength that is food], vi yuyota, separate, make parted [from it]; likewise ojasā, with strength, vi yuyota; yuṣmākābhiḥ ūtibhiḥ, with your protections, those that belong to you, vi yuyota. Yuṣmeṣitaḥ: 'yuṣmābhir iṣitaḥ'; when the case-ending is elided, the ā for the d of yuṣmad, asmad by pratyayalakṣaṇa … (the clause read in full: subluki pratyayalakṣaṇena yuṣmadasmador anādeśa ity ātvam); the prohibition na lumatāṅgasya does not apply, as is said to be optional from the word aci in iko 'ci vibhaktau [Pā. 7-1-73]; the accent of the first member by tṛtīyā karmaṇi. Martyeṣitaḥ: as before. Abhvaḥ: 'ābhavati', one who overpowers; by belonging to the pṛṣodarādi group the desired form and accent are established. Īṣate: root īṣa gatihiṃsādarśaneṣu; the root accent. Yuyota: root yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ; ślu for śap; tap for the ending; guṇa because tap is pit. Yuṣmākābhiḥ: 'belonging to you': the substitute yuṣmāka by tasminn aṇi ca yuṣmākāsmākau [Pā. 4-3-2]; ṅīp and vṛddhi are not made, being Vedic (ṅībvṛddhī chāndasatvān na kriyete). Ūtibhiḥ: root ava, ktin, ūṭh by jvaratvara… (so abbreviated in the bhāṣya); the suffix accent by ūtiyūti…."

Page 366 (better scan PDF 381)

Pratipadārtha — "marutaḥ — O Maruts; yaḥ — whichever; abhvaḥ — enemy; yuṣmeṣitaḥ — sent by you (whether); martyeṣitaḥ — (or) sent by some other enemy in human form; naḥ — towards us (against us); ā īṣate — rises up and goes against [us]; tam — that enemy; śavasā — [separate him] from food; vi yuyota — make [him] devoid [of it] (that is, do not give him food); ojasā — from strength; vi (yuyota) — separate [him] (do not give him strength); yuṣmākābhir ūtibhiḥ — from the protection that comes from you; vi yuyota — separate and part [him] (do not protect [him])."

Bhāvārtha — "O Maruts, whether the enemy who does us harm has got your help or the help of another enemy in human form, when he comes to harm us, deprive such an enemy utterly of food, of strength and of your protection."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 366) — "O Maruts, if any adversary instigated by you or by man attacks us deprive him of food, strength and your assistance."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), pp. 366–367 - Main intention — "O Marut-deities, whatever man opposes us with enmity, whether by your hot anger or by the instigation of others: to such a man do not give food or strength; do not give him any help whatever." - yuṣmeṣitaḥ = yuṣmābhiḥ preṣitaḥ — "sent by you, or incited by you; having your strength." - martyeṣitaḥ = mārakair anyair vā preṣitaḥ — "our enemy, sent by some man who wishes to kill us: this is the sense." - abhvaḥ — "since the word abhvaḥ is read among the twenty-five names of mahat beginning with mahat, bradhnaḥ (Ni. 3-13), abhvaḥ means a man of great strength; here the intention that he is an enemy is suggested." - vi taṃ yuyota śavasā — "make him devoid of food: that is, do not give him food and the like." - yuṣmākābhiḥ = yuṣmatsambandhibhiḥ — "belonging to you; or given by you."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 367–369 — large grammar pages, characterized in outline; very crowded - yuṣmeṣitaḥ: iṣa gatau, divādi; iṣa icchāyām, tudādi; iṣa ābhīkṣṇye, kryādi: there are three roots iṣa; some read the tudādi root as iṣu icchāyām, with u as an indicatory letter; since this has no purpose, "iṣa" is enough; tīṣasahaluṣarucariṣaḥ — तीषसहलुभरुषरिषः — (Pā. Sū. 7-2-48) need not read iṣu; the print notes the vārttika that, for the root iṣ with a śyan-suffix, the prohibition of optional iṭ before a suffix beginning with t has to be stated, so that here iṭ always comes; the root iṣa gatau is the one taken here; with kta: iṣita; the compound "yuṣmābhir iṣitaḥ"; supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ — सुपो धातुप्रातिपदिकयोः — (Pā. Sū. 2-4-71) the loss (luk) of the case-endings: yuṣmad + iṣita; pratyayalope pratyayalakṣaṇam — प्रत्ययलोपे प्रत्ययलक्षणम् — (Pā. Sū. 1-1-62): when a suffix has been lost, the operations that depend on it occur as if it were still present; but na lumatāṅgasya — न लुमताङ्गस्य — (Pā. Sū. 1-1-63) prohibits this where the loss is named lu (luk, ślu, lup); the prohibition is anitya and so does not apply here; the print then gives a long argument on the sūtra iko 'ci vibhaktau — इकोऽचि विभक्तौ — (Pā. Sū. 7-1-73) (the augment num in a neuter ik-ending base before a vowel-initial case-ending, e.g. vāriṇī) and on the use of the word aci in it, the prohibition nalumatā…, and the svādiṣv asarvanāmasthāne (Pā. Sū. 1-4-17) and nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya (Pā. Sū. 8-2-7; also naṅi sambuddhyoḥ, Pā. Sū. 8-2-8, and svamor napuṃsakāt, Pā. Sū. 7-1-23) rules, concluding that the word aci is meaningful. Then yuṣmadasmador anādeśe — युष्मदस्मदोरनादेशे — (Pā. Sū. 7-2-86; p. 368, whose page number is misprinted "268"): before a case-ending which is not beginning with a vowel [print: ajādiyallada], the d of yuṣmad, asmad becomes ā: yuṣmā + iṣita; guṇa: yuṣmeṣita; tṛtīyā karmaṇi — तृतीया कर्मणि — (Pā. Sū. 6-2-48) gives the accent of the first member. - martyeṣitaḥ: the process of iṣitaḥ as before; the first-member accent also as before. - abhvaḥ: "ābhavati, so abhvaḥ": enemy; the print says one must derive the form by reading this word in the pṛṣodarādi group. - īṣate: root īṣa gatihiṃsādarśaneṣu, first class, ātmanepada; laṭ, ta, e; śap: īṣ + a + te; no guṇa as the penultimate is not light; śap is pit and so unaccented; the root accent remains. - yuyota: root yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ, adādi; loṭ, madhyama plural tha → ta by tasthasthamipāṃ; tapta-nap-tana-thanāś ca gives tap; bahulaṃ chandasi (Pā. Sū. 2-4-76) śap → ślu; ślau — doubling: yu + yu + ta; tap is pit, so the prohibition of guṇa does not come; sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ gives guṇa: yuyota. - yuṣmākābhiḥ: "yuṣmākam imāḥ"; yuṣmadasmador anyatarasyāṃ khañ ca — युष्मदस्मदोरन्यतरस्यां खञ् च — (Pā. Sū. 4-3-1): after yuṣmad and asmad, in senses other than those through the fourth case, khañ [kha] and aṇ optionally; since anyatarasyām is read, these suffixes are optional, and in the alternative where they do not come, the suffix aṇ comes by tasyedam (Pā. Sū. 4-3-120); the print uses pāre madhye ṣaṣṭhyā vā — पारे मध्ये षष्ठ्या वा — (Pā. Sū. 2-1-18) and the principle "yatrotsargāpavādau mahāvibhāṣayā vikalpyete tatrāpavādena mukte punar utsargo na pravartate" ["where the general rule and the exception are both made optional by the great option, when the exception is released the general rule does not operate again"] to show that, since here anyatarasyām is used, the option is not the mahāvibhāṣā; therefore aṇ comes by the general rule; tasminn aṇi ca yuṣmākāsmākau — तस्मिन्नणि च युष्माकास्माकौ — (Pā. Sū. 4-3-2; p. 369): when khañ or aṇ follows, the substitutes yuṣmāka and asmāka for yuṣmad and asmad: yuṣmāka + a; yasyeti ca the loss of the a; because the feminine is intended, ṭiḍḍhāṇañ-… (no number printed) would give ṅīp, and taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ vṛddhi; but, as all operations are optional in the Veda (sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante, Paribhāṣā 35), they do not come here; ajādyatas ṭāp — ṭāp; bhis, ru, visarga: yuṣmākābhiḥ. - ūtibhiḥ: root ava rakṣaṇe; striyāṃ ktin: ktin; jvaratvarasrivyaviruvamavām upadhāyāś ca — ज्वरत्वरस्रिव्यविरुवमवामुपधायाश्च — (no number printed): ūṭh for av; ūtiyūtijūti… — ऊतियूतिजूति… — (no number printed) the accent of ktin: acute on the first syllable. Rik 8 ends here (|| 8 ||).

असामि हि सम्पूर्णमेव यथा भवति तथा प्रयज्यवः प्रकर्षेण यष्टव्याः प्रचेतसः प्रकृष्टज्ञानयुक्ताः हे मरुतः कण्वं मेधाविनं यजमानमेतन्नामकमृषिं वा दद । धारयेत । हि यस्माद्यूयं कण्वनामकमृषिं धारितवन्तस्तस्मात्कारणादसामिभिरूतिभिः सम्पूर्णै रक्षणैर्नोऽस्मान्प्रत्या गन्त । आगच्छत । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । वृष्टिं न विद्युतः । यथा विद्युतो वृष्टिं गच्छन्ति तद्वत् ॥ असामि । साम्यर्थं । न सामि असामि । अव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । प्रयज्यवः । प्रकर्षेण यष्टव्याः । यजिमनिशुन्धिदसिजनिभ्यो युः । उ. ३-२० । इति कर्मणि युप्रत्ययः । आमन्त्रितनिघातः । दद । डुदाञ् दाने । लोण्मध्यमबहुवचनस्य तिङां तिङो भवन्तीति लक्षणादात्मनेपदप्रथमपुरुषबहुवचनादेशः । श्लौ द्विर्भावे सति श्नाभ्यस्तयोरात इत्याकारलोपः । लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेषु । पा. ७-१-४१ । इति तलोपः । अतो गुण इति पररूपत्वं । छन्दस्युभयथेत्यार्धधातुकत्वाद्भ्यस्तानामादिरित्याद्युदात्तत्वं न भवति किंतु प्रत्ययस्वर एव । हि चेति निघातप्रतिषेधः । प्रचेतसः । प्रकृष्टं चेतो येषां । आमन्त्रितनिघातः । गन्त । गमेर्लोण्मध्यमबहुवचनस्य तस्य तबादेशः । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । प्रत्ययस्य पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः । पादादित्वान्निघाताभावः । द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङ इति संहितायां दीर्घत्वं । विद्युतः । विद्योतत इति विद्युत् । भ्राजभासेत्यादिना । पा. ३-२-१७७ । क्विप् ॥

asāmi hi sampūrṇam eva yathā bhavati tathā prayajyavaḥ prakarṣeṇa yaṣṭavyāḥ pracetasaḥ prakṛṣṭajñānayuktāḥ he marutaḥ kaṇvaṃ medhāvinaṃ yajamānam etannāmakam ṛṣiṃ vā dada | dhārayeta | hi yasmād yūyaṃ kaṇvanāmakam ṛṣiṃ dhāritavantas tasmāt kāraṇād asāmibhir ūtibhiḥ sampūrṇai rakṣaṇair no 'smān pratyā ganta | āgacchata | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | vṛṣṭiṃ na vidyutaḥ | yathā vidyuto vṛṣṭiṃ gacchanti tadvat || asāmi | sāmyarthaṃ | na sāmi asāmi | avyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | prayajyavaḥ | prakarṣeṇa yaṣṭavyāḥ | yajimaniśundhidasijanibhyo yuḥ | u. 3-20 | iti karmaṇi yupratyayaḥ | āmantritanighātaḥ | dada | ḍudāñ dāne | loṇmadhyamabahuvacanasya tiṅāṃ tiṅo bhavantīti lakṣaṇād ātmanepadaprathamapuruṣabahuvacanādeśaḥ | ślau dvirbhāve sati śnābhyastayor āta ity ākāralopaḥ | lopas ta ātmanepadeṣu | pā. 7-1-41 | iti talopaḥ | ato guṇa iti pararūpatvaṃ | chandasy ubhayathety ārdhadhātukatvād bhyastānām ādir ity ādyudāttatvaṃ na bhavati kiṃtu pratyayasvara eva | hi ceti nighātapratiṣedhaḥ | pracetasaḥ | prakṛṣṭaṃ ceto yeṣāṃ | āmantritanighātaḥ | ganta | gamer loṇmadhyamabahuvacanasya tasya tabādeśaḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | pratyayasya pittvād anudāttatve dhātusvaraḥ | pādāditvān nighātābhāvaḥ | dvyaco 'tastiṅa iti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghatvaṃ | vidyutaḥ | vidyotata iti vidyut | bhrājabhāsety ādinā | pā. 3-2-177 | kvip ||

Translation: "Asāmi hi — in full, as it were — prayajyavaḥ, those to be worshipped greatly, pracetasaḥ, endowed with excellent knowledge, O Maruts: kaṇvam, the wise sacrificer, or the ṛṣi so named, dada — support. Hi — because you have supported the ṛṣi named Kaṇva, therefore asāmibhiḥ ūtibhiḥ, with complete protections, naḥ, towards us, ā ganta, come. The example: vṛṣṭiṃ na vidyutaḥ — as the lightnings go to the rain, so. Asāmi: sāmy-artham [as printed: "in the sense of sāmi", i.e. 'half', as the Special Topics and grammar explain]; na sāmi: asāmi; the accent of the first member as an indeclinable. Prayajyavaḥ: 'to be worshipped greatly'; the suffix yu in the passive sense by yaji-mani-śundhi-dasi-janibhyo yuḥ (U. 3-20); unaccented as a vocative. Dada: root ḍudāñ dāne; the substitution of the ātmanepada third-person plural for the second-person plural of the loṭ by the principle tiṅāṃ tiṅo bhavanti; in ślu, after doubling, the loss of the ā by śnābhyastayor ātaḥ; the loss of ta by lopas ta ātmanepadeṣu (Pā. 7-1-41); pararūpa by ato guṇe; because by chandasy ubhayathā it is ārdhadhātuka, the first-syllable acute of the reduplicated [abhyastānām ādiḥ] does not come, but only the accent of the suffix; no nighāta by hi ca. Pracetasaḥ: 'of whom the mind is excellent'; unaccented vocative. Ganta: the substitute ta for the tha of loṭ of gam; śap elided by bahulaṃ chandasi; because the suffix is pit it is unaccented, the root accent remains; at the beginning of a pāda there is no nighāta; in the Saṃhitā the long vowel by dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ. Vidyutaḥ: 'vidyotate', so vidyut; kvip by bhrājabhāsa… (Pā. 3-2-177)."

Pratipadārtha — "asāmi hi — completely; prayajyavaḥ — worthy of the best worship; pracetasaḥ — endowed with excellent knowledge; marutaḥ — O Maruts; kaṇvam — the wise sacrificer (or the ṛṣi Kaṇva); dada — (giving shelter) support; hi — because you have given shelter; asāmibhiḥ — complete; ūtibhiḥ — with the means of protecting [us]; vidyutaḥ — the lightnings; vṛṣṭiṃ na — as [they] join the rain (come to us as they do); naḥ — to us; ā ganta — come."

Bhāvārtha — "O Maruts, who are worshipped with full and excellent sacrificial rites, you are possessed of excellent knowledge. Give support to the sacrificer Kaṇva, the ṛṣi. Then, as lightning follows the rain, come to us with your protections." The English translation, the Special Topics and the grammar of Rik 9 begin on p. 371, below.

English Translation (the source's own, p. 371) — "Wise Maruts, who are to be unreservedly worshipped, support Kanwa ( the sacrificer ); come to us, Maruts, with complete protection as the lightnings bring the rain."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 371 - asāmi — "sāmi means 'half'. Asāmi means 'not half', 'complete'." - prayajyavaḥ = prakarṣeṇa yaṣṭavyāḥ — "those fit to be worshipped well." - dada = dhārayeta — "give support, give shelter, and protect." - pracetasaḥ = prakṛṣṭaṃ ceto yeṣāṃ te | prakṛṣṭajñānayuktāḥ — "those who have excellent knowledge." - vṛṣṭiṃ na vidyutaḥ — "there is no lightning without rain; and when lightning is seen, rain is well known to come; therefore the ṛṣi has used this example: 'As the lightnings bring the rain, you, Maruts, bring us protections.'"

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 371–372 — grammar pages, noted briefly - asāmi: "sāmi is a word whose sense is 'half'; na sāmi: a nañ-compound, with the loss of the n; tatpuruṣe tulyārtha— (abbreviated, no number printed): the first member, an indeclinable, keeps its accent." - prayajyavaḥ: yaja devapūjādau; yaji-mani-śundhi-dasi-janibhyo yuc — यजिमनिशुन्धिदसिजनिभ्यो युच् — (U. Sū. 3-300, as printed here; the bhāṣya gives U. 3-20): after these roots the suffix yuc; since the u of yu is an indicatory ut letter, the substitute ana [for yu, by yuvor anākau] is not applied; jas after prayajya; jasi ca — जसि च — (Pā. Sū. 7-3-109) guṇa, av-substitution; āmantritasya ca — the verb is wholly unaccented. - dada: root ḍudāñ dāne; loṭ, madhyama plural dhvam; tiṅāṃ tiṅo bhavanti — तिङां तिङो भवन्ति — (printed "Pā. Ma. 7-1-39"): in place of one tiṅ a different tiṅ [intended] comes in the Veda; hence for the plural dhvam of the ātmanepada the jha [= third-person plural ātmanepada] substitute: dhā + jha; juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ (no number printed) śap → ślu; doubling and shortening of the reduplicate; ātmanepadeṣv nataḥ — आत्मनेपदेष्वनतः — (Pā. Sū. 7-1-5): at for the jha of the ātmanepada after a non-short-a; jha → at; śnābhyastayor ātaḥ — श्नाभ्यस्तयोरातः — (Pā. Sū. 6-4-112) the loss of the ā of a śnā and of a reduplicated root before a kit/ṅit sārvadhātuka: dad + ata; lopas ta ātmanepadeṣu — लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेषु — (Pā. Sū. 7-1-41) the loss of the t of an ātmanepada ending in the Veda: dad + a + a; ato guṇe — अतो गुणे — (Pā. Sū. 6-1-97; p. 372) pararūpa: dada. Chandasy ubhayathā (Pā. Sū. 3-4-117): in the Veda the suffixes laid down in the dhātvadhikāra are both sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka; because of its ārdhadhātuka name, the first-syllable acute of abhyastānām ādiḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-189) before a non-it sārvadhātuka beginning with a vowel, does not come; hi ca — हि च — (Pā. Sū. 8-1-34) prohibits wholly-unaccented; the accent of the suffix. - pracetasaḥ: "prakṛṣṭaṃ cetaḥ yeṣāṃ te": those with excellent understanding; āmantritasya ca: unaccented-in-verse. - ganta: root gamḷ gatau; loṭ, madhyama tha; because of the la-substitute, by tasthasthamipāṃ… ta; tapta-nap-tana-thanāś ca gives tap; bahulaṃ chandasi (Pā. Sū. 2-4-73) luk for śap; tap is pit, so it does not become ṅit; anudāttopadeśa… the nasal is not lost; the suffix is pit and unaccented; the root accent remains; it is at the beginning of the fourth pāda, hence apādādau (no number printed) does not give wholly-unaccented; dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-3-135) gives the long vowel in the Saṃhitā. - vidyutaḥ: "vidyotate, so vidyut": "shines well"; bhrāja-bhāsa-dhurvi-dyuta-ūrji-pṛ-ju-grāvastuvaḥ kvip — भ्राजभासधुर्विद्युतोर्जिपॄजुग्रावस्तुवः क्विप् — (Pā. Sū. 3-2-177): kvip after each of these eight, in the sense of habitual disposition and so on; so kvip after dyut with the prefix vi. Rik 9 ends here (|| 9 ||).

हे सुदानवः शोभनदानोपेता मरुतः असामि सम्पूर्णमोजो बलं बिभृथ । धारयथ । हे धूतयः कम्पनकारिणो मरुतः असामि सम्पूर्णं शवो बलं । परिमन्यवे कोपपरिवृताय ऋषिद्विषे ऋषीणां द्वेषं कुर्वते शत्रवे तद्विनाशार्थं द्विषं द्वेषकारिणं हन्तारं सृजत । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । इषुं न । यथा शत्रोरुपरि बाणं मुञ्चन्ति तद्वत् । अत्र निरुक्तं । असामि सामिप्रतिषिद्धं सामि स्यतेः । असाम्योजो बिभृथा सुदानवः । असुसमाप्तं बलं बिभृथ । कल्याणदानाः । नि. ६-२३ । इति ॥ बिभृथ । डुभृञ् धारणपोषणयोः । जुहोत्यादित्वात् श्लुः । भृञामित्यभ्यासस्येत्वं । ऋषिद्विषे । ऋषीन् द्वेष्टीति ऋषिद्विट् । सत्सूद्विषेत्यादिना क्विप् । परिमन्यवे । मन्युना परिवृतः परिमन्युः । प्रादिसमासे परेरभितोभावि मण्डलं । पा. ६-२-१८७ । इत्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वं । इषुं । इषु गतौ । इष्यति गच्छतीतीषुः । इषेः किच्च । उ. १-१३ । इत्युप्रत्ययः । धान्ये निदित्यनुवृत्तेर्नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं । सृजत । सृज विसर्गे । विकरणस्य ञित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । द्विषं । क्विप्चेति क्विप् ॥

he sudānavaḥ śobhanadānopetā marutaḥ asāmi sampūrṇam ojo balaṃ bibhṛtha | dhārayatha | he dhūtayaḥ kampanakāriṇo marutaḥ asāmi sampūrṇaṃ śavo balaṃ | parimanyave kopaparivṛtāya ṛṣidviṣe ṛṣīṇāṃ dveṣaṃ kurvate śatrave tadvināśārthaṃ dviṣaṃ dveṣakāriṇaṃ hantāraṃ sṛjata | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | iṣuṃ na | yathā śatror upari bāṇaṃ muñcanti tadvat | atra niruktaṃ | asāmi sāmipratiṣiddhaṃ sāmi syateḥ | asāmy ojo bibhṛthā sudānavaḥ | asusamāptaṃ balaṃ bibhṛtha | kalyāṇadānāḥ | ni. 6-23 | iti || bibhṛtha | ḍubhṛñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ | juhotyāditvāt śluḥ | bhṛñām ity abhyāsasyetvaṃ | ṛṣidviṣe | ṛṣīn dveṣṭīti ṛṣidviṭ | satsūdviṣety ādinā kvip | parimanyave | manyunā parivṛtaḥ parimanyuḥ | prādisamāse pareḥ abhito bhāvi maṇḍalaṃ | pā. 6-2-187 | ity uttarapadāntodāttatvaṃ | iṣuṃ | iṣu gatau | iṣyati gacchatīti iṣuḥ | iṣeḥ kic ca | u. 1-13 | ity upratyayaḥ | dhānye nid ity anuvṛtter nittvād ādyudāttatvaṃ | sṛjata | sṛja visarge | vikaraṇasya ñittvād guṇābhāvaḥ | dviṣaṃ | kvip ceti kvip ||

Translation: "O sudānavaḥ, Maruts endowed with fine giving, asāmi, complete, ojaḥ, strength, bibhṛtha, you bear. O dhūtayaḥ, shakers, Maruts, asāmi, complete, śavaḥ, strength. Parimanyave, to [him who is] surrounded by anger, ṛṣidviṣe, to the enemy who makes hatred against the ṛṣis, for his destruction, dviṣam, the hate-causing, slaying one [your weapon], sṛjata, discharge. The example: iṣuṃ na — as they discharge an arrow upon an enemy, so. Here the Nirukta: 'asāmi: opposed to sāmi; sāmi is from [the root] syati [so, 'to end']. Asāmy ojo bibhṛthā sudānavaḥ: you bear strength that is not left unfinished; you are of auspicious gifts' (Ni. 6-23). Bibhṛtha: root ḍubhṛñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; ślu since of the juhotyādi class; the i in the reduplicate by bhṛñām it. Ṛṣidviṣe: 'ṛṣīn dveṣṭi', one who hates the ṛṣis: ṛṣidviṭ; kvip by satsūdviṣa…. Parimanyave: 'surrounded by anger': parimanyuḥ; in a prādi compound, by the rule pareḥ abhito bhāvi maṇḍalam (Pā. 6-2-187 [as printed; for 6-2-182]) the final syllable of the latter member is acute. Iṣum: root iṣu gatau; 'iṣyati, it goes': iṣuḥ; the suffix u by iṣeḥ kic ca (U. 1-13]]; since nit is carried forward from dhānye nit, it is first-syllable acute. Sṛjata: root sṛja visarge; the vikaraṇa being ñit, no guṇa. Dviṣam: kvip by kvip ca."

Pratipadārtha — "sudānavaḥ — O Maruts, endowed with auspicious (and abundant) gifts; marutaḥ — O Maruts; asāmi — fully; ojaḥ — [your] strength; bibhṛtha — you bear; dhūtayaḥ — O Maruts, who make [things] tremble; asāmi — fully; śavaḥ — [your] power; parimanyave — full of anger; ṛṣidviṣe — [against] the enemy who hates the ṛṣis (for his destruction); iṣuṃ na — as one shoots a sharp arrow; dviṣam — your destructive hatred (anger); sṛjata — discharge upon the enemy."

Page 374 (better scan PDF 389)

Bhāvārtha — "O Maruts, you are good givers; your strength is surpassing. As a sharpened arrow is used to destroy an enemy, use your anger in the form of hatred against the enemy who harms and hates the ṛṣis."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 374) — "O most liberal givers, you possess perfect vigor ; shakers of the ( earth ), you possess undiminished strength. O Maruts, let loose your anger, like an arrow, upon the wrathfull [sic] enemy of the Rishis." Printed "Rishis".

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 374 - asāmy ojaḥ — "perfect strength" (the source adds in English: "perfect strength"). - sudānavaḥ — "givers of plenty: those who give many desired things." (English as printed: "givers of plenty".) - dhūtayaḥ — "those who make trees and the like shake." - ṛṣidviṣe parimanyave — "enemies who, full of anger, hate or injure the ṛṣis." - iṣuṃ na sṛjata dviṣam — "the prayer is: as an arrow is discharged against an enemy, direct your hatred or anger against those who hate the ṛṣis."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 374–375 — grammar pages, noted briefly - bibhṛtha: root ḍubhṛñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ, laṭ; being ñit, it is ubhayapadī; parasmaipada, madhyama plural tha; juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ — जुहोत्यादिभ्यः श्लुः — (Pā. Sū. 2-4-75) śap → ślu; ślau: doubling: bhṛ + bhṛ + tha; ur at — उरत् — (Pā. Sū. 7-4-66): when a suffix follows, an ṛ in the reduplicate becomes a, and that a is followed by r (raparatva); halādiḥ śeṣaḥ — the loss of the r, and jaś: bha; bhṛñām it — भृञामित् — (Pā. Sū. 7-4-76): the reduplicate of bhṛñ, māṅ, ohāṅ takes i: bibhṛtha. - ṛṣidviṣe: "ṛṣīn dveṣṭi, so ṛṣidviṭ": satsūdviṣa-druha-duha-yuja-vida-bhida-chida-jida-nīrājām upasargepi kvip — सत्सूद्विषद्रुहदुहयुजविदभिदच्छिदजिन्नीराजामुपसर्गेऽपि क्विप् — (printed abbreviated, "satsūdviṣa", no number): kvip. - parimanyave: "manyunā parivṛtaḥ": by kugatiprādayaḥ — कुगतिप्रादयः — (Pā. Sū. 2-2-18; p. 375) a compound; although the vārttikakāra says that paryādayo glānādyarthe caturthyā — "pari and the like [compound] with a fourth-case ending word in senses such as glāna" — yet in senses such as parivṛta belonging to that group a compound with another case-ending word also arises; or it may be called a bahuvrīhi, "paritaḥ manyuḥ yasya saḥ"; pareḥ abhito bhāvi maṇḍalam — परेरभितोभावि मण्डलम् — (Pā. Sū. 6-2-187 [as printed; for 6-2-182]): after the prefix pari, a word meaning "on both sides" or "on all sides" (abhitobhāvi), and the word maṇḍala, are final-acute; hence the word manyu is final-acute. The print's examples of abhitobhāvi — the print cites supy ajātau — सुप्यजातौ — for the ṇini-ending word abhitobhāvin, and explains that by this word is meant either the bank (kūla) on both sides in nava and the like, or anger and the like pervading a man all round. - iṣum: iṣa gatau, divādi; no need for the u-mark (iṣu), as shown at the 8th mantra of this sūkta [printed ೮; cf. the grammar of Ṛk 8]; "iṣyati, he goes", i.e. an arrow that goes far, instantly after being shot. Iṣeḥ kic ca — इषेः किच्च — (U. Sū. 1-13); "nit" is carried forward from dhānye nit — धान्ये नित् — (U. Sū. 1-9); the suffix u after iṣ, which is kit and nit; the suffix being kit, no guṇa of the light penultimate; being nit, the word is first-syllable acute. The print adds that the commentators (vyākhyākāra) quote a reading from the Uṇādi sūtras following unde ricchādeḥ — उन्दे रिच्चादेः — the reading īṣeḥ kic ca (U. Sū. 1-13): īṣagatihiṃsādarśaneṣu — "the root īṣ in the senses of going, injuring, seeing; the suffix uk, which is kit and nit; and the initial ī of the root becomes i"; the root īṣa in the first class has these three senses; īṣate: goes, or injures, or "is not seen"; "it goes swiftly, kills enemies; by the excess of its speed it is not seen"; whichever of the three senses is intended, the word iṣu is formed. - sṛjata: sṛja visarge, tudādi; loṭ, madhyama plural tha, ta; tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ — तुदादिभ्यः शः — (no number printed) the śa vikaraṇa, which is ñit [the print says śit-effect, i.e. ñit-like], so no guṇa of the preceding vowel. - dviṣam: dviṣa apritau, adādi; kvip ca — क्विप् च — (no number printed) kvip. Rik 10 ends here (|| 10 ||).

Close of Sūkta 39. Printed on p. 375 after the grammar: "illige 39ne sūkta mugiyitu" — "Here the 39th sūkta has ended." The numeral, printed ೩೯, zoom-checked on the better scan, PDF 390. A flourish follows. The next leaf, p. 376 = PDF 390, begins with the large title "nalavattaneya sūktavu" ("the fortieth sūkta") — the Sanskrit introduction and Kannada anuvāda of Sūkta 40 (uttiṣṭha brahmaṇas pate; the print's introduction gives it as the fifth sūkta of the anuvāka, eight Riks) occupy the upper part of that page; they are not yet written and belong to the next session.

Summary of Sūkta 39. Ten Riks to the Maruts. Rik 1 asks to whom the Maruts are travelling, their power falling from afar like sunlight; Riks 2–3 pray that their weapons be firm and describe how they break trees and make their way through mountains; Rik 4 says no enemy of theirs exists in heaven or on earth; Riks 5–6 describe the shaking of mountains and trees and the spotted does and red deer yoked to their chariots; Riks 7–10 are prayers: for the protection of the sacrificer's sons (7), that the Maruts deprive hostile men of food, strength and help (8), that they come to Kaṇva with complete protection as lightning brings rain (9), and that they hurl their anger like an arrow at the enemy of the ṛṣis (10). All ten Riks are written in full; the heavily crowded grammar pages (pp. 360–361, 367–369) are characterized only.

Sāyaṇa's introduction and the Kannada anuvāda

Sāyaṇa's introduction printed in Kannada script; re-read from the better scan, PDF 391

उत्तिष्ठेत्यष्टर्चं पञ्चमं सूक्तं कण्वस्यार्षं बार्हतं । युजः सतोबृहत्यः । अयुजो बृहत्यः । ब्रह्मणस्पतिदेवताकं । अनुक्रम्यते च । उत्तिष्ठाष्टौ ब्राह्मणस्पत्यमिति ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो लैङ्गिकः । चतुर्विंशेऽहनि मरुत्वतीये प्राकृताद्ब्राह्मणस्पत्यात्प्रगाथात्पूर्वमुत्तिष्ठ ब्रह्मणस्पत इत्ययं प्रगाथः । मरुत्वतीये इति खण्डे सूत्रितं । प्रैतु ब्रह्मणस्पतिरुत्तिष्ठ ब्रह्मणस्पत इति ब्राह्मणस्पत्यावापते पूर्वौ नित्यात् । आ. ७-३ । इति ॥ आद्या तु प्रवर्ग्येऽप्यभिष्टवे विनियुक्ता । उत्तिष्ठ ब्रह्मणस्पत इत्येतामुक्त्वावतिष्ठते । आ. ४-७ । इति सूत्रितत्वात् ॥

uttiṣṭhety aṣṭarcaṃ pañcamaṃ sūktaṃ kaṇvasyārṣaṃ bārhataṃ | yujaḥ satobṛhatyaḥ | ayujo bṛhatyaḥ | brahmaṇaspatidevatākaṃ | anukramyate ca | uttiṣṭhāṣṭau brāhmaṇaspatyam iti || sūktaviniyogo laiṅgikaḥ | caturviṃśe 'hani marutvatīye prākṛtād brāhmaṇaspatyāt pragāthāt pūrvam uttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspata ity ayaṃ pragāthaḥ | marutvatīye iti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | praitu brahmaṇaspatir uttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspata iti brāhmaṇaspatyāvāpate pūrvau nityāt | ā. 7-3 | iti || ādyā tu pravargye 'py abhiṣṭave viniyuktā | uttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspata ity etām uktvāvatiṣṭhate | ā. 4-7 | iti sūtritatvāt ||

Translation: "Uttiṣṭha — the fifth sūkta [of the anuvāka], of eight ṛks, the seer's work of Kaṇva, of the Bārhata [Prāgātha] kind; the even-numbered [ṛks] are Satobṛhatī, the odd-numbered Bṛhatī; its deity is Brahmaṇaspati. And the Anukramaṇikā says: 'uttiṣṭhāṣṭau brāhmaṇaspatyam'. The application (viniyoga) of the sūkta is laiṅgika: on the twenty-fourth day [of the Soma sacrifice], in the Marutvatīya [śastra], before the regular Brāhmaṇaspatya pragātha, this pragātha 'uttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspate'. It is laid down in the section called Marutvatīya: 'praitu brahmaṇaspatiḥ' and 'uttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspate' — the two Brāhmaṇaspatya [verses] are the earlier ones before the āvāpa [insertion], since they are constant (Ā. 7-3). The first ṛk is applied in the Pravargya, also in the abhiṣṭava: 'uttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspate' — having said this one stands up (Ā. 4-7), as it is laid down." Translation tentative; numerals zoom-checked; the 7s are the flat-footed form.

Anuvāda (Kannada), p. 376 — "Uttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspate is the fifth sūkta in this eighth anuvāka. It has eight ṛks. The even-numbered ṛks are in the Satobṛhatī metre; the odd-numbered in the Bṛhatī metre. Brahmaṇaspati is the deity of this sūkta. In the Anukramaṇikā: 'uttiṣṭhāṣṭau brāhmaṇaspatyam' — the sūkta of eight ṛks beginning uttiṣṭha has Brahmaṇaspati as deity. The application of the sūkta is laiṅgika; and in the Somayāga, on the twenty-fourth day, when the Marutvatīya śastra mantras are recited, this sūkta uttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspate is recited for the ṛks of the Prāgātha metre that concern Brahmaṇaspati. This matter is explained in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section called Marutvatīya, by the sūtra 'praitu brahmaṇaspatir (Ṛ. Sa. 1-40-3) uttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspata (printed "Pā. Sū. 1-40-1" [sic], a Ṛgveda reference) iti brāhmaṇaspatyāvāpate pūrvau nityāt' (Ā. 7-3). The application of the first ṛk of this sūkta in the Pravargya and abhiṣṭava sacrifices is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 4-7) 'uttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspata ity etām uktvāvatiṣṭhate'." हे ब्रह्मणस्पते एतन्नामक देव उत्तिष्ठ । अस्मदनुग्रहाय त्वदीयनिवासादुत्थानं कुरु । देवयन्तो देवान् कामयमाना वयं त्वा त्वामीमहे । याचामहे । सुदानवः शोभनदानयुक्ता मरुत उप प्र यन्तु । समीपे प्रकर्षेण गच्छन्तु । हे इन्द्र त्वं सचा ब्रह्मणस्पतिना सह प्राशूः सोमस्य प्राशको भव । यद्वा । वृत्रस्य हिंसको भव ॥ उत्तिष्ठ । ऊर्ध्वकर्मत्वादात्मनेपदाभावः । पा. १-३-२४ । ब्रह्मणस्पते । सुबामन्त्रित इति परांगवद्भावात् षष्ठ्यामन्त्रितसमुदायकस्याष्टमिकं सर्वानुदात्तत्वं । देवयन्तः । देवानात्मन इच्छन्तः । सुप आत्मनः क्यच् । न छन्दस्यपुत्रस्येत्यस्यैव दीर्घस्यापि निषेधः । अश्वाघस्यादिति पुनरात्वविधानसामर्थ्यात् । ईमह इत्यादयो गताः । प्राशूः । शॄ हिंसायां । प्रकर्षेण समन्तात् शृणाति हिनस्तीति प्राशूः । बहुलं छन्दसीत्यत्वं । वोरुपधाया छैर्घः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । भव । द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङ इति संहितायां दीर्घत्वं ॥

he brahmaṇaspate etannāmaka deva uttiṣṭha | asmadanugrahāya tvadīyanivāsād utthānaṃ kuru | devayanto devān kāmayamānā vayaṃ tvā tvām īmahe | yācāmahe | sudānavaḥ śobhanadānayuktā maruta upa pra yantu | samīpe prakarṣeṇa gacchantu | he indra tvaṃ sacā brahmaṇaspatinā saha prāśūḥ somasya prāśako bhava | yadvā | vṛtrasya hiṃsako bhava || uttiṣṭha | ūrdhvakarmatvād ātmanepadābhāvaḥ | pā. 1-3-24 | brahmaṇaspate | subāmantrita iti parāṅgavadbhāvāt ṣaṣṭhyāmantritasamudāyakasyāṣṭamikaṃ sarvānudāttatvaṃ | devayantaḥ | devān ātmana icchantaḥ | supa ātmanaḥ kyac | na chandasy aputrasyety asyaiva dīrghasyāpi niṣedhaḥ | aśvāghasyād iti punarātvavidhānasāmarthyāt | īmaha ity ādayo gatāḥ | prāśūḥ | śṝ hiṃsāyāṃ | prakarṣeṇa samantāt śṛṇāti hinastīti prāśūḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīty atvaṃ | vor upadhāyā chair ghaḥ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | bhava | dvyaco 'tastiṅa iti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghatvaṃ ||

Translation: "O Brahmaṇaspati — god of this name — uttiṣṭha, rise up. For our favour, make a rising from your dwelling. Devayantaḥ, we who desire the gods, tvā īmahe, ask you; we beg. Sudānavaḥ, endowed with fine giving, Maruts, upa pra yantu, let them go close up, strongly. O Indra, you, sacā, with Brahmaṇaspati, prāśūḥ bhava, be a partaker of the Soma; or be a slayer of Vṛtra. Uttiṣṭha: since the action is an upward one there is no ātmanepada (Pā. 1-3-24). Brahmaṇaspate: by subāmantrite parāṅgavat… the whole group, genitive plus vocative, takes the eighth-adhyāya unaccentedness (āṣṭamika sarvānudāttatva). Devayantaḥ: 'desiring the gods for themselves'; kyac by supa ātmanaḥ kyac; the prohibition of the lengthening by na chandasy aputrasya (no number in the bhāṣya) applies here; the ability of aśvāghasyāt to prescribe ā again [shows this]. Īmahe and the rest have been dealt with. Prāśūḥ: root śṝ hiṃsāyām; 'prakarṣeṇa samantāt śṛṇāti', it injures; the u by bahulaṃ chandasi; the lengthening by vor upadhāyā…; the accent of the first member in a compound ending in a kṛt. Bhava: in the Saṃhitā the long vowel by dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ."

Pratipadārtha — "brahmaṇaspate — O Brahmaṇaspati, the god; uttiṣṭha — (for the sake of favouring us) rise up; devayantaḥ — we who desire the help of the gods; tvā — you; īmahe — we beseech; sudānavaḥ — [those] with auspicious gifts; marutaḥ — the Maruts; upa pra yantu — let them come exceedingly near [to us]; indra — O Indra, [you]; sacā — with Brahmaṇaspati; prāśūḥ — one who drinks the Soma juice, or one who destroys Vṛtra; bhava — be."

Bhāvārtha — "O Brahmaṇaspati, rise from your seat to favour us. We, who desire the help of the gods, beseech you: 'Give your protection.' Let the Maruts, who give auspicious and noble gifts, come near us. O Indra, drink the Soma juice together with Brahmaṇaspati, or become the destroyer of Vṛtra."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 378) — "Rise up, Brahmanaspati ; we who desire to worship the gods Solicit you ; may the liberal Maruts also come up with you ; and Indra, be a partaker of the libation."

Page 379 (better scan PDF 394)

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), pp. 379–380 - brahmaṇaspate — "Brahmaṇaspati is the deity of this sūkta. Who is this Brahmaṇaspati? We shall explain in brief what his place and station among the deities are. The great ṛṣi Yāska in the Nirukta (Ni. 10-14), when considering Brahmaṇaspati, says: ब्रह्मणस्पतिः । ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्ब्रह्मणः पाता वा पालयिता वा ॥ — brahmaṇaspatiḥ | brahmaṇaspatir brahmaṇaḥ pātā vā pālayitā vā — 'Brahmaṇaspati is the protector, or the sustainer, of brahman.' Here the word brahma has the senses 'food', 'wealth' and 'praise' (Ni. 3-9). So 'brahmaṇaḥ pātā' means lord or master of food (of food, āhāra). How Brahmaṇaspati is lord of food Yāska shows by an example, quoting the ṛk अश्मास्यमवतं ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्मधुधारमभि यमोजसातृणत् । तमेव विश्वे पपिरे स्वर्दृशो बहुसाकं सिसिचुरुत्समुद्रिणम् ॥ (Ṛ. Sa. 2-24-4) — aśmāsyam avataṃ brahmaṇaspatir madhudhāram abhi yam ojasātṛṇat | tam eva viśve papire svardṛśo bahusākaṃ sisicur utsam udriṇam — editorial and tentative: "Brahmaṇaspati, with might, split open the stone-mouthed well, the stream of honey; all the sun-seeing ones drank just that; together they poured out the spring that holds water"; and then giving the Nirukta explanation अशनवन्तमास्यन्तनवन्तमवातितं ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्मधुधारमभियमोजसा बलेनाभ्यतृणत्तमेव सर्वे पिबन्ति रश्मयः सूर्यदृशो बह्वेनं सह सिञ्चन्त्युत्समुद्रिणमुदकवन्तम् (Ni. 10-13) — aśanavantam āsyantanavantam avātitaṃ brahmaṇaspatir madhudhāram abhi yam ojasā balenābhyatṛṇat tam eva sarve pibanti raśmayaḥ sūryadṛśo bahv enaṃ saha siñcanty utsam udriṇam udakavantam — re-read from the better scan, PDF 394; editorial and tentative: "…a stream full of water; the rays, seeing from the sun, all drink it; together they pour much of this spring, rich in water." The main intention is that Brahmaṇaspati, by the help of the sun's rays, makes the clouds drink the water of the ocean and makes that water fall specially on the earth as rain; from rain come plants and trees, and from them food and the like; hence Brahmaṇaspati is the protector of food. When brahma is taken as 'praise' or 'wealth', Brahmaṇaspati is lord of mantras and lord of wealth. The commentator [Sāyaṇa] says this very thing in explaining the ṛk quoted above. "Hymns to Brahmaṇaspati are numerous in the Ṛgveda; in them Brahmaṇaspati is said to give wealth and food. Many doubt whether this Brahmaṇaspati is a separate deity or another form of Agni. As he gives wealth and food together with Agni and other deities, some say Brahmaṇaspati is a special form of Agni. Yāska has remained silent on this point, that is, he has said nothing clearly. In the ṛks on Brahmaṇaspati there is likewise no sufficient basis to say that this deity is another form of Agni. Therefore it may be said confidently that Brahmaṇaspati is a separate deity, like Indra and Agni." - upa pra yantu marutaḥ — "let the Marut-deities come near you: that is, come together with you." - prāśūḥ = somasya prāśakaḥ — "one who partakes of the Soma juice: that is, one who drinks." - sacā = sahitaḥ — "accompanied: accompanied by Brahmaṇaspati."
