Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

हे सहसस्पुत्र बलस्य बहुपालक ब्रह्मणस्पते । पुत्रः पुरु त्रायते निपरणाद्वेति निरुक्तं । नि. २-११ । मर्त्यो मनुष्यो हिते शत्रुषु प्रक्षिप्ते धने निमित्तभूते सति त्वामित् । त्वामेवोपब्रूते हि । समीपं प्राप्य स्तौति खलु । तद्धनसम्पादनाय प्रार्थयत इत्यर्थः । हे मरुतो यो धनार्थी मर्त्यो वो युष्मान् ब्रह्मणस्पतिसहितानाचके स्तौति । स मर्त्यः स्वश्व्यं शोभनाश्वयुक्तं सुवीर्यं शोभनवीर्ययुक्तं च धनं दधीत । धारयेत् ॥ सहसस्पुत्र । ब्रह्मणस्पत इतिवत् । षष्ठ्याः पतिपुत्रेति विसर्जनीयस्य सत्वं । उपब्रूते । हि चेति निघातप्रतिषेधः । तिङश्चोदात्तवतीति गतेरनुदात्तत्वं । हिते । निष्ठायां दधातेर्हिरिति हिरादेशः । सुवीर्यं । शोभनं वीर्यं यस्येति बहुव्रीहौ वीरवीर्यौ चेत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । स्वश्व्यं । अश्वानां समूहोऽश्वीयं । केशाश्वाभ्यां यञ्छावन्यतरस्यां । पा. ४-२-४८ [?] । इति समूहार्थे छप्रत्ययः । छस्य ईयादेशः । शोभनमश्वीयं यस्य तत् स्वश्व्यं । ईकारलोपश्छान्दसः । परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलमित्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । दधीत । सीयुटः सकारलोपे सत्यभ्यस्तानामादिरित्याद्युदात्तत्वं । पादादित्वान्निघाताभावः । आचके । कै गै रै शब्दे । आदेच इत्यात्वं । लिटि द्विर्वचनेऽभ्यासस्य ह्रस्वचुत्वे । आतो लोप इटि चेत्याकारलोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः ॥

he sahasas putra balasya bahupālaka brahmaṇaspate | putraḥ puru trāyate niparaṇād veti niruktaṃ | ni. 2-11 | martyo manuṣyo hite śatruṣu prakṣipte dhane nimittabhūte sati tvām it | tvām evopabrūte hi | samīpaṃ prāpya stauti khalu | taddhanasampādanāya prārthayata ity arthaḥ | he maruto yo dhanārthī martyo vo yuṣmān brahmaṇaspatisahitān ācake stauti | sa martyaḥ svaśvyaṃ śobhanāśvayuktaṃ suvīryaṃ śobhanavīryayuktaṃ ca dhanaṃ dadhīta | dhārayet || sahasas putra | brahmaṇaspata itivat | ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputreti visarjanīyasya satvaṃ | upabrūte | hi ceti nighātapratiṣedhaḥ | tiṅaś codāttavatīti gater anudāttatvaṃ | hite | niṣṭhāyāṃ dadhāter hir iti hirādeśaḥ | suvīryaṃ | śobhanaṃ vīryaṃ yasyeti bahuvrīhau vīravīryau cety uttarapadādyudāttatvaṃ | svaśvyaṃ | aśvānāṃ samūho 'śvīyaṃ | keśāśvābhyāṃ yañchāvanyatarasyāṃ | pā. 4-2-48 [?] | iti samūhārthe chapratyayaḥ | chasya īyādeśaḥ | śobhanam aśvīyaṃ yasya tat svaśvyaṃ | īkāralopaś chāndasaḥ | parādiś chandasi bahulam ity uttarapadādyudāttatvaṃ | dadhīta | sīyuṭaḥ sakāralope saty abhyastānām ādir ity ādyudāttatvaṃ | pādāditvān nighātābhāvaḥ | ācake | kai gai rai śabde | ādeca ity ātvaṃ | liṭi dvirvacane 'bhyāsasya hrasvacutve | āto lopa iṭi cety ākāralopaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | yadvṛttayogād anighātaḥ ||

Translation: "O son of strength [sahasas putra], great protector of strength, Brahmaṇaspati. 'Putra: he protects much, or he protects from the hell pura', says the Nirukta (Ni. 2-11). Martyaḥ, the man, hite, when wealth has been thrown among the enemies [= abandoned by them] becomes the occasion, tvām it, on you alone upabrūte, he calls: having come close, he praises; the sense is: he prays for the winning of that wealth. O Maruts, the man who, wanting wealth, ācake, praises you, who are with Brahmaṇaspati — may that man dadhīta, hold, obtain, wealth that has good horses (svaśvya) and good heroism (suvīrya). Sahasas putra: as [in] brahmaṇaspate; by patiputra… the visarga becomes s. Upabrūte: the prohibition of nighāta by hi ca; the preverb is unaccented by tiṅaś codāttavati. Hite: in the participle, the substitute hi for dhā. Suvīryam: a bahuvrīhi, 'of which the heroism is good'; the first syllable of the latter member is acute by vīravīryau ca. Svaśvyam: 'a collection of horses' is aśvīya; by keśāśvābhyāṃ yañchāv anyatarasyām [Pā. 4-2-48 [?]] the suffix cha in the sense of collection; īya for cha; 'svaśvya, that which has fine horses'; the loss of ī is Vedic; the first syllable of the latter member is acute by parādiś chandasi bahulam. Dadhīta: when the s of sīyuṭ is lost, the first syllable is acute by abhyastānām ādiḥ; no nighāta because it begins a pāda. Ācake: root kai gai rai śabde; ā by ādeca…; in liṭ, doubling, shortening and palatalization of the reduplicate; loss of the ā by āto lopa iṭi ca; accent of the suffix; no nighāta because of the connection with yat."

Page 383 (better scan PDF 398)

Pratipadārtha — "sahasas putra — O Brahmaṇaspati, protector of strength; martyaḥ — man; hite — placed (with the enemy); dhane — for the sake of wealth; tvām it — you alone; upabrūte — comes close and praises; marutaḥ — O Maruts; yaḥ — which man, desiring wealth; vaḥ — you (together with Brahmaṇaspati); ā cake — praises; svaśvyam — with excellent horses; suvīryam — with excellent heroism; [and] (iratakka) dhanam — wealth that is [with these]; dadhīta — may he obtain."

Bhāvārtha — "O Brahmaṇaspati, you are the protector of strength, that is, you are exceedingly mighty. With the help of your strength, a man approaches you with his praises for the sake of wealth lying among enemies. O Maruts, since you are together with Brahmaṇaspati, the man who, desiring wealth, praises you will obtain excellent horses, excellent heroism and wealth."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 383) — "O Son of strength, ( Brahmanaspati ) the mortal worships you with praises for the sake of wealth abandoned by the enemy ; Maruts, may he who praises you obtain (wealth consisting of) excellent horses and great strength."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), pp. 383–384 - sahasas putra — "sahas means strength or power. Putra son. Although this word is specially established as used of Agni, here it is used of Indra and, in this ṛk, of Brahmaṇaspati. The commentator takes the word putra in this ṛk as 'protector', following Yāska's explanation 'putraḥ puru trāyate niparaṇād vā' (Ni. 2-11); 'balasya putra' means 'giver of strength'." - upa brūte = samīpaṃ prāpya stauti — "comes to your presence and praises." - hite — "a word formed from the root dhā. Its sense is: in a battle, when enemies flee and run away, the wealth they abandon — horses, chariots and the like, and goods such as money —" - svaśvyam = śobhanāśvayuktatvam — "the gain of excellent horses." - ā dadhīta = dhārayet — "will obtain without doubt" (niḥsaṃśayaṃ prāpnuyāt) — "may he obtain, in full." - yo va ā cake — "one who desires to praise you: that is, one who praises you."

Page 384 (better scan PDF 399)

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 384–386 — grammar pages, noted briefly - sahasaspatra: root saha marṣaṇe; the Uṇādi asun, of the oṇādika kind; "puru trāyate, so putra": the root trai pālane; ato 'nupasarge kaḥ (no number printed) ka and the loss of the ā; the s for the visarga and the wholly-unaccented as in brahmaṇaspate. - upabrūte: brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci, adādi, ubhayapadī; the ātmanepada ending here; śap elided; by hi ca the verb is not wholly unaccented, since it is joined with hi; the ending te is acute by the suffix accent. Tiṅ codāttavati — तिङ् चोदात्तवति — (Pā. Sū. 8-1-71): when a verb with an acute follows, a gati is unaccented; hence upa is unaccented. The print says that nipātā ādyudāttāḥ does not apply here, since tiṅ codāttavati is an exception to it, and discusses at length why the word tiṅ is needed in that sūtra (with the example ā mandrair indra haribhir yāhi, where mandra, ending in rak, is acute), the definition of gati by prādayas tatpratyeva gatyupasargasaṃjñāḥ… and the Kaumudī's remark tiṅgrahaṇam udāttavataḥ parimāṇārtham. Drift only; the passage is crowded. - hite: root ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ, juhotyādi; niṣṭhā: kta; dadhāter hiḥ — दधातेर्हिः — (Pā. Sū. 7-4-42; p. 385): hi for dhā before a kit suffix beginning with t. - suvīryam: bahuvrīhi; vīravīryau ca — वीरवीर्यौ च — (Pā. Sū. 6-2-120): in the Veda, in a bahuvrīhi, vīra and vīrya are first-syllable acute, even after su; the word vīra is from vīra vikrāntau with ac; vīrya by yat [acoyat] or tatra sādhuḥ. - svaśvyam: "aśvānāṃ samūhaḥ": keśāśvābhyāṃ yañchāv anyatarasyām — केशाश्वाभ्यां यञ्छावन्यतरस्याम् — (Pā. Sū. 4-2-48): after keśa and aśva, in the sense of collection, yañ and cha respectively; cha; āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ— (Pā. Sū. 7-1-2) gives īya; "śobhanam aśvīyaṃ yasya tat", a bahuvrīhi; the loss of ī by Vedic usage; parādiś chandasi bahulam (no number printed) the first syllable of the latter member is acute. - dadhīta: root ḍudhāñ; liṅ, ātmanepada; liṅaḥ sīyuṭ (no number printed); liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya (no number printed) loss of the s; suṭ tithoḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-4-107) — the print notes that the s of suṭ is also lost as before; śnābhyastayor ātaḥ — the ā → ī… [as read]; yalopa; abhyastānām ādiḥ — first-syllable acute; but the apādādau prohibition applies; so there is no wholly-unaccented form. - ācake: root kai gai rai śabde, first class [read as the 5th root]; ādeca upadeśe 'śiti — ā for ai; vyatyayo bahulam gives the ātmanepada in place of the parasmaipada; liṭ, ta; eś; doubling kā + kā + e; shortening of the reduplicate; kuhoś cuḥ — कुहोश्चुः — (no number printed) c for k: cakā + e; āto lopa iṭi ca — आतो लोप इटि च — (Pā. Sū. 6-4-64) loss of the ā before a kit or ñit ārdhadhātuka beginning with a vowel, or iṭ; the accent of the suffix; because of the connection with yat in yo va ā cake, yadvṛttān nityam prohibits wholly-unaccented. ### Page 386 (better scan PDF 401)

प्रैतु॒ ब्रह्म॑ण॒स्पतिः॒ प्र दे॒व्ये॑तु सू॒नृता॑ । अच्छा॑ वी॒रं नर्यं॑ प॒ङ्क्तिरा॑धसं दे॒वा य॒ज्ञं न॑यन्तु नः ॥ ३ ॥

Pada-pāṭha

प्र । एतु । ब्रह्मणः । पतिः । प्र । देवी । एतु । सूनृता । अच्छ । वीरम् । नर्यम् । पङ्क्तिऽराधसम् । देवाः । यज्ञम् । नयन्तु । नः ॥ ३ ॥

pra | etu | brahmaṇaḥ | patiḥ | pra | devī | etu | sūnṛtā | accha | vīram | naryam | paṅkti-rādhasam | devāḥ | yajñam | nayantu | naḥ || 3 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

चतुर्विंशेऽहनि मरुत्वतीये उत्तिष्ठ ब्रह्मणस्पत इत्यस्मात्प्रगाथात्पूर्वं प्रैतु ब्रह्मणस्पतिरित्ययं प्रगाथो विनियुक्तः । सूत्रं तूत्तिष्ठ ब्रह्मणस्पत इत्यत्रैवोदाहृतं ॥ महावीरमादाय शालां प्रतिगच्छंत्सु प्रैतु ब्रह्मणस्पतिरित्येतां पठन् होतानुगच्छेत् । सूत्रं च । प्रैतु ब्रह्मणस्पतिरित्यनुव्रजेत् । आ. ४-७ । इति ॥ एषैवाग्नीषोमीयप्रणयनेऽपि नियुक्ता । सूत्रितं च । प्रैतु ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्होता देवो अमर्त्यः । आ. ४-१० । इति ॥

caturviṃśe 'hani marutvatīye uttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspata ity asmāt pragāthāt pūrvaṃ praitu brahmaṇaspatir ity ayaṃ pragātho viniyuktaḥ | sūtraṃ tūttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspata ity atraivodāhṛtaṃ || mahāvīram ādāya śālāṃ pratigacchantsu praitu brahmaṇaspatir ity etāṃ paṭhan hotānugacchet | sūtraṃ ca | praitu brahmaṇaspatir ity anuvrajet | ā. 4-7 | iti || eṣaivāgnīṣomīyapraṇayane 'pi niyuktā | sūtritaṃ ca | praitu brahmaṇaspatir hotā devo amartyaḥ | ā. 4-10 | iti ||

Translation: "On the twenty-fourth day, in the Marutvatīya, this pragātha 'praitu brahmaṇaspatiḥ' is applied before the pragātha beginning 'uttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspate'; the sūtra has been quoted just there [in the introduction]. When [the priests] are going back to the sacrificial hall with the Mahāvīra [pot], the hotṛ, reciting this ṛk 'praitu brahmaṇaspatiḥ', follows; and the sūtra: 'praitu brahmaṇaspatir ity anuvrajet' (Ā. 4-7). It is also applied in the Agnīṣomīya praṇayana [the leading forward of the Agni-Soma victim]; it is laid down: 'praitu brahmaṇaspatir hotā devo amartyaḥ' (Ā. 4-10)."

ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्देवः प्रैतु । अस्मान्प्राप्नोतु । सूनृता देवी प्रियसत्यरूपा वाग्देवता प्रैतु । अस्मान्प्राप्नोतु । देवा ब्रह्मणस्पत्यादयो देवताः वीरं शत्रुं निःशेषेण दूरे प्रेरयन्तु । तं नर्यं मनुष्येभ्यो हितं पङ्क्तिराधसं ब्राह्मणोक्तहविष्पङ्क्त्यादिभिः समृद्धं यज्ञं प्रति नोऽस्मान् अच्छाभिमुख्येन नयन्तु ॥ प्रैतु । एजि पररूपं । पा. ६-१-९४ । इति पररूपे प्राप्ते एत्येधत्यूठ्सु । पा. ६-१-८९ । इति वृद्धिः । देव्येत्वित्यत्रोदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः स्वरितोऽनुदात्तस्येति स्वरितत्वं । नर्यं । नरेभ्यो हितं । प्राक्क्रीतीये उगवादिलक्षणो यत्प्रत्ययो द्रष्टव्यः । पा. ५-१-२ । पङ्क्तिराधसं । पङ्क्तिभी राध्नोतीति पङ्क्तिराधाः । गतिकारकयोरपि पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं च । उ. ४-२२६ । इत्यसुन् पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं च । यज्ञं । यजयाचेत्यादिना यजतेर्नङ् ॥

brahmaṇaspatir devaḥ praitu | asmān prāpnotu | sūnṛtā devī priyasatyarūpā vāgdevatā praitu | asmān prāpnotu | devā brahmaṇaspatyādayo devatāḥ vīraṃ śatruṃ niḥśeṣeṇa dūre prerayantu | taṃ naryaṃ manuṣyebhyo hitaṃ paṅktirādhasaṃ brāhmaṇoktahaviṣpaṅktyādibhiḥ samṛddhaṃ yajñaṃ prati no 'smān acchābhimukhyena nayantu || praitu | eji pararūpaṃ | pā. 6-1-94 | iti pararūpe prāpte etyedhatyūṭhsu | pā. 6-1-89 | iti vṛddhiḥ | devyetv ity atrodāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasyeti svaritatvaṃ | naryaṃ | narebhyo hitaṃ | prākkrītīye ugavādilakṣaṇo yatpratyayo draṣṭavyaḥ | pā. 5-1-2 | paṅktirādhasaṃ | paṅktibhī rādhnotīti paṅktirādhāḥ | gatikārakayor api pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ca | u. 4-226 | ity asun pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ca | yajñaṃ | yajayācety ādinā yajater naṅ || Re-read from the better scan, PDF 401–402: "atraivodāhṛtaṃ", "anuvrajet", "eṣaivāgnīṣomīya", "devyetv ity atra"; Ā. 4-7 and 4-10, U. 4-226 zoom-checked.

Translation: "Brahmaṇaspatir devaḥ praitu — let the god Brahmaṇaspati come forward: let him come to us. Sūnṛtā devī — the goddess in the form of pleasant truth, the deity of speech — praitu, let her come: let her reach us. Devāḥ — the deities, Brahmaṇaspati and the others — vīram — the enemy — drive away completely, far off. Naryam — beneficial to men — paṅktirādhasam — rich in the rows of oblations and so on spoken of in the Brāhmaṇas — yajñam prati, towards the sacrifice, naḥ, us, acchā, facing it, nayantu, let them lead. Praitu: eji pararūpam [Pā. 6-1-94] would give pararūpa; but by etyedhatyūṭhsu [Pā. 6-1-89] vṛddhi. Devy etu: the svarita by udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya. Naryam: 'beneficial to men'; the suffix yat by the ugavādi rule in the prākkrītīya section [Pā. 5-1-2]. Paṅktirādhasam: 'paṅktibhī rādhnoti', he succeeds by the rows; accent of the first member also with a gati or kāraka; the Uṇādi asun [Uṇ. 4-226 [?]]; the accent of the first member. Yajñam: naṅ after yaj by yajayācetyādinā."

Page 387 (better scan PDF 402)

Pratipadārtha — "brahmaṇaspatiḥ — Brahmaṇaspati, the god; praitu — let him come to us; sūnṛtā — [she who is] pleasant and in the form of truth; devī — the goddess of speech; praitu — let her come to us; devāḥ — the deities such as Brahmaṇaspati; vīram — [the] strong enemy; (let them drive [him] far away); naryam — [the sacrifice] that does good to men; paṅktirādhasam — full of rows of oblations (as spoken in the Brāhmaṇas); yajñam acchā — facing the sacrifice; naḥ — us; nayantu — let them lead."

Bhāvārtha — "May the god Brahmaṇaspati, the goddess of speech who is dear and in the form of truth, and the other deities, by their grace drive far away the enemy, who is strong and the destroyer of the sacrifice. May they lead us safely towards the sacrifice that does good to us and that is filled with rows of oblations as spoken in the Brāhmaṇas."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 387) — "May Brahmanaspathi approach us ; may the goddess of speech who always speaks the truth come to us ; may the Gods drive away every enemy and conduct us to the sacrifice which is benifical [sic] to man and which is well supplied with five fold oblations."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), pp. 387–388 - Application — "On the twenty-fourth day of the sacrifice, in the Marutvatīya śastra-mantra recitation, on that occasion (sandarbha), the application is stated here itself (in the introduction of this sūkta) that the ṛks uttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspate and praitu brahmaṇaspatiḥ, which are in the Prāgātha (Bṛhatī) metre, are to be recited. In the sacrifice called Pravargya, when the Hotṛ takes the Mahāvīra — the large clay vessel (pot) used in the sacrifice — and goes to the sacrificial hall, he should recite this ṛk praitu brahmaṇaspatiḥ and follow: this is explained in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (printed "A. 4-7") by the sūtra 'praitu brahmaṇaspatir ity anuvrajet'. In the leading forward of the Agni-Soma [victim] too this ṛk has application, as set forth by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (Āś. 4-10) 'praitu brahmaṇaspatir hotā devo amartyaḥ'." - sūnṛtā — "although the word sūnṛtā means the goddess Uṣas (Ni. 2-19) and also 'food' (Ni. 3-9), since in this ṛk it is an attribute of devī, the commentator has explained it as 'the goddess of speech, in the form of pleasant truth'." - vīram — "the commentator has given for this word 'enemy': a powerful enemy." - naryam = narebhyo hitam — "[the sacrifice] that does good to men." - paṅktirādhasam = brāhmaṇoktahaviṣpaṅktyādibhiḥ samṛddham — "In the Brāhmaṇas, such as the Aitareya, the word paṅkti is used in the sense 'five', as related to oblations of many kinds. Rādhas means wealth. One may say 'having five kinds of wealth' or 'having wealth in the form of rows of oblations'. The word paṅktirādhasam is not read anywhere else in the Ṛgveda but in this ṛk; therefore it is hard to give the exact sense of this word."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 388–389 — grammar pages, noted briefly - praitu: root iṇ gatau, loṭ, third-person singular, etu; when pra + etu the eṅi pararūpam — एङि पररूपम् — (Pā. Sū. 6-1-94): before an eṅ-initial root after a prefix ending in a, the pararūpa; this is barred by etyedhatyūṭhsu — एत्येधत्यूठ्सु — (Pā. Sū. 6-1-89): when eti, edhati or ūṭh follows, vṛddhi for the preceding and following vowels: a + e = ai. - devy etu: devī + etu; iko yaṇ aci (Pā. Sū. 6-1-77) gives y; the word devī is final-acute; udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya — उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः स्वरितोऽनुदात्तस्य — (Pā. Sū. 8-2-4): in the Saṃhitā the unaccented vowel after a yaṇ standing for an acute or svarita becomes svarita; so the following syllable is svarita. - naryam: "narebhyo hitam": ugavādibhyo yat — उगवादिभ्यो यत् — (Pā. Sū. 5-1-2; p. 389): after words ending in u and the gavādi group, yat in the senses prescribed up to tena krītam; the print explains that this sūtra has no sense indicated and is related to the following sūtras with their sense-indications; so also in tasmai hitam (Pā. Sū. 5-1-5), ugavādibhyo yat is carried over: after a base ending in u or in the gavādi group, yat in the sense hita with the fourth case; nara + ya; yasyeti ca the loss of the a. - paṅktirādhasam: "paṅktiviṃśati…" — पङ्क्तिविंशतित्रिंशच्चत्वारिंशत्पञ्चाशत्षष्टिसप्तत्यशीतिनवतिशतम् — (Pā. Sū. 5-1-59): the word paṅkti is given as a nipāta ending in ti; pañcan + ti; loss of ṭi; pañc + ti; coḥ kuḥ: k; anusvāra and parasavarṇa: paṅkti; the analysis "pañcaparimāṇasya paṅktiḥ"; this analysis serves only to give the etymology, since the word is a rūḍhi word and is used in many senses — number four, ten, metre and the like are denoted by it. "Paṅktibhī rādhnoti": a kāraka [instrumental] as upapada: gatikārakopapadayoḥ pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ca — (U. Sū. 4-666, as printed here; the bhāṣya gives U. 4-226): when a gati or kāraka is the upapada, after the root asi [asun] and the accent of the first member; the root rādha saṃsiddhau, then asi, and the accent of the first member. - yajñam: yaja devapūjādau; yajayācayatavichaprachrakṣo naṅ — यजयाचयतविच्छप्रच्छरक्षो नङ् — (Pā. Sū. 3-3-90): naṅ after these roots; yaj + na; stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ: the n becomes the fifth of the c-class; the combination of j and ñ is jña: yajña. Rik 3 ends here (|| 3 ||).

Pada-pāṭha

यः । वाघते । ददाति । सूनरम् । वसु । सः । धत्ते । अक्षिति । श्रवः । तस्मै । इळाम् । सुऽवीराम् । आ । यजामहे । सुऽप्रतूर्तिम् । अनेहसम् ॥ ४ ॥

yaḥ | vāghate | dadāti | sūnaram | vasu | saḥ | dhatte | akṣiti | śravaḥ | tasmai | iḷām | su-vīrām | ā | yajāmahe | su-pratūrtim | anehasam || 4 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

यो यजमानो वाघते ऋत्विजे सूनरं सुष्ठु नेतव्यं वसु धनं ददाति स यजमानो ब्रह्मणस्पतेः प्रसादादक्षिति क्षयरहितं श्रवोऽन्नं धत्ते । धारयति । तस्मै तादृशयजमानायेळामेतन्नामधेयां मनोः पुत्रीं । इळा वै मानवी यज्ञानुकाशिन्यासीदिति श्रुत्यन्तरात् । आ यजामहे । वयमृत्विजः सर्वतो यजामः । कीदृशीमिळां । सुवीरां शोभनैर्वीरैर्भटैर्युक्तां सुप्रतूर्तिं सुष्ठु प्रकर्षेण हिंसाकारिणीं अनेहसं केनाप्यहिंस्यां ॥ ददाति । अनुदात्ते चेत्यभ्यस्तस्याद्युदात्तत्वं । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । सूनरं । सुखेन नीयत इति सूनरं । ईषद्दुःसुषु कृच्छ्राकृच्छ्रार्थेषु खल् । पा. ३-३-१२६ । निपातस्य चेत्युपसर्गस्य दीर्घत्वं । अक्षिति । क्षयो नास्त्यस्येत्यक्षिति । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । नञ्सुभ्यामिति तु सर्वे विधयश्छन्दसि विकल्प्यन्त इति वचनान्न प्रवर्तते । श्रवः । श्रूयत इति श्रवः । श्रु श्रवणे । असुनो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं । सुवीरां । शोभना वीरा यस्याः सा सुवीरा । तां । वीरवीर्यौ चेत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । सुप्रतूर्तिं । तुर्वी हिंसार्थः । प्रपूर्वादस्माद्भावे क्तिन् । शोभना प्रतूर्तिः शत्रूणां हिंसनं यस्याः सा । तां । परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलमित्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । क्रत्वादिर्वा द्रष्टव्यः । अनेहसं । न हन्यत इत्यनेहाः । नञि हन एह च । उ. ४-२२३ । इत्यसुन्प्रत्ययो धातोरेहादेशश्च । नलोपो नञः । पा. ६-३-७३ । इति नकारस्य लोपः । तस्मान्नुडचि । पा. ६-३-७४ । इति नुट् ॥

yo yajamāno vāghate ṛtvije sūnaraṃ suṣṭhu netavyaṃ vasu dhanaṃ dadāti sa yajamāno brahmaṇaspateḥ prasādād akṣiti kṣayarahitaṃ śravo 'nnaṃ dhatte | dhārayati | tasmai tādṛśayajamānāyeḷām etannāmadheyāṃ manoḥ putrīṃ | iḷā vai mānavī yajñānukāśinyāsīd iti śrutyantarāt | ā yajāmahe | vayam ṛtvijaḥ sarvato yajāmaḥ | kīdṛśīm iḷāṃ | suvīrāṃ śobhanair vīrair bhaṭair yuktāṃ supratūrtiṃ suṣṭhu prakarṣeṇa hiṃsākāriṇīṃ anehasaṃ kenāpy ahiṃsyāṃ || dadāti | anudātte cety abhyastasyādyudāttatvaṃ | yadvṛttayogād anighātaḥ | sūnaraṃ | sukhena nīyata iti sūnaraṃ | īṣad-duḥ-suṣu kṛcchrākṛcchrārtheṣu khal | pā. 3-3-126 | nipātasya cety upasargasya dīrghatvaṃ | akṣiti | kṣayo nāstyasyety akṣiti | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | nañ-subhyām iti tu sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyanta iti vacanān na pravartate | śravaḥ | śrūyata iti śravaḥ | śru śravaṇe | asuno nittvād ādyudāttatvaṃ | suvīrāṃ | śobhanā vīrā yasyāḥ sā suvīrā | tāṃ | vīravīryau cety uttarapadādyudāttatvaṃ | supratūrtiṃ | turvī hiṃsārthaḥ | prapūrvād asmād bhāve ktin | śobhanā pratūrtiḥ śatrūṇāṃ hiṃsanaṃ yasyāḥ sā | tāṃ | parādiś chandasi bahulam ity uttarapadādyudāttatvaṃ | kratvādir vā draṣṭavyaḥ | anehasaṃ | na hanyata ity anehāḥ | nañi hana eha ca | u. 4-223 | ity asunpratyayo dhātor ehādeśaś ca | nalopo nañaḥ | pā. 6-3-73 | iti nakārasya lopaḥ | tasmān nuḍaci | pā. 6-3-74 | iti nuṭ ||

Translation: "The sacrificer who gives to the priest (vāghate) wealth that is sūnaram, easily led [= easily won, easy to take], that sacrificer, by the favour of Brahmaṇaspati, akṣiti, undiminished, śravaḥ, food, dhatte, obtains. Tasmai, for such a sacrificer, iḷām, [the goddess] Iḷā, the daughter of Manu ('Iḷā indeed, the daughter of Manu, was the follower of the sacrifice' — from another Śruti), ā yajāmahe, we the priests worship on all sides. What kind of Iḷā? Suvīrām, accompanied by fine heroes, warriors; supratūrtim, greatly and strongly destroying [enemies]; anehasam, that cannot be injured by anyone. Dadāti: the first syllable of the reduplicated form is acute by anudātte ca; no nighāta because of the connection with yat. Sūnaram: 'sukhena nīyate'; khal by īṣad-duḥ-suṣu kṛcchrākṛcchrārtheṣu [Pā. 3-3-126]; the lengthening of the preverb by nipātasya ca. Akṣiti: 'of which there is no kṣaya'; a bahuvrīhi, the accent of the first member; the rule nañ-subhyām does not apply, since all operations are optional in the Veda. Śravaḥ: 'śrūyate'; root śru śravaṇe; the suffix asun is nit, so first-syllable acute. Suvīrām: 'of whom the heroes are good'; the first syllable of the latter member by vīravīryau ca. Supratūrtim: turvī is in the sense of injuring; after it with pra, ktin in the abstract; 'of whom the smiting of enemies is excellent'; the accent of the latter member by parādiś chandasi bahulam; or it may be regarded as belonging to the kratvādi group. Anehasam: 'na hanyate', anehāḥ; by nañi hana eha ca (U. 4-223) the suffix asun and the substitute eha for the root; the loss of the n of nañ by [Pā. 6-3-73]; then the augment nuṭ before a vowel by [Pā. 6-3-74]."

Page 391 (better scan PDF 406)

Pratipadārtha — "yaḥ — which sacrificer; vāghate — to the priest; sūnaram — to be accepted with joy; vasu — wealth; dadāti — gives; saḥ — that sacrificer (by Brahmaṇaspati's favour); akṣiti — undiminishing; śravaḥ — food; dhatte — obtains; tasmai — for that sacrificer; suvīrām — with excellent heroes, accompanied by warriors; supratūrtim — one who destroys [enemies] well; anehasam — one who is not injured by others; iḷām — [the goddess Iḷā], aiming at Iḷā-devī; ā yajāmahe — we sacrifice well."

Bhāvārtha — "When a sacrificer, at the time of the rite, gives to the priests who help his sacrifice wealth in rich measure, they accept it with joy. Such a sacrificer, by Brahmaṇaspati's favour, obtains food that does not diminish. Since the goddess Iḷā, who destroys the crowd of enemies, is accompanied by exceedingly excellent heroes, enemies cannot injure her; she can wholly destroy enemies. Thus, aiming at the goddess Iḷā, daughter of Manu, who helps to bring the sacrifice to its end without hindrance, we perform the sacrifice for the sacrificer."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 391) — "He who presents to the priest wealth fit to be accepted recieves [sic] inexhaustible wealth ; for him, therefore we worship Ila possessed of brave worriors [sic], who inflicts injuries on enemies but cannot be herself injured."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), pp. 391–392 - vāghate = ṛtvije — "since among the eight names of the priest beginning with bhāratāḥ, karavaḥ, the word vāghataḥ is read (Ni. 3-19), vāghate means 'to the priest'." - sūnaram = suṣṭhu nīyate iti sūnaram — "easy to take, convenient." - akṣiti = kṣayo nāstyasyeti akṣiti — "without decay; always, not less, very much." - iḷām — "the word iḷā has many senses: earth (printed "Ni. 2-5"), speech (printed "Ni. 2-23"), food (Ni. 3-9), cow (Ni. 3-9), and the deity named Iḷā (Ni. 11-48). Here it must be explained as aiming at the deity Iḷā." - suvīrām = śobhanā vīrā yasyāḥ sā suvīrā tām | śobhanair bhaṭair yuktām — "the goddess Iḷā united with brave warriors of war." - supratūrtim — "turvī hiṃsārthaḥ; śobhanā pratūrtiḥ śatrūṇāṃ hiṃsanaṃ yasyāḥ sā tām | prakarṣeṇa śatrūṇāṃ hiṃsākāriṇīm — who strongly destroys enemies, that is, who ruins them." - anehasam — "na hanyata ity anehāḥ | kenāpy ahiṃsyām — who by no one can be injured, unstruck. The words suvīrām, supratūrtim, anehasam are attributes of the word iḷām."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 392–393 — grammar pages, noted briefly - dadāti: root ḍudāñ dāne; laṭ, tip; śap → ślu, doubling, shortening: dadāti; tip is pit and unaccented. By anudātte ca — अनुदात्ते च — (Pā. Sū. 6-1-190): "in the sūtra na vidyate udāttaḥ yasmin saḥ anudāttaḥ, a bahuvrīhi: when a la-substitute sārvadhātuka with no acute follows, the first syllable of the reduplicate is acute", so first-syllable acute. Since māhismadāś [as printed] is constant, the explanation of anudātte is given so that first-syllable acute comes even after the loss of the i. By connection with yat the wholly-unaccented does not come. - sūnaram: root ṇīñ prāpaṇe, kryādi [the print says nyā nayane]; "sukhena nīyate": īṣad-duḥ-suṣu kṛcchrākṛcchrārtheṣu khal (Pā. Sū. 3-3-126): khal; sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ gives guṇa; in the Saṃhitā the lengthening of su by nipātasya ca (Pā. Sū. 6-3-136). - akṣiti: kṣi kṣaye akarmakaḥ, first class (the print: kṣi kṣaye, intransitive, first class); ktin; "na vidyate kṣitiḥ kṣayo yasya tat": a bahuvrīhi; nañ-subhyām — नञ्सुभ्याम् — (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172) would give a different accent, but since sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante (Paribhāṣā 35) it does not apply; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam — बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् — [Pā. 6-2-1] gives the accent of the first member. - śravaḥ: "śrūyate iti śravaḥ": the Uṇādi asun after śru śravaṇe (the print gives sarvadhātubhyo 'sun by name, no number); being nit, first-syllable acute. - suvīrām: "śobhanāḥ vīrāḥ yasyāṃ sā suvīrā": she who is accompanied by excellent heroic warriors; accusative singular; vīravīryau ca — (no number printed on p. 393) gives first-syllable acute to the latter member. - supratūrtim: root turvī hiṃsārthaḥ, bhvādi; after it with the prefix pra, ktin in the abstract sense; "śobhanā = excellent, i.e. great; pratūrtiḥ = slaying of enemies; yasyāṃ sā, that in whom it is": an attribute of iḷām; parādiś chandasi bahulam (Pā. Sū. 6-1-199) gives the latter member first-syllable acute, as one may say; or else, by kratvādayaś ca — क्रत्वादयश्च — (Pā. Sū. 6-2-118), the words of the kratvādi group that follow su are first-syllable acute. - anehasam: nañ + han + eha ca (U. Sū. 4-663, as printed here; the bhāṣya gives U. 4-223): when nañ is upapada, after the root han the suffix asi [asun], and eh becomes the substitute for han: na + eh + as; nalopo nañaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-3-73): the loss of the n of nañ when a latter member follows: only a + eh + as; tasmān nuḍaci (Pā. Sū. 6-3-74): after nañ whose n has been lost, a vowel-initial latter member takes nuṭ: a + n + eh + as = anehas; accusative singular. "Kālo diṣṭo 'py anehāpi" (Amara): anehas is used in the sense of "time" in the lexicon; but, as it has the sense of an etymological meaning (avayavārtha) and an adjoining word that needs it, the conventional sense is not taken here; as in "padmāni yatrāgrasaroruhāṇi", where saroruha is conventional yet its etymological sense is taken; so here too. Rik 4 ends here (|| 4 ||).

Pada-pāṭha

प्र । नूनम् । ब्रह्मणः । पतिः । मन्त्रम् । वदति । उक्थ्यम् । यस्मिन् । इन्द्रः । वरुणः । मित्रः । अर्यमा । देवाः । ओकांसि । चक्रिरे ॥ ५ ॥

pra | nūnam | brahmaṇaḥ | patiḥ | mantram | vadati | ukthyam | yasmin | indraḥ | varuṇaḥ | mitraḥ | aryamā | devāḥ | okāṃsi | cakrire || 5 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

अग्नीषोमे मरुत्वतीयशस्त्र इन्द्रनिविद्प्रगाथानन्तरं प्र नूनमिति प्रगाथः । मरुत्वतीयेनेति खण्डे सूत्रितं । प्र नूनं ब्रह्मणस्पतिरिति ब्राह्मणस्पत्यः । आ. ५-१४ । इति ॥

agnīṣome marutvatīyaśastra indranivid-pragāthānantaraṃ pra nūnam iti pragāthaḥ | marutvatīyeneti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | pra nūnaṃ brahmaṇaspatir iti brāhmaṇaspatyaḥ | ā. 5-14 | iti || The first sentence is the Sāyaṇa note on the application of this ṛk; the Sanskrit "indranivid-pragāthā" is doubtful in the print [?].

ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्देव उक्थ्यं शस्त्रयोग्यं मन्त्रं नूनमवश्यं प्र वदति । होतृमुखे स्थितः सन् प्रब्रूते । यस्मिन्मन्त्र इन्द्रादयश्च सर्वे देवा ओकांसि स्थानानि चक्रिरे । तादृशं सर्वदेवप्रतिपादकं मन्त्रमिति पूर्वत्रान्वयः ॥ मन्त्रं । मत्रि गुप्तभाषणे । पचाद्यच् । वृषादिषु पाठादाद्युदात्तत्वं । उक्थ्यं । उक्थार्हं । छन्दसि चेत्यैर्हार्थे यप्रत्ययः । यद्वा । भवे छन्दसीति यत् । सर्वे विधयश्छन्दसि विकल्प्यन्त इति वचनाद्यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वाभावे व्यत्ययेन तित्स्वरितमिति स्वरितत्वं । ओकांसि । उच समवाये । समवयन्त्यस्मिन्नित्यधिकरण औणादिकोऽसुन् । बहुलग्रहणात् कुत्वं द्रष्टव्यमिति । ओके उचः के । पा. ७-३-६४ । इत्यत्र वृत्त्वा इत्युक्तं । चक्रिरे । इरेचित्त्वात्प्रत्ययस्वरः । यद्वृत्तयोगानिघातः ॥ ५ ॥

brahmaṇaspatir devaḥ ukthyaṃ śastrayogyaṃ mantraṃ nūnam avaśyaṃ pra vadati | hotṛmukhe sthitaḥ san prabrūte | yasmin mantra indrādayaś ca sarve devā okāṃsi sthānāni cakrire | tādṛśaṃ sarvadevapratipādakaṃ mantram iti pūrvatrānvayaḥ || mantraṃ | matri guptabhāṣaṇe | pacādyac | vṛṣādiṣu pāṭhād ādyudāttatvaṃ | ukthyaṃ | ukthārhaṃ | chandasi cety aihārthe yapratyayaḥ | yadvā | bhave chandasīti yat | sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyanta iti vacanād yato 'nāva ity ādyudāttatvābhāve vyatyayena titsvaritam iti svaritatvaṃ | okāṃsi | uca samavāye | samavayanty asminn ity adhikaraṇa auṇādiko 'sun | bahulagrahaṇāt kutvaṃ draṣṭavyam iti | oke ucaḥ ke | pā. 7-3-64 | ity atra vṛttvā ity uktaṃ | cakrire | irecittvāt pratyayasvaraḥ | yadvṛttayogān nighātaḥ || 5 || The print's closing numeral of this bhāṣya reads like "10" or "30"; It is read as the Rik number 5 [?].

Translation: "The god Brahmaṇaspati nūnam, surely, pra vadati, utters a mantra, ukthyam, fit for the śastra; standing in the mouth of the hotṛ he utters it — the mantra in which Indra and all the other gods have made their abodes (okāṃsi, places). 'Such a mantra, expressing all the gods': so it is to be connected with the preceding. Mantram: root matri guptabhāṣaṇe; ac of the pacādi class; first-syllable acute by belonging to the vṛṣādi group. Ukthyam: 'worthy of uktha'; the suffix ya in the sense 'fit for' by chandasi ca; or yat by bhave chandasi; since all operations are optional in the Veda, the first-syllable acute [by yato 'nāvaḥ] does not come, and by vyatyaya the svarita by tit svaritam. Okāṃsi: root uca samavāye; the Uṇādi asun in the locative sense, 'in which they come together'; because of the word bahulam, kutva is to be seen; and in oke ucaḥ ke [Pā. 7-3-64] the commentator [Vṛttikāra] has said 'bahulagrahaṇāt kutvam'. Cakrire: the suffix accent, since ire is cit; no nighāta because of the connection with yat."

Pratipadārtha — "brahmaṇaspatiḥ — the god Brahmaṇaspati; yasmin — in which mantra; indraḥ — Indra; varuṇaḥ — Varuṇa; mitraḥ — Mitra; aryamā — Aryaman [and the rest]; devāḥ — all deities; okāṃsi — places of dwelling; cakrire — have made [for themselves] (such a mantra expressing all the deities); ukthyam — fit for praise; mantram — the mantra; nūnam — certainly; pra vadati — (staying in the mouth of the hotṛ) says clearly."

Bhāvārtha — "In the mantra recited by the hotṛ at the time of the sacrifice, Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman and further all the deities have made their dwelling places; that is, the mantra expresses all the deities. Brahmaṇaspati, favouring the hotṛ and standing in his mouth, clearly recites this mantra, which is fit for praise and which expresses all the deities."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 396–397 — grammar pages, noted briefly - mantram: root matri guptabhāṣaṇe, tenth class [print: "10th class"]; idit, so idito num dhātoḥ (no number printed) gives the augment num; nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ (no number printed) the suffix ac of the pacādi kind; since the suffix is cit it would be final-acute by citaḥ, but the vṛṣādi group is an ākṛtigaṇa, so this word is added to it, and by vṛṣādīnāṃ ca it is first-syllable acute. - ukthyam: root vaca paribhāṣaṇe; pātṛtudivacirecisicibhyas thak — पात्र्तुदिवचिरिचिसिचिभ्यस्थक् — (U. Sū. 2-164) the suffix thak; vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti — the saṃprasāraṇa: u; pūrvarūpa: ukth; "uktham arhati"; chandasi ca (Pā. Sū. 5-1-67) after prātipadika words in the sense "he deserves" [taram arhati, as printed] the suffix ya; or by bhave chandasi (Pā. Sū. 4-1-110 [as printed; for 4-4-110]) yat in the locative-ending sense of bhava; the print explains that prāggitāt yat (Pā. Sū. 4-4-75) and the sūtra tasmai hitam (Pā. Sū. 5-1-5) with its sense-indication are given in a certain order, and that in bhave chandasi [Pā. 4-4-110] the sense bhava is given, so yat is carried over by adhikāra but chandasi ca has no sense-indication; hence prākkrītāc chaḥ does not reach there; yato 'nāvaḥ gives final-acute but, since all operations are optional in the Veda, it is not applied; tit svaritam gives svarita; in the first alternative by vyatyayo bahulam the svarita. Crowded; drift only. - okāṃsi: uca samavāye; "samavayanty atra", people gather here to dwell; the Uṇādi asun in the sense of locus; the substitute k for c by bahulagrahaṇa; the Vṛttikāra says in the sūtra oke ucaḥ ke (Pā. Sū. 7-3-64; p. 397): "bahulagrahaṇāt kutvaṃ draṣṭavyam". The print then argues that, if the suffix ka of igupadhajñā— is added to the root uc, then guṇa and kutva are specified in oke ucaḥ ke, giving oka ending in a; with ghañ by halaś ca the kutva by cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ comes and guṇa, oka — [accent] first-syllable acute, so not final-acute; for that reason the sūtra oke ucaḥ was made; it too ends in a. Here there is a word ending in s; the process is to be stated as before. - cakrire: root ḍukṛñ karaṇe, liṭ, ātmanepada, jha; liṭas tajhayor eśirec — लिटस्तझयोरेशिरेच् — : ire for jha; the prohibition of the substitute by dvirvacane 'ci; doubling, kṛ + kṛ + ire; uraṭ, raparatva; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ loses the r; kuhoś cuḥ c for k: ca + kṛ + ire; yaṇ: cakrire. Irec is cit, hence the final-acute accent by citaḥ; because of the connection with yat in yasmin, yadvṛttān nityam prohibits wholly-unaccented. Rik 5 ends here (|| 5 ||).

हे देवा ब्रह्मणस्पतिप्रभृतयस्तमित् तमेवेन्द्रादिसर्वदेवताप्रतिपादकं मन्त्रं विदथेषु यज्ञेषु वोचेम । वयमृत्विजो ब्रवाम । कीदृशं । शम्भुवं सुखस्य भावयितारं अनेहसमहिंसनीयं दोषरहितं । हे नरो नेतारो देवा इमामस्माभिरुच्यमानां मन्त्ररूपां वाचं प्रतिहर्यथ च । यूयं कामयध्वे चेत् । तर्हि विश्वेत् सर्वापि वामा वननीया वाग् वो युष्मानश्नवत् । व्याप्नुयात् ॥ वोचेम । वच परिभाषणे । आशीर्लिङ् । लिङ्याशिष्यङ् । वच उमित्यु-मागमः । छन्दस्युभयथेति सार्वधातुकत्वाल्लिङः सलोपोऽनन्त्यस्येति यासुटः सकारस्य लोपः । अतो येय इतीयादेशः । आद्गुणः । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । विदथेषु । विद ज्ञाने । विद्यते फलसाधनत्वेन ज्ञायत इति विदथो यज्ञः । रुविदिभ्यां कित् । उ. ३-११६ । इत्यथप्रत्ययः । शम्भुवं । भवतेरन्तर्भावितण्यर्थात् क्विप्चेति क्विप् । ओः सुपि । पा. ६-४-८३ । इति यणादेशस्य न भूसुधियोः । पा. ६-४-८५ । इति प्रतिषेधः । मन्त्रादयो गताः । प्रतिहर्यथ । हर्य गतिकान्त्योः । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वं । तिङश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वरेणाद्युदात्तत्वं । इमां चेत्यत्र चशब्दश्चेदर्थः । चेणिति निपातान्तरं न च समुच्चयार्थः । तेन निपातैर्यद्यदिहन्तकुविन्नेच्चेच्चण्कच्चिद्यत्रयुक्तम् । पा. ८-१-३० । इति निघातप्रतिषेधः । अश्नवत् । अशू व्याप्तौ । लेट्यडागमः । व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं । इतश्च लोप इतीकारलोपः । इयेजुवङ्भ्यां गुणवृद्धी भवतो विप्रतिषेधेन । का. ६-४-७७ । इति गुणः ॥ ६ ॥

he devā brahmaṇaspatiprabhṛtayas tam it tam evendrādisarvadevatāpratipādakaṃ mantraṃ vidatheṣu yajñeṣu vocema | vayam ṛtvijo bravāma | kīdṛśaṃ | śambhuvaṃ sukhasya bhāvayitāraṃ anehasam ahiṃsanīyaṃ doṣarahitaṃ | he naro netāro devā imām asmābhir ucyamānāṃ mantrarūpāṃ vācaṃ pratiharyatha ca | yūyaṃ kāmayadhve cet | tarhi viśvet sarvāpi vāmā vananīyā vāg vo yuṣmān aśnavat | vyāpnuyāt || vocema | vaca paribhāṣaṇe | āśīrliṅ | liṅyāśiṣy aṅ | vaca um ity u-māgamaḥ | chandasy ubhayatheti sārvadhātukatvāl liṅaḥ salopo 'ntyasyeti yāsuṭaḥ sakārasya lopaḥ | ato yeya itīyādeśaḥ | ād guṇaḥ | tiṅ atiṅa iti nighātaḥ | vidatheṣu | vida jñāne | vidyate phalasādhanatvena jñāyata iti vidatho yajñaḥ | ruvidibhyāṃ kit | u. 3-116 | ity athapratyayaḥ | śambhuvaṃ | bhavater antarbhāvitaṇyarthāt kvip ceti kvip | oḥ supi | pā. 6-4-83 | iti yaṇādeśasya na bhūsudhiyoḥ | pā. 6-4-85 | iti pratiṣedhaḥ | mantrādayo gatāḥ | pratiharyatha | harya gatikāntyoḥ | śapaḥ pittvād anudāttatvaṃ | tiṅaś ca lasārvadhātukasvareṇa dhātusvareṇādyudāttatvaṃ | imāṃ cety atra caśabdaś cedarthaḥ | ceṇ iti nipātāntaraṃ na ca samuccayārthaḥ | tena nipātair yadyadihantakuvinnec cec caṇkaccid yatrayuktam | pā. 8-1-30 | iti nighātapratiṣedhaḥ | aśnavat | aśū vyāptau | leṭy aḍāgamaḥ | vyatyayena parasmaipadaṃ | itaś ca lopa itīkāralopaḥ | iyejuvaṅbhyāṃ guṇavṛddhī bhavato viprati­ṣedhena | kā. 6-4-77 | iti guṇaḥ || 6 ||

Translation: "O gods, Brahmaṇaspati and the rest, tam it, that very mantra that expresses all the deities beginning with Indra, vidatheṣu, in the sacrifices, vocema, we, the priests, would speak. What kind? Śambhuvam, bringing about happiness; anehasam, not to be injured, free from fault. O naraḥ, leaders, gods, imāṃ vācam, this speech in the form of a mantra, uttered by us, pratiharyatha ca, if you desire it — viśvā it vāmā, then all the lovely speech vaḥ aśnavat, may it reach you. Vocema: root vaca paribhāṣaṇe; the benedictive (āśīrliṅ); aṅ after liṅ in the benedictive sense; the augment um for vaca; since by chandasy ubhayathā the liṅ is sārvadhātuka, the loss of the s of yāsuṭ; the substitute iya for ya by ato yeyaḥ; guṇa by ād guṇaḥ; the verb is unaccented by tiṅ atiṅaḥ. Vidatheṣu: root vida jñāne: 'vidyate, it is known as the means of the fruit': vidathaḥ, a sacrifice; the suffix atha by ruvidibhyāṃ kit (U. 3-116). Śambhuvam: from bhū with an implicit causative sense, kvip by kvip ca; the yaṇ-substitution by oḥ supi [Pā. 6-4-83] is prohibited by na bhūsudhiyoḥ [Pā. 6-4-85]. Pratiharyatha: root harya gatikāntyoḥ; the śap being pit is unaccented; the verb takes the accent of the root. In imāṃ ca the word ca is in the sense of cet, 'if'; it is a different particle ceṇ, not in the sense of conjunction; therefore the prohibition of nighāta by yadyadihanta… [Pā. 8-1-30]. Aśnavat: root aśū vyāptau; leṭ with the augment aṭ; parasmaipada by vyatyaya; the loss of the i by itaś ca lopaḥ; guṇa by the rule that when iyaṅ/uvaṅ and guṇa/vṛddhi conflict, the later rule [guṇa] applies (Kā. 6-4-77)."

Page 399 (better scan PDF 414)

Pratipadārtha — "devāḥ — O Brahmaṇaspati and the other deities; śambhuvam — one that brings happiness; anehasam — also faultless; tam it mantram — that very mantra (that expresses all the deities, Indra and the rest); vidatheṣu — in sacrifices; vocema — we, the priests, recite; naraḥ — O leaders, all deities; imām — which is recited by us, this mantra-form; vācam — speech; pratiharyatha — if you desire (have wished for); viśvet vāmā — all speech dear to you; vaḥ — you; aśnavat — may it pervade."

Bhāvārtha — "O Brahmaṇaspati and the other deities, we recite in the sacrifices that mantra which brings happiness, is faultless, and expresses all the deities. O deities, you are our leaders. If our speech in the form of the mantra, which we the priests recite, is good for you and desired by you, then may all our speech, dear to you, pervade you; may it bring you satisfaction."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 399) — "O gods, we will recite that delightful and faultless prayer in our sacrifices ; O brave leaders, if you desire to hear that prayer, that all that is said will reach you."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 400 - vidatheṣu = yajñeṣu — "vidyate phalasādhanatvena jñāyate iti vidathaḥ yajñaḥ: since the word vidathaḥ is read among the fifteen names of sacrifice beginning with yajñaḥ, vena (Ni. 3-19), vidatheṣu means 'in sacrifices'." - śambhuvam = sukhasya bhāvayitāram — "that which makes happiness; delightful to hear." - anehasam = ahiṃsanīyam | doṣarahitam — "faultless, without any deficiency." - imāṃ ca vācam — "this speech in the form of praise." - pratiharyatha — "harya gatikāntyoḥ: desire, wish to hear." - vāmā = vananīyā vāk — "pervading speech, that is, speech that all wish to hear." - aśnavat = vyāpnuyāt — "let it pervade, let it reach you, let it be heard by you."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 400–402 — grammar pages, noted briefly - vocema: root vaca paribhāṣaṇe; āśīrliṅ, uttama plural mas; nityaṃ ṅitaḥ — नित्यं ङितः — (Pā. Sū. 3-4-99): the s at the end of a ṅit [liṅ] first-person ending is always lost; yāsuṭ; liṅyāśiṣy aṅ — लिङ्याशिष्यङ् — (Pā. Sū. 3-1-86): in the Veda, after roots in the benedictive liṅ, the vikaraṇa aṅ; this is stated in general, but the vikaraṇa is seen mostly only after the roots sthā, gā, gam, vac, vid, śak, ruh; when aṅ comes: vac + a + yās + ma; vaca um — वच उम् — (Pā. Sū. 7-4-20): the augment um for vac before aṅ; chandasy ubhayathā gives the benedictive also sārvadhātuka name; liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya (Pā. Sū. 7-2-79): the loss of the non-final s of a sārvadhātuka liṅ; ato yeyaḥ — अतो येयः — (Pā. Sū. 7-2-80): iya for the yā of a sārvadhātuka liṅ after a short a; v + uc + a + iya + ma; lopo vyor vali loss of y; ād guṇaḥ gives o for a + u and e for a + i: vocema; tiṅ atiṅaḥ wholly unaccented. - vidatheṣu: vida jñāne, adādi [print: vida jñāne, vidyate svargādiphalagaḷige sādhana]; "vidathaḥ means yajña, the word vidatha in the sense of sacrifice"; rudiśvidibhyām kit (U. Sū. 3-395, as printed here; p. 401): atha after rudir aśruvimocane and vida jñāne; it is kit, so no guṇa of the light penultimate; the print holds that this reading of the sūtra (with gāṅkuṭādi—) agrees with the Mahābhāṣya; and notes that some commentators (the Daśapādīvṛttikāra) read rudivididbhyāṃ kit, with whom athaj of the earlier bhāṣya would not be consistent; hence these views are not the accepted ones. - śambhuvam: "śaṃ bhāvayatīti śambhūḥ": kvip ca after bhū; śambhū + am; oḥ supi — ओः सुपि — (Pā. Sū. 6-4-83): the yaṇ substitution for the final u/ū of a root-ending stem before an ac-initial sup; prohibited by na bhūsudhiyoḥ — न भूसुधियोः — (Pā. Sū. 6-4-85); aci śnudhātu— gives uvaṅ. - mantram: "the process was given in the preceding mantra Rik 5." anehasam: "described in the earlier Rik 4, where it was separated." - pratiharyatha: root harya gatikāntyoḥ, first class; tha, śap, with the prefix prati; because śap is pit it is unaccented; tāsyanudāttet… makes the la-substitute sārvadhātuka tha unaccented; by the root accent haryatha is first-syllable acute; by tiṅ codāttavati prati is unaccented. - imāṃ ca: "the ca here is not the ca in the sense of conjunction; it is the particle ceṇ [i.e. cet, 'if'] with its ṇ an indicatory letter, leaving ca; hence its sense is 'if'. By nipātair yadyadihantakuvinnec cec caṇ kaccid yatrayuktam — निपातैर्यद्यदिहन्तकुविन्नेच्चेच्चण्कच्चिद्यत्रयुक्तम् — (Pā. Sū. 8-1-30) it is meant that what is joined with these particles is not unaccented"; so the wholly-unaccented does not come to pratiharyatha; the bhāṣya shows the direct connection as "pratiharyatha ca". - aśnavat: root aśū vyāptau; leṭ, tip; the augment aṭ by leṭo 'ḍāṭau; itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu the loss of the i; aś + nu + at when the śnu vikaraṇa comes; āc-chnudhātu…; the substitute uvaṅ (aci śnudhātu—, Pā. Sū. 6-4-77; p. 402) and guṇa (Pā. Sū. 7-3-84) both being possible, the later rule, guṇa, prevails; from the Kāśikā text iyejuvaṅbhyāṃ guṇavṛddhī bhavato vipratiṣedhena (printed "Pā. Sū. 6-4-77"; it is the Kāśikā's statement): "where iyaṅ/uvaṅ are taught and guṇa/vṛddhi both obtain simultaneously, by the paribhāṣā vipratiṣedhe paraṃ kāryam the latter, guṇa or vṛddhi, is applied." Rik 6 ends here (|| 6 ||).

Pada-pāṭha

कः । देवऽयन्तम् । अश्नवत् । जनम् । कः । वृक्तऽबर्हिषम् । प्रऽप्र । दाश्वान् । पस्त्याभिः । अस्थित । अन्तर्वावत् । क्षयम् । दधे ॥ ७ ॥

kaḥ | deva-yantam | aśnavat | janam | kaḥ | vṛkta-barhiṣam | pra-pra | dāśvān | pastyābhiḥ | asthita | antarvāvat | kṣayam | dadhe || 7 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

देवयन्तं देवान्कामयमानं जनं कोऽश्नवत् । ब्रह्मणस्पतिव्यतिरिक्तः को नाम देवो व्याप्नुयात् । तथा वृक्तबर्हिषमनुष्ठानाय छिन्नबर्हिषं यजमानं कोऽन्यो देवोऽश्नवत् । दाश्वान् हविर्दत्तवान्यजमानः पस्त्याभिर्मनुष्यैर्ऋत्विग्भिः सह प्रप्रास्थित । देवयजनदेशं प्रति प्रस्थितवान् । अन्तर्वावत् अन्तः स्थितबहुधनोपेतं । यद्वा । अन्तः स्थितपुत्रपौत्रादिप्रयुक्तबहुविधवागुपेतं क्षयं निवासस्थानं गृहं दधे । धृतवान् भवति । देवयन्तमित्यादयो गताः । प्रप्र । प्रसमुपोदः पादपूरणे । पा. ८-१-६ । इति प्रशब्दस्य द्विर्भावः । अनुदात्तं चेत्याम्रेडितानुदात्तत्वं । अस्थित । ष्ठा गतिनिवृत्तौ । लुङि समवप्रविभ्यः स्थः । पा. १-३-२२ । इत्यात्मनेपदं । स्थाघ्वोरिच्च । पा. १-२-१७ । इति धातुसिचोरित् । कित्त्वे ह्रस्वादङ्गात् । पा. ८-२-२७ । इति सलोपः । अन्तर्वावत् । वागतिगन्धनयोः । अन्तर्वान्ति गच्छन्तीत्यन्तर्वाः पुत्रपशवादयः । आतो मनिन्नित्यादिना विच् । तदस्यास्तीति मतुप् । मतुपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । यद्वा । वावदीतेः क्विप् । क्षयं । क्षियन्ति निवसन्त्यस्मिन्निति क्षयः । पुंसि सञ्ज्ञायामित्यधिकरणे घः । क्षयो निवास इत्याद्युदात्तत्वं ॥ ७ ॥

devayantaṃ devān kāmayamānaṃ janaṃ ko 'śnavat | brahmaṇaspativyatiriktaḥ ko nāma devo vyāpnuyāt | tathā vṛktabarhiṣam anuṣṭhānāya chinnabarhiṣaṃ yajamānaṃ ko 'nyo devo 'śnavat | dāśvān havirdattavān yajamānaḥ pastyābhir manuṣyair ṛtvigbhiḥ saha prapra 'sthita | devayajanadeśaṃ prati prasthitavān | antarvāvat antaḥ sthitabahudhanopetaṃ | yadvā | antaḥ sthitaputrapautrādiprayuktabahuvidhavāgupetaṃ kṣayaṃ nivāsasthānaṃ gṛhaṃ dadhe | dhṛtavān bhavati | devayantam ity ādayo gatāḥ | prapra | prasamupodaḥ pādapūraṇe | pā. 8-1-6 | iti praśabdasya dvirbhāvaḥ | anudāttaṃ cety āmreḍitānudāttatvaṃ | asthita | ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau | luṅi samavapravibhyaḥ sthaḥ | pā. 1-3-22 | ity ātmanepadaṃ | sthāghvor ic ca | pā. 1-2-17 | iti dhātusicor it | kittve hrasvād aṅgāt | pā. 8-2-27 | iti salopaḥ | antarvāvat | vāgatigandhanayoḥ | antarvānti gacchantīty antarvāḥ putrapaśvādayaḥ | āto manin ity ādinā vic | tad asyāstīti matup | matupaḥ pittvād anudāttatve kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | yadvā | vāvadīteḥ kvip | kṣayaṃ | kṣiyanti nivasanty asminn iti kṣayaḥ | puṃsi saṃjñāyām ity adhikaraṇe ghaḥ | kṣayo nivāsa ity ādyudāttatvaṃ || 7 ||

Translation: "Devayantam, desiring the gods — janam, [which] man — kaḥ aśnavat, who would reach? Who else, other than Brahmaṇaspati, which god would reach [him]? Likewise vṛktabarhiṣam, [a sacrificer] who has clipped his sacred grass for the rite — which other god would reach him? Dāśvān, the sacrificer who has given an oblation, pastyābhiḥ, with men, with priests, prapra asthita, has set forth well, set out towards the place of the divine rite. Antarvāvat, possessed of much wealth stored inside — or: possessed of many kinds of speech belonging to the sons and grandsons within — kṣayam, a dwelling, a house, dadhe, he bears. [For the grammatical tail:] Prapra: by prasamupodaḥ pādapūraṇe [Pā. 8-1-6] the doubling of pra; the second is unaccented by anudāttaṃ ca. Asthita: root ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau; ātmanepada by samavapravibhyaḥ sthaḥ (Pā. 1-3-22); sthāghvor ic ca [Pā. 1-2-17]; the loss of s by hrasvād aṅgāt (Pā. 8-2-27). Antarvāvat: root vā gatigandhanayoḥ; 'antarvānti', that which goes within — sons, cattle and so on: antarvāḥ; the suffix vic by āto manin…; then matup; since matup is pit and unaccented, the accent of the first member of a compound ending in a kṛt; or kvip from vāvadīti. Kṣayam: 'kṣiyanti, they dwell in it': kṣayaḥ; gha in the locative sense by puṃsi saṃjñāyām; first-syllable acute as 'kṣayo nivāsaḥ'."

Pratipadārtha — "devayantam — [the sacrificer] desiring the help of the gods; janaḥ — the sacrificer; kaḥ — (other than Brahmaṇaspati) which other deity himself; aśnavat — will approach? vṛktabarhiṣam — [the sacrificer] who has the darbha grass collected (for the sacrificial rite); kaḥ — which other deity himself (will come and join [him])? dāśvān — the sacrificer who offers the oblation; pastyābhiḥ — together with the priests; pra pra asthita — has set out (towards the place of the divine sacrifice); [that sacrificer] antarvāvat — rich in much wealth within, or accompanied by sons and grandsons; kṣayam — his own dwelling, the house; dadhe — has."

Bhāvārtha — "To the sacrificer who desires the gods — which deity, other than Brahmaṇaspati, will himself come? Which other deity will himself come near the sacrificer who has collected and spread darbha sticks so that the gods may come and sit? Now the sacrificer has come to the place of sacrifice together with the priests to offer oblations to the deities. The sacrificial house of that sacrificer is full of many invaluable things; or it is full of people such as sons and grandsons."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 403) — "Who, except Brahmanaspati, will approach the man desirous of worshipping the gods ? who will approach the sacrificer by whom clipped sacred grass is spread ( for the gods to sit on ) ? the giver of oblations has proceeded with his priests to the sacrificial hall which is full of precious things." The Special Topics and grammar of Rik 7 begin on p. 404, below.

Page 404 (better scan PDF 419)

Rik 40.7, continued from p. 404

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 404 - Main intention — "A man who wishes to propitiate the deities looks for Brahmaṇaspati alone; so, apart from him, which other deity will come to such a man? Which other deity will come to the sacrificer who has clipped and spread darbha sticks as seats for the gods to sit on? Apart from Brahmaṇaspati no other deity will come. Such a sacrificer, to propitiate Brahmaṇaspati, has come to his sacrificial hall, prepared with objects of great value, together with the priests who are his helpers." - devayantam = devān kāmayamānam — "one who wishes to worship the gods" (the source adds the English: "One who desires to worship the gods"). - vṛktabarhiṣam — "a seat of darbha grass made by cutting the tips of kuśa grass and spreading them, layer upon layer, three-fold, so that the gods may come and sit on the sacrificial altar. The tips of the cut darbha are called barhis. A seat spread with such darbha is called vṛktabarhis, and the sacrificer who has prepared it is called vṛktabarhiṣa by usage." - pra pra asthita = prasthitavān — "set out. For the sake of filling the pāda, the preverb pra is repeated." - pastyābhiḥ = gṛhāntarvartibhir manuṣyair ṛtvigbhiḥ — "with the priests." - antarvāvat — "vā gatigandhanayoḥ; antarvānti gacchantīty antarvāḥ putrapaśvādayaḥ, te yasmin santi iti antarvāvat. The root vā has the sense 'going'. Because they go antaḥ, inside, they are called antarvāḥ: sons, grandsons and so on in the house, cattle and so on, or other useful things. Antarvāvat means a place that has them, the house; the intention is a house full of excellent things. Here 'house' means the sacrificial house; so a sacrificial hall prepared with the means of sacrifice — oblations, ghee, sacrificial instruments, priests and so on." - kṣayam — "kṣiyanti nivasanty asminn iti kṣayaḥ: since it is a place fit to live in, kṣaya means dwelling-place."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 405–406 — grammar pages, noted briefly - devayantam: "explained in the first mantra of this very sūkta Rik 1; but there it was nominative [prathamānta]; here accusative [dvitīyānta]." aśnavat: explained in the preceding mantra Rik 6. - pra pra: prasamupodaḥ pādapūraṇe — प्रसमुपोदः पादपूरणे — (Pā. Sū. 8-1-6): in filling out a pāda, in the Veda, the preverbs pra, sam, upa, ud are doubled; so pra is doubled; anudāttaṃ ca — अनुदात्तं च — (Pā. Sū. 8-1-3): the second form of the doubled word is unaccented; hence the second pra is unaccented. - asthita: root ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau; dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ, ṣṭutva lost: sthā; luṅ; samavapravibhyaḥ sthaḥ — समवप्रविभ्यः स्थः — (Pā. Sū. 1-3-12 [as printed; for 1-3-22]): the ātmanepada after sthā when preceded by sam, ava, pra or vi [here by Vedic usage]; so the third-person singular ta; cli luṅi: cli; cleḥ sic; sthāghvor ic ca — स्थाघ्वोरिच्च — (Pā. Sū. 1-2-17): in the ātmanepada when sic is kit, the final of a root called ghu or the root sthā becomes i — so the ā of sthā becomes i; sic is kit; the augment aṭ: a-sthi-s-ta; hrasvād aṅgāt — ह्रस्वादङ्गात् — (Pā. Sū. 8-2-27): the s of sic is lost after a short-vowel-ending stem before a jhal; the print says the sic-loss does not occur in forms like asthiṣātām etc.; the kit-ness of sic was laid down there to prevent guṇa: asthita. - antarvāvat: root vā gatigandhanayoḥ; if one means antaḥ = within, vānti = go, then by āto manin— (no number printed) the suffix vic comes; antarvāḥ: sons, cattle and so on, which enter their house without fear. Antarvāḥ asya asti: tad asyāsty asmin— (no number printed): matup; mādupadhāyāś ca matorvo 'yavādibhyaḥ (no number printed) the m of matup becomes v: antarvāvat; matup is pit and unaccented, so the accent of the first member of a compound ending in a kṛt. "This is one process." Another: root vada vyaktāyāṃ vāci; dhātor ekācaḥ— for yaṅ; yaño 'ci ca [Pā. 2-4-74 as read] the loss of yaṅ; sanyaṅoḥ doubling; loss in the reduplicate; dīrgho 'kitaḥ long vowel in the reduplicate: vāvad; after it kvip: antaḥ vāvadīti antarvāvat ["that which speaks within"]. "This is another process." - kṣayam: kṣi nivāsagatyoḥ, tudādi: "kṣiyanti nivasanty atra": puṃsi saṃjñāyāṃ ghaḥ prāyeṇa gha; guṇa, ay-substitution; kṣayo nivāse — क्षयो निवासे — (Pā. Sū. 6-1-201; p. 406): the word kṣaya in the sense of dwelling is first-syllable acute. Rik 7 ends here (|| 7 ||).

original pp. 406–409

Rik 8

Saṃhitā-pāṭha Saṃhitā accents as printed (checked at 450–600 dpi); Pada unaccented. [accent ?] in line 1: the underline near rājabhir bhaye lies under the conjunct rbha (placed on bhi), and the stroke after bhaye stands at the left edge of ci (placed on ye).

उप॑ क्ष॒त्रं पृ॑ञ्ची॒त हन्ति॒ राज॑भि॒र्भये॑ चित्सुक्षि॒तिं द॑धे । [accent ?] नास्य॑ व॒र्ता न त॑रु॒ता म॑हाध॒ने नार्भे॑ अस्ति व॒ज्रिणः॑ ॥ ८ ॥

úpa kṣatráṃ pṛñcītá hanti rā́jabhir bháye cit sukṣitíṃ dadhe | [accent ?] nā́sya vartā́ ná tarutā́ mahādhané nā́rbhe asti vajríṇaḥ || 8 ||

Pada-pāṭha

उप । क्षत्रम् । पृञ्चीत । हन्ति । राजऽभिः । भये । चित् । सुऽक्षितिम् । दधे । न । अस्य । वर्ता । न । तरुता । महाऽधने । न । अर्भे । अस्ति । वज्रिणः ॥ ८ ॥

upa | kṣatram | pṛñcīta | hanti | rāja-bhiḥ | bhaye | cit | su-kṣitim | dadhe | na | asya | vartā | na | tarutā | mahā-dhane | na | arbhe | asti | vajriṇaḥ || 8 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्देवः क्षत्रं बलमुप पृञ्चीत । स्वात्मनि सम्पृक्तं कुर्यात् । ततो राजभिर्वरुणादिभिः सह हन्ति । शत्रून्मारयति । भये चित् भीतिहेतौ युद्धेऽपि सुक्षितिं दधे । सुष्ठु निवासस्थैर्यं धारयति । न तु पलायते । वज्रिणो वज्राद्यायुधवतोऽस्य ब्रह्मणस्पतेर्महाधने प्रभूतधननिमित्ते युद्धे वर्ता प्रवर्तयिता नास्ति । कोऽपि नास्ति । स्वयमेव प्रवर्तत इत्यर्थः । महाधन इति सङ्ग्रामनाम । महाधने समीक इति तन्नामसु पाठात् । तथा तरुता तरणस्योल्लङ्घनस्य कर्तान्यः कोऽपि नास्ति । तथैवार्भे स्वल्पे युद्धेऽप्यन्यः प्रवर्तयिता नास्ति ॥ पृञ्चीत । पृची सम्पर्के । लिङ् । रुधादित्वात् श्नम् । श्नसोरल्लोप इत्यकारलोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । क्षत्रं पृञ्चीत राजभिर्हन्ति चेति समुच्चयलक्षणस्य चार्थस्य दर्शनाच्चादिलोपे विभाषेति प्रथमायास्तिङ्विभक्तेर्निघातप्रतिषेधः । हन्तीत्येषा द्वितीयापि तिङः परत्वान्न निहन्यते । सुक्षितिं । शोभना क्षितिः सुक्षितिः । मन्क्तिन्नित्यादिनोत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वं । वर्ता । वर्तेर्वृणोतेर्वा तृच्यागमानुशासनस्यानित्यत्वादिडभावः । तरुता । तॄ प्लवनतरणयोः । ग्रसितस्कभितेत्यादिना तृच्युडागमो निपातितः । चित इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वं । महाधने । महच्च तद्धनं च महाधनं । आन्महतः । पा. ६-३-४६ । इत्यात्वं । तेन शब्देन तद्धेतुभूतः सङ्ग्रामो लक्ष्यते । अर्भे । ऋ गतौ । आर्तिगृभ्यां भन् । उ. ३-१५२ । इति भन्प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥ २१ ॥

brahmaṇaspatir devaḥ kṣatraṃ balam upa pṛñcīta | svātmani saṃpṛktaṃ kuryāt | tato rājabhir varuṇādibhiḥ saha hanti | śatrūn mārayati | bhaye cit bhītihetau yuddhe 'pi sukṣitiṃ dadhe | suṣṭhu nivāsasthairyaṃ dhārayati | na tu palāyate | vajriṇo vajrādyāyudhavato 'sya brahmaṇaspater mahādhane prabhūtadhananimitte yuddhe vartā pravartayitā nāsti | ko 'pi nāsti | svayam eva pravartata ity arthaḥ | mahādhana iti saṅgrāmanāma | mahādhane samīka iti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | tathā tarutā taraṇasyollaṅghanasya kartānyaḥ ko 'pi nāsti | tathaivārbhe svalpe yuddhe 'py anyaḥ pravartayitā nāsti || pṛñcīta | pṛci samparke | liṅ | rudhāditvāt śnam | śnasor allopa ity akāralopaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | kṣatraṃ pṛñcīta rājabhir hanti ceti samuccayalakṣaṇasya cārthasya darśanāc cādilope vibhāṣeti prathamāyās tiṅvibhakter nighātapratiṣedhaḥ | hantīty eṣā dvitīyāpi tiṅaḥ paratvān na nihanyate | sukṣitiṃ | śobhanā kṣitiḥ sukṣitiḥ | man ktinn ity ādinottarapadāntodāttatvaṃ | vartā | varter vṛṇoter vā tṛcy āgamānuśāsanasyānityatvād iḍabhāvaḥ | tarutā | tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ | grasitaskabhitety ādinā tṛcy uḍāgamo nipātitaḥ | cita ity antodāttatvaṃ | mahādhane | mahac ca tad dhanaṃ ca mahādhanaṃ | ānmahataḥ | pā. 6-3-46 | ity ātvaṃ | tena śabdena taddhetubhūtaḥ saṅgrāmo lakṣyate | arbhe | ṛ gatau | ārtigṛbhyāṃ bhan | u. 3-152 | iti bhanpratyayaḥ | nittvād ādyudāttatvaṃ || 21 || The bhāṣya closes with "|| 21 ||" (the varga number; read at 600 dpi).

Translation: "The god Brahmaṇaspati kṣatram, strength, upa pṛñcīta, would unite [with himself]; make it joined with his own self. Then with the rājabhiḥ, the kings Varuṇa and the others, hanti, he slays: he makes the enemies die. Bhaye cit, even in a battle that is the cause of fear, sukṣitim dadhe, he holds a firm and sound steadiness of position; he does not flee. For this vajriṇaḥ, thunderbolt-bearer [Brahmaṇaspati], who has the thunderbolt and other weapons, in the mahādhane, great-wealth [= battle], that arises for much wealth, vartā, one who sets [it] going, na asti, there is none; no one at all; the sense is that he moves of his own will. 'Mahādhana' is a name of battle, since it is read among its names ('mahādhane samīke'). Likewise tarutā, one who steps across or surpasses [him], there is no other; and in the small fight (arbhe) also, there is no other who causes it to go on. Pṛñcīta: root pṛci samparke; liṅ; śnam by the rudhādi class; the loss of a by śnasor allopaḥ; the accent of the suffix. In kṣatraṃ pṛñcīta rājabhir hanti ca — since the sense of conjunction (ca) is perceived — the dropping of a cādi word, by cādilope vibhāṣā: the prohibition of nighāta for the first verb. Hanti is a second verb, but because it follows a tiṅ it is not unaccented. Sukṣitim: 'a fine kṣiti'; the final-acute of the latter member by the rule beginning man-ktin…. Vartā: from vṛt (varteḥ) or vṛ (vṛṇoteḥ); the iṭ is not applied because the teaching of augments is not constant. Tarutā: root tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ; the augment uṭ is irregularly given before tṛc by grasita-skabhita…; final acute by citaḥ. Mahādhane: mahat + dhana; ā for mahat by ān mahataḥ [Pā. 6-3-46]; by this word the battle that is the cause of it is indicated. Ārbhe: root ṛ gatau; bhan by ārtigṛbhyāṃ bhan [U. 3-152]; because it is nit, first-syllable acute."

Pratipadārtha — "(brahmaṇaspatiḥ — Brahmaṇaspati) kṣatram — [his own] strength; upa pṛñcīta — would concentrate in himself; (by that strength) rājabhiḥ — together with the kings, Varuṇa and the others; hanti — he kills the enemies; bhaye cit — even in a fearsome battle; sukṣitim — the steadiness (without flight) in his own place; dadhe — he holds; vajriṇaḥ — [of him who has] weapons such as the thunderbolt; asya — of this Brahmaṇaspati; mahādhane — in a battle fought for abundant wealth; vartā — one who turns [him back] (none else); na asti — there is none (he goes on, moved by his own strength); likewise; tarutā — one who defeats [him], frightening him into flight; na — [none else]; arbhe — in a small battle also; na — [none] such does so."

Bhāvārtha — "Brahmaṇaspati gathers all his strength and, with the help of the kings, Mitra, Varuṇa and the others, destroys the enemies. Even in the face of any danger in battle he is steady. When he is armed with the thunderbolt, there is no man who can oppose or defeat him, either in a great battle or in a small one."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 408) — "Brahmanaspati will concentrate his strength ; with the help of royal gods, ( Varuna and others ) he kills his enemies ; he firmly hold [sic] his ground even in times of danger ; when he is armed with his thunderbolt no one can resist or defeat in a battle great or small."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 408 - kṣatram = balam — "strength; power; ability." - upa pṛñcīta — "pṛcī samparke: let him unite, let him concentrate [at one point]." - rājabhiḥ — "Here, by rājānaḥ, kings, are meant the deities spoken of before: Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman: 'together with those deities'." - bhaye — "in the battle that makes fear, or in time of calamity." - sukṣitim = nivāsasthairyam — "he stands firm; steady, without running away in fear." - vartā = pravartayitā — "one who opposes. There is none who opposes him in battle; he himself is the opposer of all." - tarutā — "he who goes beyond him, that is, who defeats or conquers him." - mahādhane — "since the word mahādhane is read among the forty-odd names of battle beginning with raṇaḥ, vivākaḥ (Ni. 3-9), the word means 'in battle'. The commentator explains the etymological sense: a great battle fought to obtain great wealth." - arbhe — "since the word arbhaka is read among the words for 'small' beginning with ṛhan, hrasvaḥ (Ni. 3-13), arbhe means 'in a small battle, in a small fight'."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 408–409 — grammar pages, noted briefly - pṛñcīta: root pṛcī samparke, rudhādi; vidhiliṅ, ta; sīyuṭ; rudhādibhyaḥ śnam (no number printed); śnasor allopaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-4-111) the loss of the a of śna before a kit or ṅit sārvadhātuka; liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya the loss of the s; n → anusvāra and the following homorganic: pṛñcīta; the accent is that of the suffix. "Brahmaṇaspatiḥ balaṃ pṛñcīta, tataḥ rājabhiḥ saha hanti ca": since the sense of ca [conjunction] is perceived, by cādilope vibhāṣā (no number printed) the prohibition of the wholly-unaccented applies to pṛñcīta, the first verb. - hanti: "although this is not the first verb, the verb pṛñcīta stands before it; so tiṅ atiṅaḥ does not make it wholly unaccented." - vartā: vṛtu vartane (first class) or vṛñ varaṇe (svādi): after one of these, tṛc; because of "āgamaśāstram anityam" the iṭ does not come to tṛc; if the first root is taken, laghūpadhaguṇa; jharo jhari savarṇe (the loss of a t); if the second, sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ gives guṇa: vartṛ. Nominative singular su; ṛduśanaspurudaṃso 'nehasāṃ ca — ऋदुशनस्पुरुदंसोऽनेहसां च — (Pā. Sū. 7-1-94): anaṅ substitute; aprāpt… [as read]; ata upadhāyāḥ…: lengthening of the penultimate; halṅyābbhyaḥ… the loss of su; nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya the loss of the n. - tarutā: tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ; grasitaskabhitastabhitottabhitacitta-vikastā-viśastṛ-śaṃstṛ-śāstṛ-tarutṛ-… — ग्रसितस्कभितस्तभितोत्तभितचित्तविकस्ताविशस्तृशंस्तृशास्तृतरुतृ… — (Pā. Sū. 7-2-34): in this sūtra the augment uṭ is nipātita for the tṛc after the root tṝ: tṝ + utṛ; guṇa: tarutṛ; su is raised as before; by citaḥ (no number printed) the final-acute. - mahādhane: mahat ca tad dhanaṃ ca; viśeṣaṇaṃ viśeṣyeṇa bahulam (no number printed): a compound; ān mahataḥ samānādhikaraṇajātīyayoḥ — आन्महतः समानाधिकरणजातीययोः — (Pā. Sū. 6-3-46): when a latter member in apposition or a jātīya suffix follows, the t of mahat becomes ā; so mahā + dhana. "The battle, which is the cause of great wealth, is conveyed by implication." - arbhe: ṛ gatau; ārtigṛbhyāṃ bhan (U. Sū. 3-432, as printed in the grammar's own Uṇādi series), after the roots ṛ gatau and gṝ nigaraṇe the suffix bhan: ṛ + bha; guṇa: arbha; the suffix is nit, so first-syllable acute. Rik 8 ends here (|| 8 ||).

Close of Sūkta 40. Printed on p. 409 after the grammar: "illige 40ne sūkta pūrṇavu" — "Here the 40th sūkta is complete." Numeral read as "40". A flourish follows. With it the Fifth Sūkta of the Eighth Anuvāka (printed pp. 376–409) ends. The next leaf, p. 410 = PDF 424, carries the title "nalavattondaneya sūktavu" ("the forty-first sūkta"), the Sanskrit introduction and Kannada anuvāda of Sūkta 41 (yaṃ rakṣanti, nine Riks, ṛṣi Kaṇva Ghaura, deities Varuṇa–Mitra–Aryaman [Riks 1–3 and 7–9] and the Ādityas [Riks 4–6], Gāyatrī metre), and the heading of Sūkta 41; these follow below.

Summary of Sūkta 40. Eight Riks to Brahmaṇaspati. Rik 1 calls him to rise and asks the Maruts to come near and Indra to drink the Soma with him; Rik 2 says the man who praises Brahmaṇaspati and the Maruts for wealth will obtain horses and heroism; Rik 3 invites Brahmaṇaspati, the goddess Sūnṛtā and the other gods to drive the enemy away and lead the worshippers to the sacrifice; Rik 4 promises undiminishing food to the sacrificer who gives to the priests and praises Iḷā; Rik 5 says Brahmaṇaspati speaks a mantra in which Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra and Aryaman dwell; Rik 6 offers that mantra to the gods; Rik 7 asks which other god would come to the sacrificer; Rik 8 says Brahmaṇaspati unites his strength with the royal gods and none can resist him, great or small. All eight Riks are written in full; the heavily crowded grammar passages are characterized only.

Sūkta 41 — "yaṃ rakṣanti"

original p. 410

Forty-first Sūkta large Kannada title line: "nalavattondaneya sūktavu"

original p. 410

Sāyaṇa's introduction, the Kannada anuvāda, and the heading

Sāyaṇa's introduction printed in Kannada script; read from the 150-dpi image

यं रक्षन्तीति नवर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तं । तत्रानुक्रमणं । यं रक्षन्ति नव वरुणमित्रार्यम्णां मध्ये तृच आदित्येभ्यो गायत्रं हीति । घोरपुत्रः कण्व ऋषिः । इदमादित्रीणि सूक्तानि गायत्राणि । आद्यन्तयोस्तृचयोर्वरुणमित्रार्यमणो देवताः । मध्यतृचस्य सुगः पन्था इत्यस्यादित्या देवताः ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

yaṃ rakṣantīti navarcaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ sūktaṃ | tatrānukramaṇaṃ | yaṃ rakṣanti nava varuṇamitrāryamṇāṃ madhye tṛca ādityebhyo gāyatraṃ hīti | ghoraputraḥ kaṇva ṛṣiḥ | idam ādi trīṇi sūktāni gāyatrāṇi | ādyantayos tṛcayor varuṇamitrāryamaṇo devatāḥ | madhyatṛcasya sugaḥ panthā ity asyādityā devatāḥ || gato viniyogaḥ ||

Translation: "Yaṃ rakṣanti — the sixth sūkta [of the anuvāka], of nine ṛks. The Anukramaṇikā there: 'yaṃ rakṣanti nava varuṇamitrāryamṇāṃ madhye tṛca ādityebhyo gāyatraṃ hi' [nine [ṛks], of Varuṇa–Mitra–Aryaman; in the middle a tṛca for the Ādityas; Gāyatra]. Kaṇva, son of Ghora, is the ṛṣi. This and the next two sūktas are in the Gāyatrī metre. For the first and the last tṛca the deities are Varuṇa, Mitra and Aryaman; for the middle tṛca — beginning sugaḥ panthāḥ — the Ādityas. The application has been stated [before]." Translation editorial; the print is clear here.

Anuvāda (Kannada), p. 410 — "Yaṃ rakṣanti is the sixth sūkta in the eighth anuvāka. It has nine ṛks. In the Anukramaṇikā: 'yaṃ rakṣanti nava varuṇamitrāryamṇāṃ madhye tṛca ādityebhyo gāyatraṃ hi'. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Kaṇva, the son of Ghora. This sūkta and the next two are of the Gāyatrī metre. For the first three ṛks and the last three ṛks the deities are Varuṇa, Mitra and Aryaman; for the middle three ṛks, that is [Riks] 4–6, the Ādityas are the deities. The application has been stated already."

Rik 1

Saṃhitā-pāṭha Saṃhitā accents as printed (checked at 300–560 dpi); Pada unaccented.

यं रक्ष॑न्ति॒ प्रचे॑तसो॒ वरु॑णो मि॒त्रो अ॑र्य॒मा । नू चि॒त्स द॑भ्यते॒ जनः॑ ॥ १ ॥

yaṃ rákṣanti prácetaso váruṇo mitró aryamā́ | nū cit sá dabhyate jánaḥ || 1 ||

Pada-pāṭha

यम् । रक्षन्ति । प्रऽचेतसः । वरुणः । मित्रः । अर्यमा । नु । चित् । सः । दभ्यते । जनः ॥ १ ॥

yam | rakṣanti | pra-cetasaḥ | varuṇaḥ | mitraḥ | aryamā | nu | cit | saḥ | dabhyate | janaḥ || 1 || The Saṃhitā prints nū, the Pada nu.

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

प्रचेतसः प्रकृष्टज्ञानयुक्ता वरुणादयो देवा यं यजमानं रक्षन्ति स जनो यजमानो नू चित् क्षिप्रमेव दभ्यते । दभ्नोति । शत्रून् हिनस्ति । प्रचेतसः । प्रकृष्टं चेतो येषां । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । नू चित् । ऋचि तुनुघेत्यादिना दीर्घः । दभ्यते । दम्भु दम्भे । व्यत्ययेन श्यन् आत्मनेपदं च ॥

pracetasaḥ prakṛṣṭajñānayuktā varuṇādayo devā yaṃ yajamānaṃ rakṣanti sa jano yajamāno nū cit kṣiprameva dabhyate | dabhnoti | śatrūn hinasti | pracetasaḥ | prakṛṣṭaṃ ceto yeṣāṃ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | nū cit | ṛci tunughety ādinā dīrghaḥ | dabhyate | dambhu dambhe | vyatyayena śyan ātmanepadaṃ ca ||

Translation: "Pracetasaḥ, endowed with excellent knowledge, the gods Varuṇa and the rest — whichever sacrificer they protect, that man, the sacrificer, nū cit, quickly indeed, dabhyate: he dabhnoti, he destroys the enemies. Pracetasaḥ: 'of whom the mind is excellent'; in the bahuvrīhi the accent of the first member. Nū cit: the lengthening by ṛci tunugha…. Dabhyate: root dambhu dambhe; by vyatyaya the suffix śyan and the ātmanepada."

Pratipadārtha — "pracetasaḥ — those of excellent knowledge; varuṇaḥ — Varuṇa; mitraḥ — Mitra; and aryamā — Aryaman; yam — which sacrificer [the performer of the sacrifice]; rakṣanti — they protect; saḥ janaḥ — that sacrificer; nū cit — carefully [quickly]; dabhyate — destroys [the enemies]."

Bhāvārtha — "The sacrificer whom Varuṇa, Mitra and Aryaman, the deities of excellent knowledge, protect, carefully destroys his enemies."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 412) — "That person whom wise Varuna, Mitra, and Aryaman protect quickly defeats his enemies."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 412 - pracetasaḥ = prakṛṣṭajñānayuktāḥ — "those who are endowed with excellent knowledge, the wise." - nū cit = kṣiprameva — "swiftly, quickly." - dabhyate — "dambhu dambhe; dabhnoti iti śatrūn hinasti — he destroys enemies; or, if the sense of the passive use must be given: nū cit dabhyate, 'he is not injured by the enemy' — in this context the word nū must be taken in the sense of a negative, na."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā p. 412 — grammar page, noted briefly - rakṣanti: root rakṣa pālane, first class; because of the connection with yat (yam) the wholly-unaccented form does not come. - pracetasaḥ: "prakṛṣṭaṃ cetaḥ yeṣāṃ te": a bahuvrīhi; the accent of the first member. - varuṇaḥ: kṛvṛdāribhya unan (no number printed): the suffix unan; since it is nit the first syllable is acute. - nū: the lengthening by the sūtra ṛci tunugha—. - dabhyate: dambhu dambhe, svādi; the śnu vikaraṇa would properly come, but by vyatyayo bahulam śyan comes, and by the same sūtra the ātmanepada in place of the parasmaipada: dan bh + ya + te; because śyan is sārvadhātukam apit it is ṅit; by aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti the penultimate nasal is lost; since anusvāra and parasavarṇa are treated as non-existent (asiddha), it is to be understood that the nasal is present as far as the sūtra that gives the loss is concerned. Rik 1 ends here (|| 1 ||).

यं बा॒हुते॑व॒ पिप्र॑ति॒ पान्ति॒ मर्त्यं॑ रि॒षः । अरि॑ष्टः॒ सर्व॑ एधते ॥ २ ॥ [accent ?]

yaṃ bāhúteva píprati pā́nti mártyaṃ riṣáḥ | áriṣṭaḥ sárva edhate || 2 || [accent ?]

Pada-pāṭha

यम् । बाहुताऽइव । पिप्रति । पान्ति । मर्त्यम् । रिषः । अरिष्टः । सर्वः । एधते ॥ २ ॥

yam | bāhutā-iva | piprati | pānti | martyam | riṣaḥ | ariṣṭaḥ | sarvaḥ | edhate || 2 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

यं यजमानं पिप्रति वरुणादयो देवा धनैः पूरयन्ति । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । बाहुतेव स्वकीयो बाहुवर्गोऽपेक्षितं धनमानीय यथा पूरयति तद्वत् । तथा यं मर्त्यं मनुष्यं यजमानं रिषो हिंसकात् पान्ति रक्षन्ति स सर्वो यजमानोऽरिष्टः केनाप्यहिंसितः सन् एधते । वर्धते ॥ बाहुतेव । बाहुता बाहुत्वं । भाववाचिनानेन शब्देन बाहवस्तदाश्रया लक्ष्यन्ते । यद्वा । समूहार्थे तल्प्रत्ययो द्रष्टव्यः । लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वं । पिप्रति । पॄ पालनपूरणयोः । पृ इत्येके । जुहोत्यादित्वात् श्लुः । अर्तिपिपर्त्योश्चेत्यभ्यासस्येत्वं । अभ्यस्तानामादिरित्याद्युदात्तत्वं । पान्ति । तिङः परत्वात्पादादित्वाद्वा निघाताभावः । रिषः । रिष हिंसायां क्विप्चेति क्विप् । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । अरिष्टः । रिष हिंसायां । एकाच इतीट्प्रतिषेधः । व्रश्चादिना षत्वं । नञ्समासेऽव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥

yaṃ yajamānaṃ piprati varuṇādayo devā dhanaiḥ pūrayanti | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | bāhuteva svakīyo bāhuvargo 'pekṣitaṃ dhanam ānīya yathā pūrayati tadvat | tathā yaṃ martyaṃ manuṣyaṃ yajamānaṃ riṣo hiṃsakāt pānti rakṣanti sa sarvo yajamāno 'riṣṭaḥ kenāpy ahiṃsitaḥ san edhate | vardhate || bāhuteva | bāhutā bāhutvaṃ | bhāvavācinānena śabdena bāhavas tadāśrayā lakṣyante | yadvā | samūhārthe talpratyayo draṣṭavyaḥ | liti iti pratyayāt pūrvasyodāttatvaṃ | piprati | pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ | pṛ ity eke | juhotyāditvāt śluḥ | artipipartyoś cety abhyāsasyetvaṃ | abhyastānām ādir ity ādyudāttatvaṃ | pānti | tiṅaḥ paratvāt pādāditvād vā nighātābhāvaḥ | riṣaḥ | riṣa hiṃsāyāṃ kvip ceti kvip | sāvekāca iti vibhakter udāttatvaṃ | ariṣṭaḥ | riṣa hiṃsāyāṃ | ekāca itīṭpratiṣedhaḥ | vraścādinā ṣatvaṃ | nañsamāse 'vyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ||

Translation: "The sacrificer whom Varuṇa and the other gods piprati, fill with wealth. The example: bāhutā iva — as a company of arms (bāhuvarga) fetches the wealth needed and fills his own [house], so. And the mortal, the man, the sacrificer whom they protect from riṣaḥ, from a destroyer, that whole sacrificer, ariṣṭaḥ, uninjured by anyone, edhate, prospers. Bāhuteva: bāhutā is 'arm-ness'; by this abstract word the arms, as that on which it rests, are indicated; or the suffix tal in the sense of a collection is to be seen; the syllable before the suffix is acute by lit. Piprati: root pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ (some read pṛ); ślu because of the juhotyādi class; i in the reduplicate by artipipartyoś ca; the first syllable acute by abhyastānām ādiḥ. Pānti: no nighāta, since it follows a tiṅ or because it is at the beginning of a pāda. Riṣaḥ: root riṣa hiṃsāyām, kvip; the ending acute by sāvekāca. Ariṣṭaḥ: the prohibition of iṭ by ekāca…; ṣatva by vraścādi…; the accent of the first member in a nañ-compound with an indeclinable."

Pratipadārtha — "bāhuteva — as with his own arms (bringing in as much as he wishes) he fills; yam — which sacrificer; piprati — [Varuṇa and the other deities] fill with wealth; and martyam — which man; riṣaḥ — from a harming enemy; pānti — they protect; sarvaḥ — each such (sacrificer); ariṣṭaḥ — uninjured by anyone; edhate — grows."

Bhāvārtha — "As one fills himself with as much goods as he needs, bringing them with his own arms, so Varuṇa and the other deities fill the sacrificer with wealth, and the man whom they protect from an injuring enemy attains prosperity without any hindrance."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 414) — "He whom they ( gods ) help with riches, as if collected by his own arms ; the man whom they defend from the malignant ; every such man safe from injury prospers."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 414 - bāhuteva = svakīyo bāhuvargo 'pekṣitaṃ dhanam ānīya yathā pūrayati tadvat — "as one's own arms bring as much wealth as he needs and fill [his house]." - piprati = pūrayanti — "they fill, they make full." - riṣaḥ = hiṃsakāt — "from the enemy who injures." - ariṣṭaḥ — "free from the injury of enemies or from hindrance."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 414–415 — grammar pages, noted briefly - bāhuteva: tasya bhāvas tvatalau — तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ — (Pā. Sū. 6-1-118 [as printed; for 5-1-119]; first digit ೬-shaped, last ೮, at 840 dpi): the suffix tal in the abstract sense; by the abstract word bāhutā the arms, as the support of bāhutva, are indicated by implication; or else, by grāmajanabandhubhyas tal — ग्रामजनबन्धुभ्यस्तल् — (Pā. Sū. 4-2-43), tal is prescribed after grāma and the like in the sense of collection, and by Vedic usage the same holds for bāhu; liti (no number printed): the syllable before the suffix is acute. - piprati: root pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ, juhotyādi (some read it as pṛ, ending in a short vowel); after it laṭ, jhi; ad abhyastāt — अदभ्यस्तात् — (no number printed) at for jh; śap → ślu; ślau doubling: pṛ + pṛ + ati; if the root ended in a long vowel, udoṣṭhyapūrvasya would give u; the print says the ṛ-form reading is not in conformity with Pāṇini, who in his view reads the root with a Vedic shortening (chāndasa hrasva) — "'pāṇinīyamate tu taṃ rodasī pipṛtam', in this and in similar passages Bhaṭṭoji Dīkṣita has said that the shortening is Vedic [chāndasatvaṃ śaraṇam]"; ur at gives a in the reduplicate, with raparatva; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ the loss of r; artipipartyoś ca — अर्तिपिपर्त्योश्च — (Pā. Sū. 7-4-77): the a of the reduplicate of the roots ṛ, pṝ (or pṛ) takes i when ślu has come: pipṛ + ati; yaṇ: piprati; by abhyastānām ādiḥ — first-syllable acute. - pānti: root pā rakṣaṇe; since it stands after a verb, or at the beginning of a pāda, tiṅ atiṅaḥ does not make it wholly unaccented. - riṣaḥ: riṣa hiṃsāyām; kvip ca (no number printed) kvip; jas; sāvekācaḥ… the ending is acute. - ariṣṭaḥ: riśa hiṃsāyām, tudādi [print: riśa]; after it kta; this being in the list riś-ruś-liś-viś-spṛś-kṛṣaḥ (the anudāttopadeśa roots enumerated), it is unaccented; ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt — the prohibition of iṭ; vraścabhrasjasṛjamṛjayajarājabhrājachśām ṣaḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-2-36) gives ṣ for the ś; ṣṭutva; "na riṣṭaḥ": a nañ-compound; tatpuruṣe tulyārtha… gives the accent of the first member as an indeclinable. Rik 2 ends here (|| 2 ||).
